intro.heading: A map pin is not a qualification
paragraphs: The phrase IB IGCSE tuition near me is a proximity query carrying a question about quality. What a parent wants is someone who knows the syllabus their child sits, the paper that is costing them marks, and the internal deadline the school has already set. What a search engine returns is a radius. Dubai widens that gap more than most cities, because the private-school market is both large and spread out: KHDA's sector figures for 2024-25 record 387,441 pupils across 227 private schools licensed to teach 17 different curricula. A family in Mirdif and a family in Jumeirah Park may both need Cambridge IGCSE 0580 help, and the nearest competent person to each of them is very unlikely to be the same person.

So this page sets out what the work itself looks like, because the work is the only thing a parent can inspect before committing money. Every session IB Gram arranges produces something you can read afterwards. That might be an annotated past-paper script with the mark scheme alongside it, showing where two marks went on a six-mark explain question. It might be a drill sheet built from the four question types your child dropped marks on. It might be a written comment on an Internal Assessment draft naming the criterion by letter and the descriptor band the draft currently sits in. Progress is a sequence of those artefacts, filed and dated, rather than a monthly reassurance that things are going well.

Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time around Dubai school timetables. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, and does not make home visits in Dubai; home visits are a service offered only in India. Saying that plainly matters, because it changes what you actually receive. The tutor is selected from the whole pool for the exact board and level, instead of from whoever can reach Al Furjan by 4.30pm on a Tuesday. Online IB tuition in Dubai takes travel out of the price and out of the timetable, and that is what makes the matching honest rather than geographic.

The order of this page follows the order a decision gets made. First, what the radius actually buys you and what it costs you. Then the evidence: marked scripts, criterion comments, a twelve-week record. Then the calendar, counted backwards from the exam window, because a Cambridge entry deadline sits months before the paper and most families meet it by accident. Then the regulator, the mandatory UAE subjects that run alongside any international curriculum in Dubai, and what tuition costs in this market with every figure attributed to whoever published it.

One honest caveat before any of it. No tutor can promise a grade, and anyone who does is telling you something about their sales process rather than their teaching. What tuition can do is make the loss visible and then shrink it: identify the question types that are costing marks, teach the content behind them, and re-test under the same conditions so the movement is measurable. If after four sessions nothing has moved on an identical paper, that is information too, and it is better to have it in writing in November than to discover it in May.

dubai/ib-igcse-tuition-near-me.programmesIntro: Dubai students arrive at tuition from four main routes, and the route changes what a session should do. These are the programmes this page covers, with what each one assesses and how it plays out in Dubai specifically.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Five years of concept-led study assessed against four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight and converted to a 1-7 grade by published boundaries. There are no external papers in most subjects, so a student can hold a solid MYP grade and still be unprepared for the timed-paper discipline of IGCSE or the Diploma. MYP 5 students sitting ePortfolios and the Personal Project meet their first real deadline-management test.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai runs MYP at continuum schools such as Uptown International School, Dubai International Academy and GEMS World Academy, and MYP 5 students often transfer into IGCSE or the Diploma elsewhere in the emirate. The practical consequence for tuition is timed-paper practice: criterion marking rewards process, while a Cambridge paper rewards precision against a mark scheme, and the switch is where confident MYP students stumble.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across three Higher Level and three Standard Level choices, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Internal Assessment carries roughly a fifth to a quarter of the grade in most subjects, and it is marked by the teacher against criteria then moderated by the IB. Higher Level adds both content and a third paper in the sciences, which is where HL and SL stop being the same course at different speeds.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools enter candidates for the May session, which is the one that matters for a UAE academic year ending in June. No IB session or results date appears on this page: ibo.org is the only authoritative source and it should be checked with your school's IB coordinator, who also sets the internal IA and Extended Essay deadlines that in practice govern a Dubai student's year far more tightly than the exam window does.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Subject-by-subject qualifications with syllabus codes that matter: 0580 Mathematics, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry, 0610 Biology, 0500 First Language English. Most are tiered into Core and Extended, with Core capped at grade C or 5 and Extended reaching A* or 9. Tier choice is made at entry, months before the paper, and it is the single decision most likely to cap a result before revision has even started.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge runs a June and a November series, with March available in some regions, and every exam centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones with its own timetable version. Cambridge states that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used, so a Dubai parent should take the timetable from the school's exams officer rather than from a generic website.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The other IGCSE in Dubai classrooms, with its own codes such as 4MA1 Mathematics A, 4PH1 Physics and 4CH1 Chemistry. Pearson offers a modular route in some subjects, meaning units can be sat in different series and banked, which changes revision planning completely. Papers are available in a May/June and a November series each year, and provisional timetables are published ahead of each one.
programmes.countryNote: A single Dubai family can easily hold two boards at once, because schools pick subject by subject and a transfer mid-IGCSE can split a child across Cambridge and Pearson. The gap shows up in command-term wording and in formula-sheet provision, not in the physics. Any Dubai Marina IGCSE tuition request therefore starts with a question about the entry code on the statement of entry, not about the subject name.

dubai/ib-igcse-tuition-near-me.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects Dubai families most often ask about, with what each one actually assesses and the specific place marks go missing. The description is deliberately narrow: a tutor who cannot name the failure mode is not diagnosing anything.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic fluency carries the paper. Marks are lost on unjustified steps in proof questions, on calculator-paper answers given to the wrong accuracy, and on the HL Paper 3 extended investigation, where students answer the mathematics but never address the question's final 'hence deduce'. The Exploration is where structure, not difficulty, decides the mark.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics with a graphic display calculator throughout. Losses cluster in interpretation: a correct regression line with no comment on its validity, a hypothesis test with the conclusion stated in statistical language the question did not ask for. Students who were strong at MYP mathematics often underestimate how much of this paper is writing.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580
subjects.description: Two papers, non-calculator and calculator, with Extended reaching the top grades and Core capped. Marks go on method lines not shown, premature rounding carried through multi-step problems, and bearings, vectors and transformations, which are taught early and then never revisited before the series.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625
subjects.description: Electricity and the practical paper account for most of the gap between a 6 and an 8. Students describe apparatus instead of controlling variables, confuse series and parallel current rules under time pressure, and lose units and significant figures in calculation chains that were otherwise correct.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620
subjects.description: Moles, electrolysis and organic nomenclature are the three recurring sinkholes. Equations are written unbalanced, state symbols omitted, and qualitative-analysis answers give the observation without the inference the mark scheme requires. The alternative-to-practical paper rewards exam technique far more than laboratory experience.

subjects.name: IB Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms at HL, plus a data-based paper that punishes loose language about uncertainty. The Internal Assessment is where most of the recoverable marks sit: a narrow, measurable research question scores better than an ambitious one that cannot be controlled in a school laboratory.

subjects.name: IB Biology
subjects.description: Command terms decide this subject. 'Outline', 'explain' and 'evaluate' carry different mark allocations and students answer all three the same way. Statistics in the data questions, and the ethics and limitations commentary in the Internal Assessment, are the two places a well-revised student still drops a band.

subjects.name: IB Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams are marks, not decoration: axes, labels, shifts and a sentence explaining the movement. Paper 3 at HL rewards quantitative accuracy and nothing else. The three commentaries ask for real published articles analysed against named theory, and most lose marks for summarising the article rather than applying the model.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is unseen analysis, Paper 2 comparative, and the Individual Oral links a global issue to two texts. Students write about content and forget form; the marks are in structure, diction and the writer's choices. HL adds the essay on one studied text, which needs an argument, not a reading.

subjects.name: Arabic and UAE Social Studies
subjects.levels: First language and additional language streams
subjects.description: Mandatory in Dubai private schools alongside any licensed international curriculum. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with the language of instruction set per group, so support must follow the stream the school has placed the child in.

sections.heading: What a near-me search actually returns in Dubai
paragraphs: A near-me search returns businesses with a verified address close to you, ranked largely on local signals: proximity, category, reviews and the completeness of a business listing. None of those signals is a measure of whether the person who turns up has taught Cambridge IGCSE 0620 or read a Diploma Chemistry Internal Assessment against criterion D. That is not a flaw in the search engine. It is a mismatch between the question a parent is asking and the question the ranking system is built to answer.

In a smaller city the mismatch costs little, because the pool inside a short drive is most of the pool. Dubai is not that city. The emirate's private sector held 387,441 pupils across 227 schools in 2024-25, licensed across 17 curricula, and the specialists are distributed by where they happen to live rather than by where the demand is. A parent in Al Furjan searching for IGCSE tuition in Dubai and a parent in Mirdif searching the same phrase will see two almost disjoint lists, and neither list is ranked on subject expertise.

The second thing a near-me search hides is the entry code. Two children in the same Year 11 class can sit Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1, which are different papers with different formula provision and different command-term habits. A local listing cannot tell you which one a tutor has actually marked. A statement of entry can, and it is the first document worth photographing before any tuition conversation starts.

So the honest answer to the query is this: use proximity to decide where your child studies, and use syllabus evidence to decide who teaches them. The rest of this page is about the second half of that sentence.

sections.heading: Proximity versus syllabus match: the trade a Dubai radius forces
paragraphs: A twenty-minute drive at 4pm on a Dubai weekday is a much smaller circle than a twenty-minute drive at 11am. That circle is the real catchment of an in-home tutor, and it is the reason specialist coverage varies so sharply by community. The table below sets out, community by community, what that circle covers, which specialists are realistically inside it, and what live video changes.

The pattern is consistent across the emirate. Generalist primary and lower-secondary cover exists almost everywhere. Higher Level Diploma sciences, Mathematics AA HL, Economics HL and anything involving Internal Assessment supervision thin out quickly once you leave the Jumeirah and Al Barsha corridor. Families in Al Furjan, Discovery Gardens and the Jebel Ali side of the city feel it most, because travel time prices independent tutors out before the subject is even discussed.

IB Gram does not provide in-person tutoring in Dubai, and no tutor arrives at a UAE address; every lesson runs over live video with a shared screen and a graphics tablet. The point of saying so on a near-me page is that the alternative is not a compromise on the same thing. It is a different offer: the whole specialist pool instead of the fraction of it inside a rush-hour radius, and a fixed start time that a closed lane on Al Khail Road cannot move.

Where the trade genuinely runs the other way is with younger children who need physical presence to stay on task, and with practical laboratory work that no screen reproduces. Those are real limits and they belong on this page as much as the advantages do.

sections.heading: The evidence pack: what each session leaves behind
paragraphs: An hour of tutoring with nothing written down is an hour you cannot audit. The habit this page is built around is simple: every session produces one artefact that a parent can read without being able to teach the subject. Three kinds do almost all of the work.

The first is a marked script. Your child sits a past paper or a section of one, to time, and it comes back annotated against the published mark scheme with the marks allocated question by question. The useful part is not the total. It is the pattern: four marks lost across three questions that all asked for an explanation, or two marks lost to premature rounding in a multi-step calculation. That pattern is a teaching plan, and it is visible to a parent in thirty seconds.

The second is a drill sheet. Once the pattern is known, the session narrows to that question type, and the sheet carries the worked models plus a short re-test on the same type. The point of a drill sheet is that it is comparable: the same type reappears three or four weeks later under the same conditions, and either the marks moved or they did not.

The third is a criterion comment on a piece of coursework the student has written. It names the criterion by letter, states the descriptor band the draft currently sits in, and lists what would move it up a band. It never contains replacement sentences, because the draft has to remain the student's own writing. That boundary is set out in full further down this page.

Internal Assessment feedback, marked scripts and drill sheets together are what we mean by evidence. They are also what makes the free trial lesson worth taking: the trial produces the first marked script, so you can judge the tutor on how they read it.

sections.heading: Twelve weeks of recorded progress, artefact by artefact
paragraphs: A term is roughly twelve teaching weeks in a Dubai school year, which is enough time for one full diagnostic-to-retest cycle and no more. Planning it as a cycle rather than as a series of lessons is what makes the end of it measurable. The table sets out how a standard twelve-week block runs and what sits in the file at each stage.

Two design choices in that table are deliberate. The first paper is sat before any teaching happens, which parents often resist because it feels like setting a child up to fail. It is the opposite: without a timed baseline there is nothing to compare the week-ten paper to, and a reported school grade is not a baseline because it is a blend of coursework, effort and classwork. The second choice is that the week-ten paper is the same question types under the same conditions, not a harder paper, because changing two variables at once tells you nothing.

Weeks seven to nine sit on coursework for a reason specific to Dubai timetables. School internal deadlines for Internal Assessment drafts and Extended Essay checkpoints cluster in the middle of a term, months before any exam window, and families who plan around the exam date routinely miss them. The tutoring block is scheduled to the school's calendar, which means asking for it in the first session.

If the twelve weeks produce no movement, the honest options are a different tutor, a different diagnosis, or an acceptance that the ceiling is in the tier choice rather than in the teaching. All three are better conversations to have at week twelve with a file of marked papers than at week thirty with a feeling.

sections.heading: Reading a mark scheme the way an examiner reads it
paragraphs: Most recoverable marks in IGCSE and Diploma papers are lost to technique, and technique is almost entirely a question of what the mark scheme rewards. A six-mark explain question is not an invitation to write for six minutes. It is a request for a specific number of linked points, each of which earns a mark, in an order that shows cause leading to effect. Students who write beautifully and score five out of nine are usually writing the right content in a shape the mark scheme cannot credit.

The command terms do most of the damage. 'State' wants a fact with no justification and no credit for one. 'Describe' wants what happens. 'Explain' wants why, with a mechanism. 'Evaluate' wants both sides and a judgement, and loses marks when the judgement is left implicit. These distinctions are published by the boards and taught in schools, and they still account for a predictable slice of lost marks because they are easy to understand and hard to perform under time pressure.

The second common loss is arithmetic hygiene in otherwise correct work: premature rounding carried through three steps, a missing unit, a significant-figure convention ignored on the calculator paper. In IGCSE Physics 0625 and Chemistry 0620 this is worth more than any single topic. It is also the fastest thing to fix, which is why the first few weeks of a block often look unglamorous.

IGCSE past paper marking in a session means one more thing worth stating plainly. IB Gram does not reproduce or supply board syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads. Those materials belong to Cambridge, Pearson and the IB, and the right route is the school's exams officer or the board's own site, cited and linked, with the session spent on how to use them.

sections.heading: Internal Assessment and the Extended Essay: where feedback stops
paragraphs: This is the boundary that separates a tutor from an essay mill, and the Dubai search results for Diploma coursework contain both. The IB's academic-honesty rules make the student the sole author of their Internal Assessment, Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge essay and Personal Project. A tutor teaches the skills, reads the draft and gives feedback. A tutor who supplies sentences has created a malpractice case against the student, and the consequence falls on the candidate rather than on the person who was paid.

What a session can legitimately do is substantial. It can narrow a research question until it is measurable in a school laboratory or answerable from available data. It can read a draft against the criterion descriptors and say, in writing, that the analysis currently sits in the middle band and what a top band requires. It can teach referencing, uncertainty treatment, the difference between describing a result and evaluating a method, and how to structure an argument that answers the question asked. It can read a second time after the student has rewritten it.

What it cannot do is produce text, edit a draft into finished prose, or hand over a model answer for the same research question. No tutor at IB Gram writes, redrafts or submits a student's coursework, and any provider offering a completed Internal Assessment is selling the student a disciplinary risk, not a grade. The published prices for that service in this market are easy to find; that does not make it safe to buy.

Supervision deadlines are set by the school, not by the board, and in Dubai they typically run several months ahead of the exam series. Getting the internal calendar in the first session is the practical half of this section.

sections.heading: The exam calendar, counted backwards
paragraphs: Almost every competitor page in this market talks about exams without naming a session, a deadline or a results date. That is the single largest information gap in the Dubai tutoring search results, and it matters because the deadlines that decide a result sit months before the paper. The table reads the calendar backwards, from the certificate to the entry.

The Cambridge March 2027 series is the clearest worked example of why. Cambridge publishes final entries as due on 27 November 2026 for an exam period running from 3 February to 4 March 2027, with forecast grades due 27 February 2027, results released on Cambridge Direct on 13 May and certificates issued in late June. The tier decision, Core or Extended, is made at that November entry, which means a revision plan starting in January is working inside a ceiling fixed ten weeks earlier.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE papers run in a May/June and a November series. The November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. For the June 2026 series, results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and revises them, so the live PDF on the Pearson site is the only version worth planning against.

No IB session or results date appears in that table, and that is deliberate. The IB's own timetable is the authoritative source and should be confirmed with your school's IB coordinator. What can be said safely is that Dubai schools enter candidates for the May session, and that the internal Internal Assessment and Extended Essay deadlines the school sets are the dates a Diploma family should actually be planning around.

sections.heading: KHDA inspection bands and what a school report does not tell you
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. KHDA inspects annually and publishes a judgement on a six-band scale. Parents read those bands closely when choosing a school and then, understandably, assume the band says something about their own child's marks. It does not, and the gap between the two is where tuition decisions get made badly.

An inspection judges the school: teaching quality, leadership, provision, outcomes across cohorts. A high band tells you the median student is well served. It cannot tell you whether your child is in the group that is not, or whether a strong overall judgement is carried by a subject your child does not take. Equally, a lower band does not mean a particular department is weak. KHDA inspection bands are a procurement signal for parents choosing a school, not a diagnostic for an individual learner.

What is diagnostic is a timed paper marked against the mark scheme, which is why this page keeps returning to it. A school report blends classwork, effort, coursework and assessment into a single letter or number that is genuinely useful to a teacher and nearly useless for planning revision. The table below sets out what each band describes and what it leaves open.

One further Dubai-specific point belongs here. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package. For a family budgeting tuition alongside fees, a flat fee year is the context in which a weekly session is actually affordable or not.

sections.heading: Mandatory UAE subjects, permits and what to verify before paying
paragraphs: Two regulatory facts shape tutoring in Dubai and almost no competitor page mentions either. The first is that Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with KHDA's requirements to be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year, and April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, and KHDA advises that no mandatory-subject lesson runs shorter than 25 minutes.

That has a direct consequence for tuition. Support for these subjects must follow the stream the school placed the child in, because the syllabus and the language of instruction differ between streams. KHDA also notes that using different or additional content for the mandatory subjects without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited, so this is not a space for invented material.

The second fact is the permit. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount is quoted here.

A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal and needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute. IB Gram holds no regulator permit of that kind, operates no UAE premises, and makes no claim of approval or accreditation by KHDA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. Ask any provider which permit applies to them and verify it before paying.

sections.heading: What tuition costs in Dubai, in context
paragraphs: Three of the six best-ranking pages in this market publish no price at all, and two of the remaining ones quote US dollars, which is not the currency a Dubai family transacts in. So here are the market bands in dirhams, each attributed to whoever published it. These are market rates, not an IB Gram price list.

The useful way to read the table is as a set of trade-offs rather than a ladder. Budget online tutoring, often delivered by university students, sits at the bottom and is a reasonable buy for homework support and consolidation. A qualified subject tutor working online occupies the middle. Specialist IGCSE and Diploma work, especially Higher Level sciences and coursework supervision, sits above it. In-home visits carry travel inside the hourly rate, which is why that band starts higher and widens fastest, and it is the band a near-me search points you at by default.

What moves a quoted number in Dubai specifically: the level, since Diploma Higher Level pays more than IGCSE Core; the proximity of the series, since January and April are the tightest weeks in the calendar; session length, since a 90-minute slot rarely costs 1.5 times a 60-minute one; and whether coursework supervision is involved, which is more demanding than topic teaching. Group formats reduce the per-student rate and remove the diagnostic that makes a session worth buying.

IB Gram's own position: lessons are online and one-to-one, the first lesson is a free trial run as a diagnostic on a real past paper, and a quoted rate comes from the consultation once the board, level and subject are known. No price appears on this page, because a number without the subject, level and session length attached is a marketing figure rather than a quote.

process.title: Send the statement of entry, not the subject name
process.description: The first message that saves a week is a photograph of the exam entry or the school's subject list. It names the board and the syllabus code, which is what the match is made on. Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 are both called maths and are not the same paper.

process.title: Free trial lesson, run as a diagnostic
process.description: The trial is a timed section of a real past paper plus the marking conversation afterwards. You end it holding the first marked script and a short written view of where the marks are going. If the tutor is not the right fit, you have lost an hour and gained a baseline.

process.title: Agree the twelve-week shape and the school's deadlines
process.description: Before the second session, the plan is fixed: topic order from the diagnostic, the week-ten retest date, and the school's own internal deadlines for coursework drafts. In Dubai those internal dates usually bind harder than the exam window does.

process.title: Weekly sessions with an artefact each time
process.description: A fixed slot in Gulf Standard Time, one-to-one over live video. Each session returns a marked script, a drill sheet or a criterion comment. Nothing is reported as a feeling; the file either shows movement on the same question types or it does not.

process.title: Review at week ten and decide honestly
process.description: The second timed paper goes beside the first and the comparison drives the next decision: continue, change tutor, change tier expectation, or stop. All four are legitimate outcomes, and all four are better decided from two marked papers than from an opinion.

whyPoints.title: The tutor is matched to the code, not the catchment
whyPoints.description: Matching runs on board, syllabus code and level, which is the only information that predicts whether a tutor can read your child's paper. Because delivery is online, that match is made across the whole pool rather than across the fraction of it inside a 4pm driving radius.

whyPoints.title: Every session is auditable by a parent who does not teach
whyPoints.description: A marked script with per-question marks, a drill sheet with model answers, or a criterion comment naming the band. These are readable in a couple of minutes by someone who has never seen a mark scheme, which is the point of producing them.

whyPoints.title: The coursework boundary is stated, not implied
whyPoints.description: Internal Assessment and Extended Essay support is teaching, reading and written feedback on the student's own draft. No sentences are supplied and no draft is finished for the student. That boundary protects the candidate, which matters more than any grade claim.

whyPoints.title: The calendar is handled, including the deadlines nobody mentions
whyPoints.description: Entry deadlines, forecast-grade dates, results dates and the school's own internal coursework deadlines are in the plan from the second session. The Cambridge March 2027 entry deadline of 27 November 2026 is the kind of date that quietly fixes a ceiling.

whyPoints.title: Numbers on this page carry their source
whyPoints.description: Every AED band is attributed to the company or rate table that published it, and every regulatory statement to u.ae, KHDA, MoHRE, Cambridge or Pearson. No IB exam date appears here, because the IB's own site is the only authority and it should be checked with the school.

whyPoints.title: Availability is disclosed before you pay
whyPoints.description: Some niche Higher Level subjects and some Arabic streams have genuinely thin coverage. When that happens you are told the realistic match time rather than being booked with the nearest available generalist and left to discover the gap in week three.

faqs.question: What does an IB IGCSE tuition near me search actually get wrong in Dubai?
faqs.answer: It answers a question about quality with a measure of distance. Local results are ranked on proximity, category and listing completeness, none of which indicate whether a tutor has marked Cambridge 0620 Chemistry or read a Diploma Internal Assessment against its criteria. Dubai makes this worse than most cities: 227 private schools across 17 curricula in 2024-25 mean the specialists are scattered by where they live, not by where demand sits. Use proximity to choose a school. Use syllabus evidence, meaning the board, the code and a marked script, to choose who teaches the subject.

faqs.question: How will I see proof that my child is improving, week by week?
faqs.answer: Through artefacts rather than reports. Week one produces a marked past paper with marks allocated question by question, which becomes the baseline. Weeks two to six produce drill sheets on the question types that lost marks, each with a short re-test on the same type. Weeks seven to nine produce written criterion comments on coursework drafts. Week ten produces a second timed paper under identical conditions, filed beside the first. You read the two totals and, more usefully, the two patterns. If the same question type is still losing marks after six weeks of work on it, that is visible to you without any subject knowledge.

faqs.question: Can I read the tutor's marking of my child's past paper myself?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is designed for that. The script comes back annotated against the published mark scheme with the mark allocation written beside each question, so a parent can see that four marks went missing on three questions that all asked for an explanation, or that two marks went on premature rounding. You do not need to understand the chemistry to read that pattern. What you will not receive is a copy of the board's mark scheme or past paper as a download, because those documents belong to Cambridge, Pearson or the IB and the correct route to them is the school's exams officer or the board's own website.

faqs.question: My child's school report says Good. Why does the diagnostic paper disagree?
faqs.answer: Because they measure different things. A school report blends classwork, effort, coursework and assessment into one judgement, which is genuinely useful to a teacher managing a class and close to useless for planning revision. A timed past paper marked against the mark scheme measures one thing: marks available under exam conditions. A student can be attentive, organised and well liked, and still lose a grade to command-term technique and rounding. The two numbers diverging is normal and informative. The diagnostic is not a verdict on the school or the child; it is the only baseline a revision plan can be built from.

faqs.question: How many marked papers should we expect before a February exam window?
faqs.answer: For a Cambridge March series, a realistic target from a September start is six to eight full timed papers per subject, with the first sat before any teaching and the last sat about three weeks out. Sitting more than that tends to crowd out the teaching that makes the next paper better. The sequence matters more than the count: a paper, marking, two or three weeks of targeted work on what the marking exposed, then the same question types again. Papers sat without the marking cycle in between measure stamina rather than build it, and that is the most common way revision time gets spent for nothing.

faqs.question: Does a tutor outside Dubai understand my child's school deadlines?
faqs.answer: Only if the deadlines are handed over, which is why they are asked for in the first session. The dates that bind a Dubai student are mostly school-set: internal Internal Assessment draft deadlines, Extended Essay checkpoints, mock windows, and the centre's own entry cut-off ahead of the board's. Those sit months before the exam. A tutor plans the block around that calendar once it exists on paper. Lessons run on Gulf Standard Time against the school timetable, so a 5pm slot is a 5pm slot in Dubai. What matters is the written calendar, not the tutor's postcode.

faqs.question: What exactly may a tutor do with my daughter's Internal Assessment draft?
faqs.answer: Read it and comment on it. A session can narrow a research question until it is measurable, teach referencing and uncertainty treatment, explain the difference between describing a result and evaluating a method, and return written feedback naming each criterion by letter with the descriptor band the draft currently sits in and what a higher band requires. Then your daughter revises it herself and it can be read again. What a tutor must never do is supply sentences, edit the draft into finished prose, or provide a model answer to the same question. The student is the sole author under IB rules, and the penalty for breaching that falls on her.

faqs.question: Is there any point starting eight weeks before the Cambridge March series?
faqs.answer: Yes, with narrowed expectations and a different shape. Eight weeks will not cover a two-year syllabus, so the block runs as triage: a full timed paper in week one, the two or three highest-yield topics identified from it, command-term and arithmetic-hygiene drills throughout because those recover marks fastest, and a second paper around week six. One decision has already been made by then, though, and it is the big one. Tier is fixed at entry, with Cambridge final entries for March 2027 due on 27 November 2026, so a Core entry cannot be revised into an A* in February.

faqs.question: Which Dubai communities have the thinnest supply of Diploma Higher Level tutors?
faqs.answer: The pattern is consistent. Generalist primary and lower-secondary cover exists almost everywhere in the emirate. Higher Level sciences, Mathematics AA at Higher Level, Economics HL and coursework supervision thin out quickly outside the Jumeirah, Al Safa and Al Barsha corridor. Al Furjan, Discovery Gardens, Jumeirah Village Triangle and the Jebel Ali side feel it most, because a 4pm cross-city drive prices independent tutors out before the subject is discussed. Arabian Ranches and Dubai Hills Estate have reasonable IGCSE cover and sparse Economics and Business HL. Online delivery is what removes that geography from the problem.

faqs.question: How do you match a tutor to Cambridge 0580 rather than just to maths?
faqs.answer: By asking for the syllabus code before anything else. The statement of entry or the school subject list names the board and the code, and the match is made on that. Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 are both called mathematics and differ in formula provision, tiering, paper structure and command-term habits. The same is true of 0625 against 4PH1 in physics. A tutor who has taught one and not the other will teach the content competently and miss the exam technique, which is where most of the recoverable marks are. The code takes ten seconds to supply and changes the whole match.

faqs.question: Do we need separate tutors for Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel papers?
faqs.answer: Not usually, but you do need a tutor who knows which one your child sits. Many subject specialists work across both boards; the difference is in exam technique rather than in the physics or the algebra. Where separate support genuinely helps is the Pearson modular route in some subjects, which allows units to be sat in different series and banked, and which changes revision planning completely. If your child is split across two boards after a school transfer, say so at the start, because the two timetables and two sets of entry deadlines then have to be planned together rather than in sequence.

faqs.question: What happens in the free trial lesson, and what do we get out of it?
faqs.answer: The trial runs as a diagnostic, not a sales call. Your child sits a timed section of a real past paper, the tutor marks it against the published mark scheme during or straight after the session, and you end up with the first annotated script plus a short written view of where marks are going and what the first three sessions would target. If you continue, that script is the baseline for the week-ten comparison. If you do not, you have an hour's cost of nothing and a marked paper you can use with anyone else. The trial is free with no card required.

faqs.question: How does a KHDA inspection band affect what tuition my child needs?
faqs.answer: Less than parents expect. KHDA, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai, inspects annually and publishes a judgement on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak. That judgement describes the school: provision, leadership, teaching and outcomes across cohorts. It cannot tell you whether your child sits in the group the provision is not reaching, or whether a strong overall band is carried by departments your child does not study in. For an individual learner, a timed paper marked against the mark scheme is the diagnostic. The band is a school-choice signal.

faqs.question: Will Arabic and Islamic Education still be compulsory alongside IGCSE in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools whatever international curriculum the school is licensed to teach, with KHDA's current requirements to be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states combined classes are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. Support has to follow the stream the school has placed your child in, because the syllabus differs between streams.

faqs.question: Can sessions move to post-Iftar timing during Ramadan in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes, and most families ask for it. Dubai school days shorten during Ramadan and the useful study window moves late, so weekly slots shift to after Iftar, typically from about 8.30pm, and the session length often drops from 90 to 60 minutes while frequency holds. This matters for planning, because Ramadan can fall close to a Cambridge March or a Diploma May series depending on the year. The practical move is to front-load content teaching before Ramadan and keep the fasting weeks for paper practice and marking review, which is lighter cognitive work for the same mark return.

dubai/ib-igcse-tuition-near-me.closingHeading: Start with a marked paper, not a map
dubai/ib-igcse-tuition-near-me.closingBody: If you take one thing from this page, let it be the order of operations. Photograph the statement of entry so the board and syllabus code are known. Book the free trial and treat it as a diagnostic: a timed section of a real past paper, marked against the mark scheme, returned annotated. Read the pattern of lost marks rather than the total. Then decide whether to commit to a twelve-week block, with the school's own internal coursework deadlines written into it from the start. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and the tutor is chosen for the paper your child sits.

One runs on criteria scored out of eight; the other runs on papers scored against a mark scheme. They reward different behaviour, and a student who is fluent in one can lose two grades in the other. This page sets out what each system assesses at 16, where marks go missing subject by subject, and what a one-to-one online session can realistically repair in a term.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below are matched by assessment model as well as by subject: someone who marks MYP criteria is doing a different job from someone who marks a Cambridge or Pearson paper. The trial lesson is where your child's own work gets read against the right rubric for the first time.

intro.heading: Two systems, two rubrics, one confused report card
paragraphs: There is no qualification called an IB IGCSE. The phrase exists because Dubai parents hold two documents that do not line up: a school report written in the language of criteria, levels and strands, and a conversation about exams at 16 that uses grades, tiers and mark schemes. Roughly one in fourteen Dubai private-school places sits on an International Baccalaureate programme and 37 per cent on a UK curriculum, on KHDA's published 2024-25 figures, and a number of schools here run both. A family can genuinely have one child in Middle Years Programme Year 5 and another in Year 11 sitting Cambridge papers, in the same house, with the same homework hour.

The two models reward different work. In the Middle Years Programme each subject is assessed against four criteria, each scored from one to eight, and the descriptors are about process: how a hypothesis was framed, how sources were evaluated, how a conclusion was reflected on. In Cambridge or Pearson International GCSE the grade comes from timed papers marked against a published scheme, where a correct answer in the wrong form earns nothing and a wrong answer with visible correct method earns something. A student who has spent three years being praised for thoughtful process can lose a grade simply by not showing working.

That mismatch is the single most common reason a Dubai family starts looking for a tutor at 14 or 15. Nothing is wrong with the child and nothing is wrong with the school. The student is being asked, often in the space of one September, to change what good work looks like. The diagnosis takes one marked paper and about forty minutes, and it is almost always specific: exact form ignored in maths, command terms misread in science, analysis replaced by narration in English.

The reverse direction causes as much trouble and gets discussed far less. A Year 11 student who has become expert at squeezing marks out of a mark scheme moves into the Diploma Programme and meets internal assessment, where a fifth of most subject grades depends on an individual piece of work judged against criterion letters with published mark allocations. Marks there are not awarded for recall. Criterion C of the extended essay alone carries twelve of thirty-four marks and is about critical thinking, which is the one thing exam technique does not teach.

So this page is built around assessment rather than around a sales argument. It sets the two routes side by side, publishes the criterion letters and mark counts that competitor pages leave out entirely, names the subject-by-subject places where Dubai students lose marks, explains the mandatory UAE subjects that sit alongside both curricula, and states what a tutor may and may not touch when the work has to be the student's own. Lessons here are delivered online, one to one, over live video; IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, and home visiting is a service we run only in India.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor.programmesIntro: Dubai schools cover the 11 to 19 years through three recognisable routes, and a family can meet all three in one household. What matters for tutoring is which rubric a piece of work will be marked against this term.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Five years of criterion-referenced assessment across eight subject groups. Each subject carries four criteria scored from one to eight, converted to a subject grade from one to seven against published boundaries. Year 5 adds the personal project, marked against planning, applying skills and reflecting at eight marks each. Some schools enter students for on-screen eAssessment at the end; others assess internally and award the school's own report.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the key question to ask the school is whether your child's MYP Year 5 ends in eAssessment or in internal assessment only. The answer changes the final year completely: eAssessment means on-screen papers under exam conditions, which is the first formal exam many MYP students sit. Families who assume their child will walk into the Diploma Programme exam-ready often find the gap is not knowledge but stamina in a timed room.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson International GCSE
programmes.description: Two years of linear study assessed by terminal papers. Cambridge splits many subjects into Core and Extended with separate grade ceilings and adds a practical or alternative-to-practical component in the sciences; Pearson examines practical skills inside the written papers and reports on the 9-1 scale. Entry codes such as 0580, 0625, 4MA1 and 4PH1 identify the exact specification, and the tier decision closes with the entry deadline.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools frequently run a mixed basket, entering one board for sciences and another for maths or English, department by department. That is why the first thing worth asking is not the board name but the code on the statement of entry. A tutor fluent in 0580 is not automatically fluent in 4MA1's two-paper, calculator-throughout structure, and the difference shows up in the first marked paper rather than in a conversation.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard, plus the extended essay, theory of knowledge and creativity, activity, service. Scored out of 45, with up to three points from the essay and theory of knowledge combination. Internal assessment carries a fifth of most subject grades and is judged against criterion letters with published mark allocations rather than against a mark scheme.
programmes.countryNote: The Dubai version of the post-16 decision is unusually live because the emirate keeps adding capacity: KHDA reported seven new private schools for 2026-27, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 places. For a Year 11 student that means both routes are genuinely available, and the choice should be made on how your child works rather than on which school has a place. A student who produces best work under deadline pressure over weeks is a Diploma candidate; one who performs in a timed room is often better served by A Levels.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor.subjectsIntro: Each subject below names the component where Dubai students most often lose marks and the error behind it. The pattern is consistent enough that a tutor can usually confirm or rule it out inside one marked paper.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580, 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Marks leak in algebraic fractions, vectors, unequal-width histograms and bounds, and in the last parts of multi-step problems where method stops being written down. The second loss is exact form: a question asking for an answer in surd form or in terms of pi awards nothing for a decimal, however accurate.

subjects.name: Physics (0625, 4PH1)
subjects.description: Units and prefixes cost marks on questions the student understood. Moments problems with pivots away from the centre of mass defeat anyone who learned one worked example. Extended-response items want a causal chain rather than three true statements, which is a writing problem as much as a physics one.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620, 4CH1)
subjects.description: Mole calculations, electrolysis half-equations, rates graphs and organic pathways carry the grade. The quickest recoveries are procedural: balancing ionic equations and reading titration data correctly. Both are taught rather than revised, which is why they respond fast to one-to-one work.

subjects.name: Biology (0610, 4BI1)
subjects.description: Content-heavy, so students who revise by rereading notes plateau at grade 6. The separation at the top comes from data questions and from describing a trend before explaining it. Command-term drill and labelled diagrams are where the marks return.

subjects.name: Coordinated and Combined Science
subjects.description: The compressed route through all three sciences. The risk is not difficulty but coverage: a student aiming at Higher Level chemistry after a single-award course has real content gaps in moles and organic reactions. Worth auditing in Year 11 rather than in the first DP term.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: Reading marks go when a student summarises content instead of analysing method. Writing marks go when register does not match the audience the task names. Both are fixable in four or five marked attempts, and neither improves from reading more model answers.

subjects.name: English Literature
subjects.description: Quotation economy decides the band. Short embedded quotations with a comment on method score; long extracts that retell the plot do not. Students arriving from a criterion-based middle school often write beautifully about theme and never name a technique.

subjects.name: Economics and Business
subjects.levels: IGCSE and DP SL or HL
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy in economics and application to the case material in business. A correctly shifted and labelled diagram earns marks that prose cannot recover. Students with strong general knowledge lose marks by answering with examples instead of with the model named in the question.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The usual post-IGCSE landing problem. Content is familiar; the writing is not. The exploration is marked on presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics, and students who are strong in papers routinely score poorly on reflection.

subjects.name: Arabic and Islamic Education
subjects.levels: First language and additional language streams
subjects.description: Mandatory in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, and taught in separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students under KHDA requirements. Tutoring here is about access to the set content rather than about exam technique, and the stream your child sits in determines everything.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor.regionsIntro: Communities differ in which assessment model dominates locally, which changes the kind of tutor a family needs. All sessions run over live video, so the note below is about schools and timing rather than about travel.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Al Sufouh
regions.note: A dense band of both British and International Baccalaureate schools, so households here often contain one child on criteria and one on papers. The common request is a single tutor who can read both rubrics in the same week.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches and Dubai Hills Estate
regions.note: Large Year 11 cohorts with tight setting, which means a middle-set student aiming two grades up needs their own marked papers rather than more class time. Evening slots fill from 6pm.

regions.name: Umm Suqeim and Jumeirah
regions.note: Long-established British-curriculum catchment where IGCSE entry decisions are made early and firmly. Tier appeals here benefit from marked Higher-tier evidence rather than from a parental opinion at a consultation evening.

regions.name: Mirdif and Al Warqa
regions.note: Mixed British and Indian-curriculum provision with long bus routes, so students arrive home late and work best in a 6.30pm or 7.30pm slot. Combined Science coverage gaps are the most common diagnostic finding here.

regions.name: Dubai Silicon Oasis and Academic City
regions.note: Schools on site and a high proportion of students sitting mixed-board baskets. Checking the specification code on each entry matters more in this cluster than anywhere else in the emirate.

regions.name: Downtown, Business Bay and DIFC
regions.note: Apartment living, late family schedules and Diploma students writing coursework after 9pm. Short frequent sessions and draft feedback between them suit this pattern better than one long weekend block.

regions.name: Jumeirah Village Circle and Al Furjan
regions.note: Fast-growing cohorts in newer schools where Year 10 groups are large. Parents here ask most often about whether a 6 in MYP translates into a grade 6 at IGCSE, which it does not.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai schools running both programmes
schoolClusters.note: A number of Dubai schools offer a middle-years route and an exam-board route in the same building, or an International Baccalaureate diploma after a British Year 11. Students here meet two assessment languages inside one timetable, which is exactly the case this page is written for.

schoolClusters.city: Exam-board schools feeding diploma places
schoolClusters.note: British-curriculum schools whose Year 11 cohorts split at 16 between A Levels and a Diploma Programme elsewhere in the emirate. The summer between is where the assessment gap gets closed or inherited.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor.modesIntro: Three booking shapes cover the assessment problems described on this page. All three run over live video with a shared screen, and all three produce marked work you can read.

modes.title: Diagnostic and rubric reset
modes.description: Two to three sessions whose only purpose is to find out which rubric your child is actually being marked against and how well they answer it. The tutor works a mixed set of past-paper or criterion-based tasks, marks them in front of the student, and returns a ranked list of the three places marks are leaking. Many Dubai families book nothing else for a term after this, because the list is often enough for the school to act on.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one through the course
modes.description: An hour a week tracking the school's scheme of work about a fortnight behind, so the session consolidates rather than pre-teaches. Over three terms this produces a run of marked work that makes final revision targeted. For a student moving between assessment models it also gives the tutor a baseline, which is what makes the difference between a report that says progress is good and one that names a criterion.

Topic order follows your child's school
Roughly thirty minutes of marked work between sessions

modes.title: Coursework and internal assessment coaching
modes.description: Sessions built around the criterion letters: what research design means in a science investigation, what reflection means in a mathematics exploration, why criterion C of the extended essay carries twelve marks. The tutor teaches the skill, models it on different material and gives feedback on a draft the student has written. No one here supplies text or hands over finished assessed work.

sections.heading: What your child is actually being marked on at 16
paragraphs: Before buying any tutoring, establish which of four routes your child is on, because the answer determines the kind of help that works. The table below sets out the 14 to 16 routes a Dubai family realistically meets, who sets the assessment, how the route ends and where it leads. The phrase an IB IGCSE tutor is a search for someone who can work across the top two rows of that table, which is a reasonable thing to want and a specific thing to ask for.

The practical difference is who holds the standard. On an exam-board route the standard sits outside the school in a published mark scheme, and the student's job is to produce answers that match it. On a criterion-referenced middle-years route the standard sits in descriptors that a teacher applies to work produced over weeks. Neither is softer. They select for different students, and a child who thrives on one can look weak on the other for reasons that have nothing to do with ability.

Where this goes wrong in Dubai is the join. A student leaves a criterion-based Year 9, enters a two-year exam course, and spends Year 10 producing thoughtful work that scores in the middle bands. Nobody has told them that the scheme rewards a specific form of answer. One term of marked papers fixes it, and it is almost always a technique problem rather than a knowledge problem, which is why the first session should be a diagnostic rather than chapter one of anything.

sections.heading: Criteria out of eight against grades out of nine
paragraphs: The question Dubai parents ask most often about this gap is whether a 6 means the same thing in both systems. It does not, and the comparison is worth setting out properly because so much household anxiety rests on it. A criterion score of six out of eight describes performance against a descriptor on one strand of one subject. A grade 6 at International GCSE describes a total mark across complete papers converted through a grade boundary that moves between series.

The behavioural consequences matter more than the arithmetic. Criterion-referenced marking rewards planning, evaluation of sources, and reflection on process, and it is forgiving of a slow start because work is produced over weeks. Mark-scheme marking rewards showing method, using the exact form requested, answering the command term, and finishing. A student who has never been under a clock has not been bad at anything; they have simply never been assessed on speed.

For tutoring this means the first job is translation, not teaching. The tutor takes a piece of the student's own work and marks it twice, once under each rubric, and shows the student where the two disagree. That exercise takes one session and it changes behaviour faster than a term of content revision, because the student can finally see what the examiner is paid to look for. It also gives you something concrete to take to a parents' evening in Dubai: not a worry about confidence, but a sentence such as my daughter is losing method marks on structured questions and we are drilling it weekly. Teachers respond to that differently, and in a Year 11 class of twenty-five the specific request is the one that gets acted on.

sections.heading: Where the marks actually go, subject by subject
paragraphs: Mark loss at this level is not random and it is not mysterious. Across Dubai cohorts the same handful of errors account for most of the gap between a 6 and an 8, and all of them are diagnosable from one marked paper. The table names the component, the error and the fix, so you can check it against your child's last mock before paying anyone anything.

Two of these deserve emphasis because they cross subjects. The first is the command term. State, describe, explain, compare and evaluate are instructions with different mark values, and a student who explains when asked to describe wastes time without gaining marks while one who describes when asked to explain loses them outright. Ten minutes of drilling on the front of each paper is worth more than another chapter of notes.

The second is exact form. In maths it is surds and multiples of pi; in chemistry it is significant figures and state symbols; in physics it is units and prefixes. None of this is difficult content. All of it is a habit that a tutor can install in two or three sessions, which is why a diagnostic often produces an immediate jump that then plateaus until the real content work starts. Treat that plateau as expected rather than as a sign the tutoring stopped working: the first gain is technique and the second is knowledge, and the second takes a term. Families who understand that sequence stop renegotiating the plan every three weeks, which is itself worth a grade.

sections.heading: Criterion letters and what each one actually rewards
paragraphs: Internal assessment is where the Diploma Programme separates students, and it is the part of the system no competitor page in this market explains with numbers. Each piece is marked against criteria identified by letter, each letter carries a published mark allocation, and the allocations tell you where to spend time. The table lists the main ones a Dubai student meets between 16 and 18, with the word or page limit that applies.

Read criterion C of the extended essay first. Twelve of thirty-four marks sit there, under critical thinking, which means an essay that researches thoroughly and argues descriptively cannot reach the top band however well presented it is. Students who are strong in examinations are the most likely to get this wrong, because papers reward accurate recall and the essay does not. The same logic applies to criterion D of a science investigation: evaluation means saying what each limitation did to the result, not listing limitations.

The mathematics exploration is the one Dubai students most often underestimate. Presentation and mathematical communication carry four marks each, personal engagement and reflection three each, and use of mathematics six. Reflection has to run through the work rather than appear as a closing paragraph, and that is a writing habit, not a mathematical one. A tutor who teaches the criteria explicitly in the planning stage saves a student weeks of redrafting later. The other recurring Dubai problem is topic choice: an exploration built on a dataset the student cannot actually manipulate caps criterion E no matter how much work goes in afterwards. Thirty minutes spent testing the topic against the criteria before any writing starts is the highest-value half hour in the whole process.
