sections.heading: Command terms are the hidden syllabus
paragraphs: Both systems publish the verbs they use and both expect students to treat them as instructions with price tags. A command term tells the examiner what to look for and the student how much to write. Ignoring them is the most expensive habit in the room, and it is invisible on a report card because the content knowledge is genuinely there.

The hierarchy is consistent enough to teach in one session. State and identify want a word or a phrase and no justification. Describe wants what happened, in order, without cause. Explain wants cause, which means the word because or its equivalent has to appear. Compare wants both things in the same sentence, not two paragraphs side by side. Evaluate and discuss want a judgement supported by both sides, and they are the only terms where a conclusion earns marks. Calculate wants working; determine often wants a method chosen as well.

The drill that works is brutal and brief. Take ten past-paper questions, cover the content, and have the student say only what the term demands and how many lines it is worth. Five minutes a session for a fortnight. Dubai students arriving from criterion-based middle years gain the most from this, because their instinct is to write thoroughly about everything, which is rewarded in a process rubric and penalised by a clock. The same drill pays off again at diploma level, where the command terms are published in each subject guide and carry the same contract. A student who learns to read the verb first at 15 is still doing it at 18, which is one of the few tutoring gains that genuinely compounds.
bullets: State and identify: no justification, no marks for extra prose
Describe before explain: the trend first, then the cause
Compare: both items in the same sentence or the mark is not awarded
Evaluate and discuss: a judgement is required, and a conclusion earns marks here only

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside both routes
paragraphs: Whatever curriculum a Dubai private school is licensed to teach, three subjects run alongside it, and almost no tutoring page in this market mentions them. Arabic, Islamic Education and social and moral studies are mandatory in Dubai private schools, with KHDA's requirements set out in its mandatory-subjects guidance for the 2025-26 academic year. Federal rules behind that are simple: private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must follow the ministry's general regulations.

The organisational detail matters for tutoring. KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and social studies, and states that combined classes for both groups are prohibited because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arab students and for Arabic as a first language; the school's licensed-curriculum language applies for non-Arab students in Islamic Education and in moral, social and cultural studies. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, and schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met.

Two practical consequences follow. First, a tutor has to know which stream your child sits in, because first-language and additional-language Arabic are different subjects with different expectations. Second, the content is tightly controlled: use of any different or additional material without prior permission from the ministry is prohibited for these subjects, so legitimate tutoring works through the school's own set content rather than importing a syllabus from elsewhere. Schools are also required to ensure that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic have appropriate KHDA permission to teach those subjects, which is a reasonable thing to ask your school about.

sections.heading: From International GCSE into the Diploma Programme
paragraphs: The subject-by-subject transition is where a Dubai Year 11 either banks an advantage or inherits a problem, and the gaps are predictable. In mathematics, a Higher tier or Extended student has met quadratics, trigonometry and basic calculus-adjacent reasoning but not mathematical writing, which is what the exploration assesses. In the sciences, a single-award or combined route leaves genuine content holes in moles, organic chemistry and quantitative physics that Higher Level assumes from week one.

In English the move is from analysing a short extract to sustaining an argument across a whole text and an unseen passage, plus an oral component. In economics and business it is from applying one model to a prompt to evaluating competing models under a key concept. None of these are insurmountable and all of them are cheaper to close in the summer between Year 11 and the first diploma term than in the panic of the following March.

A useful planning rule: audit, do not guess. Take the Higher Level syllabus for the subject your child intends to take, and have a tutor check the first three topics against what the International GCSE course actually covered. Three hours of audit in July beats twenty hours of catch-up in November, and it also answers the question Dubai parents ask most at this point, which is whether the child should take the subject at Higher Level at all. Do the audit before the school's option forms are returned, because changing a Higher Level choice after the first term is disruptive and sometimes impossible where class sizes are set. Two hours with a subject specialist in June is cheaper than a subject change in October and considerably cheaper than a dropped Higher Level in May.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not touch
paragraphs: Internal assessment, coursework and the extended essay must be the student's own work, and the rules are not advisory. A student whose assessed piece is not their own faces a malpractice finding, which can cost the award. That makes the boundary a practical question for every Dubai family paying for support, and it is the boundary this market is worst at respecting: one provider in this search result sells completed internal assessments outright.

What legitimate support looks like is specific. A tutor reads the criteria with the student and explains what each letter rewards. The tutor models technique on different material, not on the student's task. The tutor reads a draft the student wrote and gives feedback in the form of questions and criterion references. The tutor helps plan a timeline against the school's internal deadlines. All of that is teaching, all of it is recorded, and none of it puts a student at risk.

What no tutor here does is supply sentences for an assessed piece, restructure a draft into its final shape, or hand over work for submission. We also do not reproduce or distribute board syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads: we reference them and link to the boards' own pages, because reproducing them is a copyright matter. If a provider offers a finished piece for a fee, the student carries the consequence, not the provider. There is a simple test a parent can apply without knowing the subject: ask what the student will have done by the end of the session. If the answer describes something the tutor produces rather than something the student produces, the arrangement is wrong whatever it is called on the invoice.
bullets: Allowed: teaching criteria, modelling on other material, feedback on the student's own draft
Allowed: planning a timeline against the school's internal deadlines
Not allowed: supplying text, redrafting to completion, or submitting on a student's behalf
Not allowed: distributing board papers, mark schemes or boundary tables as files

process.title: Name the rubric, not just the subject
process.description: Tell us whether the next piece of assessed work is a criterion-marked task, a timed paper or an internal assessment, and which code or programme it sits under. That single detail decides which tutor is right, because marking MYP criteria and marking a Cambridge paper are different professional skills.

process.title: A free first lesson with no card details
process.description: One full lesson with the proposed tutor at no charge, with no payment method taken beforehand. It tests whether your child talks during the hour and whether the tutor can explain something a second way. If either answer is no, we propose someone else rather than defending the match.

process.title: One piece of work, marked twice
process.description: Early on, the tutor takes a piece of your child's own work and marks it against the rubric it will actually be judged by, in front of the student. Where two systems are in play, they mark it both ways and show the disagreement. This is the session that changes behaviour fastest.

process.title: A ranked list, then weekly work
process.description: You receive three named causes of mark loss in priority order, with whether each is content, method or timing. From there the weekly pattern is one hour taught, roughly thirty minutes marked between sessions, and a short written note naming what moved.

process.title: A review at each assessment point
process.description: Before mocks, before an internal assessment deadline and before an exam series, we review whether the shape of the booking still fits. Sometimes the answer is fewer hours, and we say so. Specialist availability tightens about eight weeks before each series, so plan that review early.

whyPoints.title: Both rubrics read fluently
whyPoints.description: Tutors are matched by assessment model as well as subject, which is the whole point of this page. A household with one child on criteria and one on papers does not need two providers; it needs a tutor who can state what each rubric pays for.

whyPoints.title: Criterion letters published, not implied
whyPoints.description: Every criterion and mark allocation a Dubai student meets between 14 and 18 is set out above with its length limit. No other page in this search result names a single one, which is strange given that a fifth of most diploma subject grades depends on them.

whyPoints.title: Diagnosis before teaching
whyPoints.description: The first paid sessions produce a ranked list of mark-loss causes from your child's own work rather than a syllabus restart. It is faster, it is cheaper, and it often tells you that you need fewer hours than you expected.

whyPoints.title: Delivered online, stated plainly
whyPoints.description: Lessons run one to one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in the UAE; home visiting is a service we run only in India. We hold no regulator or examination-board accreditation and make no claim to any.

whyPoints.title: The mandatory subjects are covered honestly
whyPoints.description: Arabic, Islamic Education and social studies run alongside both curricula in Dubai, in separate streams, with content the ministry controls. We explain how that works and match to the correct stream rather than pretending the subjects do not exist.

whyPoints.title: No grade promises
whyPoints.description: Nobody here will tell you a number before teaching your child. What we will tell you, inside a fortnight, is which three things are costing marks and roughly how long each takes to fix. That is a forecast you can check against marked work.

faqs.question: Is there actually a qualification called the IB IGCSE?
faqs.answer: No. IGCSE is a qualification offered by Cambridge and, as the International GCSE, by Pearson Edexcel; the IB runs the Middle Years Programme to 16 and the Diploma Programme after it. The phrase appears in searches because Dubai families hold reports from one system and face exams from the other, often inside the same school group. What you are usually looking for is a tutor who can work across both assessment models in the same week. That is a real and specific thing to ask for, and it is what the tutors on this page are matched on.

faqs.question: My child is in MYP Year 5 and has never sat a formal exam. Is that a problem?
faqs.answer: It is a gap rather than a problem, and it is about stamina and timing rather than knowledge. Ask the school first whether Year 5 ends in on-screen eAssessment or in internal assessment only, because that changes the year completely. If your child will meet timed conditions for the first time in the Diploma Programme, the fix is practice under a clock during Year 11: full-length tasks, marked, with the time written on the top. Three or four of those tell you far more than a term of content revision, and they are cheap to arrange.

faqs.question: Does a 6 in MYP mean the same thing as a grade 6 at IGCSE?
faqs.answer: No, and conflating the two causes a lot of unnecessary worry in Dubai households. A criterion score of six out of eight describes performance against a descriptor on one strand of one subject. An IGCSE grade 6 is a total mark across complete papers converted through a boundary that moves between series. They are different units measuring different behaviour: one rewards planning and reflection over weeks, the other rewards method, exact form and finishing on time. The useful exercise is having a tutor mark one piece of your child's work under both rubrics and show you where they disagree.

faqs.question: How much of an IB subject grade comes from internal assessment?
faqs.answer: For most Diploma Programme subjects the internally assessed component is worth about a fifth of the subject grade, with the written papers carrying the rest. That single piece is marked against criteria identified by letter, each with a published mark allocation: a mathematics exploration runs to twenty marks across five criteria, and a science investigation to twenty-four across four. Because it is produced over weeks rather than in an exam room, it is the most controllable part of the grade, and it is where a tutor working inside the academic-honesty rules adds most value.

faqs.question: What do the criterion letters on my child's report actually mean?
faqs.answer: Each letter is a separate skill with its own marks, and the allocation tells you where to spend time. In a mathematics exploration, presentation and mathematical communication carry four marks each, personal engagement and reflection three each, and use of mathematics six. In a science investigation, research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation carry six marks each. In the extended essay, critical thinking alone carries twelve of thirty-four. Students who are strong in exams often score badly on reflection and evaluation, because papers reward recall and these criteria reward thinking about the work.

faqs.question: Which command terms cost IGCSE students the most marks in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Explain and describe, in that order, followed by compare and evaluate. Students who explain when asked to describe lose time without gaining marks; students who describe when asked to explain lose the marks outright because no cause appears. Compare requires both items in the same sentence, and evaluate is one of the few terms where a conclusion earns anything. The drill that works takes five minutes a session: cover the content on ten past-paper questions and have the student say only what the term demands and how many lines it is worth.

faqs.question: How long can the extended essay be, and what is it marked against?
faqs.answer: The limit is 4,000 words and it is marked out of 34 across five criteria: focus and method, knowledge and understanding, critical thinking, presentation, and engagement. Critical thinking carries twelve marks, more than a third of the total, which is why a well-researched descriptive essay stalls in the middle bands. Engagement is assessed through the student's own reflections with their supervisor, so those sessions are part of the assessment rather than an administrative step. A tutor can teach what each criterion rewards and respond to a draft the student wrote; nobody may write any part of it for them.

faqs.question: Does my child have to study Arabic alongside an International GCSE in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes. Arabic, Islamic Education and social and moral studies are mandatory in Dubai private schools whatever curriculum the school is licensed to teach, under KHDA's mandatory-subjects requirements, and the federal position is that private schools must cover Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies regardless. Schools run separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in these subjects because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ, and combined classes are not permitted. For tutoring, the stream your child sits in matters more than the subject name, so confirm it with the school first.

faqs.question: Can a tutor read a draft of my child's internal assessment?
faqs.answer: Yes, within the rules, and this is where good support shows. A tutor reads the criteria with the student, explains what each letter rewards, models technique on different material, and gives feedback on a draft the student wrote themselves, usually as questions and criterion references rather than corrections. What no legitimate tutor does is supply sentences, restructure a piece into its final form, or hand over anything for submission. The consequence of crossing that line lands on the student as a malpractice finding, not on the tutor, which is why the boundary is stated plainly here.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects does a Dubai student usually take?
faqs.answer: Most Dubai British-curriculum students take between seven and ten, including English, mathematics and either combined or separate sciences, alongside the mandatory UAE subjects. For families planning on Ministry of Education equivalency, the published British-track requirement is five accredited subjects at grade E or 3 or better, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus either one Advanced Level subject at grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. One competitor page states six subjects, which does not match the published rule. Verify your own case through the official channel rather than any tutoring site.

faqs.question: Is Combined Science enough if my child wants a science at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: It can be, but it needs auditing rather than assuming. A combined or coordinated route compresses three sciences, and the usual casualties are moles and quantitative chemistry, organic reaction pathways, and the more mathematical physics topics. Higher Level diploma courses assume those from early on. The cheap fix is three hours in Year 11 or the following summer: take the Higher Level syllabus, check its first topics against what the course actually covered, and close the specific gaps. The expensive version is discovering them in the November of the first diploma year.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover a middle-years subject and a diploma subject in the same household?
faqs.answer: Often yes for related subjects, and it is a sensible request because it cuts coordination to one conversation. A mathematics specialist can usually hold a Year 10 International GCSE student and a Standard Level diploma student in the same week, because the content overlaps even though the rubrics do not. Where it breaks down is across subject families: a chemistry specialist marking an English literature essay is not a saving. Tell us the full household picture at the start and we will say honestly whether one tutor or two is the better arrangement.

faqs.question: How soon should we expect something to change after starting tutoring?
faqs.answer: Technique problems move in two or three sessions, because habits like writing down method, reading what form the answer must take, and answering the command term are installed rather than learned. Content gaps take a term, sometimes two if a year was lost. The honest signal in the first fortnight is not a grade but a ranked list: three named causes of mark loss with an estimate of how long each takes. If a provider gives you a grade prediction before marking your child's work, they are selling confidence rather than diagnosis.

faqs.question: Does online teaching work for a student who needs watching to stay on task?
faqs.answer: One to one over video is usually better for this than a group room, because there is nowhere to hide for sixty minutes and the work is on a shared screen that both people are writing on. What matters is the lesson structure: short tasks, the tutor marking in real time, and the student talking rather than listening. For a younger or very distractible student, two thirty-minute sessions beat one hour. Use the free first lesson specifically to watch for this, and tell us honestly what you saw, because that is the cheapest moment to change the plan.

intro.heading: Near me is a logistics question. The grade is an evidence question.
paragraphs: A Dubai parent types tutor near me for sound reasons. The evening is short, the roads are full between five and seven, and a plan that needs somebody to cross the emirate twice a week will fail by the third week whatever anybody promises. Proximity is a real constraint and this page is not going to pretend it is irrational. It will, though, separate it from the thing families usually confuse it with, which is quality.

Here is the separation. Proximity determines whether a session happens at all in the in-home model, and nothing else. It does not determine whether the tutor has taught your child's specification, whether they mark to the board's scheme, whether anything is written down between sessions, or whether the errors identified in September have closed by December. Those four things determine the grade, and none of them has an address. Over video, proximity stops being a constraint at all, which is what makes the other four the only questions left.

So the useful reframe is this: instead of asking who is near me, ask what should exist in my hands after four weeks, and then buy from whoever can produce it. The answer is specific. An annotated script with marks awarded and withheld at named points. A timed attempt with the minutes recorded per question, not just the total. A short written note after each session saying what the hour changed. And by week four, three named causes of mark loss, ranked, each labelled content, method or timing.

That file is also the thing that makes the school take you seriously. A Dubai Year 11 parent who arrives at a consultation evening saying their child is struggling gets sympathy. A parent who arrives saying their daughter is losing method marks on structured algebra questions, here are four scripts showing it, and we are drilling it weekly, gets a different conversation and sometimes a different set. In a class of twenty-five, the specific request is the one that gets acted on. That is not a trick and it is not adversarial. A head of department with a hundred and fifty students is making decisions on the information in front of them, and a dated folder of scripts is simply better information than a worried sentence at the end of a long evening. The file is there to inform the school, never to argue with it.

Everything below is built around that file: what proximity does and does not buy, a twelve-week evidence ledger, how to read a marked script the way an examiner reads it, how to tell real grade movement from noise, how drafts of an internal assessment work as evidence without crossing the academic-honesty line, what a weekly note should contain, and the questions that expose a tutor who has no evidence to show. Lessons here run one to one over live video; IB Gram does not provide home visits in the UAE, where home visiting is a service we offer only in India.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson International GCSE

programmes.name: Diploma Programme

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580, 4MA1)

subjects.description: Look at the six-mark extended responses specifically. Evidence of progress is a causal chain appearing where three unlinked statements used to be, and it is visible to a parent without any physics knowledge at all.

sections.heading: What proximity actually buys in Dubai
paragraphs: Take the near-me question seriously enough to answer it properly. The table lists what families are really trying to secure when they search that phrase, says whether being close helps with each, and names what actually determines it instead. Three of the seven rows are genuinely improved by proximity. The other four are not, and two of them are made worse by it, because a short list of nearby tutors is a short list.

The rows worth reading twice are the subject-match ones. For mainstream Year 10 mathematics or Year 11 biology, enough people teach those in this emirate that proximity costs you almost nothing. The arithmetic changes at the edges: further pure mathematics, Higher Level chemistry, an unfamiliar Pearson code, Arabic first language for a student who moved streams, or diploma economics with a key-concept evaluation problem. Those are exactly the cases exam-year families need, and they are where a twenty-minute radius leaves you choosing from almost nobody.

There is also a cost to getting this wrong that does not show up until January. A family hires the best nearby option in September, the match holds for a term while the work is general, and then the work gets specific and the tutor cannot follow it. Changing tutor mid-year costs four to six weeks of rebuilding in the most expensive term of the year, which is why the evidence questions in this page's later sections are worth asking in September rather than in February.

None of that argues against convenience. It argues for ordering the questions correctly: specification and level first, evidence second, hour of the evening third, and geography only where it still matters after those three. Over video the fourth question disappears entirely, which is the honest reason this site exists rather than a claim that screens are inherently better than rooms.

sections.heading: The twelve-week evidence ledger
paragraphs: Below is what should exist, and when, if tutoring is working. It is deliberately a ledger rather than a promise: each row names an artefact, how to read it and the red flag that tells you something is wrong. Nothing in it requires you to understand the subject, which is the point. A parent who cannot do quadratics can still see whether the number of marks lost to missing working fell between September and November.

Week four is the decision point and it should be treated as one. By then you either have three named, ranked causes of mark loss from your child's own work, or you have an impression that things are going well. The first is a product. The second is a feeling, and it is the single most common reason Dubai families spend a full term discovering that the tutoring was pleasant and ineffective. If week four produces nothing nameable, change the tutor or the shape rather than adding hours.

Week twelve is where you should see closure rather than activity. The same three errors, tracked across dated scripts, should be measurably less expensive. Not absent, because habits regress under pressure, but cheaper. If the errors are the same size in December as in September while the sessions continued weekly, the diagnosis was wrong or the work between sessions was not happening, and both of those are fixable conversations rather than reasons to abandon the plan.

Keep every artefact in one folder, dated. It takes no effort and it does three jobs: it makes the four-week and twelve-week tests possible, it hands a replacement tutor a diagnosis on day one if the first one becomes unavailable, and it is the document that makes a Dubai school conversation specific rather than general.

sections.heading: Reading a marked script the way an examiner does
paragraphs: Most parents look at the number in the corner. The number is the least informative thing on the page. What matters is the distribution: where in the paper the marks were lost, whether they were lost to not knowing or to not writing, and whether the last two questions are blank because time ran out or because they were skipped on sight.

Four quick checks need no subject knowledge. First, count blank spaces and incomplete final questions: that is a timing problem, not a knowledge problem. Second, look for correct answers with no working in subjects where method is credited: those are given-away marks and the cheapest to recover. Third, read the long-answer questions and see whether sentences connect to each other or merely sit next to each other. Fourth, check whether the same topic appears in the lost column across several papers.

Then look at the annotation itself, because its quality tells you about the tutor rather than the student. Credible marking quotes the scheme's own phrasing, says what would have earned the mark, and distinguishes between a mark not available and a mark available and missed. Weak marking is a tick, a cross and a score out of sixty. If what arrives is the second kind, you are paying for attendance, and that is as true of a visiting tutor in Dubai as of a video session.

One caution about marks and grades. Grade boundaries move between series, so a mark of 62 is not a fixed grade and no honest tutor will convert one for you with confidence. What a mark does tell you reliably is direction: 62 after 48 on comparable papers is real movement. Treat boundary conversions as estimates and insist that progress is reported in marks and errors rather than in predicted letters.
bullets: Blanks and unfinished final questions mean timing, not knowledge

sections.heading: Grade movement: signal against noise
paragraphs: Progress claims in this market are mostly noise, and it is worth knowing how to tell. A higher score on an easier paper is not progress. A better mock after a mock season where the whole cohort improved is partly the cohort. A two-grade jump in three weeks is almost always a difficulty difference between papers, or a topic the student happened to have revised. None of that means tutoring is failing; it means the measurement was weak.

Real signal looks different and it is slower. The cost of a named error falls across dated scripts on comparable papers. Timing data improves: fewer minutes on low-mark questions, fewer blanks at the end. A student starts annotating the question before answering it. In essay subjects, paragraphs begin with a method rather than a plot event. Those are structural changes and they persist, which is exactly why they are worth more than a single flattering score.

The table separates the two. Use it when a provider reports progress, and use it on yourself when a mock result arrives and feels like either a triumph or a disaster. Dubai mock seasons generate a great deal of unnecessary panic in November, most of which is a difficulty effect, and a great deal of unwarranted relief in February for the same reason.

One timescale worth internalising, because it prevents most mid-term crises of faith: technique habits move in two or three sessions, structural writing changes in four to six weeks, and content gaps take a term, sometimes two if a year was genuinely lost. A plan judged on the wrong timescale gets abandoned a fortnight before it would have worked.

sections.heading: Drafts as evidence, without crossing the line
paragraphs: Internal assessment is worth about a fifth of most diploma subject grades and it is produced over weeks, which makes it the most evidence-rich part of the whole system and the part where the academic-honesty boundary matters most. The evidence you want is a trail of the student's own decisions: a planning note, an early draft, feedback given as questions and criterion references, and a later draft where the student has acted on some of it and ignored the rest.

That last detail is the tell. A genuine trail shows a student exercising judgement, including judgement a tutor disagreed with. A manufactured one shows each piece of feedback implemented perfectly, in a register that does not match the student's other writing. Schools notice the second kind, and the consequence of a malpractice finding lands on the student rather than on whoever supplied the text.

So the rules here are firm and they also happen to produce better evidence. A tutor reads the criteria with the student and explains what each letter rewards. A tutor models technique on different material, never on the student's own task. A tutor responds to a draft the student wrote in their own words. A tutor helps build a timeline against the school's internal deadlines. Nobody writes, restructures to completion or submits anything, and one provider in this search result sells completed internal assessments outright, which is the clearest available signal to go elsewhere.

For middle-years students the equivalent is the personal project journal, where the reflecting criterion carries eight marks and cannot be awarded from a thin record. Coaching a student to log as they go is legitimate, useful and entirely their own work, and it is the single cheapest set of marks on this page to protect.

A real trail shows the student accepting some feedback and rejecting some

sections.heading: What a weekly note should actually contain
paragraphs: A session note is four sentences and takes two minutes to write, which is why its absence is informative. It should say what was worked on, what the student got wrong and why, what was set for next time, and whether the three named errors are moving. That is it. Anything longer is usually padding and anything shorter is usually a receipt.

What a note should not contain: adjectives about attitude without evidence, a grade prediction, a request for more hours in place of a diagnosis, or a summary of what the tutor explained rather than what the student produced. The last of those is the commonest and the most misleading, because a note describing excellent explanations of trigonometry tells you nothing about whether your child can now do trigonometry under a clock.

Over a term these notes do work that nothing else does. They let you answer the four-week and twelve-week tests honestly. They hand a replacement tutor a diagnosis on day one, which in a market where mid-year changes are routine is worth more than loyalty to any individual. And they let you walk into a Dubai consultation evening with dates, scripts and a sentence that names a specific loss, which is a different conversation from a worried parent describing a feeling.

Ask for the notes in writing, in a form you can keep, and read them. A provider who sends them and a parent who never opens them end up in the same place as a provider who sends nothing, and the four-week test cannot be run from memory.

No grade predictions, no attitude adjectives without evidence

sections.heading: Six questions that expose a tutor with no evidence
paragraphs: Ask these before the first paid hour, to every provider you are considering, including us. They take a tutor thirty seconds each to answer if the answers exist, and they are unanswerable if they do not. That asymmetry is the whole value: you are not testing charm, you are testing whether a working method is in place.

Watch for the shape of the deflection rather than the content. Pointing at a testimonial instead of a script, offering a free consultation instead of answering, listing qualifications instead of describing the method, or quoting an unverifiable success statistic are all the same move. A statistic without a number of students, a date and a method behind it is not evidence, and in a market where competitors publish satisfaction percentages nobody can reproduce, treating those claims as noise is simply accurate.

The flip side is worth saying. A tutor who answers all six plainly, admits the limits of what they can promise, and offers one anonymised marked script is demonstrating the thing you are actually buying. We hold no regulator or examination-board accreditation, we do not describe tutors as examiners, and nobody here will predict a grade before teaching your child. What we will do is produce the week-four list and the twelve-week tally.

If you are hiring a visiting tutor locally instead, the same six questions apply unchanged, plus two more: ask for identification and for confirmation of the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which is issued free of charge for two years under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. Those two are about compliance rather than teaching, and they are reasonable to ask of anyone.

sections.heading: Using the file at a Dubai parents' evening
paragraphs: The evidence file has a second job that families rarely plan for: it changes what the school can do for you. Dubai Year 11 and Year 12 classes are large and teachers are triaging. A parent describing a worry is one of twenty-five such conversations in an evening. A parent arriving with four dated scripts and one specific sentence is giving a head of department something they can act on inside the school's own processes.

Three things it can open up. A tier or set review, where entries for Core or Extended, Foundation or Higher, close months before the exam and are moved on evidence rather than on confidence. A second look at a predicted grade, which is a professional judgement a teacher is entitled to revisit when new marked work exists. And clarity on a coursework or internal assessment deadline, where seeing the draft trail tells a teacher the student is working rather than drifting.

How to do it well: bring no more than four scripts, have the sentence ready, and ask a question rather than making a case. Our daughter is losing method marks on structured algebra; here are four papers; what would you want to see before reviewing her tier? That phrasing puts the school in charge of its own decision, which is both appropriate and far more effective than arriving with a demand or a tutor's opinion attached.

What not to do: never present a tutor's prediction as a forecast the school should adopt, never imply any provider can influence an entry, a boundary or an equivalency decision, and never let a tutoring arrangement become a reason to disengage from the school. The teacher who sets the work and knows the cohort remains the most important adult in this picture, and the file exists to inform them, not to argue with them.

process.title: Send a recent marked paper
process.description: A photograph of the last marked script or piece of work, with the specification code and level, is worth more than any description of the problem. It lets the tutor arrive at the free lesson already knowing where to look, and it is the first item in your evidence folder.

process.title: A free first lesson, no card details
process.description: One full lesson at no charge with no payment method taken. Judge it on one question: did your child's own work appear on the screen and did they spend most of the hour producing something. The note that follows should describe their work, not the tutor's plan.

process.title: Week four: the ranked list
process.description: Three named causes of mark loss from your child's own work, in priority order, each labelled content, method or timing, with a realistic estimate of how long each takes to close. This is the deliverable to judge the arrangement on, and it is why the first month is worth paying for even if nothing follows it.

process.title: A marked cycle and a timed paper
process.description: An hour taught, about thirty minutes of marked work between sessions, and a full timed paper every two or three weeks with minutes recorded per question. That cadence is what fills the twelve-week ledger, and the ledger is what tells you whether to continue.

process.title: Week twelve: closure, not activity
process.description: We review the error tally across every dated script and say plainly whether the three named errors are cheaper than they were. If they are not, we change the diagnosis or the tutor rather than adding hours, and we tell you which we think it is.

whyPoints.title: Evidence, in writing, by default
whyPoints.description: Annotated scripts keyed to mark-scheme wording, timing data per question, a four-sentence note after every session, and a ranked diagnosis by week four. All of it dated, all of it yours to keep and to show the school.

whyPoints.title: Progress reported in marks and errors
whyPoints.description: Grade boundaries move between series, so nobody here converts a mark into a confident grade or issues a prediction. What we report is the cost of named errors across comparable papers, which is the only measure that holds up.

whyPoints.title: Geography stops being a filter
whyPoints.description: Over video, the near-me question collapses to a question about the hour of the evening. That leaves specification match, marking quality and written output as the things you are choosing between, which is where the grade actually lives.

whyPoints.title: Honest about what evidence cannot do
whyPoints.description: A file does not change a boundary, an entry, a prediction or an equivalency decision, and no provider can. What it can do is give a head of department something concrete to act on inside the school's own processes.

whyPoints.title: Stated limits
whyPoints.description: Lessons run one to one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not provide home visits in the UAE; home visiting is a service we offer only in India. We hold no regulator or board accreditation, and we publish no success statistics we cannot evidence.

whyPoints.title: The work stays the student's own
whyPoints.description: On internal assessment and coursework, feedback comes as questions and criterion references on a draft they wrote. A trail showing their own judgement is both the only legitimate kind and the better evidence.

faqs.question: Does it genuinely matter whether a tutor lives near us in Dubai?
faqs.answer: It matters for exactly one thing: whether an in-home session reliably happens on a school night, given what the roads do between five and seven. It does not affect whether the tutor has taught your child's specification, whether they mark to the board's scheme, or whether anything useful arrives in writing between sessions. Those three decide the grade. For mainstream subjects a nearby tutor costs you nothing; for scarce codes and Higher Level sciences, insisting on proximity means selecting from a very short list, which is how families end up with a generalist.

faqs.question: What should I have in my hands after four weeks of tutoring?
faqs.answer: Three named causes of mark loss from your child's own work, ranked in priority order, each labelled content, method or timing, with a rough estimate of how long each takes to close. Plus at least one annotated script showing marks awarded and withheld at specific points, and a short note after each session. If what you have instead is a general sense that things are going well, the arrangement has not produced anything yet, and adding hours will not fix that.

faqs.question: How do I read the annotations on a marked script if I do not know the subject?
faqs.answer: Four checks need no subject knowledge. Count blanks and unfinished final questions, which indicate timing rather than knowledge. Look for correct answers with no working in subjects where method is credited, because those are the cheapest marks to recover. Read the long answers and see whether sentences connect or merely sit beside each other. Then check whether the same topic appears in the lost column across several papers. Finally, judge the marking itself: credible annotation quotes the scheme and names the mark that was missed.

faqs.question: My child jumped two grades in a mock. Should I believe it?
faqs.answer: Probably not as a sustainable change. Two grades in three weeks is usually a paper-difficulty effect or luck with topics, and the honest response is to re-test on a comparable paper before treating it as real. That is not cynicism: the same caution applies to a sudden drop, which causes a great deal of unnecessary panic in Dubai mock seasons. Durable progress looks slower and duller: the cost of a named error falling across dated scripts, fewer blanks at the end, better minutes per question.

faqs.question: How often should I receive a written update?
faqs.answer: After every session, and it should be four sentences: what was worked on, what the student got wrong and why, what was set for next time, and whether the three named errors are moving. Longer than that is usually padding. What a note should never contain is a grade prediction, adjectives about attitude with no evidence behind them, or a summary of what the tutor explained rather than what your child produced. That last one is the commonest and the most misleading.

faqs.question: Can a tutor give me a predicted grade for my child?
faqs.answer: No, and you should be wary of one who offers. Predicted grades are issued by the school as a professional judgement for university applications, and no tutor has the standing or the cohort data to produce one. What a tutor can legitimately do is report marks on comparable papers, the cost of named errors over time, and timing data, and note that grade boundaries move between series so a mark does not convert cleanly. If the school is reconsidering a prediction, that file is exactly what a teacher reviews.

faqs.question: What evidence does a Dubai school actually accept for a tier review?
faqs.answer: Marked work at the tier you are asking for, dated, and ideally four pieces rather than one. A head of department deciding between Foundation and Higher, or Core and Extended, is weighing whether a student can access the harder paper without collapsing, and the only persuasive answer is scripts from the harder paper. Bring no more than four, have one specific sentence ready, and ask what else they would want to see rather than making a case. Entries close months before the exam, so raise it in the autumn term.

faqs.question: How do I know the improvement is not just easier papers?
faqs.answer: Insist on comparability and on error tracking. Two papers from the same board, same tier and similar vintage give a usable comparison; a mark from an unspecified source does not. More reliably, track the cost of the three named errors across every dated script: if marks lost to missing working fell from eleven to four across four papers, that is real regardless of paper difficulty. Score alone is the weakest measure available, which is why progress should be reported in errors and marks rather than in a single number.

faqs.question: What does progress look like week by week in an essay subject?
faqs.answer: Structural rather than numerical, and visible to a parent who has not read the text. Count the paragraphs that begin with a method or technique rather than with a plot event. Watch for short embedded quotations replacing long retold extracts. Look for the register matching the audience the task names. Those changes take four to six weeks and they persist, whereas an essay mark out of thirty bounces around with the question. Keep two essays six weeks apart and compare them side by side; the difference is usually obvious.

faqs.question: Should I ask a tutor for their previous students' results?
faqs.answer: Ask for one anonymised marked script with the mark scheme beside it instead. Results claims are unverifiable, and a provider quoting a satisfaction percentage or an average improvement without the number of students, the date and the method behind it is quoting noise. A marked script shows you how they mark, which is the thing you are actually buying. Competitors in this market publish review counts and ratings that contradict each other on the same page, which is a reasonable argument for ignoring that entire category of claim.

faqs.question: How can I be sure a coursework draft is my child's own work?
faqs.answer: Look at the trail rather than the final text. A genuine one shows planning notes, an early draft, feedback given as questions and criterion references, and a later draft where your child acted on some of it and ignored some. That pattern of judgement, including judgement the tutor disagreed with, is what an honest process looks like. A draft where every suggestion is implemented perfectly in a register unlike your child's other writing is the pattern schools notice, and the malpractice consequence falls on the student.

faqs.question: What are the warning signs in a tutor's progress report?
faqs.answer: A percentage with no annotation. A recommendation for more hours offered in place of a sharper diagnosis. A description of what the tutor explained rather than what the student produced. A grade prediction. Attitude adjectives with nothing behind them. And any statistic about past students without a number, a date and a method attached. Each of those is a substitute for evidence, and the substitution is usually unconscious rather than dishonest, which does not make it less expensive over a term.

faqs.question: How many marked papers before a pattern is trustworthy?
faqs.answer: Three to four scripts across a few weeks is usually enough to see clustering, and one is almost never enough. What you are looking for is repetition: the same topic in the lost column, the same marks given away for missing working, the same time overspend on low-value questions. A single bad paper can be illness, a hard question or a bad morning. Four papers showing the same three errors is a diagnosis, and that is the point at which spending money on fixing them is a sound decision.

faqs.question: If we want someone physically nearby, can you arrange that?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visiting is a service we offer only in India, and tutoring for families here runs one to one over live video. If what your child needs is an adult in the room, the useful part of this page for you is the six-question list and the two compliance checks: identification and the MoHRE private tuition work permit, issued free of charge for two years under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. Those questions work on any tutor, in any format.

faqs.question: How do we hand over to a new tutor without losing the diagnosis?
faqs.answer: By keeping the file. Dated annotated scripts, the session notes and the ranked list of named errors hand a replacement tutor a working diagnosis on day one instead of costing you a fortnight of rediscovery. In a market where mid-year changes are routine, that folder is worth more than loyalty to any individual, and it is also the reason a tutor change in February need not be a disaster. Ask for everything in a form you can keep rather than inside a platform you might lose access to.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me.closingHeading: Ask for the evidence before you ask for the postcode
dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me.closingBody: Reorder the questions and this search gets easier. Specification and level first. Then evidence: one anonymised marked script, and what will exist in writing after four weeks. Then the hour of the evening that genuinely works in your household. Geography comes last, and over video it does not come up at all. Send a photograph of a recent marked paper with the code and the level, and we will propose a tutor who teaches that paper. The first lesson is free and takes no card details, and by week four you will have three named causes of mark loss in writing or a clear reason to change.

intro.heading: Why Diploma maths goes wrong in a Ranches household, and what actually fixes it
paragraphs: An IB maths tutor in Arabian Ranches almost never gets called in because a child cannot do maths. The call comes in October of DP1, or in January of DP2 after the mocks, and the trigger is nearly always one of three specific failures. The first is a route mismatch: a student who liked statistics and context questions at IGCSE was put into Analysis and Approaches Higher Level because it sounded more ambitious, and is now sitting in front of proof by induction with no idea why. The second is an algebra debt. Extended IGCSE rewarded a student who could follow a procedure; Paper 1 of Analysis and Approaches permits no calculator at all, and a weak grip on index laws, surds and rearrangement turns a four-mark question into a blank. The third is the exploration, which has been put off since February and is now three weeks from a school deadline with no usable mathematics in it.

None of those three is a general maths problem, and none of them is solved by generic revision. They need different work. A route mismatch needs an honest conversation with the school about dropping to Standard Level or switching course, and it needs that conversation in the first term rather than the fourth. An algebra debt needs twenty minutes of non-negotiable manipulation drill at the start of every session for about eight weeks, which feels slow and then suddenly is not. A stalled exploration needs a narrower question, which almost always means less ambition and more mathematics.

Arabian Ranches shapes the logistics rather than the maths. This is a villa community spread across Al Reem, Mirador, Saheel, Savannah, Hattan, Alvorada and Polo Homes, with Arabian Ranches 2 and 3 pushing further into Dubailand. Jumeirah English Speaking School Arabian Ranches and Ranches Primary School sit inside the gates, and the rest of the secondary cohort scatters to Motor City, Al Barsha South, Dubai Hills Estate and the Sustainable City. A child who is home from school by about 15:45 can comfortably sit a 17:00 session. A tutor driving in from Jumeirah or Mirdif during the afternoon peak cannot reliably arrive before 18:00, and the hour you pay for includes that drive.

That is the practical case for online IB maths tuition in Dubai, and it is not a compromise. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a villa in Arabian Ranches; home visits are a service we run only in India. What a Ranches family gets instead is a tutor matched to Analysis and Approaches Higher Level or Applications and Interpretation Standard Level specifically, rather than whichever maths graduate happens to live within a twenty-minute drive of Dubailand. On a Paper 3 problem, or on criterion E of the exploration, that distinction is the whole thing.

Everything below is written for the maths, not for the marketing. The two courses are compared properly. The paper weightings are set out with durations. The exploration criteria are listed by letter with their mark allocations, because almost no page in this market names a single one. Market rates are published in AED with the source of each figure attributed. If your child is in DP1 and the question is which course, read the next section. If your child is in DP2 and the question is marks, start at the mark-scheme section.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-arabian-ranches.programmesIntro: Arabian Ranches children move through several programmes before they reach Diploma maths, and the maths demand changes at each handover. These are the stages that matter for a family planning support, with the specific Dubai detail that applies to each.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Mathematics is compulsory: every Diploma candidate takes either Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, at Standard or Higher Level. That makes maths the one subject no student can avoid, and the one where a route chosen badly in Year 11 follows a student for two years.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai is a KHDA-inspected market, and KHDA reported 227 private schools serving 387,441 students in 2024-25, with International Baccalaureate programmes accounting for 7% of enrolment. Diploma cohorts are therefore small relative to the British-curriculum majority, which is precisely why a single school rarely has spare capacity in Analysis and Approaches Higher Level when a student needs extra hours.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Mathematics in the Middle Years Programme is assessed against four criteria rather than by examination: knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Students are graded 1-8 per criterion and the totals convert to a 1-7 subject grade. Standard and extended mathematics streams exist in MYP 4 and 5, and the stream a child sits in at fifteen quietly predicts which Diploma course will fit.
programmes.countryNote: Continuum schools in the Dubailand belt, including Fairgreen International School in the Sustainable City and GEMS International School Al Khail in Dubai Hills Estate, run the Middle Years Programme straight into the Diploma. Students arriving in DP1 from that route have strong investigation and communication habits and often a thinner procedural base than an IGCSE cohort, so their first weeks of Higher Level maths need different support.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE, as the route into DP maths
programmes.description: Most Arabian Ranches secondary students sit IGCSE rather than the Middle Years Programme, because British-curriculum schools dominate Dubai enrolment. Extended Mathematics, and in particular Additional Mathematics, is the best single predictor of whether a student will cope with Analysis and Approaches Higher Level. A student who found Extended algebra uncomfortable is being set up to fail by that choice, however good the rest of the report looks.
programmes.countryNote: Jumeirah English Speaking School Arabian Ranches runs the British curriculum through to post-16, and several nearby schools offer the Diploma alongside or instead of A Level. Families here are therefore making a real choice at sixteen rather than following a single track, and the maths question is usually the deciding one. Check the post-16 pages of your own school before assuming a route is available.

programmes.name: IB Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led, with mathematics taught through transdisciplinary units rather than as a separate timetabled block in the early years. Number sense, pattern and measurement are developed in context. Parents sometimes read that as mathematically light, which it is not, but it does mean a Primary Years Programme child arriving in a British-curriculum Year 7 can look behind on written method while being ahead on reasoning.
programmes.countryNote: Ranches Primary School and the primary phase at Jumeirah English Speaking School Arabian Ranches draw from inside the community, while continuum Primary Years Programme provision sits further out towards Dubai Hills Estate and the Sustainable City. Families moving a child between the two at Year 6 or Year 7 should expect a written-method gap that takes a term of short, regular work to close.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-arabian-ranches.subjectsIntro: On a maths page the useful subject list is not every Diploma course on offer. It is the courses where mathematics decides the grade. Each entry below names the maths actually demanded and where it bites, so a parent can see whether a maths tutor is the right fix for a grade that is slipping in a different subject.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The algebraic route. Proof, functions, trigonometric identities, calculus by hand. Higher Level adds proof by induction, complex numbers, three-dimensional vectors, Maclaurin series and differential equations. Paper 1 bans technology at both levels, which is the single feature that catches students out most often.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The modelling route. Data, regression, financial mathematics and technology throughout. Standard Level includes Voronoi diagrams, the chi-squared test for independence and Spearman's rank. Higher Level adds matrices, graph theory, non-linear regression and hypothesis testing. Every paper allows a graphic display calculator, which changes how practice has to be structured.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The Diploma subject with the highest hidden maths load. Rearranging before substituting, logarithmic linearisation of graphs, propagating uncertainty through a calculation, and vector resolution. Students who lose physics marks on algebra rather than on physics are common, and the fix is a maths fix.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles, dilutions, equilibrium constants, Gibbs free energy and pH all sit on index laws and logarithms. A student who cannot handle a negative exponent cleanly will drop marks across every calculation question, and the error will be recorded as a chemistry weakness on the report.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Higher Level carries genuine calculation: elasticities, marginal and average cost curves, the money multiplier. Quantitative questions are where Higher Level economics grades are made and lost, and they are maths questions with economics vocabulary on top.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Binary and hexadecimal conversion, Boolean logic, recursion and complexity reasoning. The algorithmic thinking rewarded here overlaps heavily with Analysis and Approaches, and students taking both often find each subject makes the other easier.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Ratio analysis, break-even, investment appraisal and cash-flow forecasting. The arithmetic is not hard but the interpretation marks depend on getting it right first, so a small percentage slip costs the whole chain of a long-answer question.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Statistics decide the data-analysis marks: standard deviation, error bars, correlation and the difference between a significant result and an interesting-looking graph. The internal assessment is where this matters most, and it is often the first place a student meets real statistical reasoning.

subjects.name: Design Technology
subjects.description: Scale, tolerance, material properties and basic stress calculation. Students choose this course expecting it to be practical and then meet quantitative questions in the papers, which is a predictable place for a maths-driven grade drop.

subjects.name: Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.description: Population models, flow diagrams with quantified inputs and outputs, and data interpretation under time pressure. A popular choice for students who want to limit their maths exposure, and still a course where the numerical questions separate a 5 from a 7.

sections.heading: What a parent in Arabian Ranches is really asking when they search for an IB maths tutor
paragraphs: An IB maths tutor in Arabian Ranches teaches either Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches or Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation, at Standard or Higher Level, one-to-one over live video. Market rates in Dubai for a genuine International Baccalaureate subject specialist run roughly AED 200 to AED 450 an hour as published by other providers in October 2026. IB Gram delivers these lessons online to Arabian Ranches rather than by sending a tutor to a villa, and the reason is supply rather than cost.

Behind the search there is almost always a specific document. Sometimes it is a DP1 report with a 4 in Higher Level maths and a comment about needing to show more working. Sometimes it is a mock paper with eleven marks out of forty on Paper 1 and a note that the student ran out of time. Sometimes it is an email from the maths teacher about an exploration draft that has no mathematics in it yet. A tutor is useful in proportion to how precisely that document is read, which is why the first session should be spent on evidence rather than on introductions.

The second thing behind the search is a timing problem that is specific to this part of Dubai. Arabian Ranches is a villa community in the Dubailand belt, and the secondary cohort is dispersed across Motor City, Al Barsha South, Dubai Hills Estate and the Sustainable City. A child is rarely home before 15:30, and a tutor crossing the city at that hour is rarely reliable before 18:00. The practical consequence is that the available pool of in-home Diploma maths specialists for this neighbourhood is small, and it shrinks further once you specify Analysis and Approaches Higher Level rather than maths in general.

That is the honest case for online delivery, and it is worth stating as a trade rather than as a benefit. You give up the physical presence of a person in the room. You gain access to a tutor who teaches your child's exact course, a session that starts on time whatever Al Qudra Road is doing, a shared screen on which a graph can be built and rebuilt in seconds, and a recording of the worked solution to go back to on Thursday night.

sections.heading: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation: the decision that sets the next two years
paragraphs: The two Diploma maths courses are not an easy version and a hard version. They are different subjects that share five syllabus topics. Both run at Standard and Higher Level. Analysis and Approaches is built on algebraic method, proof and calculus done by hand; Applications and Interpretation is built on modelling, data and technology. Teaching time is 150 hours at Standard Level and 240 at Higher Level in both courses, so the difference is in what those hours contain.

The feature that decides most cases is Paper 1 of Analysis and Approaches, which permits no technology at either level. Every paper in Applications and Interpretation allows a graphic display calculator. A student who relied on a calculator through Extended IGCSE and who has never practised simplifying a surd or differentiating from first principles without one is walking into a paper worth 40% of a Standard Level grade or 30% of a Higher Level grade with a tool they cannot use. That is not a talent problem, but it does take a term of deliberate work to repair.

The second deciding factor is the Higher Level content. Analysis and Approaches Higher Level adds proof by induction, complex numbers including De Moivre's theorem, three-dimensional vectors with lines and planes, Maclaurin series, implicit differentiation and differential equations solved by separation of variables and by Euler's method. Applications and Interpretation Higher Level adds matrices and eigenvalues, graph theory, non-linear regression, transition matrices and formal hypothesis testing. A tutor who knows one of those lists well does not automatically know the other, which is why the match has to be to the course rather than to the subject.

The honest advice to an Arabian Ranches family making this choice in Year 11 is to look at the IGCSE evidence rather than at ambition. A student who enjoyed Additional Mathematics, or who scored well on the algebra and calculus-adjacent questions of Extended Mathematics, belongs in Analysis and Approaches. A student who was strong on statistics, probability and contextual questions and uncomfortable with abstract manipulation belongs in Applications and Interpretation, and will very likely get a better Diploma total there. Course requirements for specific university programmes differ by department, so check the published entry requirements of the actual course before the decision is locked.

sections.heading: The papers, the durations and the weightings, set out properly
paragraphs: Both courses are assessed on written papers plus one internal assessment. Standard Level sits two papers; Higher Level sits three. The exploration is worth 20% at both levels in both courses, which means a fifth of the grade is decided before the student walks into an examination hall. A great many Diploma families do not know this until DP2, by which point the opportunity to take it seriously has largely gone.

At Standard Level, Paper 1 and Paper 2 are each an hour and a half and each carries 40%. At Higher Level, Paper 1 and Paper 2 are each two hours and carry 30% apiece, and Paper 3 is one hour carrying 20%. Paper 3 is the component most students meet last and prepare least. It consists of two extended problem-solving questions, and it tests something the other papers do not: sustaining a single unfamiliar problem across many parts, where a wrong answer in part (b) poisons parts (c) through (f).

A formula booklet is supplied in every paper. The skill it demands is knowing what is not in it. Students lose marks waiting to find a result they are expected to know, or using a listed formula without recognising which variable in the question maps to which symbol. Working through the booklet deliberately, early in DP2, and annotating it with what each entry is actually for, is twenty minutes that pays back repeatedly.

Calculator discipline is the other recoverable loss. A graphic display calculator is required for Analysis and Approaches Papers 2 and 3 and for every Applications and Interpretation paper. Angle mode left in radians when the question is in degrees, a stored variable from the previous question, and a regression run on the wrong column have all cost students more marks than any topic gap. These are mechanical errors with mechanical fixes, and they are worth checking before the final eight weeks, not during them.

sections.heading: Where the marks actually go: method marks, reasoning marks and the words that tell you what to do
paragraphs: Diploma maths mark schemes award marks for method, for accuracy and for reasoning separately. A student who writes only a final answer to a six-mark question and gets it wrong scores zero, where a student who sets up the same question correctly and then slips in arithmetic can score four. Teaching a student to write the setup line before touching the calculator is the single highest-yield habit change available in DP1, and it is almost entirely a habit rather than an ability.

The command terms are instructions with mark-scheme consequences, not stylistic preferences. Show that means the answer is given and the marks are entirely in the derivation, so a student who writes down the given answer scores nothing. Hence means the previous part must be used, and a fresh approach that reaches the same answer can be refused the marks. Hence or otherwise permits any valid method. Justify and determine require a stated reason. Write down signals that no working is expected and that spending four minutes on it is time stolen from a later question.

Topic-level losses are predictable enough to diagnose from one marked paper. In Analysis and Approaches the recurring failures are index and surd manipulation under no-calculator conditions, the chain rule inside a product, trigonometric identities applied in the wrong direction, and integration by substitution where the limits are not transformed. In Applications and Interpretation the recurring failures are interpreting a regression coefficient in context, stating hypotheses in the right form, confusing correlation strength with model suitability, and rounding too early in a financial calculation so that the final figure drifts.

The practical routine that fixes this is unexciting. Sit a paper under timing. Mark it against the published scheme rather than by feel. Write each lost mark against a cause: did not know it, knew it but misread, knew it and ran out of time, arithmetic slip, or no working shown. Then spend the next session on the two largest categories. Three cycles of that in DP2 move more marks than three months of re-teaching content the student already knows.

sections.heading: The maths exploration, criterion by criterion with the marks named
paragraphs: The exploration is a piece of independent written mathematics, recommended at 12 to 20 pages, carrying 20% of the Diploma maths grade at both levels and in both courses. It is marked out of 20 across five criteria, and almost no commercial tutoring page in this market names a single one of them. Knowing the letters and their mark allocations changes how a student spends their time, because the largest single block of marks is not where most students think it is.

Criterion E, use of mathematics, carries six marks: the mathematics must be relevant, correct, and commensurate with the level of the course or beyond it. That is the heaviest criterion and the one most often undersold by students who choose an enormous topic and then run only a surface treatment of it. Criterion A, presentation, and criterion B, mathematical communication, carry four marks each. Criterion C, personal engagement, and criterion D, reflection, carry three each. Reflection must be critical rather than descriptive, which in practice means writing about what the mathematics failed to capture, not summarising what was done.

The commonest failure pattern in a Dubai Diploma cohort is a topic that is too large. A student proposes to model traffic flow on Al Qudra Road, collects nothing usable, and writes eleven pages of description with two equations in it. A narrower question with real mathematics in it scores better every time: the optimal angle for a single shot, the cooling curve of one drink in one room, the geometry of one specific roof. Narrowing is the first conversation in any exploration clinic, and it is usually the only one that matters.

What a tutor may do here is bounded and the boundary should be stated plainly. A tutor may teach the mathematics a student needs, discuss whether a question is answerable, ask what a paragraph is trying to say, point out that notation is inconsistent, and explain what a criterion rewards. A tutor may not write, draft, restructure or complete any part of the exploration, and may not supply text for the student to adopt. The work must be the student's own, and under International Baccalaureate academic honesty rules anything else puts the whole Diploma at risk.

Our own position is a free first lesson and a consultation, because the right rate depends on the course, the level and how many weeks are left.

The number that moves most between models is not the headline hourly rate but what the hour contains. An in-home visit in Dubailand prices the tutor's drive into the hour you pay for, and on a Thursday afternoon crossing from Al Barsha that drive can be forty minutes each way. A tutor who charges AED 250 and spends eighty minutes travelling is pricing differently from a tutor who charges AED 250 and spends that time preparing against your child's school scheme of work. That is the comparison worth making, and it is rarely the one presented.

Context helps too. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package. Against a school fee that is held flat, a weekly Diploma maths session for the final two terms of DP2 is a known and bounded cost, and it is worth planning as one rather than reaching for an emergency intensive in April. One warning about how rates are presented in this market. Where a provider quotes a monthly package, check the number of sessions and their length before comparing it with an hourly figure. sections.heading: The Diploma maths year counted backwards from the May session
paragraphs: UAE schools sit the May examination session, and the useful way to plan Diploma maths is to count backwards from it rather than forwards from September. The table below is deliberately built around who sets each date, because families routinely assume the International Baccalaureate sets the deadline that is actually set by their own school, and then miss it. Exact session and results dates are published by the International Baccalaureate and administered through your child's Diploma coordinator; confirm them with the school rather than with any tutoring page, including this one.

The dates that genuinely bind a student are mostly internal. The school sets the exploration topic deadline, the draft deadline and the final submission date, and it sets them months before the examination session because the teacher has to mark and the work has to be uploaded. By the time a family starts worrying about exams in February, the exploration mark is usually already fixed. That is the single most useful thing a DP1 parent in Arabian Ranches can know, and it is the reason the exploration work belongs in DP1.

The mock window, typically January into February of DP2, is the other date worth protecting. Mocks are the only realistic rehearsal of the full paper set under timing, and at Higher Level they are often the first time a student sits Paper 3 for real. A student who treats mocks as a diagnostic rather than as a verdict gets eight to ten weeks of precisely targeted work out of them. A student who treats them as a verdict loses two weeks to demoralisation and then starts late.

Ramadan falls inside the Diploma preparation window in the current cycle, and it changes when revision can actually happen in a UAE household. School hours shorten, evenings reorganise around Iftar, and a 17:00 session may need to move to late evening or to the early afternoon. Planning that shift in advance, rather than cancelling four weeks of sessions and resuming in a panic, is one of the quiet advantages of a fixed online slot that can be moved in a day.
