sections.heading: Academic honesty, tutor permits and what happens when no specialist is free
paragraphs: Three things in this market are worth being blunt about, because competitors are not. The first is academic honesty. Pages in this search sell completed internal assessments. A completed exploration bought from a third party is malpractice under International Baccalaureate rules, and the consequence falls on the student, not the seller. A tutor teaches the mathematics, questions the reasoning, explains what a criterion rewards and reads what the student has written. A tutor does not write it. Saying so is not a disclaimer; it is the difference between support and a risk to the whole Diploma.

The second is permits. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, granted free of charge for two years, with eligibility extending to registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so any page quoting an amount is guessing. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules additionally bar school staff from paid tutoring of students at their own school. Dubai's private schools are regulated by KHDA, which is an authority to understand rather than an endorsement anyone can claim: IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, Ministry of Education, International Baccalaureate or Cambridge accreditation, and neither do most of the pages implying otherwise.

The third is availability, which nobody in this search discloses. Analysis and Approaches Higher Level specialists are a narrow pool, and demand concentrates in the eight weeks before the May session. There are weeks when no UAE-based tutor for a specific course and level is free at the slot a family needs. When that happens we say so, and the options are an alternative slot, a tutor based outside the UAE teaching the identical syllabus over the same live video, or a wait with a date attached. What we do not do is substitute a generalist and describe them as a specialist.

The same transparency applies to delivery. IB Gram does not run a UAE office, and does not offer home visits in the UAE; those are an India-only service. Every Arabian Ranches lesson is one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, and the first one is free with no card details taken.

faqs.question: Which IB maths route should a JESS Arabian Ranches student pick, AA or AI?
faqs.answer: Decide on IGCSE evidence rather than on ambition. A student who enjoyed Additional Mathematics, or who scored well on the algebra and manipulation questions in Extended Mathematics, generally belongs in Analysis and Approaches. A student who was strong on statistics, probability and contextual questions but uncomfortable with abstract algebra will usually score higher in Applications and Interpretation. Check the published entry requirements of the university courses your child is considering, because some engineering, physics and economics departments name Analysis and Approaches specifically, while a growing number accept Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level. Confirm what your own school offers before assuming both courses run at both levels.

faqs.question: How many marks is the Mathematics internal assessment worth at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: The exploration is marked out of 20 and carries 20% of the final maths grade, at Higher Level and at Standard Level, in both courses. The 20 marks are split across five criteria: presentation 4, mathematical communication 4, personal engagement 3, reflection 3, and use of mathematics 6. Use of mathematics is the heaviest single criterion, which is why a narrow topic treated thoroughly beats an ambitious topic treated superficially. Your child's teacher marks it and the International Baccalaureate moderates. Because the school's internal deadline falls months before the examination session, the exploration mark is usually settled before exam revision begins.

faqs.question: What does Paper 3 ask for in Mathematics Analysis and Approaches HL?
faqs.answer: Paper 3 is sat only at Higher Level. It lasts one hour, carries 20% of the grade and contains two extended problem-solving questions set in unfamiliar contexts. A graphic display calculator is required. The skill it tests is sustaining one long problem across many parts, where part (a) sets up a structure that parts (b) to (f) depend on. Students who have only practised short exam questions find it disorientating, and most schools cover it late in DP2. A block of six to eight weeks working only Paper 3 style questions under timing is usually the highest-yield single intervention available in the second Diploma year.

faqs.question: Why does my child lose method marks even when the final answer is right?
faqs.answer: Diploma mark schemes award method, accuracy and reasoning marks separately, and a correct answer with no visible working can still forfeit most of them. This is particularly common with calculator papers, where a student types a long expression and writes only the output. The fix is mechanical: write the setup line, with variables defined and the substitution shown, before touching the calculator. It takes about fifteen seconds and protects the majority of the marks on a six-mark question. Command terms matter here too. Show that gives the answer away deliberately, so every mark lives in the derivation and writing the given result scores nothing.

faqs.question: Is a graphic display calculator allowed in every IB maths paper?
faqs.answer: No. Paper 1 in Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches permits no technology at either level, while Papers 2 and 3 require a graphic display calculator. Every paper in Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation allows one. This single difference catches out more Dubai students than any topic. A child who passed Extended IGCSE with a calculator in hand needs deliberate no-calculator practice on surds, indices, exact trigonometric values and differentiation from first principles, starting in DP1. Leaving it until the mocks means discovering the problem with ten weeks left rather than ten months, which is a far more expensive place to start.

faqs.question: Which Analysis and Approaches topics cause the most trouble in DP2?
faqs.answer: Four recur. Index and surd manipulation under no-calculator conditions, where a weak foundation from IGCSE shows immediately. The chain rule used inside a product or quotient, where students apply one rule and forget the other. Trigonometric identities applied in the wrong direction, because the student has learnt them as facts rather than as tools. Integration by substitution where the limits are not transformed, which costs the final accuracy mark on an otherwise correct solution. At Higher Level, proof by induction and Maclaurin series are the usual additions. All five are diagnosable from one marked paper, which is why the first session should be spent on evidence.

faqs.question: How long should the maths exploration be, and can a tutor write it?
faqs.answer: The recommended length is 12 to 20 pages, and a tutor cannot write any of it. What a tutor may do is teach the mathematics required, discuss whether a research question is answerable in that space, ask what a paragraph is trying to say, point out inconsistent notation, and explain what each criterion rewards. What a tutor must not do is draft, restructure or supply text, because the exploration must be the student's own work under International Baccalaureate academic honesty rules. Pages in this market sell completed internal assessments. That is malpractice, and the consequence falls on the student rather than on the seller.

faqs.question: Can a student move from Analysis and Approaches HL down to SL mid-course?
faqs.answer: It is often possible, it is a school decision rather than a tutoring one, and it has a deadline. The school's Diploma coordinator has to confirm subject levels with the International Baccalaureate well before the examination session, so a change needs to be requested early rather than after the DP2 mocks. The practical consideration is university requirements: some courses name Higher Level mathematics, so check the published entry requirements for the actual course before moving. A term of focused algebra work in DP1 sometimes makes the move unnecessary, which is a better outcome than either dropping down or struggling on.

faqs.question: What does a 7 in IB Mathematics actually require on the papers?
faqs.answer: Grade boundaries are set by the International Baccalaureate for each session and are not fixed in advance, so no tutor can tell you a percentage that converts to a 7, and nobody can promise your child a grade. What is visible is the shape of the work a top grade needs: near-complete method marks because setup lines are always written, confident no-calculator work in Analysis and Approaches Paper 1, a Paper 3 technique that survives an unfamiliar context at Higher Level, and an exploration scoring well on use of mathematics. Those four are trainable. Treat any page that promises a specific grade in advance with real scepticism.

faqs.question: How much does an online IB maths tutor cost for a family in Arabian Ranches?
faqs.answer: Published market rates in Dubai, read in October 2026, put generalist online tutors at roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, qualified subject tutors at AED 150 to 300, and International Baccalaureate specialists at AED 200 to 450 or more. Unitors publishes IB from AED 200, TutorChase AED 270, BartyED AED 650 for premium examiner-led work. In-home visits run AED 180 to 500 and price the tutor's drive into your hour. Those are other providers' figures, not ours. IB Gram starts with a free first lesson and a consultation, because the right plan depends on the course, the level and the weeks remaining.

faqs.question: What evening session times work with an Al Qudra Road school run?
faqs.answer: Most Arabian Ranches families settle on 17:00 or 17:30 on weekdays. A child at Jumeirah English Speaking School Arabian Ranches is usually home by about 15:45, which leaves time to eat before a session. Families in Arabian Ranches 2, Mudon, DAMAC Hills and Town Square typically need 17:30 or 18:00 because the run is longer. Saturday mornings work well for intensive blocks in the final weeks before the May session. Because lessons are delivered over live video, the start time depends only on when your child is at a desk, not on when a tutor can cross Dubai.

faqs.question: Do your tutors cover both Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation?
faqs.answer: Yes, but not usually the same tutor at Higher Level. The two Higher Level syllabuses diverge sharply: one adds proof by induction, complex numbers, three-dimensional vectors, Maclaurin series and differential equations, while the other adds matrices and eigenvalues, graph theory, non-linear regression and hypothesis testing. A tutor who is genuinely fluent in one of those lists is not automatically fluent in the other. We match to the exact course and level your child sits. At Standard Level the overlap is larger and a strong tutor can cover both comfortably.

faqs.question: Which UAE universities expect Analysis and Approaches rather than Applications?
faqs.answer: Requirements are set by individual departments and change between admission cycles, so the only reliable answer is the published entry requirements on the course page itself. The general pattern is that engineering, physics, mathematics and quantitative economics programmes most often name Analysis and Approaches, while business, design, life-science and social-science routes accept either, with Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level increasingly accepted. Check the specific programme at the specific university before locking a Year 11 decision, and ask your school's university counsellor, who tracks this annually. No tutoring page should be your source for an admissions requirement.

faqs.question: How many weeks before the May session should past-paper work start?
faqs.answer: Timed full papers should start about twelve weeks out, and ideally earlier at Higher Level because Paper 3 needs its own practice. The useful pattern is a cycle rather than a count: sit a paper to time, mark it against the published scheme, sort every lost mark by cause, then spend the following session on the two biggest causes. Three complete cycles move more marks than three months of re-teaching familiar content. Before twelve weeks out, the work is content and technique. Papers used too early, before the syllabus is covered, tend to teach discouragement rather than exam craft.

faqs.question: What happens if no Analysis and Approaches HL specialist is free this term?
faqs.answer: You get told, with a date, rather than quietly matched to a generalist. Higher Level specialists are a narrow pool and demand concentrates in the weeks before the May session, so there are genuinely weeks when no UAE-based tutor for a specific course and level is available at the slot you want. The options are then an alternative time, a tutor based outside the UAE teaching the identical syllabus over the same live video, or a wait with a named start date. No competitor page in this market discloses a coverage limit, which does not mean they do not have one.

If your child is in DP2, send the marked mock. One paper, sorted by cause of lost mark, tells an IB maths tutor more than any conversation about confidence. The first lesson is free, with no card details taken and no obligation to continue, and it is spent working through real questions with a tutor who teaches your child's exact course. Lessons run one-to-one over live video, in Gulf Standard Time, at a slot that fits around the Arabian Ranches school run.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-dubai-hills-esta.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB Mathematics to Diploma students in Dubai Hills Estate and the surrounding Dubailand communities. Each one works to a dated plan that ends at the May examination session and passes through your own school's internal deadlines on the way.

intro.heading: An IB maths tutor in Dubai Hills Estate, read off the calendar
paragraphs: Parents in Dubai Hills Estate rarely search for an IB maths tutor in Dubai Hills Estate in the abstract. The search happens on a specific evening: a Paper 2 mock has come back at a 4, the exploration is still a vague idea about basketball statistics, and the DP coordinator has emailed a draft deadline that is six weeks away. The useful question is therefore not whether tutoring helps in general. It is what this term, from this starting point, can still change before each of those dates arrives.

That framing matters more in IB Mathematics than in most subjects, because the grade is assembled from pieces that close at different times. The mathematical exploration is worth a fifth of the final grade and is finished, marked internally and moderated long before the examinations begin. Paper 1 and Paper 2 are sat in a single fortnight. At Higher Level a third paper arrives, sixty minutes long, worth a further fifth of the grade and built from two extended problems that reward students who can sustain an argument rather than recognise a question type. A plan that treats all of this as one undifferentiated block of revision wastes the term.

Dubai Hills Estate adds its own constraint, which is geography rather than curriculum. The community sits between Al Khail Road and Umm Suqeim Street, so the schools its families use are spread across Al Quoz, Al Barsha South, Sobha Hartland, Motor City and Meydan rather than concentrated in one spot. A bus that arrives at 15:40 and a sibling collection at 16:15 leave a narrow, immovable window for anything academic. A tutor who has to drive into that window spends part of it on the road. A tutor on live video does not, which is why every lesson described on this page is delivered online, one-to-one, with the student's own exploration draft and past papers on a shared screen.

The practical consequence is that tuition here is planned backwards. We start from the examination session your child is entered for, then mark in the school's own exploration deadlines, the mock window and the date predicted grades are issued. Only then do we decide what a weekly hour should contain. An eight-week block in October looks nothing like an eight-week block in February: the first is almost entirely exploration work and topic repair, the second is timed papers, command-term discipline and calculator technique. Both are useful. Confusing one for the other is how a term disappears.

What follows is the whole of that plan written out: the calendar counted backwards, the paper weightings, the exploration criteria letter by letter, what the Dubai market charges for IB maths tuition and who charges it, and how a session fits around a Dubai Hills school run, a half-term and Ramadan. Confirm every IB date with your school's DP coordinator or on ibo.org before you build a schedule on it, because sessions and deadlines are set by the IB and administered by the school, not by us.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-dubai-hills-esta.programmesIntro: IB Mathematics does not start in the Diploma. A Dubai Hills Estate student arriving in DP1 has usually come through MYP mathematics at an IB continuum school or through IGCSE at a British one, and the two produce different gaps. These are the programmes we support and what each one hands the next.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Mathematics
programmes.description: Two courses sit side by side: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches, which is algebraic, proof-aware and calculus-heavy, and Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation, which is modelling-led and statistical. Each runs at Standard Level with 150 prescribed teaching hours and Higher Level with 240. Both share five syllabus topics: number and algebra, functions, geometry and trigonometry, statistics and probability, and calculus. The depth inside those topics is what separates the courses and the levels.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai Hills Estate families choose between the two courses at the end of Year 11, often on incomplete information. Schools nearby offering the Diploma include GEMS Wellington Academy Al Khail, Dubai International Academy Al Barsha, Hartland International School and GEMS Dubai American Academy, and each runs its own combination of AA and AI at both levels. Which combinations your school can timetable is a real constraint on the choice, and it is worth asking before the option form goes in.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme Mathematics
programmes.description: MYP mathematics is assessed against four criteria rather than papers: knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Standard and extended routes diverge in MYP 4 and 5. The criterion-based habits built here transfer directly to the exploration, which is also marked against criteria rather than right answers. What does not transfer automatically is sustained algebraic fluency under time pressure.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP to Diploma step is the single most common reason a Dubai Hills Estate family contacts us in the first term of DP1. Students from Dubai International Academy Al Barsha and other continuum schools arrive comfortable with investigation and modelling, then meet Paper 1 with no calculator and find that algebraic manipulation has been doing quiet background work they never had to make explicit. Six to eight weeks of focused algebra usually closes it.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme Mathematics
programmes.description: PYP mathematics is taught through units of inquiry rather than a numbered syllabus, with number, pattern and function, data handling, measurement, and shape and space threaded through transdisciplinary themes. Support at this stage is about fluency and confidence with number rather than examination technique, and it is usually short-term: a term of weekly work on times tables, fractions or place value.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai Hills Estate has a large primary population, and PYP enquiries here tend to come from families who have moved mid-year between curricula. A child arriving from a British Year 4 into PYP, or the reverse, meets the same mathematics in a different order. Mapping what has been covered against what the new class assumes takes one diagnostic session and is worth doing before any tutoring is booked.

programmes.name: IGCSE Mathematics as the route into the Diploma
programmes.description: Most Dubai Hills Estate students who join DP1 from a British-curriculum school arrive with Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 Extended or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE 4MA1 Higher. Both end at a grade 9 ceiling and both stop short of the calculus, proof and vector work that Analysis and Approaches opens with. The gap is not a reflection of the student; it is a syllabus boundary.
programmes.countryNote: Repton Al Barsha, Kings' School Al Barsha, GEMS Metropole Motor City and Dubai Heights Academy all feed IGCSE students into Diploma or A Level routes, and the IGCSE-to-AA HL step is the steepest of them. A student who scored a 7 at IGCSE and chose AA HL on that basis is the typical DP1 autumn enquiry from this part of Dubai. Bridging work on differentiation, binomial expansion and trigonometric identities is what the first term needs.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-dubai-hills-esta.subjectsIntro: Within IB Mathematics the work divides cleanly by topic, and the diagnosis in a first lesson is almost always topic-level rather than general. These are the areas a Dubai Hills Estate DP student most often needs, with what each one actually assesses.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The algebraic and calculus-led course. Rewards fluent manipulation, proof technique and the ability to follow a 'show that' instruction without a calculator. Paper 1 is sat without technology at both levels, which exposes any dependence on a graphic display calculator built up during IGCSE or MYP.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The modelling and statistics course, with a calculator permitted on every paper. Marks are lost less often on calculation than on interpretation: a regression line computed correctly and then described in words that say nothing about the context scores the calculation and loses the rest.

subjects.name: Calculus
subjects.description: Differentiation, integration, kinematics and, at HL, implicit differentiation, related rates, differential equations and Maclaurin series. The HL extension is where most Dubai Hills Estate students who dropped from a 6 to a 4 lost the ground, usually because the chain rule was never fully automatic.

subjects.name: Functions
subjects.description: Transformations, composite and inverse functions, rational functions and, at HL, modulus and reciprocal graphs. The common failure is sketching: a graph drawn without asymptotes, intercepts or stated domain loses method marks even when the algebra underneath it is right.

subjects.name: Number and algebra
subjects.description: Sequences, series, exponentials, logarithms, binomial expansion and, at HL, proof by induction, complex numbers in Cartesian and polar form, and partial fractions. Proof by induction is the most reliably mishandled topic on the HL syllabus and the most teachable in a fortnight.

subjects.name: Geometry and trigonometry
subjects.description: Triangle rules, radian measure, trigonometric identities and equations, and at HL vectors, scalar and vector products, and lines and planes in three dimensions. Vector geometry is where a student who can do the algebra still loses marks for not drawing the situation first.

subjects.name: Statistics and probability
subjects.description: Data presentation, regression, probability, binomial and normal distributions, and at HL conditional probability, Bayes' theorem, and probability generating work. This is the dominant topic in Applications and Interpretation and the one most explorations are built on, which makes it double-weighted in practice.

subjects.name: The mathematical exploration
subjects.levels: SL and HL · 20% of the grade
subjects.description: A 12 to 20 page individual investigation marked internally against five criteria and moderated by the IB. It is the student's own work throughout. A tutor may teach the mathematics it needs, question the reasoning and give written feedback on a draft; a tutor may not write, edit to completion or supply any part of it.

subjects.name: Paper 3 extended response
subjects.description: Sixty minutes, two compulsory extended problems that build in stages. Each later part depends on the earlier ones, so a student who guesses at part (b) usually forfeits (c) and (d) as well. Practice here is about reading the whole question before starting, not about speed.

subjects.name: Calculator technique
subjects.description: The graphic display calculator is required on Paper 2 and Paper 3 and barred on Paper 1 in Analysis and Approaches. Students lose method marks by producing a correct answer with no recorded intermediate step, because the examiner cannot award the method that was never written down.

sections.heading: What eight weeks of IB maths tutoring can realistically change
paragraphs: Eight weekly hours is about as much as a Dubai Hills Estate family typically commits to before deciding whether to continue. It is enough to do one of three things well and not enough to do all three. Either you repair two or three specific topics to the point where they stop costing marks, or you take an exploration from a vague idea to a complete draft, or you convert a student who knows the mathematics into one who can produce it under timed conditions. Choosing which, in the first session, is the most valuable decision in the whole block.

The choice follows from where the marks are going. If mock papers show scattered losses across every topic with correct method and arithmetic slips, the problem is recording and timing, and the fix is timed papers with line-by-line marking. If losses cluster in calculus and functions while statistics is fine, the problem is topic knowledge and the fix is sequenced teaching. If the exploration has not started and the school deadline is inside the block, nothing else matters: a fifth of the grade is sitting unclaimed and the deadline will not move.

What eight weeks cannot do is rebuild two years of Higher Level content, and anyone who says otherwise is selling. A student sitting at a 3 in AA HL in January has a level decision to make with the school, not a tutoring decision, and we will say that in the first lesson rather than after the eighth. The honest version of this service includes telling a family when the sensible move is a conversation with the DP coordinator about dropping to SL while the option is still open.

The first session is therefore a diagnostic rather than a lesson. The student brings their last two mock papers, the mark scheme if the school released it, their exploration draft or notes, and the school's internal deadline dates. We work through where marks were actually lost, write the eight-week plan against those dates, and send it to you in writing. If the plan says tutoring is not the right spend this term, it says that.

Bring the school's exploration deadline dates, which are set by the school and not by the IB

sections.heading: The IB Mathematics year, counted backwards
paragraphs: Every IB Mathematics deadline that matters to a Dubai Hills Estate student is set by one of two bodies, and families routinely confuse them. The IB sets the examination session and the final submission windows for internally assessed work. Your child's school sets everything else: the topic approval date, the first draft deadline, the mock window, the date predicted grades are issued. School deadlines sit months ahead of IB ones, deliberately, because the school has to mark and internally standardise the work before uploading it.

That is why a plan built on the examination session alone fails. The exploration is finished, marked and gone while the student is still in the middle of the syllabus. The predicted grade that universities see is issued off work completed well before any final paper is sat. A student who treats May as the only deadline arrives at February with two unmoved deadlines behind them and no way to recover either.

The table below is the structure of that year rather than a list of dates, and the reason is honesty: ibo.org blocks automated checking, so no IB session or results date on this page has been confirmed from the IB itself. Ask your DP coordinator for the dated version for your cohort, or read it on ibo.org directly, and build your schedule on that. Cambridge and Pearson publish their own timetables for IGCSE and International A Level students, which is useful if you have a younger child on a British route in the same house.

Used properly, the backward count turns a vague worry into a sequence. Count the weeks from today to the school's exploration deadline. Count the weeks from there to the mock window. Count the weeks from the mocks to the session. Each gap gets one job. Most families find that the gap they thought was comfortable is the shortest one on the list.

sections.heading: Where Analysis and Approaches marks go missing between October and March
paragraphs: Mark loss in IB Mathematics is boringly predictable, which is good news: predictable problems are fixable problems. Across DP2 students we work with in Dubai, the same five patterns account for most of the gap between what a student knows and what they score, and four of the five are technique rather than knowledge.

The first is the 'show that' chain. A question gives a result and asks the student to reach it. Marks are awarded for the steps, not the destination, and a student who writes three lines where the mark scheme expects six has forfeited the middle marks even though the final line matches. Paper 1 is dense with these, and because no calculator is permitted, there is nowhere to hide an unshown step.

The second is the unwritten calculator step. On Paper 2 and Paper 3 the graphic display calculator does the arithmetic, and students stop writing down what they asked it to do. An examiner awards method marks for the method that appears on the page. A correct final answer with no visible setup scores the answer mark alone. This single habit is worth several marks a paper and takes about three weeks to change.

The third is sketching. Curve sketches drawn without asymptotes, intercepts, stated domain or turning points lose marks that the underlying algebra had already earned. The fourth is the HL multi-part problem: students attempt part (b) by guessing rather than deriving, which contaminates (c) and (d). The fifth, and the only genuine knowledge gap, is proof by induction and the HL calculus extension, where a term of sequenced teaching is the only remedy.

A diagnostic in the first session separates these. We mark two recent papers against the published scheme and count which of the five categories each lost mark belongs to. Families are usually surprised: the student they thought needed more calculus often needs three weeks of method recording and then nothing else.

'Show that' questions are marked on the steps, so write more lines than feel necessary
Write down every calculator input; the method mark follows the writing, not the answer
Sketches need asymptotes, intercepts and domain stated every time
Proof by induction and HL calculus are the two real knowledge gaps worth teaching from scratch

sections.heading: Papers, weightings and what each one actually rewards
paragraphs: A Dubai Hills Estate parent planning a term of tuition needs the weightings in front of them, because the weightings decide where an hour is best spent. The structure is the same for both IB Mathematics courses and differs between Standard and Higher Level in a way that changes the whole revision strategy.

At Standard Level there are two papers, each worth two fifths of the grade, plus the exploration at one fifth. At Higher Level there are three papers, worth three tenths, three tenths and one fifth, plus the exploration at one fifth. The arithmetic matters: at HL, Paper 3 and the exploration together are worth as much as Paper 1, and Paper 3 is the component students practise least because schools often reach it last.

The difference between the two courses is the calculator. In Analysis and Approaches, Paper 1 is sat with no technology at all, which makes algebraic fluency a scoring component in its own right. In Applications and Interpretation the graphic display calculator is permitted throughout, which moves the difficulty from manipulation to interpretation: the marks sit in explaining what a model means in context, and an answer that stops at the number stops short of the marks.

Read the table as a spending guide. If your child is at HL and has never sat a full Paper 3 to time, that is the highest-yield hour available. If they are at SL in Analysis and Approaches and rely on a calculator for routine algebra, Paper 1 practice without one is the highest-yield hour. These are different problems with different fixes, and a tutor who runs the same lesson for both is not reading the weightings.

sections.heading: The exploration, criterion by criterion
paragraphs: No competitor page we found names a single IB assessment criterion by letter, which is strange, because the criteria are published, they are what the teacher marks against, and they tell a student exactly where the twenty marks are. A Dubai Hills Estate student who has read them before choosing a topic writes a different exploration from one who reads them after the first draft comes back.

The most common failure is not weak mathematics but mathematics in the wrong place. Criterion E rewards mathematics that is relevant, commensurate with the level of the course, and correct. A statistical survey of classmates' sleeping habits analysed with a mean and a bar chart is commensurate with nothing; the same survey with a chi-squared test, stated hypotheses, a discussion of assumptions and a reflection on sample bias is an exploration. The topic did not change. The mathematics did.

The second failure is reflection treated as a conclusion. Criterion D is not a summary of what was done; it is critical, forward-looking commentary about the limitations of the approach and what a better version would do. Students write 'in future I would use a larger sample' and consider the criterion addressed. Reflection that earns full marks is woven through the work, not appended to it.

What a tutor does here has a hard boundary and it is worth stating plainly, because two pages ranking for these queries sell completed Internal Assessments outright. The exploration must be the student's own work. We teach the mathematics it requires, ask the questions a moderator would ask, and give written feedback on a draft the student has written. We do not write, draft, rewrite or supply any part of it. Submitting work that is not your own is academic malpractice under IB rules and the consequence falls on the student, not the tutor.

sections.heading: What IB maths tuition costs around Dubai Hills Estate, and how to read the rates
paragraphs: Three of the six competitor pages we examined for this query publish no price at all, and two of the three that do quote in US dollars, which is not the currency a Dubai Hills Estate family transacts in. So here are the market bands in dirhams, attributed to whoever published them, as of October 2026.

At the bottom, online tutoring from university students and generalist platforms runs from roughly AED 33 to 150 an hour, with Tutopiya advertising from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. A qualified subject tutor working online sits between AED 150 and 300, which is where Unitors prices IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Specialist IB, IGCSE and A Level tutors run from AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and the Bestimate rate survey for Dubai putting specialists at AED 200 to 450 or more. A named or examiner-level tutor can reach AED 650, which is BartyED's published figure. In-home visits carry the travel premium: Bestimate puts them at AED 180 to 350, and independent home tutors quote AED 200 to 500.

Two things follow from those numbers. First, the in-home premium buys travel, not teaching: the same qualified tutor costs more because an hour of their day is spent driving, and in the Dubai Hills to Al Barsha corridor at 16:30 that can be most of an hour. Second, hourly rate is a poor comparison unit on its own. A session that includes written notes, marked work between lessons and a plan against your school's deadlines is not the same product as sixty minutes of conversation at the same price.

We do not publish an IB Gram rate card on this page, for the straightforward reason that the right figure depends on level, subject combination and how many weeks are left. The first lesson is free, the plan is written down before anything is paid for, and the quote comes with that plan. Monthly packages visible in this market for context: around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions.

sections.heading: Fitting a session around the Dubai Hills school run, half-terms and Ramadan
paragraphs: The scheduling question decides more tutoring outcomes than the teaching question, and it is the one competitor pages skip entirely. A Dubai Hills Estate DP student whose bus returns from Al Barsha South at 15:50, eats, and has a sibling collected at 16:20 has a genuine window from about 16:40. Push a lesson to 19:30 and you are teaching calculus to a tired sixteen-year-old who still has homework. Put it at 16:40 and you are teaching the same student with two useful hours still ahead of them.

Online delivery is what makes the earlier slot possible, and that is the whole practical case for it in this community rather than any claim about learning styles. Nobody drives from Al Quoz to Dubai Hills at 16:15 and arrives reliably. A video lesson starts when the student sits down. The same logic applies in reverse during the school holidays, when Dubai Hills families travel: a student in London, Mumbai or Amman keeps the same tutor and the same plan, with the slot shifted for the time difference rather than cancelled.

The UAE calendar then imposes its own shape. The academic year runs from late August or early September to late June or early July, with a winter break around the turn of the year and a spring break in the second term. Ramadan compresses the school day and moves the household's evening entirely: lessons that ran at 17:00 work better after Iftar, and many families prefer two shorter sessions to one long one for that month. We shift slots for Ramadan as a matter of course rather than as an exception, and we ask about it in advance instead of waiting for a cancellation.

The last piece is the mock window. Schools in this belt tend to run DP mocks in the term before the examination session, and the fortnight before them is when a weekly hour is worth most. Families who pause tuition during mocks because the week looks busy usually lose the single most useful session of the term.

sections.heading: How lessons are delivered to Dubai Hills Estate, stated plainly
paragraphs: This page targets a phrase parents type, and parents in Dubai Hills Estate type things like home tutor and tutor near me because that is how the question forms in your head. The honest answer is that IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE, and never has; home visits are a service we run only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one and live over video, with a shared whiteboard, the student's own book on camera and recorded notes afterwards.

We would rather make the case than bury it. A Dubai Hills Estate family hiring within driving distance is choosing from the mathematics teachers who happen to live twenty minutes away and have a free evening. Online, the same family is choosing from Analysis and Approaches HL specialists wherever they are, which matters most for the narrow requests: Paper 3 technique, proof by induction, an exploration built on a chi-squared test, or Applications and Interpretation HL, which fewer teachers have actually taught. Specialism beats proximity for exactly the problems a tutor is hired to solve.

There are honest trade-offs and the comparison table names them. A video lesson needs a quiet corner and a charged laptop, which is harder in a shared apartment in Sports City than in a Dubai Hills villa study. Younger children need a parent nearby for the first few sessions. A tutor on screen cannot confiscate a phone. What a video lesson does give you is a visible session you can hear from the next room, written notes you can read, and the ability to change tutor after one lesson without an awkward conversation at your own front door.

On the legal position, which no competitor page explains properly: an individual providing private lessons in the UAE needs a private tuition work permit from MoHRE, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws; the schedule of amounts is not published, so treat any page quoting a specific figure with caution. Abu Dhabi's ADEK rules additionally bar school staff from paid tutoring of students at their own school, and the MoHRE code of conduct carries the same restriction, so 'your child's own teacher, privately' is not a service anyone should be offering you.

sections.heading: KHDA, the Ministry of Education and the paperwork nobody explains
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are licensed and inspected by KHDA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Inspections report on a six-band scale from Outstanding down to Very Weak. A Dubai Hills Estate family comparing two schools across Al Barsha and Al Quoz is usually comparing inspection bands without knowing that the band is a whole-school judgement: a school rated Good can have an Outstanding mathematics department and the reverse is equally possible. Ask about the subject, not just the band.

The emirate's scale explains why this market behaves as it does. Dubai had 387,441 private-school students across 227 private schools offering 17 curricula in 2024-25, with UK curriculum schools accounting for the largest share of enrolment and the International Baccalaureate a much smaller slice. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees for the 2026-27 academic year under Dubai's second economic incentives package, and the 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three IB, creating 16,846 new places. More IB places nearby means more DP1 students arriving from non-IB backgrounds, which is precisely the cohort that needs bridging work in mathematics.

Alongside the licensed curriculum, Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools whatever the international programme, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. This is a real part of a Dubai Hills Estate student's week and it competes with mathematics for revision time, which is worth factoring into a plan rather than discovering in March.

Finally, equivalency. Families planning on a UAE university need Ministry of Education equivalency for the school certificate, and the published requirements differ by curriculum. For the British track, students must show five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. One competitor page states six IGCSE subjects are required, which is wrong. For the IB there is no points threshold we have been able to read on an official source, so we publish none: check moe.gov.ae or the emirate's attestation authority directly. Equivalency is a process you complete with the Ministry, not something a tutoring service performs or influences, and no tutoring is required for it.

process.title: Send the dates, not just the subject
process.description: Tell us the level, the course, the school, and the two dates that matter: the school's exploration deadline and the examination session your child is entered for. Those four facts are enough to say whether we have a specialist free and what an eight-week block should contain.

process.title: A free diagnostic lesson
process.description: Sixty minutes with the tutor who would teach the block, paid for by nobody. The student brings two marked mock papers and any exploration notes. The tutor marks where the losses are by category rather than asking how the student feels about maths.

process.title: A written plan dated backwards
process.description: You receive the plan in writing: which topics, which papers, which weeks, and what the exploration work has to achieve before the school deadline. If the plan concludes that a level conversation with the DP coordinator matters more than tuition, it says so in the first paragraph.

process.title: Weekly lessons with work in between
process.description: A fixed slot on Gulf Standard Time, a short written exercise between sessions, and notes you can read. Every session starts by marking the exercise, which is how a tutor knows whether last week stuck before building on it.

process.description: After school mocks the plan is rewritten against the new paper evidence. Topics that stopped costing marks come off the list. New ones go on. This is also the natural point to stop if the gap has closed, and we will tell you when that has happened.

process.title: Change the tutor, not the plan, if the match misses
process.description: A mathematics specialist who is right for an Applications and Interpretation modelling exploration may be wrong for Analysis and Approaches HL proof work. Say so after one lesson and we move the student to a different tutor and keep the plan. No explanation owed to anyone.

whyPoints.description: Every block starts from your school's dates and the examination session rather than from a generic syllabus sweep. Dubai Hills Estate families consistently find the exploration deadline is nearer than they thought and the mock window is where a term is won or lost.

whyPoints.description: Sometimes the right move is a level change, a conversation with the DP coordinator, or the school's own support sessions, which cost nothing. We say that in the first lesson. A family told the truth in October is a family that comes back in January.

faqs.question: How many weeks before the May session is it too late to start IB maths tutoring in Dubai Hills Estate?
faqs.answer: It is never too late to improve paper technique, but what can change narrows sharply. With twelve weeks or more, topic repair and timed-paper work both fit. With six to eight weeks, choose one: either two or three topics taught properly, or full-paper technique and method recording. With under four weeks, the only realistic work is examination technique, command terms and calculator discipline, which can still be worth several marks a paper. What cannot be rescued late is the exploration, because that deadline is set by the school months earlier and will not move.

faqs.question: My son is in DP2 near Dubai Hills Estate and still has no exploration topic. What should happen this week?
faqs.answer: Topic choice this week, not next. The viable topics are the ones where he can get real data or a real model and apply mathematics at the level of his course. Criterion C rewards personal engagement, which cannot be added later, so the topic should connect to something he actually does. Criterion E carries six of the twenty marks and needs mathematics commensurate with the course, which rules out anything that ends at a mean and a bar chart. Book a single session to test two or three candidate topics against the criteria before he commits to one.

faqs.question: Can an IB maths tutor help with the exploration without writing any part of it?
faqs.answer: Yes, and that is the only version we offer. A tutor can teach mathematics the exploration needs beyond the class syllabus, check whether the aim is answerable, ask the questions a moderator would ask, and give written feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor cannot write, redraft, edit to completion or supply text, data or analysis. Submitting work that is not the student's own is academic malpractice under IB rules and the penalty falls on the student. Any service offering a completed Internal Assessment is selling your child a disciplinary risk.

faqs.question: Should my daughter move from Analysis and Approaches HL to SL, and when is the last sensible moment?
faqs.answer: That decision belongs to your daughter and her DP coordinator, because the school holds the entry and the timetable. What a tutor can contribute is evidence: whether the marks lost are knowledge gaps that a term of teaching closes, or whether the HL calculus and proof content is genuinely out of reach alongside her other five subjects. Make the call early in DP2 rather than after the mocks, because option changes get harder once final entries are submitted. A student scoring consistently at a 3 in HL in January is usually better served by a strong SL grade.

faqs.question: How many IB maths sessions a week does a DP2 student in this part of Dubai usually take?
faqs.answer: One weekly hour is the normal starting point and is enough when the problem is a specific topic or technique. Two sessions a week make sense in two situations: an exploration deadline inside the next month, where one session handles the exploration and the other keeps pace with class content, or the run into mocks, where one session sits a paper and the other marks and repairs it. More than two weekly hours in one subject rarely helps, because the limiting factor becomes the student's own practice time rather than teaching.

faqs.question: What does IB maths tuition cost per hour around Dubai Hills Estate in 2026?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai market figures as of October 2026: budget online platforms from roughly AED 33 to 150, with Tutopiya advertising AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik AED 45 to 65; qualified online subject tutors AED 150 to 300, with Unitors pricing IB from AED 200; IB and IGCSE specialists AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270 and the Bestimate Dubai survey at 200 to 450+; premium named tutors up to AED 650 at BartyED. In-home visits run AED 180 to 500 because the rate carries travel. Those are market rates, not ours; our quote follows the free first lesson and the written plan.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a maths tutor to a villa in Dubai Hills Estate?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one and live over video, with a shared whiteboard, the student's own working on camera and written notes afterwards. The practical gain is specialism: instead of choosing among mathematics teachers who live a short drive from Dubai Hills Estate and have that evening free, you choose an Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation specialist at the exact level your child sits, and the 16:30 slot is actually reachable.

faqs.question: What time can a lesson start if the bus gets back to Dubai Hills Estate at 15:50?
faqs.answer: Most families here settle on 16:30 or 17:00. That leaves time to eat and change, and it finishes early enough that homework still gets done and the student is not working at 21:00. Slots run to about 21:00 on school nights for older students who have co-curricular commitments, and weekend mornings work well for exploration sessions that need a longer unbroken block. During Ramadan the same lesson usually moves to after Iftar. Because delivery is online, none of these times depends on anyone completing a drive through the Al Quoz corridor at rush hour.

faqs.question: For engineering at a UAE university, is Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation the right course?
faqs.answer: Check the specific programme's published entry requirements rather than relying on a general rule, because UAE universities set their own. The broad pattern is that engineering, physics, mathematics and economics degrees commonly expect Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level, because of the calculus and algebra content, while Applications and Interpretation suits business, design, social sciences and health routes. Ask the admissions page of each target university and ask your DP coordinator what the school can timetable, then decide. A tutor can explain the content difference; only the university can tell you what it accepts.

faqs.question: How is Paper 3 different from Paper 1 and Paper 2 at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Paper 3 is sixty minutes long, worth a fifth of the Higher Level grade, and consists of two compulsory extended problems rather than a spread of shorter questions. Each problem builds in stages, so part (c) usually depends on part (b) being right. A calculator is required. The skill it tests is sustaining an unfamiliar argument across twenty or thirty minutes, which is different from recognising a question type. It is also the component schools often reach last, which makes a full timed Paper 3 under examination conditions one of the highest-yield tutoring hours available at HL.

faqs.question: Can lessons shift to after Iftar during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and we ask about it before the month starts rather than waiting for a cancellation. School days compress during Ramadan and the household's evening moves entirely, so a lesson that worked at 17:00 generally works better after Iftar. Many families switch from one long weekly session to two shorter ones for the month, because concentration is better in shorter blocks during fasting. The slot returns to its usual time afterwards. Eid and the spring break are planned around in the same conversation, so the plan absorbs the month instead of losing it.

faqs.question: My child's calculator work keeps losing method marks. Can that be fixed in a term?
faqs.answer: Usually in about three weeks. The cause is almost always the same: on Paper 2 and Paper 3 the graphic display calculator produces the number, the student writes the number, and the method that earned the marks never appears on the page. An examiner can only award what is written. The fix is mechanical, not conceptual: define the variables, write the equation or command being solved, then the result, then the answer in context. Practised on five timed papers it becomes automatic, and it is often worth more marks than any new topic taught in the same three weeks.

faqs.question: Do you follow my child's school scheme of work or the IB subject guide?
faqs.answer: Both, in that order of priority. The school's sequence decides what gets taught when, because a lesson that runs three topics ahead of the class is of little use in Thursday's test. The IB subject guide decides the standard and the assessment objectives, which is what keeps the work aimed at the examination rather than at the test. Where they conflict, the school wins on timing and the subject guide wins on depth. Bring the school's scheme of work and the published internal deadlines to the first lesson and the plan is built around them.

faqs.question: Is a maths tutor needed for Ministry of Education equivalency in the UAE?
faqs.answer: No. Equivalency is an administrative process you complete with the Ministry of Education or your emirate's attestation authority, and no tutoring service performs, influences or speeds it up. Anyone implying otherwise is manufacturing urgency about a regulatory process. For the British track the published requirements are five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one Advanced Level subject at E or two at AS Level. For the IB, verify the requirement on moe.gov.ae directly, because we have found no official source stating a points threshold.

faqs.question: What actually happens in the first three lessons?
faqs.answer: Lesson one is a diagnostic: two marked mock papers are reviewed and each lost mark is sorted into a category, which is knowledge, method recording, command-term misreading, sketching or timing. Lesson two begins the highest-yield category and sets a short written exercise. Lesson three starts by marking that exercise, which is the first real evidence of whether the change is sticking. By the end of lesson three you have a written plan dated back from the examination session and a clear view of whether this tutor is the right match. If not, we change the tutor.

If the honest answer is that tuition is not this term's best spend, we will say so.

intro.heading: What the hour actually costs, and what it buys
paragraphs: Families in the Marina tend to arrive at maths tuition with a number already in their head, usually something another parent mentioned at a school gate in Al Sufouh or over coffee in JBR. The number is rarely wrong. It is incomplete. A rate of AED 180 an hour and a rate of AED 400 an hour both exist in this market, and they are not the same product. One is a graduate with a strong maths degree who has read the subject guide. The other is someone who has marked scripts at this level and can tell you inside twenty minutes whether your child is losing marks on method, on arithmetic, or on reading the command term.

The second thing worth saying early is that the price of maths tuition around Dubai Marina has less and less to do with where the tutor lives. It used to have everything to do with that, because a tutor driving from Mirdif to a tower on Marina Walk charged for the drive whether the invoice said so or not. Published rates for in-home visits in Dubai sit above online rates at every tier, and travel is the main reason. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE, which is an India-only service, so what a Marina family pays covers teaching time rather than a car on Sheikh Zayed Road at six in the evening.

Where the money leaks is more specific than bad tutors. It leaks when a family buys a weekly hour for two years when the student needed a six-week block on sequences, series and binomial expansion before the Year 12 mock. It leaks when nobody checks whether the child sits Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, and three sessions go on calculus that the second course does not assess to that depth. It leaks when the mathematics exploration is left until February of the final year and then needs six emergency hours that one conversation in September would have prevented. And it leaks when a general maths tutor is paid specialist rates for content that is really Year 10 algebra.

A Marina week makes some of this worse. Most schools these households attend finish between 2:45pm and 3:30pm, and the drive back along Al Khail Road or Sheikh Zayed Road at that hour decides everything after it. A lesson booked at 4pm is a lesson the student arrives at hungry and flat. The same hour at 6:30pm or 7:30pm, after food, returns more per dirham, and over video it costs nothing extra to put it there. Households that travel over Eid or spend part of the summer abroad keep the same tutor and the same slot shifted by a few hours.

So the plan this page recommends is unglamorous. Find out which course and which paper pattern your child sits. Decide whether the problem is content, speed under timed conditions, or the exploration. Buy the smallest block that fits that problem, from someone who can name the criterion they are working on. Review at the end of term and cut it if the need has gone. That is a cheaper two years than a standing weekly order nobody re-examines, and it is usually a better grade as well.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-dubai-marina.programmesIntro: Mathematics runs through every IB programme a Marina family is likely to meet, and the spending question is different at each stage. What follows is what each programme assesses in maths and what a household near the Marina typically needs from an hour of paid support at that point.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Maths in the PYP is taught through units of inquiry rather than as a separate timetabled subject with weekly tests. Number, pattern, measurement, shape and data handling all appear, but they appear inside a transdisciplinary theme, which is why a parent can read a PYP report and still not know whether their child can subtract across a boundary. Paid tutoring at this stage is usually a short diagnostic block rather than a standing weekly hour.
programmes.countryNote: Several Marina and Greens families use PYP schools nearby and then move to a British-curriculum school for Year 7. That switch is where paid maths support earns its money: an incoming Year 7 in Dubai is expected to have secure column arithmetic, times tables to twelve and fraction equivalence, and the PYP report will not have told you whether those are in place.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP Mathematics is marked against four criteria, each out of eight, and splits into Standard and Extended routes in Years 4 and 5. Extended is the route that keeps Higher Level open two years later. A student can sit comfortably in the middle of the class on Criterion A knowing and understanding while scoring poorly on Criterion B investigating patterns, and the resulting grade of 5 hides which half is the problem.
programmes.countryNote: For Marina households the Standard-or-Extended decision in MYP Year 4 is the single most expensive fork in the whole journey. Choosing Standard and later wanting Analysis and Approaches Higher Level means buying a bridging block in the summer before Year 12. Asking the maths coordinator in Term 1 of Year 4 costs nothing and routinely saves a term of paid hours.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Every Diploma candidate takes one of two mathematics courses, each available at Standard or Higher Level. Analysis and Approaches is built on algebra, proof and calculus. Applications and Interpretation is built on modelling, statistics and financial maths. Both carry an internally assessed exploration worth 20%. Higher Level adds a third paper of extended problem solving. The four combinations are genuinely different subjects and need genuinely different tutors.
programmes.countryNote: This is where almost all paid maths tuition in the Marina is bought, and where most of it is bought badly. The common error is hiring on reputation rather than on course: a tutor who is excellent on Analysis and Approaches calculus can be mediocre on Applications and Interpretation statistical tests, because the content barely overlaps. Ask which of the four combinations the tutor has taught most recently.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-dubai-marina.subjectsIntro: An IB maths tutor in Dubai Marina is most often asked for one of the four Diploma combinations, but the subjects that lean hardest on mathematics are booked alongside it almost as often. These are the courses our maths-side specialists cover for students in this area.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebra, functions, trigonometry, calculus and proof, with Paper 1 sat without a calculator. Marks go missing on unshown method, on differentiating a quotient under time pressure, and on candidates who can integrate but cannot say what the integral represents in the context the question set.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics, probability distributions and financial mathematics, with a graphic display calculator permitted throughout. The usual failure is treating it as the easier course: the statistical tests and the modelling questions punish anyone who has not practised writing a conclusion in the language of the context.

subjects.name: Mathematics Higher Level Paper 3
subjects.description: Two extended-response questions in one hour, each building across several parts so that an early slip propagates. It rewards stamina and structured working rather than new content, which is why it is best treated as a separate block of timed practice in the final two terms rather than as part of a general weekly hour.

subjects.name: The mathematics exploration
subjects.description: A written investigation of around twelve to twenty pages, assessed on presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics. Supervision means helping a student choose a workable question and read the criteria honestly. The mathematics, the writing and the conclusions stay the student's own.

subjects.name: MYP Mathematics, Standard and Extended
subjects.description: Four criteria out of eight each, converted to a grade from one to seven. Investigating patterns is the criterion that most often drags a Marina student's grade down, because it asks for generalisation and proof of a rule rather than for correct arithmetic, and it is rarely practised at home.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The Diploma subject most often paired with maths tuition, because the algebra of rearranging equations and the calculus in the fields theme are the real obstacle for many students rather than the physics itself. A maths-led session on logarithmic graph linearisation often moves a physics grade faster than more physics.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles, dilution, equilibrium constants and energetics all collapse into proportional reasoning and unit handling. Students who lose marks consistently on calculation questions rarely have a chemistry problem; they have an arithmetic and significant-figures problem that a maths specialist can close in a short block.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Higher Level adds quantitative content that catches Applications and Interpretation students out less than it catches the ones who dropped maths to Standard Level. Elasticity, marginal analysis and diagram-reading all reward a student who is comfortable with gradients and rates of change.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Discrete structures, Boolean logic, complexity and the Higher Level content on abstract data types sit much closer to Analysis and Approaches than to anything else on the timetable. Students who find recursion opaque are usually missing the mathematical idea of a base case rather than the syntax.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The finance and accounts unit is where grades are won and lost, and it is arithmetic: investment appraisal, break-even, working capital and ratio analysis. A student who can set up a payback calculation cleanly picks up marks that a stronger essay writer with weaker numeracy leaves on the table.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-dubai-marina.regionsTitle: Where Marina maths students actually come from
dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-dubai-marina.regionsIntro: Dubai Marina does not sit on its own. The same towers, villas and school buses pull from a ring of communities along Sheikh Zayed Road and Al Khail Road, and the timing and cost of a session changes a little across that ring. These are the areas our Marina-side maths students live in.

regions.name: JBR
regions.note: A five-minute walk from much of the Marina and sharing the same school buses. Families here book the same 6:30pm and 7:30pm slots, and for the same reason: the beach-road traffic between 3pm and 5pm makes anything earlier unreliable.

regions.name: JLT
regions.note: Across the tram line and a different parking proposition entirely. JLT households were the ones who most often paid a visiting tutor for the drive, and they are the quickest to see what moving the hour over video does to the rate.

regions.name: The Greens and The Views
regions.note: Low-rise, short school runs, and within reach of a British-curriculum school on foot for some families. Maths tuition here skews younger: Years 7 to 9 bridging work rather than Diploma exam preparation.

regions.name: Al Sufouh
regions.note: Close enough to the Marina that the same households appear in both, and home to two of the schools these students attend. An Al Sufouh family can often get a 4:30pm slot to work, which is unusual in this cluster.

regions.name: Bluewaters Island
regions.note: One causeway in and out, which does for a visiting tutor's schedule what you would expect. Small student numbers, so a specialist in Applications and Interpretation Higher Level would never be found living on the island.

regions.name: The Springs and The Meadows
regions.note: Villa communities with a strong pull towards the IB school on the Meadows side. Sessions here often start later again, because co-curricular activities at school run to 5pm before anyone gets home.

regions.name: Emirates Hills
regions.note: A longer drive from the Marina than the map suggests once Al Khail Road is involved. Higher Level maths demand here is strong, and the pool of local tutors who can actually teach Paper 3 is not.

regions.name: Al Furjan and Discovery Gardens
regions.note: Newer communities on the far side of the Marina with a growing Year 10 and Year 11 population. Price sensitivity is higher here, which makes the block-versus-weekly decision on this page the most useful part of it.

schoolClusters.city: Schools on the Marina side of Al Khail Road
schoolClusters.note: These are the schools Marina, JBR and Bluewaters households most often name when they ask about maths support. The mix matters for pricing: a British-curriculum school moving into A Level needs different help from an IB continuum school running Analysis and Approaches from Year 12.

schoolClusters.city: Schools reached inland from the Marina
schoolClusters.note: The second ring, reached along Al Khail Road or Hessa Street. Pick-up times here are later and co-curricular programmes run longer, which is why the evening slots fill first and why an in-home tutor serving this ring is quoting for an hour of driving before any teaching happens.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-dubai-marina.modesIntro: Three ways of buying maths support, priced by what the problem actually is. The point of separating them is that the weekly standing order is the right purchase far less often than it is the one families default to.

modes.title: A six-week block on one named topic
modes.description: The cheapest useful purchase in this market. You name the topic, the tutor runs a diagnostic in lesson one, teaches for four, and tests under timed conditions in the sixth. Sequences and series, trigonometric identities, integration by substitution and hypothesis testing are the four blocks Marina students buy most.
bullets: Six hours, with an end date written down before you start
A timed past-paper section at the end, marked against the real scheme
No commitment past the sixth lesson

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one through the exam year
modes.description: Appropriate when the gap is broad rather than topical, or when the student needs the external deadline that a standing appointment creates. Worth re-examining every term rather than renewing by default, because the commonest waste in the Marina is a weekly hour that outlived the problem it was bought for.
bullets: One fixed slot, usually 6:30pm or 7:30pm Gulf Standard Time
A written note of what was covered after each lesson
A term-end review that may recommend reducing or stopping

modes.title: Exploration supervision across a term
modes.description: Spread thin on purpose: a session to choose a question, one to check the mathematics is deep enough to score on use of mathematics, one on structure, one on reflection, and a last read before the school's internal deadline. The student writes it. The tutor reads criteria and asks awkward questions.
bullets: Four to six sessions spread over a full term, not a rescue week
Criteria read out loud with the student, not summarised for them
Every word and every calculation stays the student's own

sections.heading: What maths tuition costs around Dubai Marina, tier by tier
paragraphs: Market rates for maths tuition in Dubai run from roughly AED 45 an hour at the bottom to AED 650 at the top, and the spread is not noise. Each band buys something different. The table below collects figures each provider published on its own site, recorded in October 2026, so you can see which part of the market a quote belongs to before you accept or refuse it. These are market rates and not an IB Gram price list; our own figure comes with the consultation, after the free first lesson.

The band that matters for most Diploma families is AED 200 to 450. Below it you are usually buying general maths help from someone who has not taught the course, which can be the right purchase for a Year 8 arithmetic gap and is the wrong one for Paper 3. Above it you are paying scarcity pricing. The premium tier is real and sometimes worth it in the last two terms of Higher Level, but a family paying it from Year 12 Term 1 is spending at the top of the market for work a mid-band specialist does equally well.

One figure in the table deserves separating out. In-home visits are quoted from around AED 180 to 500 an hour, and the gap between that and the equivalent online band is the drive. A tutor coming into a Marina tower spends time on Sheikh Zayed Road, then on parking, then in a lift. Nobody itemises it, but every family in this neighbourhood is paying for it somewhere in the rate. Monthly packages seen in this market run around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits, which tells you the same story in a different unit.

sections.heading: The four places maths money leaks in a Marina household
paragraphs: The first leak is buying a subject instead of a problem. A parent who books maths tuition has usually diagnosed the symptom, a grade of 4 where a 6 was expected, and left the diagnosis there. Maths at this level fails in at least four distinguishable ways: missing prior content, correct method executed too slowly, correct work presented in a way the mark scheme cannot reward, and an exploration drifting without a question. Each needs a different number of hours and in two of the four cases the right answer is fewer hours, not more.

The second leak is the wrong course. Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation share a name and little else at the margins where grades are decided. A tutor who has spent five years on algebraic proof and calculus can be genuinely weak on chi-squared tests and on writing a conclusion about a correlation coefficient. Families pay specialist rates for sessions that drift into content the student's course does not assess, which feels like progress and shows up nowhere in the final grade.

The third leak is timing, and it is the most expensive. An exploration started in September needs four or five calm sessions. The same exploration opened six weeks before the school's internal deadline needs ten anxious ones, and produces a weaker piece of work. The fourth leak is the standing order nobody cancels: a weekly hour booked in Year 11 for a genuine gap, still running in Year 13 after the gap closed, now functioning as supervised homework at AED 300 an hour. Review at the end of every term and the fourth leak closes itself.
bullets: Diagnose which of the four failure modes applies before booking a single hour
Confirm the exact course and level in writing: AA SL, AA HL, AI SL or AI HL
Open the exploration conversation in September of the final year, not February
Put a review date in the calendar at the same time as the first lesson

sections.heading: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation: the choice that sets your bill
paragraphs: Most of the money a Marina family will spend on Diploma maths is determined by a decision made in Year 11, often in a ten-minute conversation about which course looks easier. It is not a question of difficulty. It is a question of which kind of mathematics the student can sustain for two years and which prerequisite their intended degree expects. Engineering and physics courses at competitive universities commonly ask for Analysis and Approaches Higher Level. Business, design and several life-science routes accept Applications and Interpretation. Checking the prerequisite before the choice is free; correcting it afterwards is not.

The tutoring consequence is sharper than the academic one. Because Paper 1 of Analysis and Approaches is sat without a calculator, that course rewards drilled algebraic fluency in a way nothing else on the Diploma timetable does, and fluency is built by volume of short practice rather than by long explanatory lessons. Applications and Interpretation allows a graphic display calculator on every paper, which moves the difficulty from manipulation to interpretation: knowing which test to run, and writing what the output means in the context of the question.

That is why the same weekly hour produces different value on the two courses. An Analysis and Approaches student often does better with two short sessions a week than one long one. An Applications and Interpretation student usually needs the longer session, because a modelling question cannot be set up, solved and written up in twenty minutes. Ask a prospective tutor which of the four combinations they taught most recently and what they would do differently between them. The answer separates a specialist from a generalist faster than any qualification on a profile.
