sections.heading: How these sessions run, what they cost in this market, and what we will not claim
paragraphs: Lessons are one-to-one on live video, scheduled to Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; visiting tutors are a service we run only in India. For on-screen preparation specifically, the online format has an unusual advantage: the student works on their own keyboard, in their own browser, typing into a timed document while the tutor watches the response appear. That is closer to the real examination than any in-person session at a kitchen table with a notebook.

On price, the published Dubai market as we read it in October 2026: EdFlik advertises online tuition from AED 45 to 65 per hour and Tutopiya from roughly AED 33 to 52 at the budget end. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB tuition from AED 200. TutorChase lists AED 270 per hour for specialist IB support. Bestimate's Dubai survey puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 and specialist exam-year help at AED 200 to 450 and above, with BartyED at AED 650 for premium named tutors. Those are other providers' published figures with their reading date, not IB Gram prices. We publish structure and a free first lesson rather than a fixed hourly rate, because the right tutor for an interdisciplinary paper and the right tutor for extended mathematics are different people.

What we will not claim: no regulator or examination board endorses us. KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai, per the UAE government's own information service, and that is a fact about KHDA rather than a credential of ours. We hold no permit, accreditation or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. We publish no predicted grades and no success statistics. Private tutors in the UAE need the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, and tutoring without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so we quote none.

process.title: Confirm what your child is actually entered for
process.description: Before anything else, get three answers from the school in writing: does it register candidates, is it for the certificate or individual results, and which subject groups. We will ask for those in the first conversation because preparation for an on-screen paper and preparation for a moderated portfolio have almost nothing in common.

process.title: Free 45-minute first lesson
process.description: One lesson at no cost with no card details taken. For an on-screen subject it includes a short timed response, marked aloud against the criterion descriptors, so the diagnosis comes from the student's own writing rather than from a conversation about how they feel in tests.

process.title: Diagnose from a marked mock, not a worry
process.description: Where there is time, we would rather a family paid for one properly marked two-hour mock than four hours of general revision. Front-loaded timing, command-term blindness and the interdisciplinary error are invisible without a script and obvious with one.

process.title: Match on the subject group and the paper
process.description: Delivery is online for every UAE family, so matching is about who has taught this subject group at this level rather than who lives nearby. The interdisciplinary paper in particular needs someone comfortable across two disciplines, which is a smaller pool than any single Dubai community contains.

process.title: Timed practice every session, marked together
process.description: Twenty to thirty minutes of each hour is spent answering under conditions on the student's own keyboard, and the rest marking it against the descriptors. Students who only write untimed answers get better at writing untimed answers, which is not what May asks for.

process.title: Stop at the session, or bridge into DP1
process.description: Preparation ends when the session does. There is no rolling commitment and no automatic renewal. For students continuing into the Diploma we offer a short bridge block in the summer, including handwriting stamina, which catches out candidates who have typed for two years.

whyPoints.title: We ask what your child is entered for first
whyPoints.description: Many Dubai schools do not use eAssessment at all, and others register for individual results rather than the certificate. Establishing that takes one email and saves families from buying preparation for a format their child will never sit. No provider should start selling before that answer exists.

whyPoints.title: Timed answers in every session
whyPoints.description: The format is the difficulty. A student who has only ever written at their own pace, with time to redraft, meets two hours and unseen stimulus material for the first time in a room they cannot leave. Practice on their own keyboard, marked against descriptors, is the only thing that reliably changes that.

whyPoints.title: Command terms isolated and drilled
whyPoints.description: Analyse, evaluate, explain and justify demand different answer shapes, and marks follow the shape. We take ten minutes a session, one term, and the same stimulus answered two ways so the student feels the difference rather than reading a definition of it.

whyPoints.title: ePortfolio help that stays outside the portfolio

That survives moderation and it teaches something that lasts beyond one submission.

whyPoints.title: Honest about availability and about limits

faqs.question: What exactly is an on-screen examination, and how is it different from a paper my child writes by hand?
faqs.answer: It is two hours at a computer in a secure examination application, with the stimulus material embedded in the paper: short video, audio, images, data tables, text extracts, some of it interactive. The candidate reads or watches, then types responses into fields on the same screen. The practical differences are navigation, which quietly consumes minutes, and typing speed, which limits how much of their thinking a candidate can actually get down. There is no content list to memorise, because the material is provided and the marks are for what the candidate does with it.

faqs.question: How do I find out whether my child's Dubai school even registers candidates for eAssessment?
faqs.answer: Ask the MYP coordinator three things in one email: does the school register candidates, is it for the full certificate or individual subject results, and which subject groups will my child be entered in. eAssessment is optional for schools and a substantial number of Dubai schools do not use it, moving students onto Cambridge or Pearson International GCSE for Years 10 and 11 instead. Until those answers exist, nobody can tell you what preparation is useful, and a tutoring provider who starts selling before asking should be treated carefully.

faqs.question: Which subjects are examined on screen and which are submitted as a portfolio?
faqs.answer: Broadly, language and literature, individuals and societies, sciences, mathematics and the interdisciplinary paper are examined on screen, while language acquisition, arts, design and physical and health education are submitted as ePortfolios marked by the school and moderated externally by the IB. Your child's exact entry pattern depends on the options chosen in Year 10, so confirm it with the coordinator. The split matters because on-screen subjects respond to six weeks of timed technique, whereas portfolio subjects are decided by work done months earlier.

faqs.question: My son's mock on-screen paper came back much lower than his coursework grades - why?
faqs.answer: Almost always timing and judgement rather than knowledge. Coursework rewards a student who can produce careful work over weeks with redrafting; an on-screen paper rewards someone who can reach a defensible judgement about unseen material in a fixed number of minutes. The three errors that produce exactly this gap are summarising sources instead of evaluating them, spending thirty minutes on the first task, and answering a command term with the wrong answer shape. All three are visible in a marked script and all three are habits, which means they respond quickly.

faqs.question: Is there any point revising content for an examination where the material is provided?
faqs.answer: Much less than families assume, and this is the single most liberating thing to tell a stressed MYP 5 student. Because stimulus material is supplied, the paper cannot test recall of a content list. What it tests is the ability to read a source critically, apply subject thinking to it, and write to the shape the command term demands. Time spent memorising definitions in the spring term is largely wasted; time spent producing timed responses and marking them against the criterion descriptors is not.

faqs.question: How much does a typing problem really matter in a two-hour paper?
faqs.answer: More than parents expect and less than students fear. No criterion gives credit for an argument that was in the candidate's head when the clock stopped, so a slow typist writes a shorter answer than their thinking deserves. The fix is outside sessions and cheap: fifteen minutes of daily typing practice across six weeks moves most fifteen-year-olds from hunting for keys to adequate fluency. We check it in the first session by timing a short response, because it is a constraint worth knowing about in January rather than discovering in May.

faqs.question: What is the interdisciplinary paper, and why do candidates find it the hardest?
faqs.answer: It presents material drawn from two disciplines and asks for a response that genuinely integrates both. Candidates lose marks by writing two separate subject answers and placing them back to back, which reads like diligence and satisfies no integration descriptor. It is also the paper schools have the least practice material for, so it tends to be under-prepared relative to its weight in the certificate arithmetic. Two or three sessions on integration technique is usually all it takes, and the gain is disproportionate to the time.

faqs.question: Can a tutor work on my daughter's design ePortfolio before it is submitted?
faqs.answer: We will not, and we would be cautious about anyone who offers to. The portfolio is coursework: the student's own work, marked by the school's teachers and then moderated externally by the IB. What we do instead is teach the skill on a parallel example. If the gap is evaluating against a specification, we take a completely different brief, read the criterion descriptor and work an evaluation through on that, and your daughter then applies it to her own portfolio alone. That version survives moderation and actually teaches something durable.

faqs.question: When does the session happen, and can you tell me the results date?
faqs.answer: UAE schools sit the session in May, at the end of MYP 5. We deliberately do not publish a specific examination or results date, because ibo.org blocks automated checking and an unverified date on a tutoring page is worse than no date at all. Your school's MYP coordinator holds the live timetable and the internal deadlines, and the internal deadlines are what actually govern your family's calendar: portfolio submission, the project report, and the school's own mock schedule.

faqs.question: What does the MYP certificate require, and is my child's Diploma place at risk without it?
faqs.answer: The certificate needs validated results across the required subject groups including the interdisciplinary paper, plus the personal project and satisfactory completion of service as action, with both a minimum total and a minimum grade per required result set by the IB. Confirm the current figures with your coordinator rather than any tutoring site. A shortfall is less serious than families fear: subject results still stand, the school still reports grades, and entry to the Diploma at a Dubai school is a school admissions decision, not an IB entitlement.

faqs.question: My child joined the programme in Year 10 - can they still be entered?
faqs.answer: It depends on how much course evidence exists, and it is a question for the school rather than for us. On-screen subjects are less affected, because the paper assesses what the candidate can do with unseen material rather than a record of coursework. The moderated portfolio subjects are the constraint: a student who arrived in Year 10 may not have enough course work banked in language acquisition or arts for a portfolio to be submitted. Ask the coordinator before enrolment if the certificate matters to your family.

faqs.question: How many weeks of preparation does one on-screen subject actually need?
faqs.answer: For a student who already performs reasonably in the subject, six to eight weekly sessions with timed practice in each is usually enough to fix the habits that cost marks. Front-loaded timing goes in one session plus a mock. Command-term shape takes two. Evaluation rather than summary takes three or four. Beyond that the returns fall away quickly, because the remaining variable is subject understanding built across two years rather than anything a spring block can supply. Spreading a small budget across four subjects is the common mistake.

faqs.question: Do Ramadan timings disrupt the last stretch of preparation before May?
faqs.answer: They change it rather than disrupt it. School days shorten, family evenings shift, and in some years the period overlaps the clearest run of on-screen practice before the session. The workable pattern in Dubai is to move sessions to post-Iftar slots, which many of our families prefer anyway because the student is more alert, and to plan it in September rather than negotiating it in week two. Independent typing and timing practice is easier to sustain through a shortened day than new teaching is.

faqs.question: Should my child stay in the programme for Years 10 and 11 or move to International GCSE?
faqs.answer: It depends on what happens after sixteen rather than on which assessment is harder. A student continuing into the IB Diploma at the same Dubai school usually gains from staying: criteria, command terms and integrated thinking carry straight over. A student likely to move to a British-curriculum school, to A Levels, or to a country expecting subject certificates at sixteen often gains from International GCSE, partly because UAE Ministry of Education equivalency rules for the British track are written in GCSE and A Level terms.

faqs.question: How does this preparation differ from the IGCSE tutoring my older child had?
faqs.answer: Substantially. International GCSE preparation is syllabus-led: a published specification with a code, a bank of past papers, mark schemes and predictable question types. On-screen MYP preparation has none of that, because the paper is criterion-referenced against material nobody has seen. So there is nothing to work through in the conventional sense. Sessions are built from the criterion descriptors, the command terms and timed responses to varied stimulus, and progress is judged on marked scripts rather than on past-paper percentages.

faqs.question: What happens if no tutor with the right subject-group experience is free?
faqs.answer: We tell you, rather than putting a generalist in the slot and letting you discover the mismatch. The interdisciplinary paper and extended mathematics are the two areas where the pool is smallest, and for those it sometimes means a short wait or a tutor based outside the UAE working to Gulf Standard Time. Because every lesson for UAE families is one-to-one live video, availability is a question of subject match and timetable rather than driving distance from your community.

dubai/ib-myp-eassessment-tutor.closingHeading: Start with one email to the coordinator
dubai/ib-myp-eassessment-tutor.closingBody: Before you buy anything, ask your child's MYP coordinator whether the school registers candidates, whether it is for the certificate or individual results, and which subject groups your child is entered in. Those three answers decide what preparation means. Then take the free 45-minute first lesson: for an on-screen subject it includes a short timed response marked aloud against the criterion descriptors, so the diagnosis comes from your child's own writing. No card details are taken. Lessons run one-to-one on live video across the UAE, timed to Gulf Standard Time, on the keyboard your child will actually use.

dubai/ib-myp-extended-mathematics-home-t.tutorsIntro: These tutors teach extended content in the order it has to be learned: index laws and factorisation before algebraic fractions, right-angled work before the sine and cosine rules, and generalisation before justification. Each checks the prerequisite before teaching the topic you asked for.

intro.heading: Extended failures are almost never about ability
paragraphs: A Dubai parent with an able child in an extended set and a report that says 4 is looking at one of three things, and none of them is a ceiling on what the child can do. The first is sequencing: a topic was taught on top of a prerequisite that had never been secured, so the new work had nowhere to attach. The second is pace: the extended scheme makes one pass over most topics, so an absence turns into a permanent hole rather than a temporary lag. The third is criterion B, where the extended route's harder patterns demand a justification the student has never been shown how to write.

Each of those has a different fix and they are easy to tell apart from marked work. Sequencing failures look like confident method with wrong manipulation: the student knows what to do with an algebraic fraction and cannot factorise the denominator. Pace failures are topic-shaped: everything fine except one unit, and the unit coincides with a fortnight away. Criterion B failures are structural: patterns found, rules written, nothing justified, and the mark stuck at 4 or 5 however good the algebra is.

What the extended route actually adds is a defined list rather than a general difficulty. Harder factorisation, including non-unit coefficients and completing the square. Algebraic fractions. Function notation and the transformations of graphs. Non-right-angled trigonometry, with the sine and cosine rules and work in three dimensions. More demanding generalisation, including quadratic and non-linear patterns and reasoning that edges towards proof. Those five groups are where a Dubai extended-set student needs teaching, and everything else on the course is shared with the standard route.

Now the search term. Families type home tutor because that is how one-to-one help is described, and the market answer is worth giving straight: visiting tutors in this city publish hourly figures of roughly AED 180 to AED 350 according to the Bestimate rate survey, with individual listings to AED 500. IB Gram does not arrange home visits in Dubai; home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. Lessons for UAE families are delivered one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, with the student writing on a shared whiteboard.

On an extended brief that delivery choice has a concrete advantage beyond the obvious. The thing that separates a useful extended session from a wasted one is whether the tutor checks the prerequisite before teaching the requested topic, and that habit belongs to people who have taught the sequence many times. In a city where a visiting tutor is selected from whoever can reach your community before the evening closes, the selection is made on geography. Video makes it on experience, which on this route is the whole game.

The page that follows is therefore about the mathematics and the order of it. The extended additions, topic by topic. The dependency chain, written out so you can diagnose at home. Where extended students lose marks standard students do not. Criterion B at extended depth. Three-dimensional trigonometry and the diagram habit. The collision between the extended pace and the Personal Project year. What a session can fix, and what needs a conversation with the school instead.

dubai/ib-myp-extended-mathematics-home-t.programmesIntro: Extended mathematics only makes sense in relation to what comes after it, because the whole point of the additional content is a later course. Here are the stages, with what each assumes.

programmes.name: Middle Years extended mathematics
programmes.ageRange: Ages 14-16 · MYP 4 and MYP 5 in most Dubai schools
programmes.description: The same four branches and the same four criteria as the standard route, plus additional algebra, function work and trigonometry, taught at a faster pace with a single pass over most topics. Assessment is unchanged: knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts, each marked 0 to 8. The additional content is not harder to understand in isolation; it is harder to survive because it is sequenced tightly and never revisited.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools set extended groups at different points and movement between routes varies by school rather than by programme rule. Ask the department three questions: when placement is reviewed, what evidence is used, and whether a student may move down mid-year without losing the criterion marks already banked.

programmes.name: Analysis and Approaches, higher level
programmes.description: The course the extended route is built for. It assumes fluent algebraic manipulation, confident function work and comfort with formal reasoning, and it extends them into calculus, proof and series. Students who arrive with the five extended topic groups secure find the first term demanding rather than impossible. Students who arrive having passed extended assessments on partially understood algebra find the term brutal, because calculus exposes manipulation weaknesses immediately.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the practical test of readiness is not the extended grade but the criterion B mark alongside it. A student with a strong knowing-and-understanding mark and a weak investigating-patterns mark has been rewarded for computation, and higher-level Analysis and Approaches is where that profile stops working. Ask for an honest read before the Diploma choices are filed.

programmes.name: Applications and Interpretation
programmes.description: The modelling, statistics and technology course, which the standard route feeds and which an extended-route student can of course take. It rewards the criterion D skills the extended course also develops: model selection, interpretation in context and evaluation of validity. A student whose extended strength is modelling rather than algebra is often better served here, and the Middle Years criterion profile usually says which.
programmes.countryNote: Worth checking against target university courses while your child is in Year 10. Some UAE and overseas engineering and economics programmes specify a route or a level, and reading two published requirements takes ten minutes and settles two years of planning.

programmes.name: International GCSE additional mathematics
programmes.description: Where a Dubai school leaves the programme at Year 10, the closest equivalent of extended work is an additional mathematics qualification alongside the main one, examined by timed papers. An extended-route transfer student usually has the content and lacks the pace, so the retraining is about marks per minute, question triage and knowing when to leave a question rather than about new mathematics.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge examines International GCSE in June and November series and allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, warning that the correct zone timetable must be used and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong version. Get the zone timetable from your school's examinations officer.

dubai/ib-myp-extended-mathematics-home-t.subjectsIntro: Extended briefs should name the topic and, ideally, the prerequisite. These are the areas Dubai extended-set families bring, with what the content demands and the dependency underneath it.

subjects.name: Index laws and surd handling
subjects.description: Rarely the reason a parent calls and frequently the reason the called-about topic failed. Negative and fractional indices, and exact-form answers, sit under factorisation, function work and trigonometric manipulation. A student who computes indices on a calculator rather than reasoning about them will stall in algebraic fractions without either of you knowing why.

subjects.name: Harder factorisation
subjects.description: Non-unit coefficients, difference of two squares in disguise, grouping, and recognising when nothing factorises. The load-bearing topic of the whole extended route: algebraic fractions, quadratic solving and function behaviour all rest on it. Most apparent algebraic-fraction weakness is factorisation weakness wearing a different hat.

subjects.name: Completing the square and the discriminant
subjects.description: Turning points, maximum and minimum values, and the number of roots. Taught as a procedure in many schemes and assessed as a connection to graph behaviour, which is where marks are lost. The test of understanding is whether a student can read a discriminant and sketch without computing roots.

subjects.name: Algebraic fractions
subjects.description: Simplifying, adding and subtracting with algebraic denominators, and solving equations containing them. Hard to self-teach because textbook examples are chosen to factorise neatly. Errors are nearly always in the factorisation or in cancelling across an addition, which is the single most common extended algebra mistake we see in Dubai marked work.

subjects.name: Function notation and transformations
subjects.description: Reading function notation, substituting into it, and translating, reflecting and stretching graphs. Procedural rules are easy to memorise and useless without a model of what the notation means. The diagnostic question is whether a student can predict the effect of an unfamiliar transformation in words before touching a calculator.

subjects.name: Sine and cosine rules
subjects.description: Non-right-angled triangles, the area formula with sine, and the ambiguous case. The judgement of which rule to use is the skill; the arithmetic is not. Students who were never fully secure in right-angled trigonometry struggle here for a reason that has nothing to do with the new content.

subjects.name: Three-dimensional trigonometry
subjects.description: Angles between lines and planes, diagonals of solids, and extracting a two-dimensional triangle from a three-dimensional picture. The whole topic turns on drawing the extracted triangle separately, labelled. Students who work on the original diagram lose marks they could have earned, and the habit is teachable in one session.

subjects.name: Quadratic and non-linear generalisation
subjects.description: Second differences, non-linear growth, and patterns where the rule is not immediately polynomial. The extended route's criterion B tasks are genuinely harder than the standard route's, so the justification step carries more weight and more marks, and it is the most common place an able extended student is capped.

subjects.name: Model selection and rejection
subjects.description: Extended modelling tasks often admit more than one defensible model, and the marks sit in explaining why one was chosen and another rejected. Students trained to produce an answer find this uncomfortable, because it requires committing to a judgement in writing and defending it.

subjects.name: Exact answers and rounding discipline
subjects.description: Working in exact form until the final step, then rounding appropriately for the context and saying so. Extended tasks penalise premature rounding more than standard ones because answers are chained through several steps. A short habit block fixes it and recovers marks across every topic simultaneously.

modes.title: Prerequisite-first topic work

This is the format most extended families should buy and the one least often offered, because checking the prerequisite risks telling a parent the brief was wrong.

sections.heading: What the extended route adds, topic by topic
paragraphs: Extended mathematics is not a different subject and it does not carry a different grade scale. It is the same four branches, the same four criteria and the same conversion to a grade from 1 to 7. The additional content is a finite, nameable list, and knowing the list changes what a family buys, because it separates the topics that genuinely need a specialist from the ones shared with the standard route and available at the qualified band.

The five groups are harder factorisation including completing the square and the discriminant; algebraic fractions; function notation and graph transformations; non-right-angled trigonometry including three-dimensional work; and more demanding generalisation at criterion B. Everything else your child meets in an extended set is standard-route content taught faster. That distinction is useful in a first conversation with a prospective tutor, because a brief that names one of the five groups tests whether the tutor knows the sequence.

Each addition exists for a later purpose, and that purpose is worth knowing. Completing the square exists so that quadratic behaviour can be read rather than computed. Algebraic fractions exist so that rational functions are manageable at Diploma level. Function notation exists so that transformations and composition are available in calculus. The sine and cosine rules exist because real geometry is not right-angled. Students taught the reason remember the procedure; students taught only the procedure forget it over a summer.

The table lists the additions against what the standard route does in the same slot. Use it to decide which parts of your child's difficulty need a specialist and which do not, and to recognise when a tutor is teaching standard content at an extended price.

sections.heading: The dependency chain: why the topic you asked about is not the problem
paragraphs: Extended mathematics is more tightly sequenced than anything else in the Middle Years framework, and that produces a diagnostic rule a parent can apply without a tutor. If a student is failing a topic while clearly knowing what the topic is for, the failure is almost always one level down. The student who cannot simplify an algebraic fraction usually knows exactly what to do and cannot factorise the denominator. The student who cannot handle a transformation usually knows the rule and cannot read the function notation it is written in.

The chain runs roughly like this. Index laws and surds sit under factorisation. Factorisation sits under algebraic fractions, under completing the square, and under solving quadratics. Function notation sits under transformations and under anything involving composition. Right-angled trigonometry sits under the sine and cosine rules, which sit under three-dimensional work. Arithmetic with negatives and fractions sits under all of it, which is why an able Year 10 student with a Year 7 fraction gap can look like a mystery.

You can test this at home in ten minutes with four questions: simplify an expression with a negative index; factorise a quadratic with a non-unit coefficient; evaluate a function at a given value using notation; and find a missing side in a right-angled triangle, giving an exact answer. A student who stumbles on any of those should not be having a session on algebraic fractions next week, and a tutor who teaches one anyway is being paid to build on sand.

This is also the reason extended sessions should be booked by topic with the prerequisite named rather than by the month. A block that begins with a prerequisite check is one or two sessions longer and several sessions cheaper overall. The table sets out the chain so you can look up what to test before you buy.

sections.heading: Where extended students lose marks that standard students do not
paragraphs: Three losses are specific to the extended route, and none of them is about knowing less. The first is at the top of criterion A. An extended task's final part is set in a genuinely unfamiliar context with harder content behind it, so the gap between the practised version and the assessed version is wider than on the standard route. Students who have only ever met the practised version leave it blank, and on the extended route that blank costs more because the upper bands are where extended students are expected to live.

The second is criterion B justification. Extended patterns are quadratic or non-linear, which means the general rule is harder to state and much harder to justify. A student can reach a correct quadratic rule, verify it on two further cases and still sit mid-band because no reason was offered for why the structure of the problem produces that rule. On the standard route the rule itself is often enough to reach a decent mark; on the extended route it is not.

The third is rounding and exact form. Extended answers are chained through more steps, so premature rounding propagates and the final answer is marked wrong despite correct reasoning throughout. Worse, the student cannot see the error, because every individual line looks right. This is the cheapest of the three to fix and the one most often ignored, since it reads as carelessness rather than as a habit nobody taught.

The table maps the four criteria at extended depth to the characteristic loss and the fix. Read it next to marked work rather than instead of it: the pattern in a teacher's comments will usually match one row, and that row is the plan.

sections.heading: Criterion B at extended depth: from second differences to a reason
paragraphs: Pattern work on the extended route starts where the standard route finishes. A constant second difference signals a quadratic rule, and building that rule is mechanical once a student has done it a dozen times. The extended difficulty sits in the two steps after it. Verification means testing the rule on cases outside the table, which requires generating terms from a rule rather than a rule from terms, and students who have only practised one direction cannot do it. Justification means explaining why the structure of the problem produces that rule, and almost nobody is taught how.

Justification at Middle Years level is not formal proof, and saying so relieves a great deal of anxiety. If the pattern counts the squares on the surface of a growing cube arrangement, the justification explains why each new layer contributes what it contributes, in words tied to the picture. If the pattern is the number of handshakes in a growing group, it explains why each new person adds the number already present. Three worked examples across different structures, with the student writing each one, is usually enough for a fourth to appear unaided.

Extended tasks also include patterns whose rule is not polynomial at all, and here the useful teaching is diagnostic: how to tell from the data whether to look for a constant difference, a constant second difference or a constant ratio. Students who only know the difference-table method try it on exponential growth, find no constant difference, and conclude the task is impossible. Ten minutes on the ratio test prevents an entire wasted investigation.

None of this is content the student is missing. It is method nobody showed them, which is why a bounded block beats a term of general support here. It is also the single highest-value purchase on the extended route, because criterion B carries the widest mark range in the subject and is where able extended students are most often capped at 5.

sections.heading: Three-dimensional trigonometry and the diagram habit
paragraphs: Three-dimensional trigonometry is where extended students most often decide that they are bad at mathematics, and the decision is almost always wrong. The content is two topics they already hold: Pythagoras and the trigonometric ratios. The difficulty is entirely in extracting the right two-dimensional triangle from a three-dimensional picture, and that is a drawing habit rather than a mathematical one.

The habit is specific. Redraw the triangle you are working in, separately, at a sensible size, with every known length and angle labelled on it. Mark the right angle if there is one, and name the vertices consistently with the original solid. Students who work directly on the printed three-dimensional diagram cannot see which length is the hypotenuse of which triangle, make an error that looks arithmetical, and lose marks a redrawn sketch would have secured.

The second habit is working in stages and keeping exact values. A typical question requires a base diagonal before the angle to a vertex, and a rounded base diagonal corrupts the final angle. Writing the intermediate length in exact form, carrying it, and rounding only at the end is the difference between a correct answer and one that is wrong by a degree, which a marker treats as wrong.

Both habits are teachable in one or two sessions, which makes this topic a good example of why session estimates belong in a quote. Families arrive expecting three-dimensional trigonometry to need a long course. It needs a drawing discipline, a rounding discipline, and a dozen problems worked with the student holding the pen while someone watches which triangle they extract.

sections.heading: The year the extended set collides with the Personal Project
paragraphs: In most Dubai schools the Personal Project runs through MYP 5, the same year the extended mathematics course is at its most demanding and, in schools that enter candidates, the year of the end-of-programme examination. The collision is real and predictable, and families who plan for it lose nothing while families who do not lose a term of mathematics momentum. The project consumes evenings in bursts around its own internal deadlines, which rarely align with the mathematics assessment calendar.

The practical answer is to front-load. Extended algebra content that arrives early in MYP 5 should be secured while there is capacity, because an extended scheme makes one pass and the project weeks are the weeks a student will miss consolidation. Where a mathematics block and a project deadline fall together, the block moves rather than the deadline, and we would rather reschedule than run a session a student cannot attend to.

On the project itself, the boundary is identical to the one on any assessed task. The Personal Project is the student's own work, marked against its own criteria, and a tutor's role in relation to it is nil beyond helping a student manage time. We do not advise on project content, supply material for it, or review drafts of it, because that work must be the student's and the supervision belongs to the school's supervisor. Saying so plainly matters in a market where some providers are less careful.

One scheduling note specific to Dubai: the mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies stream runs alongside all of this, with the Knowledge and Human Development Authority requiring separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in several of those subjects and instructional time calculated against a 40-minute lesson unit. An MYP 5 student therefore carries eight subject groups, the mandatory stream and the project. One protected mathematics slot a week is realistic; two is not, whatever is promised in September.

sections.heading: What a session can fix, and what needs the school instead
paragraphs: Tutoring has a boundary of usefulness and extended-route families deserve to know where it sits. A session can teach a topic, test and repair a prerequisite, install a habit such as redrawing a triangle or holding exact form, coach the process of an investigation, and rehearse examination conditions. Those are real and measurable. What a session cannot do is change a set placement, alter a scheme of work, recover a term of missed content in a fortnight, or make a tired student less tired.

Three situations belong with the school rather than with us, and we say so in the trial lesson. The first is a placement that looks wrong: a student whose criterion B marks are consistently low in an extended set may be better served on the standard route, and that conversation is with the department, not a purchase. The second is a class-wide difficulty, where the whole set found a unit hard; waiting a fortnight for the class to revisit it costs nothing. The third is a timetable problem rather than a mathematics problem, which is common in MYP 5.

Where the right answer is a conversation with the school, the evidence file helps. A sequence of dated marked tasks with the criterion written on each is a far better basis for a departmental meeting than a general worry, and it is yours to take. We write session notes so they can be handed over without translation, and nothing in them predicts a grade, because predictions are not evidence.

The measure we commit to instead is specific: what should appear on the next school-marked task if the block worked, or what a cold re-test should show. For extended work that is usually a mixed set attempted without prompts, a justified rule verified beyond the given cases, or a three-dimensional problem with the extracted triangle drawn and labelled. If it does not appear, the plan was wrong and the next conversation starts there.

sections.heading: Ramadan, travel and a set that does not wait
paragraphs: Two features of the Dubai year interact badly with an extended scheme of work, and both are manageable with notice. The first is Ramadan, when school days shorten, timetables compress and evening energy moves to after Iftar. Families here routinely shift sessions to a post-Iftar slot for the month, and the sensible mathematics plan is to front-load new extended content into the weeks before and keep the month for consolidation, habit work and rounding discipline, which are lower-energy tasks that still earn marks.

The second is travel. Dubai families travel more than most, and an extended set does not pause for it. Two weeks away in the middle of an algebraic-fractions unit is a specific missing topic, not a general lag, and it will be assumed by every unit that follows. The practical protocol is simple: before travelling, ask the department which topics and assessments the set will cover; on returning, book a short block scoped to exactly that list. Done within a fortnight it stays small.

Where a trip is long or a relocation is involved, the honest conversation is about route rather than catch-up. A student who misses a third of a year of extended content may be better placed on the standard route for the remainder, with a bridging plan later if higher-level Diploma mathematics is still the aim. That is a school conversation we will support with evidence and will not pretend to solve with sessions.

The smaller, recurring version of the problem is worth naming too: a student who misses single lessons repeatedly across a year does not look absent, they look weak. Nothing identifies that except an attendance pattern laid next to a criterion profile, which is one more reason the evidence file is dated. An able extended student sitting at a flat 4 with scattered absences is usually an attendance story misread as an ability story.

sections.heading: How lessons are delivered, and the claims we will not make
paragraphs: Delivery is online, one-to-one, over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with a shared whiteboard the student writes on and a recording the family keeps. IB Gram does not arrange home visits in Dubai; home tutoring is a service we offer only in India, which is true of every emirate rather than a restriction on this page. Published visiting-tutor figures in this city are AED 180 to AED 350 an hour from the Bestimate rate survey, with individual listings to AED 500, quoted here as market context for a service we do not sell.

The argument for video on an extended brief is the prerequisite habit. The tutor who checks index laws before teaching algebraic fractions is someone who has taught the sequence often enough to know what fails, and that person is selected from the whole pool rather than from your community. A shared whiteboard also lets a tutor watch which triangle a student extracts from a three-dimensional diagram, in real time, in a second colour, which is precisely the moment the teaching happens.

On assessed work the boundary is explicit and stated to the student in the first session. A tutor teaches, explains descriptors, asks the questions a marker would ask, annotates completed work and coaches process. A tutor does not supply a conjecture, a general rule, a justification or any sentence that reaches a submission, and has no role in the Personal Project beyond time management. Every assessed word is the student's own. This market contains providers who sell finished internal assessments, and a student who buys one risks a malpractice finding that no grade is worth.

What we will not claim: approval, accreditation, licensing or partnership from any regulator, examination board, school or school group, because IB Gram holds none; a UAE office, because there is not one; examiner status for individuals whose current status cannot be evidenced; any grade outcome; or any statistic about our own students without the sample size, date and method on the same page. Private tutors in the UAE need the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation private tuition work permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, and those without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, with no fine schedule published.

process.title: Name the topic and the suspected prerequisite
process.description: Algebraic fractions, functions, the sine and cosine rules, three-dimensional trigonometry or criterion B justification, plus anything underneath it you already doubt. Four home questions on indices, factorisation, function notation and right-angled work will tell you more than a placement test.

process.title: Send marked work, including the unit that went wrong
process.description: Three recent extended tasks with the teacher's comments and the task-specific clarification sheets. If an absence coincided with a unit, say which dates, and ask the department which topics and assessments the set covered then.

process.title: Free 45-minute trial, one per family
process.description: The specialist tests the prerequisite live before agreeing to teach the topic, which occasionally changes the brief. You get a session estimate, a dependency order and a stated test of success. No card details are taken, and if the honest answer is a conversation with the school, that is what you will hear.

process.title: Work in dependency order, in a protected slot
process.description: Prerequisite first where needed, then the topic, in one weekly time the household can actually hold through assessment weeks and project deadlines. In MYP 5 that is one slot rather than two, whatever the September calendar suggests.

process.title: Re-test cold, then re-decide
process.description: Blocks end with a mixed set attempted without prompts, a justified rule verified beyond the given cases, or a three-dimensional problem with the triangle redrawn and labelled. Then you decide on the next block with the Diploma destination in view rather than by default.

whyPoints.title: The prerequisite is tested before the topic is taught
whyPoints.description: Most extended failures are one level down from where they appear: factorisation under algebraic fractions, function notation under transformations, right-angled work under the sine rule. Checking first adds a session or two and saves more, and it is the step most arrangements skip.

whyPoints.title: Justification taught as a method, not as an attitude
whyPoints.description: Criterion B at extended depth caps able students because nobody shows them what a justification is. Three worked justifications across different structures, with the student writing each, usually produces a fourth unaided. That is where the widest mark range in the subject sits.

whyPoints.title: Habits that recover marks across every topic
whyPoints.description: Holding exact form through chained working, and redrawing the extracted triangle from a three-dimensional diagram. Both are one-session habits and both recover marks the student had already earned mathematically, which makes them the cheapest work on the route.

whyPoints.title: Absence handled as a scoped list
whyPoints.description: An extended scheme makes one pass, so missed content is a specific list rather than a general lag. We scope it from what the department says the set covered, cover exactly that in order, then check what later units assumed.

whyPoints.title: Honest about where tutoring stops
whyPoints.description: A session cannot change a set placement, alter a scheme of work or make a tired MYP 5 student less tired. Where the right answer is a departmental conversation, we say so and hand you a dated file of marked work to take into it.

whyPoints.title: A stated boundary on assessed work
whyPoints.description: The student writes every assessed word, and we have no role in the Personal Project beyond time management. Said aloud in the first session with the parent present, because the alternative risks a malpractice finding worse than any mark.

faqs.question: My daughter is in the extended set and cannot do algebraic fractions. Where do we start?
faqs.answer: With factorisation, almost certainly. Algebraic fraction work rests on factorising denominators confidently, including quadratics with non-unit coefficients, and textbook examples are chosen to factorise neatly, which hides the dependency. The tell in marked work is a correct plan with a wrong denominator: she knows exactly what to do and cannot get the expression into a form where she can do it. Test it at home by asking her to factorise a quadratic whose leading coefficient is not one. If that is shaky, teaching the fractions first wastes two sessions.

faqs.question: What exactly does the extended route add that the standard route does not have?
faqs.answer: Five groups. Harder factorisation, including completing the square and the discriminant. Algebraic fractions. Function notation and graph transformations. Non-right-angled trigonometry, with the sine and cosine rules and three-dimensional work. And more demanding generalisation at criterion B, including quadratic and non-linear patterns. Everything else in an extended set is standard-route content taught at a faster pace. Knowing the list is useful commercially as well as educationally: it tells you which parts of a difficulty genuinely need a specialist and which are available at the ordinary qualified rate.

faqs.question: Why does my able son keep scoring 5 on investigating patterns?
faqs.answer: Because he is almost certainly stopping at a verified rule without justifying it. On the standard route a correct general rule often reaches a decent mark; on the extended route, where patterns are quadratic or non-linear, the upper bands require a reason tied to the structure of the problem. Justification at this level is not formal proof: if the pattern counts layers on a growing solid, it explains why each layer adds what it adds. Three worked justifications across different structures, with him writing each one, usually produces a fourth unaided.

faqs.question: How do I test at home whether the prerequisites are secure?
faqs.answer: Four questions, ten minutes, no calculator for the first three. Simplify an expression containing a negative index. Factorise a quadratic with a leading coefficient other than one. Evaluate a function at a given value using function notation, then say what the notation means. Find a missing side in a right-angled triangle and leave the answer in exact form. A stumble on any of them means the next session should not be on algebraic fractions or transformations. This is the test we run in the trial lesson, and parents can run it first.

faqs.question: Is three-dimensional trigonometry as hard as it looks?
faqs.answer: The content is Pythagoras and the trigonometric ratios, both of which your child already holds. The difficulty is extracting the right two-dimensional triangle from a three-dimensional picture, which is a drawing habit rather than a mathematical one. Redraw the triangle separately, at a sensible size, with every known length and angle labelled and the right angle marked. Then work in stages, keeping intermediate lengths in exact form, because a rounded base diagonal corrupts the final angle. One or two sessions installs both habits for good.

faqs.question: Why are correct answers being marked wrong on his extended work?
faqs.answer: Usually premature rounding. Extended answers are chained through more steps than standard ones, so a value rounded at step two propagates and the final answer sits outside the acceptable range while every individual line looks right. The student cannot see the error, which is why it recurs. The fix is a short rounding-discipline block: work in exact form until the final line, then round appropriately for the context and state the degree of accuracy. It recovers marks across every topic at once and takes a session or two.

faqs.question: Can a tutor come to our home in Dubai for extended maths?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. Home tutoring is a service we run only in India, and UAE lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. The market answer is that visiting tutors here publish AED 180 to AED 350 an hour according to the Bestimate rate survey, with individual listings to AED 500. For an extended brief we would argue for video on a specific ground: the tutor who checks index laws before teaching algebraic fractions is selected from the whole pool rather than from whoever can reach your community before the evening closes.

faqs.question: Should my son move down to the standard route?
faqs.answer: That is a conversation with the department rather than a purchase, and the evidence that matters is the criterion profile rather than the overall grade. A student with consistently low investigating-patterns marks in an extended set may do better on the standard route and can still reach higher-level Diploma mathematics later with a bridging plan. Ask the school three questions: when placement is reviewed, what evidence is used, and whether marks already banked travel with him. We will provide a dated file of marked work to take into that meeting and no opinion dressed up as a prediction.

faqs.question: How do we handle two weeks of travel in the middle of a unit?
faqs.answer: Ask the department, before you go, which topics and assessments the set will cover, then book a short block on exactly that list within a fortnight of returning. An extended scheme makes one pass, so missed content is a specific gap that every later unit will assume rather than a general lag you can catch up gradually. Handled promptly it is three to five sessions. Left until the next reporting point it becomes a diffuse problem across several topics, and the first two sessions are then spent working out what was missed.

faqs.question: Does the Personal Project year make extended maths harder?
faqs.answer: It makes it more crowded, which amounts to the same thing if nobody plans for it. In most Dubai schools the Personal Project runs through MYP 5 alongside the most demanding extended content and, where the school enters candidates, the end-of-programme examination. Project deadlines rarely align with the mathematics calendar, so the sensible move is to front-load extended algebra while there is capacity and to move a maths block rather than a project deadline. We have no role in the project itself beyond helping a student manage time.

faqs.question: How should an extended maths plan be adjusted for Ramadan in a Dubai school?
faqs.answer: Yes, and most Dubai families do. School days shorten, timetables compress and evening energy shifts, so a post-Iftar slot is usually the honest option for the month. The mathematics plan should shift with it: front-load new extended content into the weeks before and use the month for consolidation, rounding discipline and habit work, which still earn marks and demand less. Booking that change in advance rather than improvising week by week is the difference between losing the month and using it.

faqs.question: What makes a tutor good at extended work specifically?
faqs.answer: One habit: checking the prerequisite before teaching the topic you asked about. Ask a prospective tutor what they would test before teaching algebraic fractions, and listen for factorisation and indices. Ask how they would move a student from a correct second difference to a justified quadratic rule, and listen for a method rather than reassurance. Qualifications matter less than sequence knowledge on this route, because extended content is tightly ordered and teaching it out of order produces sessions that feel productive and marks that do not move.

faqs.question: Does my child need a graphing calculator for extended maths?
faqs.answer: Ask the school which device is permitted in assessments, then practise on that one. Students who learn a method on a phone application frequently cannot reproduce it on the calculator they are handed in the room, and the loss is in time rather than understanding. For extended work the functions that matter are exact-form display, the statistics menu and graph windows. Where the school collects tasks digitally, the equation editor matters just as much, since typeset notation is a separate skill and mangled fractions cost communication marks.

faqs.question: What should the next marked task show if a block has worked?
faqs.answer: Something specific, agreed in advance. For an algebra block, a mixed set attempted without prompts, including the questions that need factorising first. For criterion B work, an investigation reaching a justified rule verified on cases beyond the table. For three-dimensional trigonometry, the extracted triangle redrawn and labelled with exact intermediate values. For rounding discipline, exact form held to the final line. If none of that appears, the plan was wrong and we would rather say so at the checkpoint than keep selling sessions.

faqs.question: Is it too late to start if the final year has already begun?
faqs.answer: No, but the plan changes shape. In the final year the useful work is retrieval and habits rather than new content: holding exact form, redrawing diagrams, writing justifications and model-rejection paragraphs, and rehearsing timed conditions where the school enters candidates for the end-of-programme examination. Those produce marks quickly. What a late start cannot do is rebuild a year of missed algebra in a term, and any provider implying otherwise is selling hope. The trial lesson will say which of the two situations you are in.

intro.heading: The extended premium is a supply problem, and it is quantifiable
paragraphs: Families in Dubai are often quoted more for extended-route Middle Years mathematics than for standard, and told vaguely that it is harder. That is the wrong explanation. The hour is not harder to deliver; the number of people who can deliver it well is smaller. A tutor who can teach number, ratio and right-angled trigonometry to a Year 9 class is easy to find at AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, which is the published band for qualified online subject tutors in this market. A tutor fluent in algebraic fractions, function transformations, non-right-angled trigonometry and formal generalisation, who also reads criterion descriptors confidently, sits in the specialist band of AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with one named provider publishing AED 650.

Those figures belong to the providers and rate surveys that published them and were read in October 2026. Visiting tutors in Dubai are published at AED 180 to AED 350 an hour by the Bestimate rate survey, with individual listings reaching AED 500, and monthly in-home packages advertised at AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour sessions. We publish no price list of our own on these pages. What we do is quote against a named topic after a free trial lesson, with a session estimate attached, so that the quantity is visible as well as the rate.

The quantity is where extended-route families overspend. Extended sets move faster and consolidate less, which produces a very particular cost pattern: nothing for months, then a sudden need for catch-up after two weeks of travel or illness, because the scheme of work met the topic once and did not return. A family that understands this buys in short, targeted bursts. A family that does not buys a weekly slot in October as insurance and pays for thirty sessions to cover work that needed eight.

Second, extended-route spending has a tail. The route exists to prepare students for higher-level Diploma mathematics, and the Diploma years are the most expensive stage of the whole continuum because the specialist pool is thinner again and the exploration carries assessment weight. A two-year budget that stops at the end of MYP 5 is not a budget; it is the first half of one. This page prices both halves, because a family deciding in Year 10 whether to stay on the extended route deserves the real number.

The Dubai backdrop is favourable for once. The Knowledge and Human Development Authority confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in the emirate would not increase for 2026-27, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total, and the emirate added seven new private schools and 16,846 places for the same intake. A frozen fee line plus new capacity means the pressure on a family's education budget this year is demand-side rather than cost-side, and tutoring is usually where the freed money goes.

What follows: why the specialist band exists and what it buys, the arithmetic of a missed fortnight in an extended set, per-topic session estimates, the two-year picture through to higher level, how exam sessions move the market twice a year, whether sharing a tutor works, and what the Ministry of Education equivalency process does and does not require you to buy. Lessons themselves are online, one-to-one, over live video; IB Gram does not arrange home visits in Dubai, and home tutoring is a service we offer only in India.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme, extended mathematics

The spending driver is pace: content is met once, assessed, and not revisited, so the cost of absence is higher than on any other route in the continuum.

Ask the department when movement between routes is possible, because a student placed up and then struggling on criterion B is a common and avoidable expense in this city.

programmes.name: Diploma Analysis and Approaches, higher level
programmes.description: The destination the extended route is built for, and the most expensive tutoring stage in the continuum. Published specialist bands in this market run from AED 200 to AED 450 and above for International Baccalaureate work, and higher-level work sits at the top of that range because fewer tutors teach it confidently. The internal assessment is a single mathematical exploration written entirely by the student, which means supervision is coaching rather than content delivery and is bought in bounded blocks.

Read two target courses in Year 10 while the extended decision is live, because the cost of continuing on extended is only justified if the Diploma route actually requires it.

programmes.description: The alternative Diploma course, and the reason some extended-route families are overspending. A student who completes extended mathematics and then takes Applications and Interpretation has paid for two years of additional algebra and trigonometry the Diploma course does not require. That is a legitimate choice if the student wanted the stretch, and an expensive accident if nobody checked the destination.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the route conversation often happens informally, in a corridor, in Year 11. Buying a single diagnostic session at the end of Year 10 to ask whether extended is still the right route for the intended Diploma course is the cheapest decision in this whole budget.

programmes.name: International GCSE, where a school switches
programmes.description: Some Dubai schools leave the programme at Year 10, and an extended-route student transferring into International GCSE mathematics is typically over-prepared on content and under-prepared on pace. The cost shape changes from blocks against task deadlines to a sustained run of timed past-paper practice, which is more predictable to budget and usually cheaper per mark gained.

dubai/ib-myp-extended-mathematics-tutor.subjectsIntro: Extended briefs are priced by topic, because the topics differ sharply in how hard they are to find a tutor for and how many sessions they take. These are the requests we see from Dubai families, with honest session estimates.

subjects.name: Algebraic fractions
subjects.description: Simplifying, adding and solving with algebraic denominators. Four to six sessions for most students, because the obstacle is usually incomplete factorisation rather than the fractions themselves. Hard to self-teach from a textbook, which is why it appears in the specialist band rather than the qualified one.

subjects.name: Function notation and transformations
subjects.description: Reading and using function notation, composite ideas, and translating, stretching and reflecting graphs. Three to five sessions. The usual failure is procedural confidence with no mental model of what the notation means, which shows up later as an inability to interpret a transformation in context.

subjects.name: Non-right-angled trigonometry
subjects.description: Sine and cosine rules, area with the sine formula, and problems in three dimensions. Three to four sessions when the right-angled work is secure, and considerably more when it is not, which is the single most common reason an extended-route quote comes in higher than expected.

subjects.name: Harder factorisation and quadratics
subjects.description: Non-unit coefficients, completing the square, the discriminant and the link to graph behaviour. Four to six sessions. This is the load-bearing topic for higher-level Diploma mathematics, so it is the one where a cheap generalist is poor value even though the content looks routine.

subjects.name: Formal generalisation and justification
subjects.description: Quadratic and non-linear patterns, proof-adjacent reasoning, and justification tied to the structure of a problem. Four to six sessions and the highest-value purchase on the extended route, because criterion B carries the widest mark range and extended patterns are harder to justify than standard ones.

subjects.name: Extended modelling tasks
subjects.description: Model selection and evaluation where more than one model is defensible. Two to four sessions. Extended tasks reward a student who can say why a linear model was rejected in favour of a quadratic one, which is a different skill from computing either.

subjects.name: Pace recovery after absence
subjects.description: The characteristic extended-route purchase. Two weeks missed in an extended set is typically three to five sessions of catch-up, because the scheme of work met the topic once and moved on. Booked promptly it stays at that; left until the next assessment it compounds into something larger.

subjects.name: Set-placement second opinion
subjects.levels: End of MYP 4 or during MYP 5
subjects.description: One session. A specialist reads the four criterion marks and recent tasks and says whether the extended set is the right place for this student and what it would cost in weekly hours to make it comfortable. Families who buy this before committing to a year of weekly support frequently save most of it.

subjects.name: Bridging into higher-level Diploma mathematics
subjects.description: Fifteen to twenty sessions across a summer, covering the specific gaps between extended Middle Years work and higher-level Analysis and Approaches. Budget it deliberately: the same work bought in the first term of Year 12 competes with five other Diploma subjects and costs more in every sense.

subjects.name: Technology for extended work
subjects.description: One or two sessions on the permitted graphing calculator and the school's graphing software, focused on window choice, intersections and reading values accurately. Low cost and disproportionate return, since a default screenshot with unlabelled axes loses communication marks on an otherwise strong modelling task.

sections.heading: Why the specialist band exists, and what the extended premium buys
paragraphs: The published bands in this market are not arbitrary. Budget online platforms advertise from AED 33 to AED 65 an hour, qualified online subject tutors from AED 150 to AED 300, and subject specialists from AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with one named provider at AED 650 and visiting tutors at AED 180 to AED 350 per the Bestimate rate survey. The bands separate by supply. Teaching ratio and right-angled trigonometry to a Year 8 class is a widely held skill. Teaching algebraic fractions, function transformations and formal justification to a Year 10 extended set is not.

For an extended brief that scarcity has a practical consequence a parent can test. Ask a prospective tutor to explain, in two minutes, how they would get a student from a correct second-difference calculation to a justified quadratic rule. The answer separates the bands faster than any qualification list. A tutor who answers with a method is worth the specialist rate; one who answers with reassurance is being paid a specialist rate for qualified-band work.

What the premium should buy is threefold: recognition, so that the diagnosis happens in the first session rather than the fourth; sequencing, so that algebraic fractions are not attempted before factorisation is secure; and honesty about hours, so that you are given an estimate rather than a subscription. None of those are functions of where the tutor lives, which is why removing the travel radius matters more on this route than on any other.

The table sets out what we can actually cover, how long matching takes, and what we do if the right specialist is not free. No competitor in the researched set discloses a coverage limit, and several conceal non-UAE delivery behind a local-looking contact number. Publishing the limit is more useful to you than pretending it does not exist.

sections.heading: The arithmetic of a missed fortnight in an extended set
paragraphs: Every tutoring market talks about falling behind. On the extended route the phrase has a measurable meaning, because the scheme of work is built on the assumption that a topic met once is a topic learned. A standard set returns to proportional reasoning several times a year. An extended set teaches algebraic fractions in a three-week unit, assesses it, and does not come back. A student absent for two of those three weeks has not fallen behind in general; they are missing one specific, load-bearing topic that everything after it quietly assumes.

This produces a cost pattern that surprises families. Nothing is needed for months, and then the need is sharp, specific and urgent. Handled promptly it is three to five sessions on one topic, which is a bounded, affordable purchase. Left until the next reporting point it becomes a diffuse problem across several topics, because the subsequent units were built on the missing one, and the diffuse version takes twice as long to diagnose and considerably longer to fix.

The practical move is to treat absence as a trigger rather than an inconvenience. On returning from travel, ask the department one question: which topics did the set cover and which assessments were set while my child was away. That one email, answered in a line, scopes the catch-up precisely. Without it a tutor spends the first two sessions finding out what was missed, which is the family paying specialist rates for reconnaissance.

The table puts numbers on it. The session figures are what we see in practice on extended briefs in this city, not a formula, and the final column is the part most families do not anticipate: the delay before the hole becomes visible on a report, which is exactly why it gets left.

sections.heading: What each extended topic actually costs in sessions
paragraphs: A rate without a quantity is not a price, and extended-route families are quoted rates far more often than quantities. The honest way to buy this work is topic by topic with an estimate attached, because extended content is naturally block-shaped. Algebraic fractions take four to six sessions for most students, and the obstacle is nearly always incomplete factorisation rather than fractions, which means the sequencing matters: attempting the fractions first wastes two sessions.

Function notation and transformations run three to five sessions. Non-right-angled trigonometry runs three to four when the right-angled work is secure and considerably more when it is not, which is the commonest reason an extended quote arrives higher than the parent expected. Harder factorisation and quadratic work, including completing the square and the discriminant, runs four to six and is the single most load-bearing purchase for anyone heading to higher-level Diploma mathematics.

Criterion B justification at extended depth is four to six sessions and the highest-value block on the route, because that criterion carries the widest mark range and extended patterns are harder to justify than standard ones. Extended modelling, where more than one model is defensible, runs two to four. Add them up and the full extended-route need for a student with no inherited gaps is roughly twenty to thirty sessions across two years, not a hundred.

The table gives the estimates with what should prove the block landed. Treat the ranges as planning figures rather than promises: a student with shaky underlying algebra will need the groundwork first, and an honest tutor tells you that at the trial lesson rather than discovering it at session four.

sections.heading: The two-year number: extended route plus a higher-level Diploma year
paragraphs: A budget that stops at the end of MYP 5 is half a budget. The extended route exists to prepare a student for higher-level Diploma mathematics, and the Diploma years are where the real money sits. Published specialist bands for International Baccalaureate work in this market run from AED 200 to AED 450 and above, and higher-level work sits towards the top because fewer tutors teach it with confidence. A family making the extended decision in Year 10 should have the four-year picture, not the one-term quote.

The shape, in sessions: extended Middle Years support for a student without inherited gaps is roughly twenty to thirty sessions across MYP 4 and MYP 5, bought as blocks. The bridging summer, if it is needed, is fifteen to twenty. A Diploma year with weekly support is twenty-eight to thirty-two sessions, and exploration coaching is a bounded block of four to six on top. Nobody needs all of that, and a student with secure algebra may need a third of it, but those are the units the arithmetic is built from.

This is also why the single most valuable purchase on this page is a diagnostic session at the end of Year 10. If the intended Diploma course is Applications and Interpretation, two further years of extended content is stretch rather than requirement, and the money is better spent elsewhere. If it is higher-level Analysis and Approaches, the extended route is the cheaper path and the bridging summer may be unnecessary. One session answers a question worth many.

The checkpoint discipline matters more as the sums get larger. Every block we quote carries a stated measure: what should appear on the next school-marked task, or what a cold re-test should show. A plan without a measure has no natural end, which is how a family ends up four years into continuous tutoring without ever having decided to be.

sections.heading: Exam sessions move this market twice a year
paragraphs: Tutoring demand in Dubai is not flat, and extended-route families feel the peaks because the specialist pool is small. Two surges dominate. The first builds from January towards the spring examination window and the internal deadlines that precede it. The second is a shorter autumn surge tied to the November board series and to first-term reporting. In both, the 5pm to 7pm Gulf Standard Time slots go first, and the narrower the specialism the earlier they go.

Booking against a deadline rather than a calendar month is therefore both cheaper and more effective. A criterion B block three weeks before a submission does the actual work of building justification. The same block four days out can tidy a draft, which is a worse outcome for more money, since late work displaces other commitments and the market prices that. The task sheet almost always arrives earlier than parents notice it, so the discipline is to diarise the deadline on the day it appears.

Board dates are published by the boards and should be read there. Cambridge runs International GCSE, O Level and International A Level in June and November series, with Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, and allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones whose timetable version must be used correctly. For the March 2027 series, Cambridge lists an exam period of 3 February to 4 March 2027, final entries due 27 November 2026, forecast grades due 27 February 2027 and results on Direct from 13 May. Pearson examines International GCSE in May or June and November, with the November 2026 final timetable running to 19 November 2026, and publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series.

On International Baccalaureate dates, this project publishes none. The organisation's site returns an error to automated requests, so no session or results date here has been confirmed from the board itself. Treat the May session as the one Dubai schools sit, get the exact windows from your school's coordinator, and be sceptical of any tutoring page that prints an IB examination date without naming where it came from.
