A tutor interrogates the question; the student writes it

sections.heading: Source work: origin, purpose, value, limitation
paragraphs: Criterion D asks students to analyse and evaluate a range of sources or data in terms of origin and purpose, recognising value and limitations. Four words, and they are the whole of what separates a middling humanities student from a strong one in the MYP. The usual first attempt summarises what the source says and then asserts that it is reliable or biased. Neither summary nor assertion earns the strand, because neither is an evaluation.

Origin is who produced the document, when, and in what circumstances. Purpose is why: to persuade, to record, to sell, to justify, to inform a particular audience. Value follows from those two and must be stated as a consequence: because this was written by a participant shortly afterwards, it gives direct access to how the decision was understood at the time. Limitation follows the same way: because the author was defending their own conduct, the account of the alternatives considered is likely to be incomplete.

Written like that, the evaluation does work. The word because is the hinge, and teaching students to require it of themselves is the single most efficient intervention available in this subject group. It takes two or three sessions and it moves criterion D by a mark or two across every unit that follows, which is why it is worth doing early rather than in the weeks before a Year 5 deadline.

Data sources need the same treatment, and students find this harder because a graph looks neutral. Who collected these figures, how, over what period, with what definitions, and who commissioned the collection. A development indicator reported by a government and the same indicator estimated by an external body are different sources with different limitations, and a student who can say why is doing exactly what criterion D asks. Practise on unfamiliar documents rather than ones the class has already discussed, because the strand is about transfer.
bullets: Summary is not evaluation, and reliable or biased is an assertion not an argument
Value and limitation must be written as consequences, using because

Practise on unfamiliar documents, because the strand is about transfer

sections.heading: UAE Social Studies, Moral Education and the MYP course: three separate things
paragraphs: Every private school in Dubai teaches Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral studies alongside whatever international curriculum it is licensed for, and this is where families most often become confused about what their child is actually being graded on. These mandatory subjects are set by the Ministry of Education, required by KHDA, reported separately, and are not part of the MYP Individuals and Societies course. A low Social Studies mark and a low Individuals and Societies criterion mark are different problems with different answers.

The requirements are specific and public. KHDA's mandatory-subject guidelines state that schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, and Arabic is the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students, while non-Arab students take Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies in the school's licensed-curriculum language.

Two further details matter for anyone arranging support. Instructional time for these subjects is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit; schools may vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and KHDA advises that any mandatory subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes. And the guidelines state that the use of any different or additional content, without prior permission from the Ministry of Education, is strictly prohibited. That is a real constraint on tutoring: legitimate support for UAE Social Studies works from the school's own materials and on study skills, not from substituted content.

There is also a federal baseline worth knowing. UAE government guidance states that private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. KHDA regulates private education in Dubai; Abu Dhabi and Al Ain fall under ADEK, Sharjah under the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah under its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah under the federal Ministry. IB Gram holds no approval from any of them and claims none.

sections.heading: Command terms and the shape of a humanities answer
paragraphs: MYP tasks are written with command terms, and in Individuals and Societies the terms do more work than in any other subject group, because the content rarely tells a student what structure to use. Identify, outline, describe, explain, analyse, compare, discuss, evaluate, justify and to what extent all appear, and each demands a different shape. A student who writes the same essay for discuss and for explain will be marked down on one of them without ever being told why.

The crucial boundary in this subject group is between explain and discuss. Explain wants causes and mechanisms, organised and supported: why the migration happened, why the price changed, why the policy produced that outcome. Discuss wants a balanced review in which more than one position is considered and the student reaches a judgement. A beautifully argued one-sided answer to a discuss question is capped, and the student usually believes they wrote a strong response, because they did write a strong response to a different question.

Evaluate and to what extent sit higher still. Both require a judgement and both require the limitations of the evidence to be acknowledged. To what extent in particular invites a graded answer, largely or only in part, rather than a yes or a no, and students who commit to an absolute position lose the strand even when their reasoning is sound. Compare and contrast have their own trap: a paragraph about one case followed by a paragraph about the other is not a comparison, because nothing is held side by side.

The teaching here is mechanical and quick. Take a question the student has already answered, identify the command term, write the shape the term requires as a short plan, and have them re-answer it from the plan. Twenty minutes, one question, and the structure sticks because they can see the difference between their own two versions. Repeated across three or four terms it is worth more marks than any amount of additional content.
bullets: Explain wants causes and mechanisms; discuss wants more than one position weighed
A one-sided answer to a discuss question is capped, however well written

sections.heading: From the MYP into Diploma humanities
paragraphs: At the end of MYP Year 5 the subject group splits into named Diploma courses, and the choice is consequential in a way MYP unit selection never is. History, Geography, Economics, Business Management, Global Politics, Psychology and Digital Society all draw on the same four MYP criteria in different proportions. A student whose criterion D marks were strong and whose criterion A marks were ordinary is usually better suited to History or Global Politics, where argument carries the paper. A student with the reverse profile often does better in Geography or Business Management, where structured content and applied method count for more.

What the Diploma assumes, in all of them, is the criterion B skill set: a student who can frame a question, plan an investigation, record sources and evaluate their own process. Every Diploma humanities subject has an internally assessed component that is, in effect, a longer and stricter MYP investigation. The students who struggle in Year 12 are rarely the ones with content gaps; they are the ones who have never independently framed a question and are being asked to do it for marks that count externally.

There is a second thing worth saying plainly, because this market frequently implies otherwise. No tutoring arrangement can promise a university place, and no particular humanities subject guarantees an admission outcome. Entry requirements differ by country, by institution and by programme, and the only reliable source is the admissions page of the specific university. Students in the UAE whose qualifications need Ministry of Education equivalency should check the requirements on the Ministry's own channels rather than relying on any provider's summary.

The useful work in MYP Year 5 therefore has a clear shape. Close the criterion B and D gaps while the stakes are still internal. Write two investigations properly, start to finish, including the evaluation of the process. Get fluent with the command-term distinctions, because Diploma papers apply them far more strictly. A student who arrives in Year 12 able to frame a question and weigh a source has bought themselves two much easier years, whichever subject they choose.
bullets: Diploma humanities subjects weight the same four MYP skills differently
Every Diploma humanities course assumes criterion B independence
No subject choice or tutoring arrangement can promise an admission outcome

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not touch in an MYP investigation
paragraphs: This subject group is assessed largely through work produced outside the classroom, which makes the academic-honesty boundary more than a formality. IB rules require the work to be the student's own. A tutoring arrangement that crosses that line does not help a Dubai student; it puts their MYP record at risk and leaves them without the skill the task was designed to build. It is worth stating in detail, because the UAE search results for IB support include providers openly selling finished coursework.

Legitimate help is substantial. Teaching the content of a unit. Explaining what a criterion strand means in plain words. Marking a draft and identifying exactly where it falls short. Modelling source evaluation on a document the student is not using. Asking the questions that make a student notice their own missing counter-argument. Teaching a referencing convention and checking a bibliography for completeness and internal consistency. Coaching the planning and reflection behind a Personal Project. All of that leaves authorship untouched.

Illegitimate help is equally clear. Supplying the research question. Choosing and reading the sources on the student's behalf. Providing sentences or paragraphs to be inserted. Restructuring a draft so thoroughly that the voice changes. Writing the evaluation of the process. None of these should ever be offered, and a provider who offers them is selling a risk rather than a service. The test a parent can apply without reading the subject guide is the same one that works everywhere: ask your child to explain any paragraph and why it is there.

Materials follow the same logic. Official IB, Cambridge and Pearson documents are copyright and should reach a student through their school or the board's own site, not through a tutor's file share. For UAE Social Studies the constraint is tighter still, since KHDA's guidelines state that different or additional content requires prior permission from the Ministry of Education. Sessions built on the school's own task briefs, the student's own drafts and published criterion descriptors are both legitimate and more useful, because that is the material being marked.
bullets: A tutor teaches, marks, questions and models; the student writes
The research question must be the student's own, or everything built on it is compromised
No supplied sentences, no restructuring until the voice changes

process.title: Name the discipline, not just the subject group
process.description: Send the current unit's statement of inquiry or task brief. Either names whether this is history, geography, economics, business or civics, which decides who should teach the sessions. Asking for a tutor for Individuals and Societies without that detail is how a capable tutor ends up being the wrong one.

process.title: Send two marked tasks with their criterion sheets
process.description: The criterion sheets tell us which of the four criteria is costing marks and which strand inside it. Two tasks are usually enough. A description of the problem is far less diagnostic than one annotated script, and reading them beforehand means the first session is teaching rather than questions.

process.title: Free trial lesson with the discipline-matched tutor
process.description: One free trial per student, taught by the tutor who would continue, with no card details taken and no obligation. It is a working session on the current task, ending with one small piece of work set. If the discipline match is wrong, a different tutor is proposed at no cost.

process.title: Start with the research question if one is live
process.description: When an investigation is underway, the question comes first regardless of what else looks weak. Everything downstream, the plan, the sources, the argument and the evaluation, inherits the question's faults. Fixing it late means rebuilding work the student has already done.

process.title: Weekly sessions, one small marked task between each
process.description: A single short piece of work set at the end of every session, marked against the named strand and returned with annotations before the next lesson. Small enough to come back: one source evaluation, one paragraph, one action plan. A task that does not come back costs the next session its purpose.

process.title: Switch discipline when the school does
process.description: When the class moves from a history unit to a geography or economics one, the tutor can change with it rather than the student making do. That is only possible because nobody is travelling, and it is the main practical advantage of online delivery in this subject group.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the discipline, not to the subject-group label
whyPoints.description: History source evaluation and economics diagram explanation are different teaching jobs. faqs.question: What is actually inside MYP Individuals and Societies?
faqs.answer: History, geography, economics, business management, civics and global politics, with sociology, anthropology or psychology appearing in some schools. Units are framed by key concepts such as time, place and space, systems, change and global interactions, and reported under one subject-group heading. The content changes shape every term while the four assessment criteria stay fixed, which is why students who revise content alone perform unevenly. For a parent arranging support, the subject-group name on the report is far less useful than the discipline of the current unit, which the statement of inquiry or task brief will name directly.

faqs.question: Is MYP Individuals and Societies history, geography or economics?
faqs.answer: All of them, at different points in the year, which is the single most common misunderstanding about this subject. A Dubai school might run a history unit in the autumn, a geography unit in the spring and an introductory economics unit in Year 4 or 5, reporting one set of criterion marks across the lot. That means a tutor who is excellent for one unit can be the wrong choice for the next. Before booking anything, find the current unit's task brief and establish which discipline it belongs to. Schools that separate the disciplines from MYP Year 4 make this easier, and many Dubai IB schools do.

faqs.question: What does criterion B, investigating, require in MYP Individuals and Societies?
faqs.answer: Four things, each a separate strand. Formulating a clear and focused research question and explaining its relevance. Formulating and following an action plan to investigate it. Using research methods to collect and record appropriate, varied and relevant information. And evaluating the process and results of the investigation. Most students lose marks on the first and the last. They write a topic instead of a question, which leaves nothing to plan towards, and they skip the evaluation because it feels like admitting failure when it is in fact an explicitly marked strand. Both are quick to fix once someone shows them the shape.

faqs.question: How is a source-analysis answer marked in MYP Individuals and Societies?
faqs.answer: Under criterion D, which asks students to analyse and evaluate sources or data in terms of origin and purpose, recognising value and limitations. Summarising the content earns nothing, and asserting that a source is reliable or biased earns nothing either, because neither is an evaluation. The mark comes from stating value and limitation as consequences: because this was written by a participant shortly afterwards, it shows how the decision was understood at the time; because the author was defending their own conduct, the account of alternatives is probably incomplete. The word because is doing the work, and teaching students to demand it of themselves is the fastest gain in the subject.

faqs.question: Do Dubai home tutors cover MYP Individuals and Societies or only exam subjects?
faqs.answer: The in-home market in Dubai is strongest in mathematics and the sciences, and thinner in humanities, thinner still if you need a specific discipline. Published in-home rates run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour, and visits are usually sold as two-hour sittings because travel has to be recovered. The practical problem is not price but matching: finding someone within a reasonable drive who can mark a historical source evaluation this term and an economics diagram next term is unlikely. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE; lessons are one-to-one over live video, which is what makes the discipline match possible.

faqs.question: How does MYP Individuals and Societies sit alongside the UAE Social Studies my child must take?
faqs.answer: They are separate subjects, separately taught and separately reported. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral studies in every Dubai private school regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with content set by the Ministry of Education. MYP Individuals and Societies is the IB course, assessed on four criteria out of eight each. Families regularly read a weak Social Studies mark as a humanities problem, or the reverse. They need different responses. KHDA's guidelines also state that different or additional content for the mandatory subjects requires prior MoE permission, so legitimate support there works from the school's own materials.

faqs.question: Where do MYP Individuals and Societies students lose the most marks?
faqs.answer: In five predictable places, one per discipline. In history, reading a source for content rather than asking who produced it and why. In geography, describing a pattern when the task asked for the process behind it. In economics, drawing and labelling a diagram without the written account of what shifted. In business management, describing the company instead of applying a concept to it. In civics and politics, writing a persuasive one-sided case where the command term asked for a discussion. Each has a short fix that transfers to the rest of the course, which is why a diagnostic read of two marked tasks is worth more than a term of general revision.

faqs.question: What is a research question in MYP Individuals and Societies and why does it matter?
faqs.answer: It is the sentence the student writes to define their own investigation, and criterion B marks both the question and an explanation of its relevance. It matters because everything downstream inherits its faults. A topic rather than a question leaves nothing to plan towards, no rational basis for choosing sources, and no honest evaluation to write. A workable question names something specific, names how it will be measured or judged, and is bounded in time or place so that the available evidence is sufficient. The test: can the student say what evidence would change their answer. If not, it is still a topic.

faqs.question: Does MYP Individuals and Societies lead anywhere in the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: Directly into History, Geography, Economics, Business Management, Global Politics, Psychology and Digital Society, each of which draws on the same four MYP skills in different proportions. A student strong on criterion D and ordinary on criterion A usually suits History or Global Politics, where argument carries the paper; the reverse profile often does better in Geography or Business Management. Every one of those Diploma courses has an internally assessed component that is essentially a longer, stricter MYP investigation, so criterion B independence is the skill that transfers most. No subject choice guarantees any university outcome, and entry requirements should be checked on the institution's own admissions pages.

faqs.question: How much writing does MYP Individuals and Societies actually involve?
faqs.answer: More than most Dubai families expect, and the volume rises sharply from MYP Year 3. A typical year includes two or three extended investigations, several source-based responses, at least one case study or data analysis, and in Year 5 the Personal Project running alongside. Criterion C explicitly marks style appropriate to audience and purpose, structure appropriate to the format, and sources documented by a recognised convention, so written presentation is assessed rather than incidental. This is why a student weak in written English loses humanities marks that look like understanding marks, and why fixing the writing often lifts several subjects at once.

faqs.question: What are global contexts and key concepts in MYP Individuals and Societies?
faqs.answer: They are the framing devices the MYP uses instead of a prescribed content list. Key concepts in this subject group include time, place and space, systems, change, global interactions and identity, and each unit also carries related concepts specific to its discipline, such as causation in history or sustainability in geography. Global contexts set the real-world lens, for example fairness and development or globalisation and sustainability. For a student the practical consequence is that unit titles describe a concept rather than a topic, so the same body of history can appear under quite different headings in two Dubai schools.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both MYP Individuals and Societies and the Personal Project?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and it is a sensible pairing, because the Personal Project is assessed on planning, applying skills and reflecting, which are close relatives of criterion B. A tutor who has taught investigation design can coach the process journal, the goal setting and the reflection without touching the product. The boundary has to be explicit: Personal Project support is process coaching only. Nobody should be producing the outcome, writing the report or selecting the student's sources. The arrangement works best when the same person sees both pieces of work, because the habits that weaken one usually weaken the other.

faqs.question: Does my child need to memorise content for MYP Individuals and Societies?
faqs.answer: Some, but much less than in a content-examined system, and this surprises families arriving from Indian or British curricula. Criterion A asks for terminology used in context and for content and concepts demonstrated through description, explanation and example, so facts are needed as evidence rather than as recall for its own sake. The other three criteria reward investigation, communication and critical thinking. A student who memorises a unit and cannot frame a question or evaluate a source will sit in the middle of the range however much they know, which is the commonest profile in the marked work Dubai families send us.

faqs.question: How is criterion D, thinking critically, different from criterion A?
faqs.answer: Criterion A asks whether the student knows and understands the material: can they use the terminology correctly and explain the content with examples. Criterion D asks what they do with it: discuss concepts and issues, synthesise information into a valid argument, evaluate sources by origin and purpose, and interpret different perspectives and their implications. A student can score 7 on A and 3 on D, and that is the most common split in Dubai MYP humanities. It means the knowledge is there and the argument is not. The response is structural practice in weighing positions, not more content teaching.

faqs.question: What does a good MYP Individuals and Societies session actually do for 60 minutes?
faqs.answer: It opens with the tutor naming the criterion strand being targeted, having read the marked task beforehand rather than during the lesson. The middle forty minutes are the student writing: their own script on a shared screen, the strand descriptor read aloud, the student identifying what they have not met, then rewriting it live. Content is taught briefly where a real gap appears. The last ten minutes set one small task, deliberately small so it comes back, to be marked against the same strand before the next session. What it does not do is cover a topic, which is a lecture rather than a lesson.

faqs.question: Is MYP Individuals and Societies easier than IGCSE History?
faqs.answer: Different rather than easier, and students moving between them in Dubai feel the difference sharply in both directions. IGCSE History rewards content coverage and timed examination technique against a defined syllabus with past papers available. MYP Individuals and Societies rewards independent investigation, source evaluation and written communication across a shifting set of disciplines, assessed on four criteria with no past papers to work through. A student who thrives on structure and revision often finds IGCSE more comfortable; one who writes well and thinks independently usually prefers the MYP. Neither is a softer option, and the skills they build are only partly the same.

dubai/ib-myp-individuals-and-societies-t.tutorsIntro: The tutors listed below teach MYP Individuals and Societies across the history, geography and economics disciplines, for MYP Years 1 to 5. Each marks against the published criterion strands, returns annotated work between sessions, and keeps a dated record of which strand was targeted and what it scored.

intro.heading: How you will know whether the tutoring is working
paragraphs: Most tutoring arrangements are judged on feeling. The sessions seem useful, the tutor is pleasant, the child is less anxious on Sunday evening. Three months later a report arrives with the same number on it as before and nobody can say what happened. For an IB MYP Individuals and Societies tutor in Dubai that is an avoidable outcome, because the MYP produces more written evidence of progress than almost any other secondary programme. The criterion sheets exist. The drafts exist. The question is whether anybody is keeping them in order.

Individuals and Societies is assessed against four criteria, each marked out of eight. Criterion A is knowing and understanding, criterion B is investigating, criterion C is communicating, and criterion D is thinking critically. Each has its own strands, and a teacher awards a best-fit mark strand by strand on every assessed task. That means a Dubai MYP student generates, across a year, perhaps eight to twelve separate criterion judgements in this subject alone. Laid out chronologically, those judgements are a progress graph that costs nothing to assemble.

What that graph usually shows is not a smooth line. A student who starts weekly support in October with criterion D sitting at 3 might see D move to 5 by December while criterion A stays at 6 and criterion C drops a mark because they are experimenting with a harder structure. The overall grade on the January report may be identical to the November one. Nothing has gone wrong. A grade is a band derived from a 32-mark total, and a four-mark gain inside band 5 does not become a 6. Without the criterion record, that term looks like a waste of money. With it, it looks exactly like what it is.

The second kind of evidence is the drafts themselves. An MYP investigation is not a one-pass piece of work, and the research question a student starts with is almost never the one they should end with. A tutor's annotations on draft one, draft two and draft three are the clearest record of teaching that exists: you can see the research question narrow, the action plan acquire dates, the sources acquire an evaluation of origin and purpose, the argument acquire a counter-position. Parents who ask for one thing from a tutor should ask for the annotated drafts to be kept.

The third kind is the between-session work, and it is the one that distinguishes support that moves marks from support that fills an hour. One small task, set at the end of a session, marked before the next one, against the same strand the school uses. Small tasks come back; large ones do not. Over twelve weeks that produces a dozen marked pieces, each with a strand name attached, and the pattern in them tells a family whether to continue, reduce or stop long before a school report arrives to confirm it.

All of this happens over live video, one-to-one, with the student's own documents shared on screen. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE; that is an India-only service. The practical benefit for this subject is specific: Individuals and Societies covers history, geography and economics, and a tutor who can mark a historical source evaluation is not necessarily the right person for an economics investigation. Choosing by discipline rather than by driving distance is what makes the evidence worth reading.

dubai/ib-myp-individuals-and-societies-t.programmesIntro: Evidence of progress looks different at each stage of the IB continuum, because each stage records learning differently. Knowing what record your child's programme actually produces decides what you can reasonably ask a tutor to show you.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Social studies arrives inside transdisciplinary units, assessed through portfolios, learning journals and exhibitions rather than criterion marks. The evidence is rich but qualitative: a child's own reflections, photographs of work, teacher commentary. There is no strand-level record to track, so progress conversations at this stage rest on the portfolio and on the exhibition in the final year.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai PYP schools vary widely in how much of the portfolio parents actually see. Families moving towards the MYP should ask to look at it before Year 6 ends, because the research and reflection habits recorded there are the ones MYP criterion B will later mark formally, and the gap between a strong PYP exhibition and a weak first MYP investigation is usually one of format rather than ability.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The most measurable of the four programmes from a parent's point of view. Every assessed task in Individuals and Societies carries criterion marks against published strands, and those marks accumulate task by task across five years. Year 5 adds the Personal Project, and schools that register for eAssessment add externally set on-screen examinations and moderated ePortfolios leading to the IB MYP Certificate.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai MYP schools issue criterion sheets with varying generosity. Some return a full strand breakdown with every task; others report only the four criterion totals at the end of a unit. Either is enough to build a record from, but the first is far more useful, and it is reasonable to ask a subject teacher for strand-level feedback on a task that went badly.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Criterion marking gives way to external examinations and a single internal assessment per subject, marked against assessment criteria specific to that subject. History, Geography, Economics, Business Management, Psychology and Global Politics each carry their own paper structure. Evidence of progress narrows to mock papers, internal assessment drafts and predicted grades, which arrive far less frequently than MYP criterion sheets.
programmes.countryNote: The Dubai families who find the Diploma transition smoothest in humanities are usually those whose MYP criterion B and D marks were strong, because independent research and critical evaluation of sources are the two skills the Diploma internal assessments assume. A student who reached Year 12 with criterion D consistently at 3 or 4 will meet that gap in the first term.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Combines a career-related study with a small number of Diploma courses, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. For a humanities-inclined student the reflective project is the closest relative of the MYP investigation: an extended piece of independent research with an ethical dimension, documented and defended by the student.
programmes.countryNote: A small number of Dubai schools offer the CP, and the reflective project is often where a student with strong MYP criterion B skills shines. Course availability should be confirmed directly with the school's coordinator, since published course lists change year to year and a tutoring provider is not a reliable source for what a particular school will run.

dubai/ib-myp-individuals-and-societies-t.subjectsIntro: Individuals and Societies is a subject group, not a single subject, and the evidence a parent reads depends on which discipline the current unit sits in. These are the subject areas most likely to appear on a Dubai MYP student's criterion sheets.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Causation, change and continuity, significance, and the evaluation of sources by origin and purpose. The evidence of progress here is specific: a source evaluation that names provenance and limitation rather than summarising content. That single shift usually moves criterion D by two marks.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: Place, process, scale and sustainability, usually with data: population pyramids, climate graphs, land-use maps, fieldwork results. Criterion C marks are frequently lost here on presentation conventions rather than on understanding, which annotated drafts expose immediately.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Scarcity, markets, trade and development, with diagram work that must be labelled and explained rather than drawn and left. Evidence of improvement shows as diagrams that carry a written explanation of the shift, which is a criterion A and D gain at once.

subjects.name: Business management
subjects.description: Stakeholders, finance basics, marketing and operations, often assessed through case studies. A student's first case-study response typically describes the business; a marked and redrafted second one applies a concept to it, which is the difference between criterion A and criterion D credit.

subjects.name: Civics, politics and global issues
subjects.description: Governance, rights, power and global interactions. These units generate the strongest criterion D evidence because they demand interpretation of different perspectives, and they are where a student's habit of writing one-sided arguments becomes visible and correctable.

subjects.name: The MYP investigation
subjects.description: Research question, action plan, collection and recording of information, and evaluation of the process. This is the single richest source of evidence in the subject group, because it exists in draft form and the drafts can be compared side by side.

subjects.name: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Criterion C in Individuals and Societies marks communication: style appropriate to audience and purpose, structure appropriate to format, and documented sources. Students weak in written English lose these marks in humanities, and the improvement shows in both subjects at once.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Geography and economics units require percentage change, index numbers, ratio and graph interpretation. A student who cannot read a compound graph will lose criterion D marks for failing to analyse data that they actually understand conceptually.

subjects.name: UAE Social Studies and Moral Education
subjects.description: KHDA requires Social Studies and Moral, Social and Cultural studies in all Dubai private schools alongside the licensed curriculum. These are separately assessed and separately reported, and families frequently confuse their marks with MYP Individuals and Societies criterion marks.

subjects.name: Personal Project
subjects.description: Assessed on its own criteria, with a process journal that is itself the evidence. Students with strong criterion B habits from Individuals and Societies handle the planning and reflection far better, which is visible in the journal long before the report is submitted.

sections.heading: The evidence a Dubai MYP family already has, and what each piece proves
paragraphs: Before any tutoring begins, a Dubai MYP household typically holds five kinds of document, and together they answer most questions a parent has about Individuals and Societies. The returned assessed task with the teacher's annotations. The criterion sheet attached to it. The unit's statement of inquiry and task brief. The termly or semester report with the four criterion grades or a single subject grade. And, in Year 5, the Personal Project process journal. Very few families have these in one place, and almost none have them in date order.

Putting them in order is the first hour of useful work, and it does not require a tutor. Chronological order reveals trends that individual documents conceal. A criterion D mark of 4, 3, 5, 3 across four tasks is not a weakness, it is a volatility, and volatility usually means the student does well on units that interest them and poorly on the rest. A criterion C mark of 6, 5, 4, 4 is a decline, and declines in communicating almost always track a change in task format rather than a loss of ability.

What each document can and cannot prove is worth being precise about. A report grade proves which band a 32-mark total fell into and nothing else; it cannot show movement inside a band, which is where most of a term's progress lives. A criterion sheet proves which strands a teacher judged met and unmet on one task. An annotated draft proves what changed between versions, which is the only direct evidence that teaching had an effect. And a between-session task marked by a tutor proves whether the teaching transferred to new work, which is the question that actually matters.

sections.heading: Reading a criterion sheet for Individuals and Societies
paragraphs: The four criteria in this subject group are specific enough that a parent can work out what went wrong from the strand wording alone. Criterion A, knowing and understanding, asks the student to use terminology in context and to demonstrate knowledge and understanding of subject-specific content and concepts through descriptions, explanations and examples. Criterion B, investigating, asks them to formulate a clear and focused research question and explain its relevance, to formulate and follow an action plan, to use research methods to collect and record appropriate and varied information, and to evaluate the process and results of the investigation.

Criterion C, communicating, asks for information and ideas communicated in a style appropriate to audience and purpose, structured appropriately to the specified format, with sources documented using a recognised convention. Criterion D, thinking critically, asks the student to discuss concepts, issues, models and theories, to synthesise information to make valid arguments, to analyse and evaluate a range of sources or data in terms of origin and purpose while recognising value and limitations, and to interpret different perspectives and their implications.

Read those four together and the diagnostic pattern is clear. A student can be strong on A and weak on D, which means they know the material and are not yet arguing with it. They can be strong on D and weak on C, which means they think well and present badly, usually a referencing and structure problem rather than a thinking one. They can be strong on everything except B, which means they can respond to a question someone else set but cannot yet frame their own. Each of those three profiles needs entirely different teaching, and each is visible on a single criterion sheet.

The strand language also tells you what evidence to demand from a tutor. If criterion D's weakest strand is analysing and evaluating sources by origin and purpose, then the between-session task should be a source evaluation, marked against that strand, and the improvement should be visible as a sentence that names provenance and limitation. Anything vaguer than that, from either the school or a tutor, is not evidence of progress on criterion D.

sections.heading: Why the report grade stands still while the work improves
paragraphs: This is the conversation that saves Dubai families the most frustration, and it rests on one piece of arithmetic. The four criterion marks are added to give a total out of 32, and that total is read against a grade-boundary table to produce the 1 to 7 figure that appears on a report. Bands are four or five marks wide in the middle of the range. So a student can gain three or four marks of genuine improvement and remain on the same reported grade, and a student who loses a mark on one criterion while gaining two on another can appear to have stood still when they have in fact moved.

The consequence for anyone paying for tutoring is immediate: a report card is the wrong instrument for judging a term of support. It is too coarse and it arrives too late. The right instrument is the criterion record, read at strand level, updated weekly. That record shows a criterion D strand moving from unmet to partially met in week three, and from partially met to met in week seven, while the report is still showing the same 5 it showed in September.

There is a second, less comfortable version of the same point. A record that shows no strand movement over eight weeks is also telling you something, and it should be acted on rather than explained away. Either the teaching is aimed at the wrong strand, or the student is not completing the between-session work, or the weakness is not actually in this subject. All three are findable in the record, and all three have different answers. What they have in common is that none of them improves by continuing unchanged for another term because the sessions feel productive.

The table below is what a twelve-week record looks like when it is working. It is an illustration of the structure rather than a particular student's results: the point is the shape, one named strand per week, a mark attached, and a visible note of what changed. A family holding something in this form can walk into a parent meeting and ask precise questions, which is worth as much as the tutoring itself.

sections.heading: The draft cycle: how many versions an investigation really needs
paragraphs: An MYP investigation that scores well has usually been through three or four versions, and the versions do different jobs. Draft zero is the research question and action plan alone, before any research happens. This is where most of the eventual mark is decided and where almost no student spends time. A question like how has tourism affected Dubai is unanswerable in two thousand words with school-accessible sources. A question about a named development, in a named period, measured by a named indicator, is answerable, and criterion B rewards the relevance explanation that justifies it.

Draft one is the research recorded. Not written up: recorded, in whatever format makes the information retrievable, with each source captured along with its origin and purpose. Students who skip this step write their investigation from memory and then cannot document their sources, which costs criterion C marks that have nothing to do with the quality of their thinking. A tutor's annotation at this stage is mostly about recording format, which sounds administrative and is worth two or three marks.

Draft two is the argument. This is where criterion D is won or lost: synthesis into a valid argument, perspectives interpreted, evidence evaluated rather than quoted. Most first attempts list what the sources say. The redraft makes them disagree with each other and then adjudicates. That single structural change, taught once on one investigation, transfers to every subsequent one, which is why a draft cycle is better value than general humanities tuition.

Draft three is the evaluation of the process and the final tidy: what the method missed, what a different source would have shown, whether the research question turned out to be the right one. Students resist this because it reads like admitting failure, and it is explicitly a marked strand of criterion B. Throughout all of it, the student writes every word. A tutor marks, explains, questions and sets the rewrite, and that boundary is not negotiable under IB academic honesty rules.

sections.heading: What a session produces, and what arrives in your inbox afterwards
paragraphs: A session that generates evidence has a fixed structure, because unstructured sessions produce impressions instead. The tutor reads the returned task before the lesson and opens by naming the criterion and strand being worked on. That naming is not ceremony: a student who knows they are working on criterion D source evaluation behaves differently for the next fifty minutes than one who has been told they are doing history.

The middle of the session is the student writing. The tutor shares the student's own script on screen, reads the strand descriptor aloud, asks the student to identify which part they have not met, and then has them rewrite the sentence or paragraph live. Rewriting during the session rather than promising it as homework is what makes the evidence reliable, because what gets written in the session definitely exists. The tutor teaches content where a genuine gap appears, briefly, and returns to the task.

The last ten minutes set the between-session task, and the size of it is a deliberate decision. One source evaluation. One introductory paragraph. One action plan. Small enough that it comes back, because a task that does not come back costs the following session its purpose. The task is marked against the same strand before the next lesson and returned with annotations, which is the piece of paper that goes into the record.

What arrives in a parent's inbox is therefore specific: the annotated task, a line naming the strand and whether it was met, and at week six and week twelve a short written review. That review is written to be read by someone else, because the most useful thing a Dubai family can do with it is take it into a parent-teacher meeting and ask the subject teacher whether they see the same pattern. Sessions run over live video in Gulf Standard Time, with no home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE.

sections.heading: When the evidence says the problem is not Individuals and Societies
paragraphs: A criterion record is useful partly because it can exonerate the subject. Three patterns recur in Dubai MYP humanities cases, and in each one buying more Individuals and Societies hours is the wrong response. The first is a criterion C weakness that appears identically in every written subject. If a student's communicating marks are low in history, in sciences and in language and literature simultaneously, the problem is writing, and it should be addressed as writing. Fixing it once lifts four subjects.

The second is a criterion D weakness in students who are fluent talkers. These students argue well out loud and write one-sided paragraphs, which is a transcription problem rather than a thinking problem. The evidence for it is specific: ask the student to explain the counter-argument verbally and they produce it immediately. The response is a structural scaffold they use until it becomes automatic, usually three or four sessions, not a term of content teaching.

The third is an attendance or workload pattern masquerading as a subject weakness. A student carrying eight MYP subjects, a Personal Project and three extracurricular commitments produces thin investigations because there is no time in the week to do otherwise. The record shows this clearly: marks drop across all subjects in the same weeks, recover in the quieter ones. The honest recommendation is a conversation about the timetable, not more tutoring, and we will make it even though it means fewer sessions.

There is also a legitimate possibility that the record shows nothing wrong at all. A student sitting at 5 across all four criteria, with no declining strand, may simply be a 5 in this subject at this stage, and the family's concern may be ambition rather than diagnosis. That is a reasonable thing to pursue, and the honest framing is enrichment rather than remediation: harder sources, longer arguments, a more demanding research question. It needs saying plainly, because the alternative is a family paying for remediation of a problem that does not exist.

Fluent speakers writing one-sided arguments need a scaffold, not content

sections.heading: Whose work the evidence is: academic honesty in MYP humanities
paragraphs: An evidence-led approach has an obvious failure mode: evidence is easy to manufacture if somebody else writes the work. So the boundary has to be explicit, especially in a subject group assessed largely through investigations and extended writing produced outside the classroom. IB academic honesty rules require the work to be the student's own, and a tutoring arrangement that blurs that puts the student's MYP record at risk rather than improving it.

What a tutor may do is wide and genuinely useful. Teach the content. Explain what a strand descriptor means. Mark a draft and say precisely where it falls short. Model source evaluation on a document the student is not using. Ask the question that makes a student notice their own missing counter-argument. Teach a referencing convention and check a bibliography for completeness and consistency. Coach the planning and reflection behind a Personal Project. None of that touches the student's authorship.

What a tutor must never do is supply the text. No sentences to paste in, no restructuring of a draft until the voice has changed, no selecting and reading the sources on the student's behalf, no writing of the evaluation paragraph that criterion B asks for. The test a Dubai parent can apply without reading a word of the subject guide is this: ask your child to explain any paragraph in the document and why it is there. If they can, the help was teaching. If they cannot, the evidence in your record is worthless and the risk is theirs.

The same boundary covers materials. IB, Cambridge and Pearson documents are copyright and should reach a student through the school or the board's own website, not through a tutor's shared folder. A session built on the school's own task briefs, the student's own drafts and the published criterion descriptors is both legitimate and more useful, because it is the material the student is actually being marked against.

No supplied sentences, no rewriting to completion, no reading sources for them

sections.heading: What the record should look like at each MYP year
paragraphs: The useful evidence changes as a student moves through the programme, and a tutor who treats MYP Year 1 like MYP Year 5 will generate the wrong record. In Years 1 and 2 the criterion marks are genuinely noisy. Students are learning what an investigation is, teachers are calibrating, and a single task can swing two marks for reasons that have nothing to do with the student. The right evidence here is qualitative: can the child use subject vocabulary in their own sentence, can they find and record a source, can they write a paragraph that makes one point.

Years 3 and 4 are where the record becomes properly readable. Criterion marks stabilise, task formats repeat, and trends mean something. This is also where the most valuable interventions sit, because a criterion B or D habit fixed here is carried through Year 5 and into the Diploma. A family who assembles a chronological record at the start of Year 3 and keeps it current has, by the middle of Year 4, better information about their child's humanities learning than any single report could give them.

Year 5 changes the question from diagnosis to management. The Personal Project, the final subject units and, in registered schools, eAssessment preparation all compete for the same hours, and the record's job becomes protecting priorities rather than finding weaknesses. The evidence to watch is the process journal and the internal deadline calendar. A student whose criterion marks are stable but whose journal has three blank weeks has a time problem, and that is what the support should address.

After Year 5 the record thins out, because the Diploma produces fewer, larger pieces of assessed work. That is precisely why the MYP record is worth keeping: a student entering Diploma History or Geography with a documented history of criterion D improvement is in a very different position from one entering with a sequence of report grades and no detail. The record also makes the first Diploma conversation with a new teacher much shorter and much more specific.

MYP Years 3-4: the record becomes readable and interventions are most valuable

process.title: Gather what you already have, in date order
process.description: Two or three recent assessed tasks with criterion sheets, any annotated drafts, and the last two reports. Date order matters more than completeness. This is the baseline, and it is usually enough to name the weak strand before the first session rather than during it.

process.title: Agree the target strand in writing
process.description: Not improve in humanities, but criterion D, the strand on evaluating sources by origin and purpose. A named strand can be reviewed; a general aim cannot. The target is written down, along with the date at which you will decide whether it has moved.

process.title: Free trial lesson that produces a marked piece of work
process.description: One free trial per student with the tutor who would continue, no card details taken. It is a working session that ends with a small task set, so even the trial adds a dated entry to the record. If the match is wrong, a different tutor is proposed at no cost.

process.title: Weekly sessions with one small task in between
process.description: One session a week, one short piece of work set at the end of it, marked against the agreed strand and returned with annotations before the next lesson. The task is deliberately small, because the whole method depends on it actually coming back.

process.title: Written review at week six and week twelve
process.description: A short written statement of what was targeted, what the marks did and what changed in the work. It is written to be shown to the school, so you can ask the subject teacher whether they see the same pattern rather than relying on our reading alone.

process.title: Decide on the evidence, including reducing or stopping
process.description: If the strand has moved and held on unfamiliar work, frequency drops to fortnightly or support ends. If it has not moved, we change the target, change the tutor, or tell you the problem sits elsewhere. Continuing unchanged because the sessions felt useful is the one option we will argue against.

whyPoints.title: A dated record, not a termly impression
whyPoints.description: Every session names a criterion strand and every between-session task is marked against it, so progress is a document rather than a feeling. Families hold twelve dated entries after a term, which is twelve more than a report card provides.

whyPoints.title: Teaching built on the school's own marking
whyPoints.description: Sessions start from the criterion sheets your child's teacher has already written, so the target is the strand the school flagged rather than one a tutor prefers. That also means the school and the tutoring are pulling in the same direction.

whyPoints.title: Discipline-matched tutors, because this is a subject group
whyPoints.description: Marking a historical source evaluation and marking an economics diagram are different skills. Online delivery means the match is made by discipline rather than by which tutor lives nearest, which matters more in Individuals and Societies than in most subjects.

whyPoints.title: Drafts kept, so improvement is legible
whyPoints.description: Annotated draft one beside annotated draft three is the clearest evidence that teaching happened. We keep them and give them to you, which also leaves your child with a model of how a strong investigation is actually built.

whyPoints.title: Reviews written to be shown to the school
whyPoints.description: The week six and week twelve summaries are phrased for a parent-teacher meeting rather than for marketing. The most valuable use of them is to ask your child's subject teacher whether the pattern we describe matches what they see.

whyPoints.description: If the record shows the weakness is writing across all subjects, or a workload problem, or nothing at all, we say so. Support that is no longer needed should end, and an arrangement that cannot imagine recommending that is not evidence-led.

faqs.question: What evidence should I see after a month of MYP Individuals and Societies support?
faqs.answer: Four dated items, one per session, each a small piece of work marked against a named criterion strand with annotations on it. Alongside them, a line recording which strand was targeted and whether it was judged met, partially met or unmet. After four weeks you should also be able to see a difference between the first marked piece and the fourth on the same strand, for example a source evaluation that now names provenance and limitation where the first only summarised content. What you should not expect in a month is a changed report grade, because grade bands are several marks wide and reports arrive termly.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether my child's MYP Individuals and Societies marks are really moving?
faqs.answer: Put the criterion marks in date order and read them strand by strand rather than looking at the subject grade. Movement shows first at strand level: a criterion D strand going from unmet to partially met is real progress that the 1 to 7 grade cannot display. Volatility is different from weakness, so a pattern of 4, 3, 5, 3 usually means the student performs well on units that interest them, while 6, 5, 4, 4 is a genuine decline and generally tracks a change in task format. If eight weeks of records show no strand movement at all, that is a finding to act on rather than a delay to wait out.

faqs.question: What does a marked MYP Individuals and Societies investigation look like once a tutor has annotated it?
faqs.answer: Dense, specific and uncomfortable to read, which is the point. Annotations name the strand rather than the sentiment: research question not narrow enough to answer with available sources, action plan has no dates, this source is quoted but not evaluated for origin and purpose, this paragraph lists two views without adjudicating between them. Each annotation implies a rewrite rather than a correction. A good annotated draft contains no praise that is not attached to a strand, and no criticism that does not say what to do instead. Kept alongside draft three, it is the clearest evidence a family will ever have that teaching actually happened.

faqs.question: Which criterion total should I watch across an MYP reporting cycle?
faqs.answer: Watch all four separately, and watch the one your child is weakest on most closely. The four criteria in this subject group are knowing and understanding, investigating, communicating, and thinking critically, each marked out of eight. They are added to a total out of 32, which is then converted to the 1 to 7 grade on the report. Because that conversion loses detail, the subject grade is the least informative number available. Criterion D is the one that most often separates a 5 from a 6 in Dubai MYP humanities, and criterion C is the one most often fixable fastest, since it is usually structure and referencing rather than understanding.

faqs.question: How many drafts does an MYP Individuals and Societies investigation normally go through?
faqs.answer: Three or four, and they do different jobs. Draft zero is the research question and action plan alone, before research begins, and it decides most of the eventual criterion B mark. Draft one is the research recorded with each source captured along with its origin and purpose. Draft two is the argument, where criterion D is won or lost, turning a list of what sources say into a weighed judgement. Draft three adds the evaluation of the process, which is a marked strand students routinely skip because it feels like admitting failure. The student writes every version; a tutor marks, explains and sets the rewrite.

faqs.question: Does the tutor work from my child's own returned school work?
faqs.answer: Yes, and that is the whole method. Every session opens with a task the school has already assessed, read by the tutor before the lesson rather than during it, with the criterion sheet beside it. Working from the school's own marking means the target is the strand your child's teacher flagged, not one a tutor finds interesting, and it keeps the school and the tutoring aligned instead of pulling in different directions. Generic worksheets produce generic sessions. If a provider cannot tell you which strand of which criterion the next session will address, they are not working from the evidence.

faqs.question: How does a tutor track MYP Individuals and Societies progress week by week?
faqs.answer: With a short record that has four columns: the date, the work marked, the criterion and strand targeted, and what changed. One line per week. The between-session task is what populates it, which is why that task is kept deliberately small, a single source evaluation or one introductory paragraph rather than a full investigation. Small tasks come back and get marked; large ones do not, and a task that does not come back costs the following session its purpose. After twelve weeks the record is a page long and tells a family more than two report cards would.

faqs.question: My child's report says 5 in Individuals and Societies but the teacher says criterion D is weak. What does that mean?
faqs.answer: It means the 5 is an average of unequal parts, and the teacher is telling you something more useful than the report is. A grade of 5 corresponds to a criterion total in the high teens to low twenties out of 32. That total can be built from four balanced marks of 5, or from a 7 on knowing and understanding sitting beside a 3 on thinking critically. The second profile is far more common in Dubai MYP cohorts, and it needs entirely different teaching: not more content, but structured practice in weighing perspectives and evaluating sources by origin and purpose. Ask the teacher for the strand detail behind that comment.

faqs.question: Can a tutor explain the gap between a school report grade and the criterion marks behind it?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is often the single most useful hour a Dubai family buys. The report grade is a band derived from a 32-mark total. Bands are four or five marks wide in the middle of the range, so two students on 5 can be four marks apart, and a term of genuine improvement can leave the reported figure untouched. A tutor reading your criterion sheets can show you where in the band your child sits, which criterion is holding the total down, and how many marks the next band actually requires. That is frequently a smaller number than parents assume, concentrated in one strand.

faqs.question: What does progress look like in MYP Individuals and Societies when the grade has not moved yet?
faqs.answer: It looks like a specific sentence that was not there before. A source paragraph that now names who produced the document and why, rather than what it says. An introduction that states a position instead of announcing a topic. A reference list that is complete and uses one convention consistently. An evaluation paragraph that admits what the method could not reach. Each of those is a strand moving from unmet to met, each is worth a mark or two, and none of them necessarily crosses a band boundary on its own. Three or four of them together usually do, which is why the strand record is the honest progress measure.

faqs.question: How do we know a tutor is marking to the MYP criteria and not to a British standard?
faqs.answer: Ask them to name the strand they are marking against before they mark it, and check the words they use against your child's criterion sheet. MYP marking language is distinctive: best-fit judgement, strands met or partially met, marks out of eight on four named criteria. British marking language is percentages, grade boundaries and assessment objectives. A tutor who returns a piece of humanities work with a percentage on it has not marked it to the MYP, whatever they say. A tutor who writes criterion D, strand on evaluation of sources, partially met, and explains why, demonstrably has.

faqs.question: What should the first MYP Individuals and Societies session produce?
faqs.answer: Three things. A named target: which criterion and which strand within it the support will address first. A short piece of work set and explained, small enough to come back before the next session. And a clear statement of what the existing marked work actually shows, including anything that contradicts what the family expected. The first session should not be spent on introductions or on general discussion of the subject. The tutor has read the criterion sheets beforehand, so the hour goes on teaching and on establishing the baseline that everything afterwards is measured against.

faqs.question: Should I ask for written feedback after every MYP Individuals and Societies session?
faqs.answer: Ask for the marked task and one line naming the strand and the outcome. That is enough, and it is sustainable. A long written report after every session sounds thorough and in practice either does not happen or consumes time that should go on marking. What is worth asking for in addition is a short written review at six weeks and twelve weeks, phrased so you can take it into a parent-teacher meeting. The most valuable thing a Dubai family can do with such a review is ask the subject teacher whether they recognise the same pattern in class.

faqs.question: How long before an MYP Individuals and Societies grade shifts by a whole band?
faqs.answer: A term is a realistic frame for one band in most cases, and the honest answer is that it depends on how many marks the band is away. A student sitting at the top of band 4 may need two marks and see the change on the next report. One sitting at the bottom of band 4 may need five or six marks and two terms, even with identical teaching. That is why the target should be a strand rather than a grade. Strands move in weeks and can be evidenced; bands move in terms and depend on arithmetic the family cannot see without the criterion totals.

faqs.question: What happens if the evidence shows the problem is not Individuals and Societies at all?
faqs.answer: We tell you, and we change or stop the arrangement. Three patterns recur. Criterion C marks that are low in every written subject point at writing rather than humanities, and fixing writing lifts four subjects at once. Fluent speakers who write one-sided arguments need a structural scaffold for three or four sessions, not a term of content teaching. Marks dropping across all subjects in the same weeks and recovering in quieter ones is a workload finding, and the right response is a timetable conversation. Occasionally the record shows nothing wrong, in which case the honest framing is enrichment rather than remediation.

faqs.question: Who sees the tutor notes on my child's Individuals and Societies work?
faqs.answer: You do, and your child does. The annotated tasks and the six-week and twelve-week reviews go to the parent who arranged the support, and the annotations themselves are written for the student to work from. Nothing is sent to the school by us; whether to share a review with a subject teacher is entirely your decision, and the reviews are written on the assumption that you might. We collect only what is needed to teach, we say what it is used for, and anything you want deleted will be deleted on request. No child's school, grades or photograph is published anywhere.
