intro.heading: You should be able to see the change before the school tells you about it
paragraphs: The hardest part of paying for language tutoring is that nothing visible happens for weeks. Maths produces a right answer the same evening. A language produces a report card in March. Parents in Dubai end up guessing, renewing out of hope, and discovering in the summer that the grade sat still. The fix is not more hours. It is insisting on evidence in a form you can read yourself, starting in week one.

MYP Language Acquisition makes that possible because it is marked on published criteria rather than on a percentage. Four criteria, each on a band out of eight: listening, reading, speaking and writing. A tutor who knows the subject can take a piece of your child's own work, put a criterion letter and a band number on it, and say in one sentence what the next band up requires. If that cannot be produced, you are buying conversation practice, which has its place and is not the same thing.

This page is about what that evidence looks like week by week. A phase estimate after the first hour. A banded practice task in week two. A different text type banded in week three, so you can tell whether the band belonged to the student or to the task. A written six-week plan at the end of the month. Then a blind re-band at week eight against the same descriptor set, which is the first point at which the word progress means anything. None of that requires a parent to learn the descriptors. It requires a tutor willing to write things down and a family willing to keep the documents in one place, which between them turn a vague monthly worry into a readable sequence.

The in-home question deserves a straight answer rather than a sales line. People do drive to villas in Dubai to teach languages, the market charges between AED 180 and 500 an hour for it, and a chunk of that figure is the car rather than the teaching. IB Gram does not do it: home visits are a service offered only in India. Dubai lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, which keeps the tutor pool national rather than local.

That trade matters most in this subject. The people who can band a Phase 5 Criterion D script in French, or teach Arabic reading to a non-Arab beginner, are thinly spread across Dubai. Choosing by postcode narrows an already narrow pool. Choosing by phase and criterion, and accepting a screen, usually produces a better teacher and a shorter session that happens twice a week instead of once a fortnight. There is one more reason to care about the format. A language criterion moves on frequency and on how fast marked work comes back, and both of those are decided by the shape of the session rather than by the talent of the person running it. An hour booked fortnightly because somebody has to drive across the city is the wrong shape for this subject, however good the teaching inside it happens to be, and no amount of goodwill fixes a feedback loop that takes two weeks to close.
bullets: Week one: a written phase estimate and one target criterion
Every week after: one task banded with a criterion letter and a band number
Week eight: the same descriptor applied blind to fresh work
In-home rates in Dubai run AED 180-500 an hour, travel included
Recorded orals, kept with consent, so Criterion C change can be heard

dubai/ib-myp-language-acquisition-home-t.programmesIntro: Reporting changes shape three times across an IB school career, and parents judging progress need to know which shape they are looking at. These are the three programmes a Dubai family meets, described by what the paperwork actually tells you at each stage.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Reports carry criterion letters and band numbers rather than percentages, which is unusually useful once you know how to read them. A 5 in Criterion B and a 7 in Criterion C on the same report is a diagnosis, not a contradiction. The subject grade from 1 to 7 is a conversion of the four criterion totals, so two students on the same grade can need completely different teaching.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools issue these reports on their own internal cycle, often three times a year, and the criterion letters are the only part worth arguing about. Ask for the band numbers if the report shows only the converted grade; most Dubai MYP schools will release them to a parent who asks the subject teacher directly rather than the office.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Reporting is narrative and there are no criterion bands, so there is nothing numerical to track and nothing to hand over into MYP 1. Progress in an additional language at this stage is best judged by what a child can do unprompted rather than by what a report says they have covered.
programmes.countryNote: The practical consequence for Dubai families is that MYP 1 phase placement arrives as a surprise. A child who seemed strong in primary French can land in Phase 1 because the placement test asked for reading and writing. That is a measurement difference rather than a collapse in ability, and it is worth saying so to a worried eleven-year-old.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Reporting returns to a 1 to 7 grade per subject with predicted grades attached, and the evidence a parent sees becomes mock papers and marked components. Language B is examined on written text types, a listening paper and an individual oral, so the feedback loop is faster and harsher than the MYP one.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools issue Diploma predicted grades to universities, which raises the stakes on evidence considerably. Families who built the habit of asking for banded work during the MYP arrive in Year 12 able to read a mock script instead of only the number on the front of it, and that habit is worth more than the tutoring that created it.

dubai/ib-myp-language-acquisition-home-t.subjectsIntro: Bookings on this page are usually made by criterion rather than by language, because that is how the subject is marked and how progress becomes visible. These are the pieces of work IB Gram is asked for most often by Dubai MYP families, with what the evidence of improvement looks like in each.

subjects.name: Criterion A listening diagnosis
subjects.description: A log of which question types keep failing: inference, numbers, negatives or speaker attitude. The evidence is the log itself across six weeks, because a single listening score tells you nothing about why. Improvement shows as one question type dropping out of the failure column.

subjects.name: Criterion B reading at and above phase
subjects.description: Timed comprehension on short authentic texts, with answers justified from the text rather than from general knowledge. Evidence is the gap between performance at phase level and one phase above, which is also the number a school wants before moving a student up.

subjects.name: Criterion C interactive oral
subjects.description: Three-minute unprepared turns, recorded with consent and played back. Evidence is audible: the same student two weeks apart on the same prompt. This is the only criterion where a parent can judge movement without reading a descriptor.

subjects.name: Criterion D text types and register
subjects.description: One written task a week, banded against the descriptor, rewritten once by the student, then compared. Evidence is the pair of scripts side by side with the band on each. Most of the first band move comes from text type and register rather than vocabulary.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language, reading focus
subjects.description: Decoding unvowelled text is the ceiling for most non-Arab students in Dubai. Evidence is reading speed and accuracy on unseen phase-level text, tracked weekly. Oral marks for these students are often already fine and do not need the hours.

subjects.name: French, agreement and tense control
subjects.description: Agreement, the perfect against the imperfect, and the pronoun order that collapses under time pressure. Evidence is an error-type tally across four scripts, which shows whether a rule has been learned or merely explained.

subjects.name: Spanish, register and connectives
subjects.description: Grades flatten at Phase 4 when register starts to carry marks. Evidence is the same content written twice for different audiences, which exposes whether a student can choose register deliberately or only has one voice.

subjects.name: ePortfolio range audit
subjects.description: A read across everything already collected, listing text types used, text types missing, and registers repeated. Evidence is the list. Portfolios cap themselves on range more often than on quality, and the fix costs nothing if it is spotted in October.

subjects.name: Phase review evidence pack
subjects.description: Three tasks across the four criteria, banded against both the current phase and the one above, written up in one page for a coordinator to read. Evidence here is the document itself, which is what a school needs before reconsidering a placement.

dubai/ib-myp-language-acquisition-home-t.regionsIntro: Where a family lives in Dubai decides the realistic start time of a session and very little else, because delivery is over video. These are the communities IB Gram schedules most MYP language work into, with the timing pattern that actually holds in each.

regions.name: Dubai Marina and Jumeirah Lakes Towers
regions.note: Apartment living, so a quiet room is the constraint rather than the commute. Thirty-minute oral slots at 5pm work better here than long evening sessions, and headphones solve most of what parents worry about.

regions.name: Palm Jumeirah
regions.note: School buses run long on the Palm and arrival times slip. Families here tend to book a fixed 6pm slot and accept a five-minute late start rather than chase an earlier one that keeps collapsing.

regions.name: Downtown Dubai and Business Bay
regions.note: Short school runs but heavy activity calendars. The pattern that survives is two short sessions on fixed weekdays, because a single long session gets traded away whenever a match or a rehearsal appears.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches and Motor City
regions.note: Villa communities with a long drive to most international schools. Weekday sessions realistically start at 5.30pm, and Saturday mornings carry the writing tasks that need an unhurried hour.

regions.name: Dubai Hills Estate
regions.note: Newer schools nearby and shorter runs, so 4.30pm is achievable. A common booking here is one child on MYP language work and a sibling on Diploma Language B in consecutive slots.

regions.name: Town Square and Damac Hills
regions.note: Long bus journeys in both directions. Families book later and shorter, and the most reliable arrangement is a thirty-minute oral slot twice a week with written work marked between them.

regions.name: Discovery Gardens and The Gardens
regions.note: Mixed school destinations across the city and later arrivals home. Weekend sessions dominate here, which suits reading and portfolio work far better than it suits oral fluency practice.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai Marina, Jumeirah Lakes Towers and Palm Jumeirah
schoolClusters.note: A high-mobility corridor where students arrive mid-year from several school systems, so phase mismatches are frequent and phase review requests are the most common reason families here get in touch. Requests skew towards French and Spanish in the middle phases.

schoolClusters.city: Arabian Ranches, Dubai Hills and the Al Khail corridor
schoolClusters.note: Villa communities whose children are spread across IB and British schools, which means siblings on different reporting systems in one household. Arabic as an additional language is the most requested language in this cluster, usually with reading as the target criterion.
schools: Jumeirah English Speaking School Arabian Ranches

dubai/ib-myp-language-acquisition-home-t.modesIntro: Each of these is built so that something readable arrives between sessions. That is the whole design principle: if a month goes by with no banded work in your inbox, there is nothing to judge and no reason to renew.

modes.title: Weekly hour with a banded task between sessions
modes.description: Sixty minutes a week, one practice task set at the end of each session, banded against the criterion descriptor and returned before the next one. The following lesson opens on the marked script. Parents receive the band and the one-line next move, which over a term becomes a readable record of what changed and when.
bullets: One task banded every week, with the criterion letter stated
The marked script opens the next session
Parent copy of the band and the next move
Target criterion fixed for a half-term at a time

modes.title: Twice-weekly oral slots, fifteen to thirty minutes
modes.description: Short, frequent speaking work for Criterion C, recorded with the family's consent so the student and the parent can hear a fortnight of change rather than take it on trust. Thirty minutes fits between the bus and dinner in most Dubai households, which is why this pattern survives a busy activity calendar while a long weekly session does not.
bullets: Two slots a week, fifteen to thirty minutes each
Recordings kept only with written consent
Same prompt revisited every fortnight for comparison
Unprepared turns rather than rehearsed answers

modes.title: Six-week evidence block before a phase review
modes.description: A fixed block aimed at one outcome: a one-page pack a coordinator can read, containing three tasks across the four criteria banded against the current phase and the phase above. It is the format Dubai schools respond to, because it answers the question they actually ask, which is what the student can show rather than what the parent believes.

Banded against two phases for comparison

Ends whether or not the review is granted

sections.heading: What a Dubai parent means by an IB MYP Language Acquisition home tutor
paragraphs: Two different requests hide behind the same phrase. Some families want a person physically in the house, usually because a younger sibling has made the kitchen table the only workable study space, or because a twelve-year-old will not concentrate without somebody in the room. Others use the words home tutor to mean private, one-to-one, outside a classroom, and hold no strong view about where it happens. The second group is much the larger of the two, and for them the delivery question is settled by whichever option produces better teaching for the money.

The in-home market in Dubai is real and priced accordingly. Bestimate's Dubai 2026 rate table puts in-home one-to-one between AED 180 and 350 an hour, independent listings advertise up to AED 500, and monthly in-home packages of AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour sessions circulate widely. Part of that premium buys teaching and part of it buys a car in evening traffic on Al Khail Road. The invoice does not separate the two, and the session length is usually stretched to ninety minutes or two hours so the trip is worth making.

IB Gram does not sell in-home visits anywhere in the UAE; that is a service offered only in India. Dubai lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. The argument for that in this subject is not convenience, it is supply. Language Acquisition is marked on four criteria against phase descriptors, and the number of people in Dubai who can band a Phase 5 Criterion D script in French, or teach Arabic reading to a non-Arab beginner, is small enough that geography should not be allowed to narrow it any further.

sections.heading: In-home against live online for a language subject
paragraphs: A comparison table is more honest than an argument here, because the two options win on different things. An in-home visit wins on presence: a reluctant student sits down because somebody is there, and a parent can see the hour happening. Live online wins on tutor choice, session shape and turnaround of marked work. For Language Acquisition specifically, the second set matters more, and the reason is the way the subject is assessed.

Criterion C speaking improves on frequency rather than duration. Two thirty-minute slots a week beat one ninety-minute session, and in-home economics pushes the opposite way: nobody drives across Dubai for half an hour. Criterion D writing improves on marking turnaround, because a student who rewrites while the feedback is fresh learns the rule, whereas one who receives a corrected script a fortnight later reads it as a verdict. A shared document closes that loop inside two days.

The cost difference compounds for the same reason. If the useful pattern is twice a week, the per-hour gap between an in-home rate of AED 250 and an online specialist rate is multiplied by eight sessions a month rather than four. None of this makes in-home a bad choice for every subject or every child. It makes it an expensive choice for a subject whose marks move on frequency and feedback speed. If presence is the real requirement, the honest advice is to buy in-home locally for a subject where one long weekly session genuinely suits the work, and to keep the language subject on a screen where the session can be short, frequent and marked by somebody chosen for the phase rather than for the postcode.

sections.heading: The evidence a language tutor should show you after four weeks
paragraphs: Ask for this at the start rather than at the point of frustration. A tutor who intends to produce banded work will agree immediately and a tutor who does not will offer a progress call instead. Both answers are useful. The schedule below is what IB Gram asks its MYP language tutors to deliver in a first month, and it exists because the alternative is a family paying for twelve weeks and then reading a report card that has not moved.

The important distinction in the table is between what each piece of evidence proves and what it does not. A single banded task in week two proves the tutor can apply a descriptor. It proves nothing about your child, because one task is one text type on one day. The second task in week three is the useful one: a different text type, banded the same way, which separates the student's ability from the task's difficulty. That is the point at which a plan can be written honestly.

Week eight is where the word progress earns its place. A fresh task, banded blind against the same descriptor set, compared with the week two and week three scripts. If the band has moved, something worked. If it has not, the approach changes, or the tutor does. Neither outcome needs a report card, and both are available two months before the school issues one. Keep the scripts in one folder as they arrive. By the end of a term you have a sequence rather than an impression, and a sequence is what makes a conversation with a subject teacher productive instead of defensive.

sections.heading: Reading a marked writing task the way a moderator reads it
paragraphs: Criterion D is the criterion parents can check themselves, because writing sits still on a page. The descriptors are published per phase and they ask about range, accuracy, organisation, text type and register. They do not ask how many errors there are, which is the single most common misreading. A script with six small agreement slips and a confidently handled formal register will usually outscore a flawless piece in the wrong register, and that surprises almost everybody the first time.

The table below describes what Criterion D work tends to look like at each band around Phases 3 and 4, which is where most Dubai MYP students sit. It is a reading aid rather than a reproduction of any board's descriptors; the official wording lives with your school and with the IB. Use it to sanity-check a tutor's band: if a script reads like the 3 to 4 row and a tutor has called it a 6, ask them to point at the descriptor language that justifies it.

The last row of the table is the one worth memorising. Choosing the wrong text type is the cheapest mark available in this subject and the one most often thrown away. A student who writes a beautiful essay when the task asked for a blog entry has lost marks that had nothing to do with their language. Reading the task's text type aloud before starting costs ten seconds and is the highest-return habit a language tutor can install.

sections.heading: Speaking is the criterion a screen helps most
paragraphs: Parents assume the opposite, which is reasonable and wrong. The instinct is that talking is a human thing and a screen gets in the way of it. In practice a video session does three things a kitchen-table session cannot. It records, with consent, so a student hears themselves from a fortnight ago. It removes the audience, which matters enormously to a thirteen-year-old who will not risk an error in front of a parent in the next room. And it puts the descriptor on screen beside the recording.

The MYP interactive oral is assessed on fluency, range, accuracy and message, and the failure mode is nearly always the same: a prepared answer that collapses when the question changes direction. Rehearsed material sounds excellent for ninety seconds and then runs out. The cure is unprepared turns, three minutes at a time, with the tutor refusing to accept the rehearsed opening. That is uncomfortable work, and doing it twice a week for twenty minutes is more effective than doing it once a fortnight for an hour.

Playback is what makes the improvement legible to a family. Two recordings of the same prompt, two weeks apart, is evidence a parent can assess without reading a single descriptor: fewer silences, longer turns, recovery after an error rather than a full stop. Recordings are kept only with written consent and only for as long as the comparison is useful, and a family can ask for them to be deleted at any point without giving a reason.

sections.heading: The report-card lag, and how to see change before it arrives
paragraphs: An MYP report is a summary of judgements a teacher made over a reporting period, which means it describes the past rather than the present. Work produced in the first fortnight of a term sits inside the grade issued at the end of it. A student who changed in week six is reported on the average of a term that included weeks one to five. Three months of real improvement can therefore produce a report that moves by nothing at all, and families read that as failure.

There is a second lag on top of the first. Schools set assessment tasks when the unit requires one, not when a parent wants a measurement, so a criterion may not be formally assessed for six or eight weeks. A student whose Criterion B reading has genuinely moved may have no Criterion B task on the record until after the report. Asking the subject teacher which criteria were assessed in the period, and when the next task for each falls, resolves most of the confusion in one email.

The practical answer is to measure independently and on a fixed cycle. Banded practice work every week, a blind re-band at six to eight weeks, and a comparison you can read. When the school report arrives it then confirms or contradicts something you already know, which is a far better position than discovering in March that a term of hours produced nothing and having no way to tell what went wrong.

sections.heading: Scheduling around the Dubai school run, activities and Ramadan
paragraphs: Most tutoring arrangements in Dubai fail on logistics rather than on teaching. A 4.30pm slot booked in September collapses in October when swimming moves, and the family concludes that tutoring did not work. Deciding the slot from the activity calendar rather than from the school day fixes a surprising amount of that. So does choosing the shorter pattern: a thirty-minute oral slot survives a busy week in a way that a ninety-minute session never does.

Dubai's school transport makes arrival times unreliable in specific communities rather than everywhere. Children bussed from Town Square, Discovery Gardens or the Palm often reach home after 4.45pm, so a 4.30pm booking starts late every week and the family slowly stops valuing the session. A 6pm slot held firmly is worth more than a 4.30pm slot renegotiated weekly, and the student arrives fed rather than resentful.

Ramadan reshapes the calendar for everybody in Dubai, not only for fasting families. School hours shorten, afternoons are quieter, evenings reorganise around Iftar and Suhoor, and attention in the late afternoon drops sharply. Sessions in that month tend to move either earlier in the day or well after Iftar, and reading and portfolio work travels better into those slots than oral practice does. Agree the Ramadan pattern in advance rather than cancelling week by week. The month is also a natural point to run the blind re-band, because the written tasks it suits are exactly the ones that measurement needs, and a quieter fortnight produces cleaner evidence than a week crowded with school assessments does.

sections.heading: Who is legally permitted to tutor your child in Dubai
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a permit, and it is worth knowing the shape of it before paying anybody. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, administered through MoHRE, and u.ae states it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students.

Two consequences follow for a parent. The first is that anyone charging for private lessons is expected to hold the permit; u.ae states that individuals offering private tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so any figure quoted to you is unverified. The second is that the permit is free, which removes the usual excuse for not having one. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time.

A separate rule catches the most tempting arrangement of all. The permit carries a code of conduct that bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school, and ADEK's professional-ethics rules for Abu Dhabi school staff prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. Hiring your child's own class teacher privately is therefore the arrangement to avoid, however convenient it looks. Verify the current wording with the relevant authority before relying on any summary, including this one.

sections.heading: What to ask in a trial lesson, and what a good answer sounds like
paragraphs: A trial lesson is an interview, and most families waste it by watching politely. Four questions do almost all the work. Which phase do you think my child is in, and what in their work tells you that? Which criterion is costing the most marks right now? Band this piece of their writing and tell me what the next band asks for. What will I have in my inbox in three weeks that I do not have today?

Good answers are specific and slightly uncomfortable. A strong tutor will name a phase and then hedge it honestly, because one hour is a thin sample. They will point at a sentence rather than at a general impression. They will name a band and quote the descriptor language that put it there. And they will commit to something datable, which is the question most providers in this market cannot answer at all because nothing in their process produces a document.

Weak answers share a shape. They talk about building confidence, they praise the child warmly and vaguely, and they promise a grade. A promise of a specific grade is a reason to end the conversation, because no honest tutor will commit to a number in a criterion-referenced subject moderated by somebody they have never met. Confidence matters and it is a consequence of competence rather than a substitute for it. Ask for the band, and judge the tutor on whether they can give you one. Ask the same four questions of every tutor you trial, because the comparison between answers is more informative than any single answer is.

process.title: Send the report and one piece of real work
process.description: The last report with its criterion letters, plus one recent piece of your child's own written work in the language. That pair tells us more in two minutes than a long phone call does, and it lets the trial hour start with a diagnosis rather than with introductions and small talk.

process.title: Free trial hour that ends with a band
process.description: Sixty minutes with a specialist who samples all four criteria and finishes by banding a piece of work against the descriptors in front of you. You keep the written phase estimate and target criterion regardless of what you decide next. No card is taken and nothing renews by default.

process.title: Fix the slot around the activity calendar
process.description: We ask for the activity timetable rather than the school day, because that is what breaks bookings in Dubai. Weekly hour, or two short oral slots, in Gulf Standard Time. Communities with long bus runs are better served by a firm 6pm slot than an optimistic 4.30pm one.

process.title: Blind re-band at six to eight weeks
process.description: A fresh task, banded against the same descriptor set without reference to the earlier marks, compared with the week two and week three scripts. If the band moved, we keep going. If it did not, we change the method or the tutor, and we tell you which of the two we think it is.

whyPoints.title: Banded work, not progress calls
whyPoints.description: Every week produces a document with a criterion letter and a band number on it. A progress call is somebody's impression; a banded script is a thing you can put next to last month's and read for yourself without knowing any of the terminology.

whyPoints.title: The same measurement twice
whyPoints.description: Movement only means something when it is measured the same way on two occasions. We re-band blind at six to eight weeks against the identical descriptor set rather than comparing a generous mark in March with a harsh one in October.

whyPoints.title: Session shape set by the criterion
whyPoints.description: Speaking gets short and frequent slots, writing gets a weekly task with fast marking, reading gets volume. One session length for every criterion is an administrative convenience rather than a teaching decision, and it is usually the in-home economics talking.

whyPoints.title: A phase specialist from anywhere in the country
whyPoints.description: Because lessons are over live video, the choice is not limited to people who can reach Arabian Ranches by 5pm. For thin combinations such as Phase 5 French or Arabic reading for a non-Arab beginner, that difference decides whether a suitable teacher exists at all.

whyPoints.title: Recordings only with written consent
whyPoints.description: Oral sessions are recorded because playback is the fastest route to a Criterion C band move, and only where a parent has agreed in writing. Recordings are kept while the comparison is useful and deleted on request, with no reason required and nothing to negotiate.

faqs.question: Is there an in-home option for MYP language lessons in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Not from IB Gram. Home visits are a service offered only in India, and for UAE families every lesson is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. The in-home market in Dubai does exist independently and charges roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included, according to Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table and independent listings. The reason we do not compete there is supply rather than cost: the small number of people who can band a Phase 5 script against a descriptor should not be filtered by which communities they can drive to by five o'clock.

faqs.question: What evidence should a language tutor show us after a month?
faqs.answer: Four things. A written phase estimate from the first session with the reasoning attached. At least two practice tasks of different text types, each banded with a criterion letter and a band number. A short written note at the four-week mark saying what moved, what did not, and what the next six weeks will target. And a stated date for the next measurement. If a month passes with nothing readable in your inbox, there is no basis on which to renew, and the polite question to ask is whether banded work can start this week.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether my child's Criterion D writing is improving?
faqs.answer: Put two scripts side by side and look at three things rather than at the error count. Has the text type been handled correctly, meaning does a letter look like a letter and a blog entry like a blog entry? Is the register consistent from start to finish, or does it slide into chatty halfway down? Are there two tenses in use with control, rather than one tense and some hopeful attempts? Band numbers from a tutor tell you the same thing in shorthand, but these three questions let you check the tutor's judgement rather than take it on faith.

faqs.question: Why does my child's report grade not move when the work clearly has?
faqs.answer: Because an MYP report summarises judgements made across a whole reporting period, so improvement in week six is averaged with weeks one to five. There is a second lag as well: schools set assessment tasks when the unit calls for one, so a criterion may not be formally assessed for six or eight weeks and genuine change may simply not be on the record yet. Ask the subject teacher which criteria were assessed during the period and when the next task for each falls. Independent banded work every week is what lets you see the change earlier.

faqs.question: Can we see a marked script with the band written on it?
faqs.answer: Yes, and you should insist on it from the first fortnight. The format that works is the student's own piece of writing, the criterion letter, the band out of eight, two or three specific places in the text that put it in that band, and one sentence on what the next band requires. Anything vaguer than that cannot be compared against next month's version, which defeats the purpose. A tutor who cannot produce this is teaching the language rather than the subject, and in the MYP those two jobs are not the same.

faqs.question: How is speaking practice better over video than at our dining table?
faqs.answer: Three reasons, and they are practical rather than ideological. Video sessions can be recorded with consent, so a student hears their own oral from a fortnight earlier, which is the single most persuasive evidence of change available in this subject. There is no audience in the next room, and a thirteen-year-old will take risks with grammar when no parent is listening. And the descriptor can sit on screen beside the recording, so the student learns to hear their own work the way it will be marked.

faqs.question: Can lessons be recorded so we can hear the progress ourselves?
faqs.answer: Oral sessions can be recorded where a parent has given written consent, and the recordings are the clearest evidence a family gets in this subject. The useful comparison is the same prompt revisited every fortnight, because it isolates change in the student rather than difference in the task. Recordings are kept only while that comparison is useful and deleted on request without any reason being needed. If you would rather nothing was recorded, the sessions run exactly the same way and the evidence shifts to the banded written work.

faqs.question: What actually happens in the first four weeks of language tutoring?
faqs.answer: Week one is diagnostic: all four criteria sampled, a phase estimate written down, and one target criterion named. Week two sets and bands a practice task in that criterion. Week three sets a different text type and bands it the same way, which separates the student's ability from the difficulty of a single task. Week four is a written review and a six-week plan. Teaching happens throughout, but the first month is deliberately structured so that by the end of it you can read what you have bought rather than hope.

faqs.question: Does a tutor need a permit to teach my child privately in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is administered by MoHRE, and u.ae states it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible categories include school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. The same source states that individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so treat any specific amount quoted at you as unverified.

faqs.question: How do we check that a tutor holds the MoHRE private tuition permit?
faqs.answer: Ask to see it, the same way you would ask a contractor for a trade licence. MoHRE issues the permit through its smart app, website and e-services system under the service name for private tutor licensing, which lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, so a working tutor has no good reason to be without one. If somebody declines to show it, that is your answer. Verify the current requirements on mohre.gov.ae rather than relying on a summary, including this one, because process details change without much notice.

faqs.question: Is it allowed for a school's own teacher to tutor their own pupils privately?
faqs.answer: This is the arrangement to avoid. The MoHRE private tuition permit carries a code of conduct that bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school, and press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules describes Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff being prohibited from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. Whatever the convenience, the exposure sits with the family as well as the teacher. Confirm the current wording with the relevant authority before acting on any summary of it, and ask any tutor directly whether they teach at your child's school.

faqs.question: How does Ramadan change the MYP language tutoring schedule in Dubai?
faqs.answer: School hours shorten across Dubai, afternoons go quiet, and evenings reorganise around Iftar, so the late-afternoon slot that worked all year becomes the worst hour of the day for concentration. Most families move either to a morning or early-afternoon slot or to a session well after Iftar. Reading comprehension and written tasks travel into those slots better than oral practice, which needs energy. Agree the whole month's pattern in advance rather than cancelling week by week, because a month of cancelled sessions is where a term's momentum is usually lost. Schools also move internal assessment dates around the month, so ask the subject teacher what has shifted before planning the block.

faqs.question: What should we ask in a trial lesson for a language subject?
faqs.answer: Four questions. Which phase do you think my child is in and what in their work tells you that? Which criterion is costing the most marks? Band this piece of writing and tell me what the next band asks for. What will be in my inbox in three weeks that is not there today? Specific, slightly hedged answers that point at sentences are a good sign. Warm general praise and a promised grade are not, and a promised grade is a reason to end the conversation rather than negotiate on price.

faqs.question: What do we do if the tutor match is wrong after three weeks?
faqs.answer: Say so and we change it, and the banded work from those three weeks goes to the new tutor so the diagnosis is not repeated from scratch. Mismatches in language subjects are usually about pace or personality rather than competence, and a student who has stopped talking in sessions will not recover with the same tutor however good the teaching is. Tell us what specifically is not working, because that detail is what makes the second match better rather than merely different. There is no notice period and nothing to argue about.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover Arabic and a second language for the same student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth checking rather than assuming. Mandatory Arabic and a Language Acquisition choice such as French are different languages taught against the same four criteria, so a tutor strong on criterion technique can sometimes carry both where their second language is genuinely solid. More often two specialists are the better answer, with the criterion-level planning shared between them. What does not work is one generalist teaching both at a shallow level, which produces two mid-band profiles instead of one improving one.

dubai/ib-myp-language-acquisition-home-t.closingHeading: Ask for the band, then judge the hour
dubai/ib-myp-language-acquisition-home-t.closingBody: Send the last report and one piece of your child's own writing in the language. The trial hour is free and ends with a written phase estimate, a named target criterion, and a band on a real piece of work, and you keep all three whether or not you book anything further. After that, something readable arrives every week and a blind re-band at six to eight weeks says plainly whether the criterion moved. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time; IB Gram does not sell in-home visits in Dubai, and the exchange is a phase specialist and a faster feedback loop in place of a car in evening traffic.

intro.heading: Language Acquisition is four skills marked separately, and most students are weak in only one
paragraphs: MYP Language Acquisition is one of the eight MYP subject groups, and it is assessed differently from the way most Dubai parents expect. There is no single end-of-year paper producing a mark out of a hundred. A teacher judges four criteria instead: Criterion A listening, Criterion B reading, Criterion C speaking, and Criterion D writing. Each is marked on a band out of eight against published descriptors. The four eights add to thirty-two, and that total is converted into the 1 to 7 grade that lands on the report card.

That structure explains something parents find baffling. A child can speak comfortably with a grandparent in Beirut or Lyon and still come home with a 4, because Criterion B reading and Criterion D writing are each worth as much as speaking. The reverse happens too: a strong reader who freezes in a recorded oral loses a quarter of the available marks in one sitting. A tutor who treats the subject as one undifferentiated block of language misses this entirely. The first job is finding out which of the four is pulling the grade down.

The second structural fact is the phase system. Language Acquisition runs in six phases, from Phase 1 for a near-beginner to Phase 6 for a student close to studying the language as literature. Phases are not tied to year groups. A Year 9 student who joined a Dubai school last August can sit in Phase 2 while a classmate sits in Phase 5, in the same room, marked against different phase descriptors. Knowing your child's phase is the difference between useful tutoring and a tutor teaching the wrong level politely.

Dubai makes this busier than it would be elsewhere. KHDA counted 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering seventeen curricula in 2024-25, and IB programmes account for roughly 7% of that enrolment. Families move in mid-year, arrive from French-system, Indian and American schools, and land in whichever phase the placement test puts them in. Alongside all of that, Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies are mandatory in every Dubai private school whatever curriculum is licensed, so a non-Arab student is often carrying two unfamiliar languages at once.

This page is written for the parent holding a report card with criterion letters on it who wants to know what to do next. It sets out what each criterion rewards, where the marks go missing, how the MYP 5 ePortfolio works, what the Dubai market charges, and what a tutor is and is not allowed to do with portfolio work. Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in Dubai, and the trade is a phase specialist instead of whoever lives nearby.

dubai/ib-myp-language-acquisition-tutor.programmesIntro: MYP Language Acquisition sits in the middle of a ten-year IB continuum. What a tutor does in Phase 3 depends on what came before it in the PYP and on what the student is heading towards in the Diploma. These are the three programmes a Dubai family meets, with the Language Acquisition detail that matters at each stage.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Five years, eight subject groups, and criterion-referenced assessment throughout. Language Acquisition is compulsory for the whole five years, and the phase a student is placed in on arrival often follows them for several years unless somebody argues for a move. Assessment is continuous: tasks through the year are marked against the four criteria, and the final grade is a professional judgement against descriptors rather than an average of percentages.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai MYP schools run the programme alongside the KHDA mandatory subjects, so a non-Arab MYP student usually studies Arabic as an additional language plus a second Language Acquisition choice such as French or Spanish. That is two unfamiliar languages in one timetable, and it is the most common reason a Dubai MYP parent starts looking for language support in Year 8 or Year 9.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Language learning in the PYP is transdisciplinary and reported without criterion letters, so there is no numerical handover into MYP 1. Schools place students using their own entry assessment. A child who had thirty minutes of French a week in Year 5 and a child who had three lessons a week arrive in MYP 1 looking similar on paper and very different in a classroom.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai PYP schools vary widely in how much additional-language time they timetable. The KHDA mandatory subjects guidance works from a 40-minute lesson unit and advises that no mandatory lesson runs shorter than 25 minutes. Parents moving between Dubai schools at Year 6 should ask the receiving school which phase its MYP 1 cohort starts in, because the answer differs by school.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Language Acquisition becomes Group 2 in the Diploma: Language B at Standard or Higher Level, or ab initio for a genuine beginner. The jump is real. Language B assessment covers text types in writing, a listening component and an individual oral, and the ab initio route is closed to students with significant prior experience in the language.
programmes.countryNote: Which route a Dubai student can take is decided by their MYP phase history, and schools check it. A student finishing MYP 5 in Phase 2 or 3 is usually steered to Language B Standard Level; Phase 5 or 6 opens Language B Higher Level. A student who never studied French before MYP may still qualify for French ab initio, but only if the school's own record supports it.

dubai/ib-myp-language-acquisition-tutor.subjectsIntro: Dubai MYP schools offer different language menus, and the phase matters more than the language name. These are the Language Acquisition options IB Gram covers for Dubai students, with the thing that most often needs work in each. All of them are marked on the same four criteria, which is why a tutor who knows the descriptors transfers across languages better than parents expect.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: The script comes first. Most non-Arab students in Dubai hold a short conversation long before they read unvowelled text, which caps Criterion B. Sessions usually split between decoding without harakat and building the handful of verb patterns that carry everyday writing.

subjects.name: French
subjects.description: Dubai has a large French-system population, so phase placement is unusually wide. Marks go missing on agreement, the passe compose against the imparfait, and listening tasks where numbers and liaison blur the words. Criterion C improves fastest with recorded orals played back in the next session.

subjects.name: Spanish
subjects.description: The most commonly chosen beginner language in Dubai MYP schools after French. Early progress is quick, then Phase 4 arrives with the subjunctive and the preterite against the imperfect, and grades flatten. Writing tasks lose marks on register rather than on vocabulary.

subjects.name: German
subjects.description: Fewer Dubai schools offer it, so classes are small and mixed-phase. Case endings and word order dominate Criterion D, and students who have learned the rules often still write English sentence shapes with German words in them. Reading marks hinge on compound nouns.

subjects.name: Mandarin
subjects.description: Characters and tones are assessed through the same four criteria as any other language, which surprises parents. Criterion B reading is the usual ceiling. Handwriting expectations vary by school, and some Dubai schools accept typed input for written tasks while others do not.

subjects.name: English as an additional language
subjects.description: Taken by students whose school language of instruction is English but who are placed in Language Acquisition rather than Language and Literature. The work is mostly Criterion D: paragraph structure, text type conventions, and the gap between spoken fluency and written accuracy.

subjects.name: Hindi
subjects.description: Offered by several Dubai schools with large South Asian cohorts. Students who speak Hindi at home frequently sit in a higher phase than their Devanagari reading supports, and the mismatch shows up in Criterion B and Criterion D rather than in speaking.

subjects.name: Urdu
subjects.description: A smaller option, usually taught in mixed-phase groups. Script direction and the Nastaliq letterforms slow reading, so tutoring time is better spent on reading fluency before writing. Oral marks are often already the strongest of the four criteria for these students.

subjects.name: Phase placement and criterion diagnosis
subjects.description: A standalone piece of work rather than a language. One session samples all four criteria, produces a phase estimate against the published descriptors, and names the single criterion costing the most marks. Useful before deciding whether to commit to a term of weekly lessons.

sections.heading: What an IB MYP Language Acquisition tutor in Dubai does in the first month
paragraphs: The direct answer first. An IB MYP Language Acquisition tutor in Dubai spends the first session diagnosing rather than teaching. They sample all four criteria in one hour: a short listening task, a reading passage at and slightly above the current phase, three minutes of unprepared speaking, and one piece of writing. At the end they tell you which criterion is costing the grade. Everything after that aims at one criterion at a time, because the four are marked separately and move at different speeds.

The second and third sessions are where the phase question gets settled. Schools place students on arrival and rarely revisit the decision, so a student who has gained two phases of competence can still be marked against Phase 2 descriptors in Year 10. A tutor who can read the published descriptors will tell you whether the placement still fits, and what evidence the school will want before moving anyone. That conversation is worth more than a term of vocabulary drills.

By the fourth session there should be a marked task in your inbox with criterion letters and band numbers on it rather than a comment saying good effort. Ask for that from week one. A language tutor who cannot show you where a script sits in a band, and what the next band up asks for, is teaching the language rather than the subject. In the MYP those two things are not the same, and only one of them changes a report card.

sections.heading: The six phases, and why your child's phase matters more than their year
paragraphs: Phase placement is the most consequential decision made about your child in this subject, and it is usually made in a forty-minute test during their first week at the school. Six phases run from emergent to proficient, and a phase describes what a student can do with the language rather than how old they are. Two students in one MYP 4 classroom can be marked against descriptors two phases apart, and both marks are correct.

The practical consequence is that a grade means very little without the phase attached to it. A 6 in Phase 2 and a 6 in Phase 5 describe different students, and only one of them is on track for Language B Higher Level. Dubai's mobility makes mismatches common: families arrive mid-year from a French-system school, an Indian board school or an American curriculum school, and the placement test catches a snapshot during a jet-lagged week.

Ask the school three questions. Which phase is my child in, what evidence would move them up, and when is placement reviewed? Most Dubai MYP schools will review on request if there is a portfolio of recent work to look at. A tutor's job in that situation is to help the student produce stronger work across all four criteria so the review has evidence in front of it, then to teach at the phase above once the move happens. Put the request in an email rather than at a parents' evening, because a written request gets a written answer and a paper trail that survives a change of teacher in August.

sections.heading: Criterion by criterion: where the marks actually go
paragraphs: Thirty-two marks, four criteria, one grade. Each criterion is marked on a band out of eight against published descriptors, and the teacher's judgement concerns which band the work sits in rather than how many errors it contains. That changes what useful practice looks like. A student can halve their error count and stay in the same band if the task was the wrong text type, because the descriptor asks about the text type.

The pattern we see most often in Dubai MYP cohorts is a split profile: strong Criterion C, weak Criterion B. Children who hear a language at home or in the community speak it well before they read it, which is the normal order of acquisition, but the marking does not reward speaking twice. Half the available marks sit in reading and writing, and those two respond to deliberate practice faster than speaking does.

The reverse profile is just as common and more urgent. A student who reads well and freezes in a recorded oral can lose six of eight marks in one sitting, and the mark stands. Oral confidence is built by frequency rather than by length, which is why thirty minutes twice a week beats one long session for Criterion C. Everything in the table below is diagnosable inside a single session if somebody asks the right four questions. What it is not is visible on a report card, which gives you one number and no indication of which quarter of the subject produced it.

sections.heading: MYP 5 Language Acquisition is a moderated ePortfolio, not an on-screen exam
paragraphs: Parents who have heard about MYP eAssessment usually picture an on-screen examination. That is the format for several subject groups, but Language Acquisition is assessed through a moderated Language Acquisition ePortfolio: a collection of the student's own work, assembled during the final MYP year and judged against the phase descriptors. The practical difference is large. There is no single day to revise for and no paper to resit.

What matters instead is the quality and the range of work collected over months. A portfolio holding four pieces of the same text type, all in the same register, caps itself whatever the language is. A portfolio showing the student handle a formal letter, a blog entry, a report and an interactive oral at phase level gives a moderator something to award the upper bands to. Planning for that starts at the beginning of MYP 5 rather than in April.

This also changes what tutoring is for in the final year. The work must be the student's own, produced under the school's conditions, so a tutor's contribution is teaching the text types, coaching the student on the descriptors so they can judge their own drafts, and building the oral fluency the interactive component needs. Confirm your school's exact eAssessment registration and submission arrangements with its IB coordinator, because schools differ in which components they enter students for. Some Dubai schools register a full MYP certificate cohort while others enter selected subjects only, and that decision changes what the final year of Language Acquisition is working towards.

sections.heading: Arabic sits alongside your child's Language Acquisition choice, and it is not optional
paragraphs: In every Dubai private school, whatever curriculum is licensed, Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies are mandatory. The KHDA mandatory subjects guidance states that schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ between them.

For an MYP student this produces one of two timetables. An Arab student usually studies Arabic as a first language, often reported inside Language and Literature, and their Language Acquisition slot goes to French, Spanish or another choice. A non-Arab student usually studies Arabic as an additional language inside the Language Acquisition framework, and may be carrying a second language on top of it. Two unfamiliar scripts in one week is the single most common reason a Dubai MYP family calls about language support.

The same guidance sets the instructional-time basis: mandatory-subject time is calculated from a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and it advises that no mandatory subject lesson runs shorter than 25 minutes. It also states that using different or additional content for these subjects without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited, so tutoring on mandatory Arabic works from the school's own scheme rather than from alternative material. The guidance further requires that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects, which is a credential a parent can reasonably ask a school about.

sections.heading: Phase placement disputes, and how to raise one without a fight
paragraphs: Placement is reviewable in most Dubai MYP schools, and the review is a documentary exercise. Schools want recent work across the four criteria that sits clearly above the current phase descriptors, a class teacher who agrees with the reading, and a slot in the next cohort that can absorb another student. None of that is unreasonable. What sinks most requests is that the parent arrives with an impression and no evidence attached to it.

The sequence that works: ask for the current phase in writing, ask which descriptors the teacher is marking against, collect three recent marked tasks, and have somebody read those tasks against the phase above. If they sit in the upper bands of the current phase and the lower bands of the next one, the case is arguable now. If they sit mid-band where they are, a term of focused work makes a stronger case in March than an argument makes in November.

There is a real cost to getting this wrong in the other direction. A student pushed into a phase they cannot sustain spends two years in the lower bands and reaches the Diploma choice with a weak MYP 5 record, which closes Higher Level. Schools are cautious for that reason rather than obstructive. The useful question to a coordinator is not whether they will move your child, but what your child would need to show them by the end of this term. That question usually produces a list, and a list is something a tutor can work through.

sections.heading: What Language Acquisition support costs in Dubai
paragraphs: These are market figures, not an IB Gram price list, and each is attributed to the provider that published it or to Bestimate's Dubai 2026 rate table. The spread is wide for a reason: an hour of conversation practice and an hour of criterion-referenced MYP teaching are different products sold under the same word. Ask what a quoted rate includes, and over what session length, before setting two numbers side by side.

Language Acquisition sits at the lower end of the specialist band more often than a science or maths subject does, because the pool of people who can hold a conversation in French or Arabic is far larger than the pool who can band a Criterion D script against a phase descriptor. That is where parents overpay and underbuy at the same time. The question separating the bands is not whether somebody is a native speaker but whether they can show you how they would band a piece of writing.

For context on the household budget, KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package. Tutoring is one of the few education costs in Dubai with no cap applied to it, so the sensible way to set the number of hours is by what the target criterion needs rather than by what a provider is offering this month. Two sessions a week for a term costs more than four scattered sessions and achieves considerably more.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do with portfolio work
paragraphs: IB academic-honesty rules apply to everything inside an MYP ePortfolio, and the line is not vague. The student produces the work. A tutor teaches the language, teaches the text types, explains the descriptors and gives feedback on work the student has already written unaided. A tutor does not supply sentences to be copied, does not rewrite a submission, and does not sit alongside a student during an assessed task.

The practical test is whether the student could reproduce the improvement unaided next week. Explaining why the imperfect tense is wrong in a sentence passes that test; dictating the corrected sentence does not. Teaching the conventions of a formal letter passes; supplying the letter does not. Marking a practice piece against Criterion D and handing back band feedback passes; editing the real submission before it goes in does not.

This matters more in languages than in most subjects because the evidence is textual and the gap between a student's spoken level and a polished script is obvious to a moderator. A portfolio that reads as though somebody else wrote it invites questions no family wants. Several providers in this market sell finished coursework outright; that is a malpractice trigger for the student, and it is the one thing we will not do at any price. If a provider offers it to you, that tells you how they treat the rest of their teaching as well, and it is a reason to walk rather than to negotiate.

sections.heading: From Phase 4 to the Diploma: the Group 2 decision at the end of MYP 5
paragraphs: The MYP 5 record decides the Diploma language route and Dubai schools apply the rules tightly. Language B Higher Level is normally offered to students finishing in Phase 4 or above with consistent upper-band marks, Standard Level covers most of the rest, and ab initio is reserved for genuine beginners with the school checking prior study before allowing it. A student who studied French throughout the MYP will not be let into French ab initio.

That makes the second half of MYP 5 the point at which a term of focused work changes an actual option rather than a report-card number. The lever is usually Criterion B or Criterion D, because those are the two a school looks at when deciding whether a student can cope with Higher Level text handling. A student with strong speaking and mid-band reading is the classic Standard Level placement that could have been a Higher Level one.

The other route worth knowing about is Language A. A student in Phase 6, or a bilingual student whose school agrees, may take the language as literature instead, which is a different subject with different assessment. In Dubai this comes up most often for Arabic and for French. Ask the Diploma coordinator during MYP 4 rather than MYP 5, because the timetable blocks for the following year are built well in advance. A request made in May for a September start is usually too late to create an option that does not already exist.

process.title: Tell us the language and the phase
process.description: Send the language, the phase on the most recent report, and the criterion letter the school flagged. If you do not know the phase, say so; finding it is the first thing the trial session does. A line about the school and the year group lets us match somebody who knows that cohort's language menu.

process.title: Free trial lesson as a four-criterion diagnostic
process.description: Sixty minutes sampling listening, reading, speaking and writing, ending with a phase estimate and one named target criterion. You get the tutor's written read on where the marks are going whether or not you book anything afterwards. No card details are needed and there is nothing to cancel.

process.title: Agree the criterion target and the slot
process.description: One criterion at a time, a weekly or twice-weekly slot in Gulf Standard Time, and a stated marking turnaround for the task between sessions. Slots are set around the school run and the activity calendar; most Dubai families land between 4.30pm and 6.30pm on weekdays.

process.title: Review at the half-term, not at the report card
process.description: Every six to eight weeks the tutor bands a fresh task against the descriptors and you see whether the target criterion moved. Report cards lag real change by weeks, so this is the honest check. If the criterion has not moved, we change the approach or we change the tutor.

whyPoints.title: Matched by phase, not by year group
whyPoints.description: The phase decides the descriptors your child is marked against, so it decides what should be taught. We ask for it before matching, and where nobody knows it, the trial session produces an estimate against the published descriptors rather than a guess from the year group.

whyPoints.title: Tutors who can band a script
whyPoints.description: The test we apply is whether a tutor can read a piece of writing, name the criterion band it sits in, and say what the next band asks for. Fluency in the language is necessary and nowhere near sufficient for a criterion-referenced subject like this one.

whyPoints.title: A specialist instead of whoever is nearby
whyPoints.description: Because lessons run over live video, the pool is not limited to people who can reach your community before 5pm. A Phase 5 French specialist, or an Arabic teacher used to non-Arab beginners, is reachable from any part of Dubai on the same evening.

whyPoints.title: Honest about the academic-honesty line
whyPoints.description: We teach, we mark practice work, and we coach the student on the descriptors so they can judge their own drafts. We do not touch assessed submissions. That is stated here rather than buried, because this market contains providers who sell the opposite openly.

whyPoints.title: Transparent about what we cannot cover
whyPoints.description: Some phase and language combinations are thin, German at Phase 4 and Urdu at Phase 3 among them. If no specialist is free for your slot we say so and offer the nearest genuine alternative rather than filling the hour with a generalist and hoping.

faqs.question: What does an MYP Language Acquisition tutor actually teach in a session?
faqs.answer: One criterion at a time. Because the subject is marked on four separate criteria, a session that tries to improve all of them improves none of them measurably. A typical hour starts with the marked task from last week, works on the specific band descriptor the student is short of, then sets the next task in the same criterion. Criterion C sessions are mostly unprepared talking with playback. Criterion B sessions are mostly reading short authentic texts and justifying answers from the text. The session is useful when you can say afterwards which criterion it was for.

faqs.question: How are the four MYP Language Acquisition criteria marked?
faqs.answer: Each of the four is marked on a band out of eight against descriptors published for the student's phase, giving thirty-two criterion marks in total. The teacher decides which band the work sits in as a whole rather than deducting marks for errors, which is why a piece can be accurate and still land mid-band if it is the wrong text type or the wrong register. The four criterion totals are then converted into the 1 to 7 subject grade on the report. Ask your school which conversion table it applies, because the boundaries are set at programme level.

faqs.question: What is an MYP language phase, and how is my child placed in one?
faqs.answer: A phase is a description of what a student can do with the language, running from Phase 1 for a near-beginner to Phase 6 for a student close to literature study. Placement is almost always decided by a school entry assessment in the first week, sometimes a written test plus a short conversation. Phases are not tied to year groups, so a Year 9 class may contain students marked against three different sets of descriptors. Ask the school in writing which phase your child is in and which descriptors their teacher is using, because the grade is meaningless without it.

faqs.question: Can my child move up a phase part-way through the year at a Dubai school?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, by request and with evidence, though it depends on the school having capacity in the higher phase group. Schools want three or four recent marked tasks across the four criteria that sit above the current phase descriptors, plus agreement from the class teacher. Mid-year moves are more common in schools with large language cohorts, where a Phase 3 and a Phase 4 group both exist. Where only one group runs, the move is a change of descriptors rather than a change of classroom. Start by asking when placement is formally reviewed.

faqs.question: Is MYP Language Acquisition assessed by an exam or by a portfolio?
faqs.answer: By a moderated ePortfolio in the final MYP year, not by an on-screen examination. Several MYP subject groups are examined on screen, which is why parents assume all of them are, but Language Acquisition is judged on a collection of the student's own work built up over months and marked against the phase descriptors. That means there is no single revision date and no resit paper. It also means range matters: a collection of four similar pieces in one register will cap the grade however good each piece is. Confirm your own school's arrangements with its IB coordinator.

faqs.question: Which languages do Dubai IB schools usually offer in Language Acquisition?
faqs.answer: French and Spanish are the most widely offered in Dubai MYP schools, with Arabic as an additional language running in parallel for non-Arab students because Arabic is mandatory in all Dubai private schools. German and Mandarin appear in a smaller number of schools, often in mixed-phase groups. Several schools with large South Asian cohorts offer Hindi, and a few offer Urdu. English as an additional language is used where the language of instruction is English but a student is not yet ready for Language and Literature. Menus change year to year, so check the current option blocks.

faqs.question: Does Arabic as an additional language count towards the KHDA Arabic requirement?
faqs.answer: Arabic is mandatory in every Dubai private school whatever curriculum is licensed, and schools deliver it to non-Arab students through an additional-language route that can sit inside the Language Acquisition framework. KHDA guidance requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and prohibits combined classes because the expectations and the language of instruction differ. How your school maps its mandatory Arabic provision onto MYP reporting varies, so ask whether your child's Arabic grade is reported as Language Acquisition, as Language and Literature, or separately.

faqs.question: My child is in Phase 2 in Year 9. Should I be worried?
faqs.answer: Not by itself. Phase 2 in Year 9 is entirely normal for a student who started the language on arriving in Dubai, and phases are not year-linked by design. What matters is the direction of travel and the Diploma consequence. Finishing MYP 5 in Phase 2 usually points to Language B Standard Level rather than Higher Level, and may keep the ab initio route open. If Higher Level matters for a university plan, the two criteria to work on are reading and writing, and the time to start is MYP 4 rather than the spring of MYP 5.

faqs.question: How long does it take to move one Language Acquisition criterion band?
faqs.answer: For Criterion D writing, a band move on practice tasks within six to ten weekly sessions is a realistic expectation when the problem is text type, register or structure rather than vocabulary range. Criterion C speaking often moves faster with two short sessions a week because fluency responds to frequency. Criterion B reading is the slowest, especially where an unfamiliar script is involved, and a term is a fair horizon. Report cards lag the change, so judge progress on freshly banded work every six to eight weeks instead of waiting for the next report.

faqs.question: What do Dubai families pay per hour for MYP Language Acquisition support?
faqs.answer: Market rates in Dubai for a qualified subject tutor working online run roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with programme specialists quoted between AED 200 and 450 and premium named tutors above that. Unitors publishes IB tutoring from AED 200, TutorChase publishes AED 270, and Bestimate's Dubai 2026 rate table gives 200 to 450 and above for specialists. In-home visits carry travel and sit higher, around AED 180 to 500. Those are other providers' published figures rather than ours; ask us for current pricing and the free trial rather than reading a number off a table.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with my child's Language Acquisition ePortfolio?
faqs.answer: A tutor can teach the text types the portfolio needs, mark practice pieces against the criterion descriptors, coach your child to judge their own drafts, and build the oral fluency the interactive component asks for. A tutor cannot supply sentences, rewrite a submission, or work on an assessed task alongside the student. The honest test is whether your child could reproduce the improvement unaided a week later. Anything that fails that test is a malpractice risk carried entirely by the student, and no grade is worth it.

faqs.question: Should my child take Language B or Language A in the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Language B is the Language Acquisition continuation and covers almost all MYP students, at Standard or Higher Level depending on the MYP 5 phase and marks. Language A treats the language as literature and suits a Phase 6 student, or a bilingual student whose school agrees to it, often for Arabic or French in Dubai. The decision is a timetable decision as much as an academic one because option blocks are built a year ahead, so raise it with the Diploma coordinator during MYP 4. Bring marked work rather than an impression of fluency.

faqs.question: How can a tutor assess listening if the lesson is over video?
faqs.answer: Listening assessment is audio either way, so a video lesson loses nothing. The tutor plays the recording through shared audio, the student answers under timed conditions, and the transcript is revealed afterwards so the pair can see exactly where comprehension broke. Screen sharing makes that comparison easier than a printed sheet does. Over several weeks the useful output is a log of which question types keep failing, inference, numbers, negatives or speaker attitude, which is the thing that turns Criterion A practice into targeted work rather than repetition.

faqs.question: Does my child need a native speaker as their Language Acquisition tutor?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily, and native-speaker status is a weaker signal than parents expect. The subject is criterion-referenced, so the tutor has to know what a Phase 4 Criterion D descriptor asks for and be able to band a script against it. Plenty of fluent speakers cannot do that, and plenty of trained non-native teachers can. For Criterion C a confident model of the spoken language matters, so accent and fluency count there. The question worth asking in a trial is how a tutor would band a specific piece of your child's writing.

faqs.question: What happens if no tutor is free for our phase and language?
faqs.answer: We say so rather than fill the slot. Some combinations are genuinely thin: German above Phase 3, Urdu beyond the early phases, and Mandarin at Phase 4 are the ones that come up most often. Where no specialist is available for your time slot we will offer the nearest honest alternative, which may be a different weekday, a shorter twice-weekly pattern, or a tutor strong in the criterion you need rather than in the whole subject. We will also tell you when the answer is simply no.

dubai/ib-myp-language-acquisition-tutor.closingHeading: Start with the phase and the criterion
dubai/ib-myp-language-acquisition-tutor.closingBody: If you have a report card with criterion letters on it, you already have what a first conversation needs. Send the language, the phase, and the letter the school flagged, and we will match an MYP Language Acquisition specialist who teaches at that phase. The first lesson is free and is used as a four-criterion diagnostic, so you get a written phase estimate and a named target criterion whether or not you book again. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in Dubai, and the trade you get in return is a phase specialist rather than whoever happens to live within driving distance.
