dubai/ib-myp-language-and-literature-hom.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach MYP Language and Literature across Years 1 to 5: literary analysis, unseen text response, creative and transactional writing, and the spoken components. Each works from the student's own marked tasks and the school's set text list, with sessions scheduled in Gulf Standard Time.

intro.heading: The subject is not English as most parents remember it
paragraphs: A Dubai parent who studied English in a different system remembers comprehension questions, a novel read aloud across a term, and an essay marked for spelling and argument. MYP Language and Literature is a different animal. It is assessed on four criteria, each out of eight: criterion A analysing, criterion B organising, criterion C producing text, and criterion D using language. Content coverage is not one of them. A student can finish a novel, remember it in detail, write accurately, and still sit at 4, because the marks are awarded for what they do with the text rather than for knowing it.

Criterion A is where the subject actually lives. It asks students to analyse the content, context, language, structure, technique and style of texts and the relationships among texts, to analyse the effects of the creator's choices on an audience, to justify opinions and ideas with examples and explanations using subject terminology, and to evaluate similarities and differences by connecting features across and within genres and texts. Read that strand list and the common Dubai complaint resolves itself: the child who writes beautifully and scores 5 is summarising, and summary earns almost nothing here.

The second surprise for families is that this is not only a writing subject. Criterion C covers producing texts that demonstrate thought, imagination and sensitivity, with stylistic choices made in awareness of their impact on an audience. Criterion D covers varied vocabulary and sentence structures, register and style serving the context, accuracy in grammar, syntax and punctuation, accurate spelling and pronunciation, and the use of appropriate non-verbal communication techniques. Pronunciation and non-verbal technique are assessed, which means the subject includes spoken tasks and many students have never rehearsed one.

The third surprise is the breadth of text. A single MYP year might include a novel, a selection of poetry, a play, a film, a graphic text, a set of advertisements and a speech. Non-literary texts carry the same analytical demand as literary ones, and the comparative strand of criterion A asks students to connect features across genres. A student comfortable with novels and lost in front of an advertisement is not weak at English; they have met half the course.

Now the phrase in the search. Home tutoring in Dubai is a real market, and for a writing subject it has one clear advantage and one clear limitation. The advantage is a person in the room while a student writes, which for a reluctant twelve-year-old genuinely matters. The limitation is the text list. Your child's school has chosen particular set texts, and the useful tutor is one who has taught them or will read them, not whoever happens to live within a twenty-minute drive of your community.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai, in Sharjah or anywhere else in the UAE. Home visits are a service we run only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video, with the student's own drafts shared on screen and annotated versions returned between sessions. For a subject assessed through drafting and through spoken delivery, screen sharing and recording are not a compromise; they are a better record of what changed than a conversation in a living room.

dubai/ib-myp-language-and-literature-hom.programmesIntro: Language teaching changes character at each stage of the continuum, and the change is sharpest at the entry to the MYP and again at the entry to the Diploma. Knowing which transition your child is in explains most sudden drops in confidence.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Language is taught across the transdisciplinary themes, with reading, writing, speaking, listening, viewing and presenting treated as linked strands. Assessment is through portfolios and teacher commentary rather than criteria. Children produce a great deal of writing and receive very little formal analysis of other people's.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai PYP leavers often arrive in MYP Year 1 as confident writers who have never been asked to explain why an author chose a particular word. That is the whole of the first-term difficulty, and it is a format gap rather than an ability gap. It closes quickly once someone demonstrates what analysis of a writer's choice actually sounds like.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Five years of Language and Literature assessed on the four criteria, with literary and non-literary texts, written and spoken production, and a comparative demand inside criterion A. Years 4 and 5 add substantially longer analytical tasks and, in registered schools, on-screen eAssessment and the Personal Project running alongside.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools differ in how much of the set text list is fixed and how much a teacher chooses, so two students in the same MYP year at different schools may share no texts at all. Any tutor should ask for the list before the first session, because teaching analysis on a text the student is not studying wastes half the value of the hour.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: English A splits into Language and Literature or Literature, each at Standard or Higher Level, with external papers, an individual oral built on a global issue, and at Higher Level an additional essay. The analytical demand is a direct continuation of MYP criterion A, applied to a prescribed framework of readers, writers and texts.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai Diploma English teachers consistently report the same gap at the start of Year 12: students who can discuss a text fluently and cannot write a paragraph that tracks the effect of a specific choice on a reader. That is criterion A, unresolved from the MYP, and it is far cheaper and less stressful to fix before the Diploma starts.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Combines a career-related study with Diploma courses, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. Language development is explicit in the CP framework, and the reflective project requires sustained written argument with an ethical dimension, researched and defended by the student.
programmes.countryNote: Few Dubai schools run the CP, so families should confirm the structure with the school rather than from a tutoring provider. For a student whose MYP criterion C and D marks are strong but whose analytical writing is weaker, the CP's applied language demands can suit better than Diploma English A.

dubai/ib-myp-language-and-literature-hom.subjectsIntro: These are the text types and skill areas a Dubai MYP Language and Literature student will actually meet. The list matters because families often arrange support for novels and essays and leave half the course unaddressed.

subjects.name: The novel and the short story
subjects.description: Narrative structure, characterisation, setting, point of view and the pacing of revelation. Marks are lost when a student retells the plot in order rather than selecting the two moments where a technique produces an effect on the reader.

subjects.name: Poetry
subjects.description: Form, line break, imagery, sound patterning, voice and tone. The most common failure is identifying a device and naming it without explaining the effect, which is exactly the strand criterion A marks. Terminology without consequence earns nothing.

subjects.name: Drama and performance text
subjects.description: Stage direction, dramatic irony, entrances and exits, silence, and the difference between what a character says and what the audience knows. Students who read a play as a story miss the layer the examiner is looking for.

subjects.name: Film and moving image
subjects.description: Shot type, framing, editing rhythm, sound and mise en scene, analysed with the same vocabulary of effect as a written text. Frequently neglected in private tutoring, and consequently one of the quickest places to pick up criterion A marks.

subjects.name: Non-literary and media texts
subjects.description: Advertisements, speeches, articles, blogs, infographics, photographs and campaign material. Purpose, audience and rhetorical technique carry the analysis, and the criterion A strands apply unchanged. Half the unseen tasks a student meets are of this kind.

subjects.name: Graphic texts and comics
subjects.description: Panel layout, gutter, perspective, colour and the interaction of word and image. A strong equaliser for students who find dense prose difficult, because the analytical moves are identical and the entry point is lower.

subjects.name: Creative and transactional writing
subjects.description: Short stories, pastiche, dramatic monologue, letters, speeches, reviews, articles and blog posts. Assessed on thought, imagination and sensitivity, on stylistic choices with an awareness of audience, and on the selection of relevant detail.

subjects.name: Spoken and multimodal tasks
subjects.levels: Criteria C and D, MYP Years 1-5
subjects.description: Presentations, recorded commentaries, dramatised readings and discussions. Criterion D explicitly assesses pronunciation and non-verbal communication technique, which means delivery is marked and almost no student rehearses it.

subjects.name: Unseen text response
subjects.description: A text the student has never read, analysed under time pressure. This is where a student who has memorised essays on set texts is exposed, and where the transferability of their analytical habit is actually tested.

subjects.name: Comparative response
subjects.description: Connecting features across and within genres and texts, which is its own criterion A strand. A paragraph on one text followed by a paragraph on the other is not a comparison, and that single structural error caps a great many otherwise strong responses.

dubai/ib-myp-language-and-literature-hom.regionsIntro: These notes describe the in-home market across Dubai, since that is what the search phrase is weighing. Our sessions are delivered over live video, so the travel and scarcity described here does not apply to them.

regions.name: Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim
regions.note: Plenty of local English tutors and early session availability, so in-home arrangements are easy to make here. The scarce thing is a tutor who has taught your child's specific set texts, which is a different question from availability.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches and Dubai Hills Estate
regions.note: In-home visits are generally two-hour sittings because of the drive, and two hours is a long time to spend on one analytical paragraph. Drafting works better in shorter bursts with marking in between than in a single long session.

regions.name: Dubai Marina and Jumeirah Beach Residence
regions.note: High household turnover, so students frequently join mid-unit with a set text already half taught. Catching up on the text is cheap; catching up on the analytical habit the class has been building since September is the real task.

regions.name: Mirdif and Al Warqa
regions.note: A mixed curriculum catchment where many students have moved from systems that assessed English by comprehension and composition. Their criterion A marks start low and rise fast, because the problem is an unfamiliar format rather than weak English.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Al Barsha South
regions.note: Dense school cluster and competitive in-home supply, with heavy competition for the early evening slot. Spoken-task rehearsal is easier to schedule later, and it is the part of the course most often left until the week before.

regions.name: Jumeirah Village Circle and Dubai Sports City
regions.note: Newer schools with smaller English departments, where one teacher may cover several MYP years. Finding an in-home tutor who knows the chosen poetry selection or film text locally is largely a matter of luck.

regions.name: Business Bay and Downtown Dubai
regions.note: Apartment households where a quiet hour is genuinely scarce, which matters more for drafting than for most subjects. Later online sessions, once the flat has settled, generally produce more writing than an earlier visit does.

regions.name: Dubai Silicon Oasis and Academic City
regions.note: Students accustomed to working and submitting on screen, which suits a subject taught through annotated drafts. Recording a spoken task for review is also straightforward here, and recording is the fastest way to improve delivery.

regions.name: Emirates Hills, Meadows and Springs

sections.heading: The home tutor question, for a subject taught through drafts
paragraphs: A parent typing home tutor is asking for something specific: a person in the room with their child, at an agreed time, working on English. That is a legitimate thing to want and in Dubai it is readily available. The in-home market here is substantial, rates for a one-to-one visit are published at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the number, and visits are generally sold long because the drive has to be recovered across the sitting.

For this subject the in-home model has one real strength. A student who will not settle in front of a screen settles with an adult beside them, and writing is the activity most vulnerable to avoidance. A twelve-year-old with a blank document and a closed door will produce nothing; the same child with someone in the room will produce a paragraph. That is not a marketing point, it is the main reason in-home tutoring persists for younger writers, and families who need it are right to buy it.

The limitation is the text list. Language and Literature is taught through particular novels, poems, plays, films and media texts chosen by your child's school, and in many Dubai schools chosen by the individual teacher. Analysis taught on a text the student is not studying still transfers, but it transfers at a discount, and a tutor who has taught your child's actual texts is worth considerably more than one who has not. The chance that such a person lives within a short drive of any given community in this city is a matter of luck.

There is a second, less obvious limitation. This subject is assessed through drafting and through spoken delivery, and both are better served by a screen than by a sofa. A shared document holds draft one beside draft three with the annotations visible, which is a record a family can keep and a student can learn from. A recorded spoken task can be watched back, which is the only method that reliably improves delivery. Neither of those survives a verbal conversation in a living room, however good the conversation was. IB Gram delivers every UAE lesson one-to-one over live video, and there are no home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE.

sections.heading: What each of the four criteria assesses
paragraphs: The four criteria are published and specific, and a parent who reads them once will interpret a criterion sheet far better than one who relies on the subject grade. Criterion A, analysing, covers analysis of content, context, language, structure, technique and style and of the relationships among texts; analysis of the effects of the creator's choices on an audience; justification of opinions with examples, explanations and terminology; and evaluation of similarities and differences by connecting features across and within genres and texts.

Criterion B, organising, covers organisational structures that serve the context and intention; opinions and ideas organised in a sustained, coherent and logical manner; and referencing and formatting tools used to create a presentation style suitable to the context and intention. Criterion C, producing text, covers texts that demonstrate thought, imagination and sensitivity while exploring and reflecting critically on new perspectives arising from personal engagement with the creative process; stylistic choices made with awareness of their impact on an audience; and the selection of relevant details and examples to develop ideas.

Criterion D, using language, covers appropriate and varied vocabulary, sentence structures and forms of expression; writing and speaking in a register and style that serve the context and intention; correct grammar, syntax and punctuation; accurate spelling, writing and pronunciation; and appropriate non-verbal communication techniques. Two of those strands only make sense for spoken work, which is the clearest evidence in the descriptors that this is not a writing-only subject.

Put together, the four criteria explain the pattern Dubai families see most often. A student with accurate, varied, well-punctuated prose scores well on criterion D. If their paragraphs summarise rather than analyse the effect of a choice, criterion A sits three or four marks lower, and the subject grade lands in the middle while the writing looks strong. That profile cannot be improved by proofreading, more reading alone, or a tutor who corrects errors, and it is the single most common reason a Dubai MYP English grade refuses to move.

sections.heading: Criterion A: the sentence that separates a 4 from a 7
paragraphs: Almost all criterion A improvement comes from one structural change, and it can be taught in a single session and then practised for a term. A middling paragraph says what happens and names a technique. A strong paragraph says what the writer did, quotes the smallest useful piece of evidence, explains what effect that choice has on a reader, and then says why that effect matters to the argument the student is making about the text.

The difference is visible in a sentence. A 4 writes that the author uses a simile to describe the storm, which shows that the storm was violent. A 7 writes that the simile borrows its vehicle from machinery rather than from nature, so the storm arrives as something manufactured, which prepares a reader to see the later flood as a consequence rather than an accident. Same observation, different work. The second sentence does what the strand asks: it analyses the effect of the creator's choice on an audience.

Teaching it is mechanical. Take a paragraph the student has already written and marked, strike out the summary sentences, keep the quotation, and require them to write two sentences after it: one that names the effect on the reader and one that connects it to the wider argument. They will resist, because the summary felt like the content. Three or four paragraphs rebuilt this way and the habit begins to hold, and from that point every piece of writing in the subject improves at once.

The comparative strand needs the same treatment and is more often missed entirely. Evaluating similarities and differences by connecting features across and within genres means the comparison has to be inside the paragraph, not spread across the essay. One text, then the other, with a transition sentence between them, is not a comparison; it is two accounts. The fix is a sentence pattern that holds both texts at once, and students who learn it pick up the strand immediately because they already have the material.
bullets: Name the choice, quote minimally, explain the effect on a reader, connect it to the argument
Devices named without consequence earn almost nothing

sections.heading: Criterion C and the spoken tasks almost nobody rehearses
paragraphs: Criterion C, producing text, is the strand Dubai families most often leave out of a support plan, because English tuition is assumed to mean essays. It asks for texts that demonstrate thought, imagination and sensitivity, for stylistic choices made in awareness of their impact on an audience, and for relevant detail selected to develop ideas. A short story, a dramatic monologue, a speech, a review or a blog post can all be the assessed product, and each is judged on deliberate choice rather than on correctness.

That word deliberate is the whole of the teaching. Most student creative writing is competent and accidental: the sentences are fine, the choices were not choices. A session that asks why this is in the first person, why the paragraph breaks there, why that detail and not the other one, converts accidental competence into criterion C marks. It is also, in practice, the most enjoyable work in the subject, and students produce extra of it voluntarily, which is rare in MYP English.

The spoken component is the other neglected half. Criterion D explicitly assesses pronunciation and the use of appropriate non-verbal communication techniques, and criterion C applies to spoken production as much as to written. Dubai students typically prepare a presentation by writing it out and reading it aloud, which produces an essay delivered badly rather than a spoken text. The structure of a spoken argument is different: shorter units, signposting, deliberate repetition, planned pauses.

Rehearsal is the only method that works, and recording is the only honest form of rehearsal. A student who watches ninety seconds of their own delivery sees the things no amount of description would convey: the dropped sentence ends, the three fillers a minute, the absence of eye contact with the camera, the pace that doubles under nerves. Online delivery makes this trivial, which is one of the few places where a video session is straightforwardly better than a tutor in the room.
bullets: Criterion C marks deliberate stylistic choice, not correctness
Ask why first person, why that break, why that detail

sections.heading: Where criterion D marks actually go
paragraphs: Criterion D is the strand parents most often ask about and the one least likely to be the problem. It covers varied vocabulary, sentence structures and forms of expression; register and style serving the context and intention; correct grammar, syntax and punctuation; accurate spelling, writing and pronunciation; and non-verbal technique. A student whose work is accurate is already meeting several of those strands, which is why proofreading support so rarely moves a grade.

Where criterion D marks do go missing, the cause is usually monotony rather than error. Twenty consecutive sentences of the same length and structure meet the accuracy strands and fail the variety strand. The fix is a short exercise rather than a term of work: take a paragraph, rewrite it so that no two adjacent sentences share a structure, and the student hears the difference immediately. Variety is a skill of the ear, and it responds to being pointed out.

Register is the other recurring loss, and in Dubai it has a specific local cause. Students who work in English as an additional language, and students who read widely in informal digital registers, frequently write analytical prose in a conversational voice: contractions, direct address, rhetorical questions. None of that is an error, and all of it costs marks on the strand that asks for register and style serving the context and intention. It is also quick to teach, because the student already has both registers and simply needs to be shown which belongs where.

The table below sorts the common losses by what actually causes them, because the response differs sharply. Some belong in a five-minute exercise, some in a half-term habit, and some are not criterion D problems at all and will not improve however much proofreading is bought.

sections.heading: Set texts, unseen texts, and why the list matters
paragraphs: The first thing any tutor should ask for in this subject is the school's set text list, and the reason is practical rather than ceremonial. Analysis is a transferable skill, but it is learned on particular texts, and a student who has rebuilt four paragraphs on the novel they are actually studying walks into their next lesson able to use the work. A student who has rebuilt four paragraphs on a different novel has learned the method at a discount and still has to apply it cold.

In Dubai the lists vary more than families expect. Some schools fix the texts at department level, so every student in a year studies the same material. Others leave the choice to individual teachers, which means two children in the same year at the same school may share nothing. Generic revision guides are of limited use in either case, and they are close to useless in the second. The list is usually on the school's online platform or in the front of the student's exercise book.

Unseen texts are the other half and they are where an analytical habit is genuinely tested. A student who has memorised strong material on a set novel can produce a convincing essay and still collapse in front of an advertisement or a poem they have not met. That is not bad luck; it is the difference between knowing a text and owning a method. Regular practice on unfamiliar material, deliberately rotating between literary and non-literary genres, is what converts one into the other.

For a Dubai family arranging support, the implication is a simple sequence. Start on the set text, because that is where the next marked task is coming from and because success there builds willingness. Move to unseen practice once the paragraph structure holds, and alternate genres so that film, media and graphic texts get their turn. End each term with one comparative pair, because the comparative strand of criterion A is the one most students never deliberately practise.
bullets: Ask for the set text list before the first session; it changes what the hour can do
Dubai schools differ on whether texts are fixed at department or teacher level

sections.heading: Academic honesty when the assessed product is writing
paragraphs: In a subject where the assessed product is a piece of writing, the boundary between teaching and doing is easier to cross and harder for a parent to see. IB academic honesty rules require the work to be the student's own, and an arrangement that crosses the line in English leaves no trace of the kind a plagiarism check would catch, because nothing has been copied from anywhere. It has simply been written by the wrong person.

Legitimate help is extensive and worth paying for. Teaching what a criterion strand asks. Marking a draft and identifying precisely where it falls short, strand by strand. Modelling an analytical paragraph on a text the student is not writing about. Asking the question that makes a student notice their own missing explanation of effect. Teaching a referencing convention and checking a reference list for consistency. Rehearsing a spoken task and reviewing a recording. None of that touches authorship.

What must never happen is the supply of text. No sentences offered for insertion, no paragraph rewritten and handed back as a model of what theirs should say, no line-editing that continues until the voice has changed, no thesis provided for a student to argue. Editing to completion is the version families struggle to identify, because the ideas are still the student's and the document reads better. The strand that has been bypassed is criterion D, which assesses the student's own control of language, and bypassing it guarantees the same mark next time.

The test a Dubai parent can apply takes two minutes and needs no knowledge of the subject. Pick a sentence at random and ask your child why it is phrased that way and what it is doing in the paragraph. If they can answer, the help was teaching. If the answer is that the tutor fixed it, the mark on that piece is not information about your child and the arrangement needs changing. The same logic covers materials: official IB and examination board documents should reach a student through the school or the board's own site, not from a tutor's shared folder.
bullets: A tutor teaches, marks, models and questions; the student writes every sentence
Editing to completion is the version parents find hardest to spot
Bypassing criterion D guarantees the same mark on the next piece

sections.heading: From MYP Language and Literature into Diploma English A
paragraphs: At the end of MYP Year 5, students choosing to continue in the IB select English A at Language and Literature or at Literature, and at Standard or Higher Level. The difference is not difficulty in the abstract: the Language and Literature route keeps non-literary and media texts in play alongside literary works, while the Literature route concentrates on literary texts across periods and places. A student whose strongest MYP work was on advertisements, speeches and film usually belongs on the first; one whose strongest work was on poetry and the novel often belongs on the second.

What both routes assume is criterion A, matured. The Diploma asks for sustained analysis of how a writer's choices produce meaning for a reader, applied to texts the student has not seen and to a global issue of their own choosing in the individual oral. Students who arrive able to discuss a text fluently and unable to track the effect of a specific choice meet that gap in the first term. It is the same gap they had in MYP Year 4, and it is far cheaper to close before the stakes become external.

The oral component deserves particular mention, because it is where MYP spoken work pays off and where its absence shows. A student who has rehearsed and reviewed recorded spoken tasks through the MYP walks into Diploma oral preparation with a method. One who has only ever read an essay aloud starts from nothing, at the point in the programme when there is least time. Three or four MYP sessions on delivery, spread across Years 4 and 5, are worth more later than their cost suggests.

One honest caution to close on. No tutoring arrangement and no subject choice can promise a grade or a university place, and entry requirements vary by institution and programme, so the only reliable source is the admissions page of the specific university. Students whose qualifications will need Ministry of Education equivalency in the UAE should check the requirements through the Ministry's own channels rather than relying on any provider's summary, including this one.

process.title: Send the set text list and the last marked task
process.description: The text list determines what the sessions can usefully work on, and the criterion sheet determines which of the four criteria the teaching should target. With both in hand before the first lesson, the hour starts on analysis rather than on establishing what your child is studying.

process.title: Identify the criterion, not the symptom
process.description: Parents arrive describing grammar, structure or confidence. The sheet usually names criterion A. Naming the actual criterion before anything is booked prevents the most common waste in this subject, which is buying proofreading support for an analytical weakness.

process.title: Free trial built around one paragraph
process.description: One free trial per student, no card details taken, with the tutor who would continue. The session takes a paragraph your child has already written and rebuilds it: choice, quotation, effect, argument. You see the method rather than hearing it described.

process.title: Weekly sessions on the live text, with one task between
process.description: Each session works on the text the class is actually studying and ends with one short analytical task, marked against the named strand and returned annotated before the next lesson. Small enough to come back: a paragraph, not an essay.

process.title: Move to unseen texts once the structure holds
process.description: When the paragraph pattern is reliable on a set text, practice shifts to unfamiliar material, rotating between poetry, prose, media, film and graphic texts. This is what shows whether the method is owned rather than memorised, and it is the honest test of progress.

process.title: Add spoken rehearsal before it is urgent
process.description: Three or four sessions on delivery across MYP Years 4 and 5, recorded and reviewed with the student. Criterion D assesses pronunciation and non-verbal technique, and almost nobody rehearses them. Doing it early is cheaper than doing it the week before a Diploma oral.

whyPoints.title: Teaching aimed at the criterion the sheet names
whyPoints.description: Sessions start from your child's marked task and target the strand the teacher flagged, which is criterion A far more often than criterion D. That single piece of discipline redirects most of the money families waste on English support in this market.

whyPoints.title: Matched to your school's actual set texts
whyPoints.description: Because the tutor is selected from a national pool rather than a driving radius, the match can be made against the texts your child is studying. Analysis learned on the live text is immediately usable in class, which analysis learned on a substitute is not.

whyPoints.title: Drafts annotated and kept, side by side
whyPoints.description: A shared document holds draft one beside draft three with the annotations visible. That is both the teaching record and a model the student can reuse, and it survives in a way a conversation in a living room does not.

whyPoints.title: The spoken components treated as assessed work
whyPoints.description: Criterion D explicitly marks pronunciation and non-verbal technique. Rehearsal happens by recording and reviewing with the student, which is straightforward over video and is the only method that reliably changes delivery.

whyPoints.title: Clear academic-honesty boundaries in a subject where they blur
whyPoints.description: No sentences supplied, no paragraph rewritten as a model of what theirs should say, no editing to completion. We say this before the first session, because in a writing subject the breach leaves no trace and the student loses the strand anyway.

whyPoints.title: Delivery stated plainly, with limits disclosed
whyPoints.description: Lessons are one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. There are no home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE. If no tutor who knows your set texts has a workable slot, we say so and give a date rather than placing someone and hoping.

faqs.question: What does MYP Language and Literature assess?
faqs.answer: Four criteria, each marked out of eight. Criterion A, analysing, covers analysis of language, structure, technique and style, the effects of the creator's choices on an audience, justified opinions using terminology, and connections across texts. Criterion B, organising, covers structure, coherence and referencing. Criterion C, producing text, covers thought and imagination, deliberate stylistic choice, and selection of detail. Criterion D, using language, covers varied vocabulary and sentence structures, register, accuracy, pronunciation and non-verbal technique. Content coverage is not a criterion, which is why a student can know a novel thoroughly and still sit in the middle of the range.

faqs.question: What is criterion C, producing text, in MYP Language and Literature?
faqs.answer: It is the creative and transactional half of the subject, and the half most Dubai support plans leave out. It asks for texts that demonstrate thought, imagination and sensitivity while reflecting critically on new perspectives, for stylistic choices made in awareness of their impact on an audience, and for relevant details selected to develop ideas. The assessed product might be a short story, a dramatic monologue, a speech, a review or a blog post. The mark comes from deliberate choice rather than correctness, so the teaching is a series of questions: why first person, why the paragraph breaks there, why that detail and not another.

faqs.question: How is criterion A, analysing, marked in MYP Language and Literature?
faqs.answer: On whether the student explains the effect of a writer's choice rather than reporting what the text contains. A middling paragraph says the author uses a simile to show the storm was violent. A strong one says the simile borrows from machinery rather than nature, so the storm reads as manufactured, which prepares a reader to see the later flood as a consequence. The difference is one sentence of explained effect plus one connecting it to the argument. Devices named without consequence earn almost nothing, which is why terminology lists rarely help and rebuilding already-marked paragraphs usually does.

faqs.question: Which text types appear in MYP Language and Literature?
faqs.answer: Far more than families expect. Novels and short stories, poetry, drama, film and moving image, graphic texts and comics, and a full range of non-literary and media material: advertisements, speeches, articles, blogs, infographics, photographs and campaign material. Non-literary texts carry exactly the same analytical demand as literary ones, and roughly half the unseen tasks a student meets are of that kind. A student who is confident with novels and lost in front of an advertisement has met half the course, and the quickest available criterion A gains are usually in the half they have not practised.

faqs.question: Does MYP Language and Literature include a spoken assessment?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the descriptors make it explicit: criterion D assesses accurate pronunciation and the use of appropriate non-verbal communication techniques, neither of which can apply to writing. Spoken products include presentations, recorded commentaries, dramatised readings and discussions, and criterion C applies to them as much as to written work. Most Dubai students prepare by writing an essay and reading it aloud, which produces exactly the wrong thing. A spoken argument needs shorter units, signposting, deliberate repetition and planned pauses, and it needs rehearsing, which almost nobody does.

faqs.question: Where do MYP Language and Literature students lose marks on criterion D?
faqs.answer: Rarely on accuracy, which is what parents expect, and usually on variety and register. Twenty consecutive sentences of identical length and structure satisfy the accuracy strands and fail the one asking for varied sentence structures and forms of expression. The fix is a single rewriting exercise rather than a term of work. Register is the other loss, and in Dubai it has a specific cause: students who read widely in informal digital registers write analytical prose conversationally, with contractions, direct address and rhetorical questions. That is not an error, and it costs the strand asking for register and style serving the context.

faqs.question: Is MYP Language and Literature the same as English?
faqs.answer: It is the IB's English course for students working at or near first-language level, but it is not English as most parents studied it. There are no comprehension questions and no marks for knowing the text. The assessment is four criteria measuring analysis, organisation, text production and language use, applied across literary and non-literary material and across written and spoken production. A student who is a strong, accurate writer can sit at 4 or 5 because their paragraphs summarise. Recognising that the subject grade reflects analytical method rather than general English ability is usually the most useful thing a family learns about it.

faqs.question: How does MYP Language and Literature differ from MYP Language Acquisition?
faqs.answer: They are separate courses for different purposes. Language Acquisition is organised in phases for students learning a language, with a focus on comprehending and communicating in it. Language and Literature assumes the language is already secure and assesses what the student can do with texts written in it: analysis, organisation, production and control of register. A student placed in Language and Literature while still building the language will struggle for reasons that have nothing to do with literary skill. Check which course the school has actually placed your child in before arranging any support, because the right destination is sometimes the other one.

faqs.question: What does MYP Language and Literature expect in a comparative response?
faqs.answer: A genuine connection, held inside the paragraph. The criterion A strand asks students to evaluate similarities and differences by connecting features across and within genres and texts, and most responses fail it structurally rather than intellectually. A paragraph on the first text followed by a paragraph on the second, with a transition sentence between them, is two accounts rather than one comparison. The fix is a sentence pattern that holds both texts at once, naming a shared technique and then the difference in its effect. Students who learn the pattern pick the strand up quickly, because they already have the material.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with MYP Language and Literature coursework without crossing IB academic-honesty rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the line is clear once stated. A tutor may teach what a strand asks, mark a draft and show exactly where it falls short, model an analytical paragraph on a text the student is not writing about, ask the question that makes them notice a missing explanation, teach referencing, and rehearse a spoken task. A tutor may not supply sentences, rewrite a paragraph as a model of what theirs should say, provide a thesis, or line-edit until the voice changes. Editing to completion is the hardest version for a parent to spot, and it bypasses criterion D, which guarantees the same mark next time.

faqs.question: How does MYP Language and Literature feed into DP English A?
faqs.answer: Directly. Diploma English A is offered as Language and Literature, which keeps non-literary and media texts alongside literary works, or as Literature, which concentrates on literary texts, each at Standard or Higher Level. Both assume a matured version of MYP criterion A: sustained analysis of how a writer's choices produce meaning, applied to unseen texts and to a global issue in the individual oral. A student whose strongest MYP work was on speeches, advertisements and film usually suits the first route; one strongest on poetry and the novel often suits the second. The oral is where MYP spoken rehearsal pays off most visibly.

faqs.question: Does my child need to read more to improve MYP Language and Literature marks?
faqs.answer: Reading volume helps criterion D enormously and criterion A only indirectly, which is worth understanding before reorganising a household around a reading target. Wide reading builds vocabulary, sentence variety and an ear for register, all of which are criterion D strands, and it does so at no cost. What it does not automatically build is the habit of explaining the effect of a specific choice on a reader, which is the criterion A strand most Dubai students are losing marks on. A student who reads constantly and writes summary needs the paragraph structure taught, not more books.

faqs.question: What does an unseen text task look like in MYP Language and Literature?
faqs.answer: A text the student has never read, to be analysed under time pressure, and it can be literary or non-literary: a poem, a passage of prose, an advertisement, a speech, a photograph, a page of a graphic novel. The task tests whether the analytical method transfers, which is why it exposes students who have memorised strong material on a set text. Preparation is practice rather than content: regular short responses on unfamiliar material, deliberately rotating genres so that media and visual texts get their turn, with planning time constrained to something close to real conditions.

faqs.question: How long does it take to lift a criterion mark in MYP Language and Literature?
faqs.answer: Criterion B moves fastest, often two marks in three or four sessions, because it usually reflects a missing structure rather than a missing skill. Criterion D variety and register also move quickly, sometimes within a session, since the student already has both registers and needs to be shown which belongs where. Criterion A is slower and measured in months, because it is a habit of thought rather than a template. A realistic expectation is a visible change in paragraph structure within six weeks and a criterion mark movement over a term, confirmed on unfamiliar work rather than on a rewritten piece.

faqs.question: Why does my child get strong content marks but weak language marks?
faqs.answer: Two patterns produce that profile. The first is genuine monotony: accurate prose in which every sentence has the same shape, which satisfies the accuracy strands and fails the one asking for varied structures and forms of expression. The second is register, where an analytically sound response is written in a conversational voice. Both are strand-level issues with quick fixes. There is also a third possibility worth checking: if the school reports a single subject grade, what looks like strong content and weak language may be an averaging artefact, and the criterion sheet for an individual task will show the real distribution.

faqs.question: Does an MYP Language and Literature tutor need my child's school text list?
faqs.answer: It is the first thing they should ask for. Analysis is transferable, but it is learned on particular texts, and a student who has rebuilt four paragraphs on the novel they are actually studying can use that work in their next lesson. Dubai schools vary: some fix texts at department level, others leave the choice to individual teachers, so two children in the same year may share nothing. Generic revision guides are of limited use in the first case and close to useless in the second. The list is normally on the school's online platform or in the front of the exercise book.

intro.heading: Why English support is priced differently from mathematics
paragraphs: Ask five Dubai providers for a rate for MYP Language and Literature and you will get five numbers, and the spread will be wider than for any other core subject. That is not disorder; it is the market pricing a genuinely variable product. A mathematics session ends when the hour ends. A Language and Literature session generates a piece of writing that someone has to read and annotate before the next lesson, and that reading is the part nobody puts on an invoice.

The arithmetic is simple enough to do at the kitchen table. A 1,000-word analytical response marked properly against the four MYP criteria, analysing, organising, producing text and using language, takes a tutor between 30 and 45 minutes. Not skimmed and given a grade: read, annotated strand by strand, with specific rewrites indicated. If a tutor teaches a 60-minute session and marks one essay a week, they have delivered roughly 100 minutes of work for a one-hour fee. Either the hourly rate reflects that, or the marking is not happening, or the tutor is absorbing it and will eventually stop.

Which is why the first question about any Dubai quote for this subject is not how much, but what is inside it. Published market rates for a qualified subject tutor working online run roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with IB and IGCSE specialists advertised at AED 200 to 450 and a premium tier quoting AED 500 to 650. Monthly packages appear in the market at around AED 799 for eight online sessions. Those figures were compiled in October 2026 from published UAE provider pages and a Dubai rate survey, and they are market rates rather than ours. None of them tells you whether an essay gets read.

There is a second reason English prices high in this city, and it is about supply. A large share of Dubai MYP cohorts work in English as an additional language, and the demand for writing support is correspondingly heavy. At the same time the tutors who can mark MYP criterion A analysis properly, as distinct from correcting grammar, are a narrower group than the number of people who can teach English conversationally. Scarce skill plus heavy demand produces a firm price, and it also produces a lot of quotes from people who will correct spelling and call it literature tuition.

The third reason is less obvious and matters most in exam-heavy years. Writing improves slowly and visibly, which makes it easy to keep paying for and hard to know when to stop. A mathematics gap closes and the student can do the questions. A writing gap narrows over months, and without a criterion record a family can fund a weekly session for two years on the strength of a general sense that it is helping. The honest version of this subject's cost conversation includes a view on when to stop, which is in the last section of this page.

Everything here is delivered one-to-one over live video, with the student's own writing shared on screen, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE; that service runs only in India. The relevant consequence for price is that no part of the rate is travel, and the full fee buys teaching and marking.

dubai/ib-myp-language-and-literature-tut.programmesIntro: The cost of language support rises through the IB continuum, and it rises in steps rather than smoothly. Each step corresponds to a change in what is being assessed rather than to a change in reading difficulty.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Reading and writing develop inside transdisciplinary units, assessed through portfolios rather than criteria. Support at this stage is generally priced at the bottom of the Dubai market, often in 30 or 45-minute sessions, because there is no extended analytical writing to mark between lessons and the work is largely oral and practical.
programmes.countryNote: The cheapest and most effective language intervention in Dubai is still reading volume at home, which costs nothing. Families who pay for specialist English support in Year 4 or 5 are frequently buying reassurance. Where there is a genuine difficulty, a short diagnostic block is better value than an open-ended weekly arrangement at this age.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Language and Literature is assessed on four criteria out of eight each: analysing, organising, producing text and using language. Extended writing arrives from Year 1 and intensifies from Year 3, which is also where the market price steps up, because marking becomes the bulk of the work rather than an extra.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai rates for MYP English sit between general secondary support and Diploma specialist support. Years 3 and 4 are the efficient place to spend: the same analytical writing weakness addressed in the Diploma costs materially more per hour and arrives under time pressure, alongside the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: English A at Language and Literature or Literature, with external papers, an individual oral and a higher level essay in some routes. The published Dubai specialist band of AED 200 to 450 an hour applies here, and support is often sold as blocks of hours around the internal assessment rather than as weekly sessions.
programmes.countryNote: A Dubai rate survey estimates specialist exam-year monthly spend at AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for weekly one-hour sessions. Across two Diploma years that is a substantial household figure, and it is the clearest financial case for closing MYP writing gaps while the stakes and the rates are both lower.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Includes a personal and professional skills course and a reflective project, both of which demand clear extended writing, alongside any Diploma courses the student takes. Language support here is usually bought in short blocks around the reflective project rather than as a continuous arrangement.
programmes.countryNote: A small number of Dubai schools offer the CP, so the private market for it is thin and quotes vary more than for the Diploma. Confirm the course structure with the school's coordinator before agreeing any block of hours, since what is actually being assessed differs from the Diploma pattern.

dubai/ib-myp-language-and-literature-tut.subjectsIntro: Writing support rarely stays inside one subject, and a family's spend is often better placed than they expect. These are the areas where MYP Language and Literature work overlaps with other subjects, and therefore where one paid hour does double duty.

subjects.name: Analytical writing
subjects.description: Analysing content, context, language, structure, technique and style, and the effects of a writer's choices on an audience. This is the costliest strand to support because every attempt needs individual annotation, and it is the strand most often mistaken for a grammar problem.

subjects.name: Essay structure and organisation
subjects.description: Organisational structures that serve the intention, ideas sustained coherently, and referencing and formatting used appropriately. The cheapest strand to fix, because it responds to a taught template, and the one that produces the fastest visible mark movement.

subjects.name: Creative and transactional text production
subjects.description: Producing texts that show thought and imagination, making stylistic choices with an audience in mind, and selecting relevant detail. Priced like analytical work because the marking is just as individual, and often neglected because families associate English tuition with essays alone.

subjects.name: Grammar, syntax and register
subjects.description: Varied vocabulary and sentence structures, register and style serving the context, and accuracy in grammar, syntax, punctuation and spelling. The strand most tutors offer and the one least likely to be the actual problem for a student sitting at 4 or 5.

subjects.name: Oral and spoken assessment
subjects.levels: Criteria C and D, MYP Years 1-5
subjects.description: MYP Language and Literature assesses speaking as well as writing, including non-verbal technique. Rehearsal time is cheap to deliver, since nothing needs marking afterwards, so it is worth asking for explicitly rather than paying essay rates for it.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies written work
subjects.description: Criterion C in humanities marks communication and documentation of sources. A student whose writing improves in English picks up those marks without additional hours, which is why English support is often the better buy when both subjects are weak.

subjects.name: Sciences extended response
subjects.description: Criterion D in Sciences asks for balanced discussion of applications of science, and the evaluation strands demand sustained argued paragraphs. Families paying separately for science writing support are usually paying twice for the same skill.

subjects.name: Language Acquisition
subjects.description: A separate course from Language and Literature, and frequently the correct and cheaper destination for a student in the early years of English. Paying literature rates for what is a phase-appropriate language need is a common and avoidable expense in Dubai.

subjects.name: Personal Project writing
subjects.description: The Personal Project report and process journal are extended writing with their own criteria. Support is process coaching and is usually sold as a short block; any arrangement implying the report will be produced for the student is both wasted money and an academic-honesty risk.

subjects.name: Arabic as a first or additional language
subjects.description: Required by KHDA alongside the licensed curriculum and separately reported, with its own teaching requirements. It is a separate spend from MYP English, and families should price and plan the two independently rather than looking for one tutor for both.

sections.heading: The marked essay is the real unit of cost
paragraphs: Everything about pricing this subject becomes clearer once you stop counting hours and start counting marked pieces. A session is a conversation about writing; a marked essay is the thing that changes the writing. The market quotes hours because hours are easy to invoice, but for MYP Language and Literature the hour is the smaller half of the work and the half that is less connected to the mark.

Consider what marking one 1,000-word analytical response actually involves if it is done properly. Reading it once for sense. Reading it again against criterion A, checking whether the student has analysed the effect of the writer's choices rather than summarised the plot, and whether opinions are justified with examples and terminology. Checking criterion B for organisational structure, sustained coherence and referencing. Checking criterion C for selection of relevant detail and stylistic choices. Checking criterion D for register, variety and accuracy. Then writing annotations that say what to do instead, not merely what is wrong. Thirty to forty-five minutes, and the lower end of that is for a practised marker.

A family who understands this can price support sensibly. One session a week plus one marked essay is roughly 100 minutes of tutor work, and a quote that reflects it will look higher per hour than a quote that does not include marking. That does not make it worse value. The useful comparison is cost per marked piece, which puts two very different-looking quotes on the same scale, and frequently reverses the apparent ranking.

It also opens a cheaper option that almost nobody in the Dubai market offers explicitly. For a student in MYP Year 4 or 5 who can read written feedback and act on it, marking without a live session is materially less expensive per piece and often just as effective. Buying one session a month and three marked essays, rather than four sessions and no marking, is a different and sometimes better product for the same money.

sections.heading: Reading a Dubai quote for MYP English, line by line
paragraphs: Two quotes AED 180 apart can describe the same product or two entirely different ones, and the difference is almost never in the headline figure. Six line items decide it, and asking about all six takes one message. The first is session length: many Dubai providers quote per session and run 45 or 50 minutes, which changes the effective hourly figure by a third without anybody saying anything misleading.

The second is marking, which for this subject is the decisive item. Ask how many minutes the tutor allows per piece and what the annotation looks like. A provider who answers in minutes is telling you they have thought about it. A provider who says marking is included without qualification is usually describing a comment and a grade. The third is reading time: if your child's set text is a novel the tutor has not taught, somebody has to read it, and that either happens unpaid, inside your session, or not at all.

The fourth is turnaround. A marked essay that arrives after the school deadline has no effect on the grade and limited effect on the learning. Agree a turnaround in advance, in days, and check it against the school's submission dates. The fifth is cancellation: what notice is required, and what happens in an assessment week when your child genuinely cannot attend. The sixth is tax: ask only whether the specific figure quoted is the figure you will pay, and do not accept a general statement about how tuition is treated.

One line is usually absent and worth adding. Who is the named tutor, and have they taught MYP Language and Literature specifically, as opposed to English generally. The honest test is to ask them to describe the difference between criterion A and criterion D. Someone who has marked to these criteria will answer immediately. Someone who corrects grammar and discusses themes will not, and that is a AED 200 answer you can get for free before booking anything.

sections.heading: Budgeting a year across the Dubai academic calendar
paragraphs: Spend in this subject should not be flat across the year, because the work is not. A UAE school year running from late August or early September to the start of July has a predictable rhythm: a settling term, a heavy middle with major written tasks, a Ramadan period that reshapes the week, an assessment-dense spring, and a long summer. Planning support to that rhythm rather than committing to the same weekly session for ten months is the single largest saving available, and it is one almost no provider will suggest.

The first term is diagnostic. Two or three sessions and two marked essays will establish which criterion strand is weak, and in a surprising number of cases the answer is criterion B, organisation, which responds quickly to a taught structure. Spending heavily in September, before anyone knows what the problem is, is how families end up funding a general English arrangement for a specific analytical weakness.

The middle of the year is where the money belongs. Major written tasks land, the set texts are properly underway, and marked feedback has time to change the next piece of work. Ramadan then moves the week: school hours shorten, energy patterns change, and sessions are best scheduled post-Iftar. Providers who cannot flex to that effectively lose a month, and a family on a prepaid package loses it with them. Per-session payment makes that month cost nothing.

The spring is assessment-dense, which is when demand and rates firm up across the Dubai market, and when the useful support shifts from new teaching to timed practice and oral rehearsal. Summer is the cheapest effective window of the year and the most neglected: reading volume costs nothing, and three or four marked pieces across July and August put a student into the next year ahead rather than behind. sections.heading: Why two Dubai quotes for the same lesson differ by AED 200
paragraphs: Five things explain almost the whole spread, and none of them is quality in the abstract. The first is who the tutor is. Dubai's market runs from university students working online, with published entry rates from roughly AED 33 to 65 an hour, through qualified subject teachers at AED 150 to 300, to specialists at AED 200 to 450 and a premium tier quoting AED 500 to 650. A AED 90 quote and a AED 350 quote are usually two different tiers rather than two prices for the same thing.

The second is format. An in-home visit carries travel inside the number, which in Dubai means anything from 30 to 150 minutes of driving depending on the community, recovered across the sitting. That is why the same tutor's in-home and online rates can differ by AED 80 to 200, and why in-home work tends to be sold in two-hour blocks. The third is marking, discussed above, and it is the item most likely to be present in the higher quote and absent from the lower one.

The fourth is risk transfer. A provider offering a replacement tutor, a free trial, flexible cancellation and no prepaid block is carrying commercial risk that a provider demanding a term's fees in advance is not. That shows up in the rate, and it is worth paying for if your child's schedule is unpredictable, which in an MYP year with trips, assessments and travel it generally is.

The fifth is simply market position, and it should be treated sceptically. Examiner claims are frequently advertised and rarely evidenced, and no tutor's examiner experience grants access to marking decisions, grade boundaries or unreleased paper content. A premium justified only by a label, with no board and no year attached, is a premium for the label. Ask what specifically is being claimed, and let the answer decide whether the AED 200 difference is buying anything.
