process.title: Send two marked physics scripts
process.description: Two is better than one, because the error types that appear in both are the real ones. Photographs are fine. Include the rubric or strand marks if the school publishes them. We read them before the first session and arrive with a counted inventory rather than a general plan, which is also how you judge whether we read them at all.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson, with the condition stated
process.description: One forty-five-minute online session at no charge, no card details taken, nothing to cancel afterwards. The tutor works on the scripts you sent and finishes by naming the error types, their counts and what a twelve-week plan would target. You keep that written inventory whether or not you book anything further.

process.title: Agree a plan counted backwards from the school's date
process.description: Ask the school when the next physics summative or end-of-year examination falls, and count back from it. The plan sets the baseline early, puts the redraft at week eight, reviews at week six, and teaches nothing new in the final three weeks. Pause weeks for school examinations and Ramadan go in at this stage, not later.

process.title: Mark a piece every fortnight and keep the tally
process.description: Every second session uses a piece of the student's own work, marked by error type against the school rubric, with the tally sent in the session note. Six marked pieces a term is the audit trail. It is also what makes a parent-teacher meeting at school a conversation about specifics rather than about impressions.

process.title: Review at week six and at week twelve, honestly
process.description: At week six the target strand can change, because first diagnoses are sometimes wrong. At week twelve we look at a school-marked piece and decide whether to continue weekly, drop to fortnightly maintenance or stop. Stopping is a normal outcome, and a tutor who never recommends it is not reading their own evidence.

whyPoints.title: Progress you can inspect without knowing physics
whyPoints.description: Marked scripts with error types counted, a redraft beside its original, and a school-marked piece at week twelve. Those three artefacts let a parent judge an arrangement in five minutes. The alternative, which is most of this market, is waiting for a report that arrives after the term it describes has ended.

whyPoints.title: Diagnosis before purchase
whyPoints.description: A three-session diagnostic block exists because the right answer is sometimes not physics at all. Where the inventory shows rearrangement and unit errors dominating, the useful intervention is a short arithmetic-habit block, not a year of physics content. We will say so, including when it means selling fewer hours.

whyPoints.title: A written note after every single session
whyPoints.description: Four lines: strand worked, what the student got wrong in the session, work set, what the next marked piece should show. Dubai parents are often at work when sessions run, and the student's own account of the lesson is not an instrument you can plan with.

whyPoints.title: No promises about grades, by policy
whyPoints.description: The MYP scores four criteria out of 8 each and the school converts the total using its own boundary table. Anyone promising a grade is describing something they cannot control. What we promise is a named strand, fortnightly marked evidence and an honest review at week six and week twelve.

whyPoints.title: Clear about what stays at school
whyPoints.description: Practical work belongs in the school laboratory with school apparatus and supervision. Design and data processing are where criterion marks live and where a shared screen genuinely helps. We also hold no accreditation from KHDA, the IB or any examination board, and we state that rather than implying otherwise.

faqs.question: How will I know by half term whether physics tutoring is working?
faqs.answer: Ask for three things at week four: the baseline script from week one, the second script, and the error tally for both. If the most frequent error type has fallen, the diagnosis was right and the plan should continue. If it has not, the target strand is probably wrong and should change at the week-six review rather than at the end of term. Week eight should add a redraft beside its original, and week twelve a school-marked piece. None of that requires you to read physics, only to compare two counts.

faqs.question: What are the most common mistakes in MYP physics scripts?
faqs.answer: Six types cover most lost marks, and only one is a knowledge gap. Unit and conversion errors come first, usually centimetres substituted where metres are expected. Then rearrangement, particularly when the unknown sits in the denominator. Then gradient misreading, where a single coordinate pair is divided instead of change over change. Then unprocessed data plotted raw. Then a conclusion that describes the graph without naming the hypothesis. The sixth is the genuine content error, such as explaining refraction as bending rather than as a change of speed.

faqs.question: Can a tutor tell me how many marks my child will gain in physics?
faqs.answer: No, and anyone who does is describing something outside their control. What a tutor can do is name the strand where marks are mechanically recoverable and show the evidence of recovery fortnightly. In MYP physics that strand is usually criterion C, because unprocessed data and conclusions that describe rather than conclude are structural losses rather than knowledge ones. Ask the MYP coordinator for the boundary table the school uses to convert the total out of 32 into a 1 to 7 grade, and you can see how far the next grade actually is.

faqs.question: Why does my child get physics right in class and wrong on tests?
faqs.answer: Usually because classwork is scaffolded and tests are not, and the scaffold hides the arithmetic. In class the equation is already rearranged on the board and the units are consistent. Under test conditions the student must rearrange before substituting and convert first, and those two operations are where the errors live. The test for this is cheap: give them six mixed-unit calculations with the unknown in the denominator, untimed. If accuracy collapses, the problem is habits rather than physics, and that is a four to six session fix.

faqs.question: Is it worth tutoring MYP physics if my child is already getting a 6?
faqs.answer: Often fortnightly maintenance rather than weekly sessions. A student at 6 usually has secure content and one or two strand-level habits still leaking marks, most often unit discipline under time pressure or an evaluation that names nothing fixable. One session every two weeks reviewing a marked piece holds the habits and catches drift, which is the usual pattern after a successful intervention. It is also considerably cheaper. Buying a weekly slot for a student at 6 generally pays for revision they would have done anyway.

faqs.question: How does an online tutor handle the physics practical work?
faqs.answer: It does not, and should not. MYP practical work is done at school, supervised, with the school's apparatus. What a tutor does is the design before it and the processing after it, which is where criteria B and C are actually marked. Before the lesson, the plan is pushed for a mechanism in the hypothesis and a method of control for each variable. Afterwards, the data goes into a spreadsheet live, repeats are averaged, a derived quantity is calculated and a line of best fit is argued over. Simulators cover variable-control demonstrations.

faqs.question: What should a tutor's written note after a physics session contain?
faqs.answer: Four things, in four lines. The strand or error type worked on, named rather than described as a topic. What the student got wrong during the session, because that is the live diagnostic. What has been set before next time. And what the next marked piece should show if the work is landing. A note saying we covered forces and he is improving cannot be checked against anything. If two notes in a row read like that, ask directly for the error tally, and the answer tells you what you need to know.

faqs.question: Does an MYP physics tutor in Dubai need a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tuition in the UAE requires the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Those operating without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and because no schedule of fines is published, any specific figure you read should be treated with caution. Since it costs nothing, ask to see it.

faqs.question: My child is strong at physics but weak at the maths inside it. What should we buy?
faqs.answer: Probably mathematics, aimed at four operations rather than at a syllabus: rearranging equations with the unknown in the denominator, standard form, unit conversion and gradient as a rate of change. That is a six to eight session block, not a year. A diagnostic that counts error types will show this clearly, because the tally will be dominated by rearrangement and conversion with very few mechanism errors. Buying physics content teaching for that profile means paying for explanations the student already understands while the actual obstacle goes untouched.

faqs.question: How long before a school-set physics mark actually moves?
faqs.answer: Usually a full term, which is why twelve weeks is the right unit for judging an intervention. Four weeks is long enough to see whether the diagnosis was right, measured in the tutor's own error tally. Eight weeks is long enough to see corrections appear in the student's own redraft. But the school's marks depend on the school's assessment calendar, and the next summative on the targeted strand may not arrive until week ten or later. Agree in advance which school-set piece will be the test, so neither side moves the goalposts.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both MYP physics and MYP mathematics?
faqs.answer: Frequently yes, and for this particular pairing it is often the better purchase. The arithmetic that damages MYP physics scripts is the same arithmetic assessed in MYP mathematics: rearrangement, standard form, ratio, gradient. A tutor working across both can fix the operation once and then apply it in the physics context immediately, which is faster than two separate tutors approaching it from opposite sides. Ask for the error tally to be kept across both subjects so you can see the same error type falling in two places.

faqs.question: What changes for physics when the MYP 5 assessment is taken on screen?
faqs.answer: Where a school registers for eAssessment, the format costs physics students more than it costs biology students, because physics thinking usually involves sketching and rearranging in the margin and the screen removes that space. Preparation has to be timed, typed and on screen, with data read from supplied tables rather than from tables the student drew. We also drill planning a long answer in two lines before typing. Confirm with the MYP coordinator whether the cohort sits eAssessment or internal examinations, because the preparation differs.

faqs.question: Should we pause physics tutoring during school examination weeks?
faqs.answer: Yes, almost always. A student revising for six or seven subjects does not benefit from a seventh commitment in the same week, and a session squeezed into that week tends to be low value for both sides. Pause rather than cancel, so the slot is still there afterwards. The same applies during Ramadan, where sessions work better moved to post-Iftar or a late weekend morning and shortened to forty-five minutes. Plan both interruptions at the start of the term and the twelve-week plan usually survives intact.

faqs.question: What if the evidence at week twelve shows no improvement at all?
faqs.answer: Then something in the arrangement is wrong, and the useful response is to identify which thing rather than to add hours. Three candidates: the diagnosis was wrong and the target strand was never the problem, the slot was unworkable and sessions kept moving, or the student is not engaging and no amount of teaching fixes that from outside. The error tally and the session notes usually distinguish them. We would rather stop and say so than roll a plan into a second term that the first term's evidence does not support.

dubai/ib-myp-physics-tutor.closingHeading: Send two marked scripts and ask for the tally
dubai/ib-myp-physics-tutor.closingBody: The useful question about physics tutoring is not whether a tutor is good. It is what you will be able to see at week four, week eight and week twelve, and whether anyone has written it down. Send two marked physics scripts and the rubric, take the free trial lesson, and read the error inventory that follows it. If the inventory names the error types and their counts, you have the baseline every later comparison depends on. If it does not, you have learned something useful at no cost. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, scheduled around the Dubai school week, with in-home visits offered only in India.

dubai/ib-myp-sciences-home-tutor.tutorsIntro: These tutors work on MYP science tasks rather than on topics in the abstract: an investigation plan that needs its variables named, a data table that needs correct processing, a reflection that needs a cited source. Send the task sheet and the rubric before the first session so the hour starts on the actual problem.

intro.heading: A 4 on a science task tells you almost nothing, and that is the real problem
paragraphs: An MYP science report line gives a grade and a comment. It rarely says which of four criteria produced the number, and parents in Dubai are then asked to buy help against a diagnosis nobody has made. The programme assesses sciences against criterion A, knowing and understanding; criterion B, inquiring and designing; criterion C, processing and evaluating; and criterion D, reflecting on the impacts of science. Each is marked from 0 to 8, for a total out of 32. Three of those four have almost nothing to do with how much science the student knows.

That is why the advice to get a science tutor so often disappoints. A student losing marks on criterion B is not short of content. They have written a hypothesis that predicts an outcome without giving the scientific reasoning behind it, or listed three variables without saying which is controlled and how. A student losing marks on criterion C has usually drawn a correct graph and then written a conclusion that restates the data instead of answering the hypothesis, and merged the evaluation into the same paragraph so neither strand is credited. These are specific, repeatable, teachable errors.

They are also strand-level errors, which is the part that matters for anyone paying by the hour. Each MYP criterion is split into strands, and the mark bands describe what a student must do in each one. An investigation can be scientifically sound and still sit in the 3 to 4 band because one strand is missing entirely. The fix is often a single sentence added in the right place, repeated until it becomes habit. Six weeks of that work changes every investigation the student writes for the rest of the programme, which is the opposite of a topic-by-topic revision plan.

The home-tutor question deserves a straight answer too. In-home MYP science tuition does exist in Dubai and the published bands for it run from roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour, with monthly packages advertised around AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour visits. What you are paying for in that premium is travel, and what you are accepting is a tutor drawn from whoever can reach your community at 5pm. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-home teaching is a service we run only in India. Everything here is one-to-one over live video.

For criterion work that is not a compromise, it is closer to an advantage. Screen sharing puts the student's own document, the school rubric and the marked script side by side, which is exactly how a strand-level correction is made. Graph work is done live in a spreadsheet the student keeps. A simulation can be run twice with one variable changed while the student narrates the control. None of that is easier across a kitchen table, and the choice of tutor stops being a function of who lives within a twenty-minute drive of your villa.

dubai/ib-myp-sciences-home-tutor.programmesIntro: The same four criteria run through MYP sciences from Year 7 to Year 11, but what a strand looks like at MYP 2 and at MYP 5 is not remotely the same thing. Here is how the demand escalates across the programmes a Dubai student moves through, and what each step asks of a science task.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme, MYP 1-3
programmes.description: Integrated sciences taught by one teacher, with criterion tasks scaffolded heavily: the variables may be given, the table may be pre-drawn, the graph axes may be labelled already. Marks are lost on precision rather than on structure, typically units omitted, scales chosen badly, and conclusions that describe the trend without referring to the hypothesis at all.
programmes.countryNote: Most Dubai continuum schools begin MYP at Year 7 with students arriving from both the PYP and from British primaries across the city. The two groups fail differently in their first year: PYP students are comfortable inquiring and vague about method, while British-primary students write tidy methods and resist designing their own. A tutor who asks which route the student came from is reading the problem correctly.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme, MYP 4-5
programmes.description: Biology, chemistry and physics usually separate, the scaffolding is withdrawn, and the student designs investigations from a bare prompt. Criterion B now expects a hypothesis with reasoning drawn from scientific understanding, a full variable list, and a method another student could follow. Criterion D expects a specific problem, a discussion of implications and sources documented in the school's referencing style.
programmes.countryNote: This is the band Dubai families ask about most, and the one where school-set deadlines across three sciences collide. A chemistry criterion C task and a physics criterion B plan due in the same week is a scheduling problem as much as an academic one, which is why a fixed weekly slot and a written note after each session matter more here than extra hours.

programmes.name: MYP 5 on-screen eAssessment
programmes.description: Schools that register for eAssessment sit on-screen examinations in sciences alongside ePortfolio components. The assessment rewards reading supplied data quickly, answering in tight written form and typing accurately under time pressure. Students who have practised only on paper lose time to the interface rather than to the science.
programmes.countryNote: Not every Dubai MYP school registers for eAssessment, and some run internal end-of-year examinations instead, so the first question to ask the MYP coordinator is which route your child's cohort is on. Preparation differs enough that buying the wrong one wastes a term. Confirm the sitting arrangements with the school rather than relying on any date published online.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme sciences
programmes.description: Biology, chemistry and physics at Standard or Higher Level, with an internal assessment the student designs independently and externally examined papers. The criterion habits built in MYP 4 and 5 carry directly across: variable control, uncertainty handling and a conclusion that answers the research question are assessed again under different names.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the decision between DP sciences and A Level sciences is often made in the final MYP 5 term, and a student's criterion C record is the most useful evidence in that conversation. Strong knowledge with weak data handling predicts trouble in a DP internal assessment more reliably than any mock paper mark does.

dubai/ib-myp-sciences-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: What follows is the MYP science work itself, written as strands and failure modes rather than as a topic list, because that is the level at which marks move. A parent can take any line below to a science teacher and ask whether it describes their child.

subjects.name: Criterion B, strand on the problem and hypothesis
subjects.description: The student must explain the problem or question being tested and state a hypothesis supported by scientific reasoning. The usual loss is a prediction with no mechanism: saying the reaction will be faster rather than saying why, in terms of particle collisions. One added clause fixes it permanently.

subjects.name: Criterion B, strand on variables and method
subjects.description: Independent, dependent and controlled variables must be named, and the method must be safe, logical and replicable. Students list variables without saying how each control is held constant, which reads as an incomplete design even when the practical work was performed properly.

subjects.name: Criterion C, strand on data presentation
subjects.description: Tables need headings, units and consistent decimal places; graphs need the independent variable on the horizontal axis, sensible scales and a line that reflects the data rather than joining every point. These are conventions, not opinions, and they are the cheapest marks in the programme to recover.

subjects.name: Criterion C, strand on conclusion against hypothesis
subjects.description: A conclusion must state explicitly whether the hypothesis was supported, using the processed data as evidence. Most students describe the trend instead. Teaching the sentence shape, naming the hypothesis and quoting the number that supports or contradicts it, moves this strand within two sessions.

subjects.name: Criterion C, strand on evaluation
subjects.description: Validity, reliability, method weaknesses and realistic improvements, discussed separately from the conclusion. Students write the words sources of error and then list human error, which earns nothing. A specific limitation tied to the apparatus used is what the band descriptors reward.

subjects.name: Criterion D, strand on science applied to a problem
subjects.description: The student applies scientific understanding to a named, authentic issue and discusses the implications. UAE contexts work well and are usually underused: desalination energy demand, construction dust and air quality, district cooling loads, food import chains and water reuse.

subjects.name: Criterion D, strand on documentation of sources
subjects.description: Sources must be documented in the style the school requires, consistently, in text and in the list. A strong reflection with four uncited claims drops a band for a reason that has nothing to do with science, and it is also where academic-honesty conversations begin.

subjects.name: Criterion A, command terms and applied questions
subjects.description: State, outline, describe, explain, analyse and evaluate each demand a different structure and a different length of answer. A student who writes an explanation when the term is describe wastes effort; one who describes when the term is explain loses the mark outright.

subjects.name: Scientific language and diagram conventions
subjects.description: Correct terminology, correctly labelled diagrams and units written in the standard form carry marks in every criterion. Biology loses more marks to imprecise wording than to misunderstanding, which is why vocabulary drills still earn their place in a secondary science session.

subjects.name: The maths inside MYP science
subjects.description: Rearranging formulae, standard form, percentage change, gradients and ratio work underpin every quantitative science task. A student who is a year behind in MYP mathematics will present as weak in physics and chemistry, and the useful intervention is often in the mathematics rather than the science.

sections.heading: What an IB MYP sciences home tutor in Dubai means in practice
paragraphs: The phrase covers two different things. One is a tutor who drives to a villa or apartment in Dubai and teaches at the dining table; the published bands for that work in this market run from roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour, with the travel carried inside the fee. The other is one-to-one teaching at home over live video, which is what most families end up with once they see what the premium buys and how it narrows the choice of tutor. IB Gram offers the second only. We do not provide home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; that service runs in India.

It is worth being clear about what is genuinely lost and gained. Lost: the physical presence of a teacher, which some younger students respond to, and the ability to handle real apparatus together. Gained: a tutor chosen for having marked MYP criterion tasks rather than for living nearby, a session that is not shortened by Sheikh Zayed Road, a shared screen with the rubric and the marked script open at once, and a written record after every lesson. For criterion-based science work the shared screen is not a consolation prize; it is where the work happens.

On apparatus, the honest position is that neither a visiting tutor nor an online one replaces a school laboratory, and MYP practical work is done at school under supervision. What a tutor can do is rehearse the design before the lesson and process the data afterwards, which is exactly where criteria B and C are won. Simulations cover the rest, and running one twice with a single variable changed is a better demonstration of control than most dining-table demonstrations manage.

sections.heading: Criterion B: the sentences that separate a 4 from a 7
paragraphs: Criterion B asks the student to explain a problem, state a hypothesis with scientific reasoning, identify and explain the handling of variables, and design a safe, replicable method. Read that list and the pattern of lost marks becomes obvious. Students who have done the practical and understand it still sit in the middle bands because they have written three of the four things and assumed the fourth was implied.

The hypothesis is the first casualty. A prediction is not a hypothesis. Writing that the rate will increase as temperature increases earns little; writing that the rate will increase because particles have greater kinetic energy and collide more frequently with sufficient energy to react is the same sentence with the mechanism restored. The second casualty is variable handling. Naming a controlled variable is half a mark; saying how it is held constant, with the apparatus that does it, is the rest. The third is replicability, which means a method another student could follow without asking a question, and the quickest test is to make the student read their own method aloud while someone attempts to follow it literally.

None of this needs new science taught. It needs the same four corrections applied to the student's own previous task until they appear without prompting, which is why a strand repair block of four to six weeks is usually better value than a term of general science support. The corrections then transfer: a student who has learned to write a mechanism into a hypothesis in MYP 4 biology does it in MYP 5 chemistry and again in a Diploma Programme internal assessment, where the strand has a different name and the same requirement.
bullets: A hypothesis needs a mechanism, not just a direction
Each controlled variable needs the method by which it is held constant
Replicable means another student could follow it with no questions asked
Safety and apparatus choice carry marks in the upper bands

sections.heading: Criterion C: five specific ways Dubai students lose data-processing marks
paragraphs: Criterion C covers data presentation, interpretation, a conclusion stated against the hypothesis, and evaluation. It is the strand group where the most marks are recoverable fastest, because the losses are conventions and structures rather than understanding. The table lists the five that recur most across the marked MYP work we see from Dubai schools, with what the band descriptors are looking for instead.

The largest single loss is the conclusion that restates the data. A student writes that the current increased as the voltage increased, which is a description of the graph, and then stops. The descriptor wants the hypothesis named and the processed data used as evidence for or against it. The second largest is the merged conclusion and evaluation, where both strands are assessed from one paragraph and neither is complete. Separating them with two subheadings is a formatting change that frequently moves a whole band.

The rest are mechanical. Human error written as a limitation earns nothing, because it identifies nothing; the apparatus resolution, the reaction-time dependency or the uncontrolled room temperature does. Processing means doing something to the raw numbers, an average, a rate, a gradient, a percentage change, rather than graphing them as collected. And a line of best fit is a judgement about the relationship, not a dot-to-dot. Each of these is one session's work, and together they are often the difference between a 4 and a 6. The reason they persist is that no school report has room to say any of them, so a parent reads a competent comment about effort and never learns that the problem is a missing subheading and an unprocessed column of numbers.

table.caption: CRITERION C — THE FIVE RECURRING LOSSES AND WHAT THE DESCRIPTORS WANT
rows: The current rose as the voltage rose
Describes the graph; the hypothesis is never named
Name the hypothesis and quote the processed value that supports or contradicts it
One paragraph covering conclusion and evaluation
Two strands assessed from one block; neither is complete
Two headed sections, conclusion first, evaluation second

Identifies nothing specific or fixable

Raw readings graphed as collected
No processing has taken place
Average repeats, then calculate a rate, gradient or percentage change

sections.heading: Criterion D: UAE contexts that score, and the referencing that sinks a good reflection
paragraphs: Criterion D asks the student to apply science to address a specific problem or issue, discuss the implications of using science to solve it, and document sources correctly. Dubai students have an advantage here that they almost never use: they live in a country where several large applied-science problems are visible from the car window. Desalination and the energy cost of producing drinking water. District cooling and peak summer electricity load. Construction dust and air quality. Food import chains and refrigeration. Treated sewage effluent used for landscape irrigation. Solar yield against panel soiling in a dusty climate.

A reflection built on one of those, with a local source, reads as authentic and specific, which is what the upper bands describe. A reflection built on a generic global statistic about plastic lifted from the first search result reads as a template, and is marked as one. The practical instruction we give is narrow: choose a problem that exists within fifty kilometres of the school, find one source with a named publisher and a date, and write about the implications for people who live here rather than for humanity in general.

Then there is the referencing, which sinks more good criterion D work than weak science does. Sources must be documented consistently in the style the school requires, in the text as well as in the list at the end. Four uncited claims drop a band on their own. This is also where academic-honesty conversations start, and it is worth being plain about the boundary: a tutor questions the argument, points at an unsupported claim and explains how to cite it. A tutor does not supply sentences for a student to submit. Every word of an MYP task, and of a Personal Project, must be the student's own, and the student who outsources that work risks far more than a low grade.
bullets: Pick a problem visible within fifty kilometres of the school
One properly cited source beats four uncited claims
In-text citation as well as the reference list, in the school's own style
A tutor questions and gives feedback; the writing is always the student's

sections.heading: Command terms: half of criterion A is reading the question properly
paragraphs: Criterion A is knowing and understanding, and it is where most parents assume the problem lies. Often it does not. A student who can talk fluently about diffusion and still scores 4 on criterion A is usually answering a different question from the one asked, because the command term sets the shape of the answer and nobody has taught them the shapes. State wants a fact. Describe wants the features or the sequence. Explain wants a reason or a mechanism. Outline wants a brief account. Analyse wants the parts and their relationships. Evaluate wants judgement with both sides.

The cost of getting this wrong runs in both directions. A student who writes a full explanation when the term is describe spends three minutes earning one mark and then runs short of time at the end of the paper. A student who describes when the term is explain writes a correct paragraph that cannot be credited, because the mechanism the mark scheme requires is absent. Both students know the science. Only one of them has been taught to read the instruction.

This is quick work and it is the right place to start when the marked evidence is unclear, because it costs little and rules out the cheapest explanation. We run it as fifteen minutes at the start of a session: a term, a question, a timed answer, a comparison against the band descriptor. After a few weeks students begin annotating the command term before writing anything, which is a habit worth more in an on-screen eAssessment than any amount of extra content revision.

sections.heading: MYP 5 on-screen eAssessment: what changes when the paper is a screen
paragraphs: Schools that register for MYP eAssessment sit on-screen examinations in sciences, and the format changes preparation more than most families expect. The science is unchanged. What changes is that the data is supplied on screen and must be read from it, the answer is typed into a box, and the student cannot annotate a diagram with a pencil while thinking. Students who revise entirely on paper arrive fluent in the content and slow in the interface, and lose marks to the clock rather than to any gap in understanding.

Preparation that works is simply practice in the medium. Timed question work on screen, typing rather than writing, reading values off a supplied table instead of one they drew themselves, and planning a long answer in two lines of notes rather than in margin scribbles. We also drill the habit of answering the command term first and adding detail second, because a half-finished typed answer that begins correctly still earns the opening marks.

Two practical cautions. First, not every Dubai MYP school registers for eAssessment, and some run internal end-of-year examinations instead; ask the MYP coordinator which route the cohort is on before buying preparation, because the two are not interchangeable. Second, we do not publish IB session or results dates on these pages. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so any date you see circulating should be confirmed with your school's IB coordinator or on ibo.org directly before you plan a revision block around it.
bullets: Practise on screen, typed and timed, not on paper
Read supplied data rather than data the student generated
Answer the command term in the first line of every typed response
Confirm the route and the dates with the school's MYP coordinator

sections.heading: The MYP 5 to Diploma Programme step, and what to fix before it
paragraphs: The jump from MYP 5 sciences into DP biology, chemistry or physics is not mainly a content jump. It is an independence jump. In the Diploma Programme the student designs an internal assessment from their own research question, handles uncertainty quantitatively, and writes an evaluation that a teacher has not scaffolded. Every one of those demands has a direct MYP ancestor, which means the MYP 5 criterion record predicts DP difficulty better than any entrance test.

The pattern to watch is a student with strong criterion A and weak criterion C. That profile means knowledge is secure and independent data handling is not, and it is the profile that struggles most in DP year one, because the internal assessment arrives before the content has finished being taught. The reverse profile, moderate criterion A and strong criterion B and C, usually copes well and catches up on content. If you are choosing between DP sciences and A Level sciences in Dubai, that breakdown is more useful than a predicted grade.

What to fix in the final MYP 5 terms is narrow and worth doing properly. Uncertainty and significant figures, because DP assesses them explicitly. Writing a research question that is actually answerable with school apparatus, which is the single most common DP internal assessment failure. Processing data without being told which calculation to use. And citing sources in a consistent style, since the DP demands it across every subject. Four things, perhaps twelve sessions, and the first DP term stops being a shock.

sections.heading: A weekly science slot that survives a Dubai school year
paragraphs: The most common reason tutoring stops working in this city is not the tutor. It is the slot. A Dubai secondary week already carries a long commute, an after-school activity or two, and the mandatory UAE subjects that every private school must run alongside its licensed curriculum. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies regardless of the international curriculum a school is licensed for, with instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit and a recommendation that no mandatory subject lesson runs shorter than 25 minutes. Those hours are real and they come out of the same week as everything else.

So choose a time you can hold in February as well as September. Students in Mirdif or Al Qusais travelling to campuses on the other side of the city should not be attempting criterion B design work at 5.30pm; schedule analysis or marked-script review in that slot and keep new thinking for a weekend morning. Students in Al Barsha or Umm Suqeim who are home by four can take the harder work early in the evening. Apartment households in the Marina usually find after dinner quieter than before it.

Then plan the interruptions in advance rather than reacting to them. During Ramadan, sessions move to post-Iftar or to late morning at weekends, and shorter forty-five-minute lessons work better than full hours. School examination weeks are for pausing, not for adding. Half terms are the best time to run a strand repair block, because there is no new content arriving to compete with it. A slot that bends twice a year and holds the rest of the time produces more progress than a more ambitious plan that quietly lapses in November.
bullets: Mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies compete for the same week
Match the task type to the hour: design work early, review work late
Move to post-Iftar or weekend mornings during Ramadan
Pause during school examination weeks; use half terms for strand repair

process.title: Send the marked task, not a description of it
process.description: A photograph of the last marked science task with the rubric attached tells us more in thirty seconds than a long conversation about how the term has gone. If the school publishes strand-level marks on the portal, send those too. We read it before the first session and come with a named strand rather than a general plan.

process.title: Free trial lesson, with the condition stated plainly
process.description: One forty-five-minute online session at no charge, with no card details taken and nothing to cancel. The tutor works on the actual task you sent and finishes by naming the strand that lost the marks and the correction that addresses it. You keep that written note whether or not you book anything else.

process.title: Pick one strand and work it to habit
process.description: Strand repair beats broad revision at this level. The student redrafts a previous task against the band descriptors, then applies the same correction to the next task the school issues. Two drafts side by side are visible evidence, which is more than a grade on a report can offer mid-term.

process.title: Mark a piece of work every fortnight
process.description: Every second session uses a short piece of the student's own writing, marked against the descriptors with written comments. This is what tells you whether the hours are working, and it also catches the drift that happens when a student learns a correction and then quietly stops applying it three weeks later.

process.title: Reset the plan at each half term
process.description: At half term we look at what the school has marked since the last review and decide whether to keep going, change strand, reduce to fortnightly or stop. Finishing is a legitimate outcome. A tutor who never recommends reducing the hours is not reading the evidence they are producing.

whyPoints.title: Strand-level teaching, not topic revision
whyPoints.description: MYP sciences marks are awarded against four criteria out of 8 each, and within each criterion against strands. Sessions target a named strand taken from your child's own marked work, which is why the first thing we ask for is the task sheet and the rubric rather than a list of topics the student finds hard.

whyPoints.title: The student writes every word
whyPoints.description: A tutor questions a hypothesis, challenges a variable list, points at an unsupported claim and gives written feedback on a draft. Nothing is supplied for submission, in a criterion task, a Personal Project or anywhere else. Being plain about that boundary is a service to the student, because an academic-honesty finding follows them much further than a 4 does.

whyPoints.title: Delivered over live video, by choice
whyPoints.description: A shared screen holds the rubric, the marked script and the student's draft at the same time, which is exactly what strand-level correction needs. It also means the tutor is chosen for having marked MYP tasks rather than for living within a twenty-minute drive, and that nobody loses half the session to Sheikh Zayed Road.

whyPoints.title: Written evidence after every session
whyPoints.description: Each lesson ends with a short note naming the strand worked on, what the student did with it and what to look for in the next marked piece. Parents in Dubai are frequently at work when sessions run, and a written record is the only honest way to judge whether the money is doing anything.

whyPoints.title: Honest about what we do not claim
whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no accreditation from KHDA, ADEK, the IB or any examination board, and we say so rather than implying otherwise. We also publish no IB examination dates, because the IB's own site cannot be checked automatically and an unverified date on a planning page is worse than no date at all.

faqs.question: Which MYP science criterion is my child most likely losing marks on?
faqs.answer: Statistically, criterion C. Processing and evaluating holds the most recoverable marks because the losses are conventions rather than understanding: a conclusion that describes the graph instead of naming the hypothesis, an evaluation merged into the conclusion so neither is complete, human error listed as a limitation, and raw data graphed without any processing. Criterion B is the next most common, usually a hypothesis with a direction but no mechanism. Ask the science teacher for the strand marks rather than the overall grade, and the answer for your child specifically takes one email to establish.

faqs.question: Can an online tutor really help with a science investigation that happens in a school laboratory?
faqs.answer: The practical work stays at school under supervision, and no tutor replaces that. What a tutor does is the part either side of it. Before the lesson, they interrogate the plan: is the hypothesis mechanistic, are the variables named, is each control explained, could another student follow the method. Afterwards, they work on the data: processing it correctly, presenting it to convention, writing a conclusion against the hypothesis and an evaluation that names something fixable. Criteria B and C are won in those two conversations, and both are easier with a shared screen than at a dining table.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a science tutor to our home in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. We do not provide in-home visits anywhere in the UAE; that is a service we run only in India. Teaching for Dubai families is one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time around the school week. The published Dubai bands for in-home tuition run from roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with the travel inside the fee, and the practical consequence of that premium is that families end up choosing from tutors who can reach their community at 5pm rather than from tutors who have marked MYP criterion tasks.

faqs.question: How do I write a hypothesis that earns the top criterion B band?
faqs.answer: Include the mechanism. A prediction states the direction: the rate will increase as temperature increases. A hypothesis states the direction and the science behind it: the rate will increase because particles gain kinetic energy, collide more frequently and more collisions exceed the activation energy. The band descriptors reward scientific reasoning, so the word because has to do real work. Then name the independent, dependent and controlled variables, and for each controlled variable say how it is held constant and with what apparatus. Those two additions move most students out of the middle bands within a fortnight.

faqs.question: What counts as a proper evaluation in MYP sciences?
faqs.answer: Something specific and fixable. Writing that there may have been human error identifies nothing and earns nothing. Writing that the stopwatch was started manually, giving a reaction-time uncertainty of roughly 0.2 seconds against readings of 4 to 6 seconds, identifies a real limitation and leads naturally to a stated improvement such as a light gate. A full evaluation discusses validity, reliability and improvements separately from the conclusion, ideally under its own heading, so the examiner can see each strand addressed rather than having to find it inside a single paragraph.

faqs.question: Which UAE topics work well for a criterion D reflection?
faqs.answer: Choose a problem visible within fifty kilometres of the school. Desalination and the energy cost of drinking water, district cooling and summer peak electricity demand, construction dust and air quality, panel soiling and solar yield in a dusty climate, treated effluent used for landscape irrigation, or refrigeration in a food import chain. Each has implications you can discuss for people who live here, which is what the upper bands describe. Then cite one source with a named publisher and a date, in the school's referencing style, in the text as well as in the list.

faqs.question: How many sessions does it take to fix a criterion C problem?
faqs.answer: Usually between four and eight, which is one short block rather than a term. The conclusion and evaluation split is often a single session, because it is a structural change. Learning to process data before graphing it takes about two. Line-of-best-fit judgement and anomaly marking is one. Replacing human error with a specific limitation is one. Then the rest is applying the same corrections to the next school-set task so they stop needing prompting. Buying a full academic year of weekly sessions for this is overbuying, and a good tutor will tell you so.

faqs.question: My child understands the science but still scores 4 on criterion A. Why?
faqs.answer: Almost always the command term. State wants a fact, describe wants features or a sequence, explain wants a mechanism, outline wants a brief account, analyse wants parts and relationships, and evaluate wants a judgement with both sides. A student who writes an explanation when asked to describe spends three minutes earning one mark and then runs out of time later in the paper. One who describes when asked to explain writes a correct paragraph that cannot be credited. Fifteen minutes of command-term work at the start of each session for a few weeks usually resolves it.

faqs.question: Is the MYP 5 on-screen science assessment different enough to need separate preparation?
faqs.answer: Yes, where a school registers for eAssessment. The science is the same, but the data is supplied on screen, the answers are typed, and there is no margin to sketch in while thinking. Students who revise only on paper lose marks to the interface and the clock rather than to gaps in knowledge. Preparation should be timed, typed and on screen, reading values from supplied tables. Check with the MYP coordinator first, because not every Dubai school uses eAssessment and some run internal examinations instead, and the two need different practice.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Personal Project as well as science tasks?
faqs.answer: Within strict limits, yes. A tutor can discuss the goal, question whether the success criteria are measurable, ask awkward questions about the plan, and give feedback on a draft the student has written themselves. What a tutor must never do is supply any part of the work for submission, in the Personal Project or in a criterion task. That boundary is not pedantry: outsourced work is an academic-honesty breach with consequences for the student that outlast any grade, and it is also the practice this market's essay sellers depend on.

faqs.question: Will a tutor follow our school's own task sheets and deadlines?
faqs.answer: That is the only sensible way to work in the MYP, because schools write their own criterion tasks within the programme framework and the rubric wording differs between campuses. Send the task sheet, the rubric and the internal deadline, and the sessions get scheduled backwards from it with a draft review built in. Where a student carries deadlines in two or three sciences in the same fortnight, which is routine in MYP 4, we plan the order with you instead of simply taking the next thing due.

faqs.question: How do we keep a weekly science session going through Ramadan and examination weeks?
faqs.answer: By planning for both at the start of the term rather than reacting. During Ramadan, sessions move to post-Iftar or to a late weekend morning, and forty-five minutes works better than a full hour. School examination weeks are for pausing, not adding; a student revising for six subjects does not need a seventh commitment. Half terms are the best window for a strand repair block because no new content is arriving to compete with it. A slot that bends twice a year outperforms an ambitious plan abandoned in November.

faqs.question: What should I ask a prospective MYP science tutor in the first message?
faqs.answer: Four things. Which MYP criterion strands they have marked, and at which year group. Whether they will work from our school's task sheet and rubric rather than their own materials. Whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which is issued free of charge for two years and which a permitted tutor will show you without fuss. And what written record arrives after each session. A tutor who answers all four concretely is reading the programme properly; one who replies with a list of topics is selling general science support.

faqs.question: Does strong MYP science performance predict success in DP sciences?
faqs.answer: The criterion breakdown does, more than the overall grade. A student with strong criterion A and weak criterion C has secure knowledge and shaky independent data handling, and that is the profile that finds the first DP year hardest, because the internal assessment arrives before the content is finished. Moderate criterion A with strong B and C usually copes well. If you are weighing DP sciences against A Levels at the end of MYP 5 in Dubai, ask for the strand record and read it as evidence about independence rather than about knowledge.

dubai/ib-myp-sciences-home-tutor.closingHeading: Send the marked task and we will name the strand
dubai/ib-myp-sciences-home-tutor.closingBody: Almost every MYP science problem that looks like a knowledge gap turns out to be a missing strand: a hypothesis without a mechanism, a conclusion that never names the hypothesis, an evaluation that says human error, a reflection with four uncited claims. Those are cheap to fix and expensive to leave, because they repeat on every task until somebody points at them. Send a photograph of the last marked science task with the rubric, take the free trial lesson, and read the written note that follows. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, timed to the Dubai school week, with in-home visits offered only in India.

intro.heading: What an hour of MYP science teaching costs in Dubai, and why the range is so wide
paragraphs: Parents who ring round for MYP science help in Dubai are quoted anything between AED 45 and AED 650 an hour, and almost nobody explains the spread. The low end is real: EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to AED 65, and Tutopiya lists online sessions from AED 33 to AED 52. The high end is real too: BartyED publishes AED 650 for a premium named tutor and TutorChase quotes around AED 270. Bestimate's Dubai rate table for 2026 puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to AED 350 and subject specialists at AED 200 to AED 450 and above. Those are the market's own published numbers, read in October 2026, not ours.

What a rate card hides is what the hour contains. A university student charging AED 60 can explain photosynthesis clearly. Reading a criterion B task sheet, noticing that the student has written a hypothesis with no independent variable named, and then rewriting the student's own method until the control variables are explicit, is a different skill. It is also the skill MYP grades are built from. The programme does not award marks for recall alone. Four criteria, each marked out of 8, give a total out of 32, and criteria B, C and D together account for three-quarters of that total.

The second thing a rate card hides is Dubai. A tutor driving from Mirdif to Dubai Marina at five in the afternoon is paid for one hour and absorbs ninety minutes of Sheikh Zayed Road either side of it, so the quoted fee carries the travel inside it. That is why in-home bands sit above online bands in every published table in this market. It is also why a family in The Springs often ends up with whoever is geographically convenient rather than whoever has marked MYP 5 chemistry before.

Dubai's school market makes specialist scarcity sharper than it first looks. The emirate had 387,441 private-school students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering 17 different curricula, with British-curriculum schools at 37 per cent of enrolment, Indian at 26 per cent, American at 14 per cent and the International Baccalaureate at 7 per cent. Seven in every hundred is a thin slice of a very large market, and MYP sciences inside that slice is thinner again. Most science tutors working in Dubai have taught Cambridge IGCSE 0620 or CBSE science far more often than they have marked a criterion C graph.

So this page is built around the number. It publishes what MYP sciences tuition costs in Dubai with each figure attributed, sets out what moves those figures in this emirate specifically, maps the marks each criterion carries so you can see what an hour is buying, and puts tutoring beside Dubai school fees, which KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 will not rise for the 2026-27 academic year. IB Gram's own model is one-to-one online teaching with a trial lesson before anything is paid for, so treat the bands below as context for your decision rather than as a price list.

dubai/ib-myp-sciences-tutor.programmesIntro: MYP sciences does not sit on its own. Dubai's IB continuum schools run the Primary Years Programme from FS2, the Middle Years Programme from Year 7, and the Diploma Programme from Year 12, and several run IGCSE alongside or instead at 16. What a science hour has to achieve depends on which of these your child is in now and which one comes next.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Science in the PYP is taught inside transdisciplinary units rather than as a named subject, so a Year 6 student can be a confident inquirer with no formal grasp of variables, units or graph conventions. The gap shows up in MYP 1 within a term, usually as marks lost on criterion C for axes, scales and lines of best fit rather than on any point of knowledge.
programmes.countryNote: Several Dubai schools, among them Dubai American Academy and Dubai International Academy Al Barsha, run the full continuum, so the PYP to MYP step happens inside one campus. Families moving in from a British primary in Dubai arrive at MYP 1 having done more structured practical write-ups and less independent inquiry, and the two groups lose marks in opposite places during the first year.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Sciences is one of the eight MYP subject groups and is assessed against four criteria, each out of 8: knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. In MYP 1 to 3 it is usually taught as integrated sciences by one teacher. In MYP 4 and 5 most schools split it into biology, chemistry and physics with separate specialists and separate criterion tasks.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the split year matters for budgeting. A family paying for one integrated science tutor in MYP 3 can find they need two or three subject specialists in MYP 4, which is where tutoring costs in this emirate typically double. Schools licensed by KHDA also run Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside the MYP, so the week your child has free for science is narrower than the timetable suggests.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The Diploma Programme sciences are taken at Standard or Higher Level with an internal assessment and externally marked papers. The jump from MYP 5 is less about content than about quantitative handling: uncertainties, propagated error, logarithmic relationships and the discipline of a formal evaluation. Students who scored well on criterion A and poorly on criterion C in MYP 5 are the ones who struggle most in DP year one.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai families often decide between DP sciences and A Level sciences at the end of MYP 5, and the choice is frequently made on which school has places rather than on which route suits the student. A tutor who has seen both routes in this city can tell you honestly whether a student who needs scaffolding for criterion B will cope with a DP internal assessment designed from scratch.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE
programmes.description: Many Dubai students sit IGCSE sciences at 16 instead of finishing MYP 5, either because they change school or because their school offers both. Cambridge IGCSE Co-ordinated Sciences and the separate 0610, 0620 and 0625 syllabuses are terminal and externally examined, with no criterion-based coursework, so the skills that earn MYP marks are weighted very differently.
programmes.countryNote: Because British-curriculum schools hold 37 per cent of Dubai enrolment, mid-year transfers from MYP into IGCSE are common here, and the reverse happens too. Cambridge runs June and November series with centres allocated to one of six administrative zones, and the zone timetable governs your child's dates, so a transfer in Year 10 needs the receiving school's exams officer consulted early.

dubai/ib-myp-sciences-tutor.subjectsIntro: What follows is the MYP science work Dubai families most often ask for, written as the tasks a tutor actually sits with rather than as a subject list. The criterion strands are listed separately because that is how marks are awarded, and because a parent reading a report line cannot tell from the grade alone which strand went wrong.

subjects.name: MYP Integrated Sciences
subjects.description: Taught as one subject spanning biology, chemistry and physics content with a shared set of criteria. The usual problem is not comprehension but transfer: a student who can define density cannot calculate it from an irregular object's displacement reading. Sessions here work best on applied question sets rather than revision notes.

subjects.name: MYP Biology
subjects.description: Cells, transport, genetics, ecology and human systems, with heavy demands on scientific vocabulary and diagram labelling. Marks go missing on criterion A when an answer describes a process correctly in everyday language without using the terms the mark scheme expects, which is a fixable problem inside three or four sessions.

subjects.name: MYP Chemistry
subjects.description: Particle model, bonding, reaction types, rates and the beginnings of mole arithmetic. The common break point is quantitative: students can balance an equation and still cannot convert grams to moles reliably under time pressure, which then costs them on criterion C when processing titration or mass-change data.

subjects.name: MYP Physics
subjects.description: Forces, motion, energy, waves and electricity, where the underlying arithmetic does most of the damage. Rearranging an equation, handling standard form and reading a gradient off a graph are the three skills that separate a 5 from a 7, and none of them is taught as physics content.

subjects.name: Criterion A: Knowing and understanding
subjects.description: Recall, application to unfamiliar situations and analysis of information to make scientifically supported judgements. It is the strand that moves fastest with teaching, because command terms are learnable: state, describe, explain, outline and evaluate each demand a different shape of answer.

subjects.name: Criterion B: Inquiring and designing
subjects.description: Explaining a problem, writing a testable hypothesis with scientific reasoning, naming independent, dependent and controlled variables, and designing a safe, replicable method. The highest-value tutoring in MYP sciences is here, because the same corrections apply across every investigation the student will ever write.

subjects.name: Criterion C: Processing and evaluating
subjects.description: Presenting data in correct form, interpreting it, stating a conclusion that explicitly answers the hypothesis, and evaluating validity, reliability and improvements. Students routinely merge conclusion and evaluation into one paragraph and lose both strands, which is a structural fix rather than a knowledge one.

subjects.name: Criterion D: Reflecting on the impacts of science
subjects.description: Applying science to address a specific problem or issue, discussing implications, using scientific language and documenting sources correctly. UAE contexts work well here, from desalination energy cost to construction dust and air quality, and a cited local source scores better than a generic global example.

subjects.name: MYP 5 on-screen eAssessment preparation
subjects.description: Schools that register for MYP eAssessment sit on-screen examinations in sciences, which reward speed of reading, careful use of the supplied data and tight written answers. Practising on paper only is poor preparation, so sessions move to screen-shared question work and timed response drills.

dubai/ib-myp-sciences-tutor.regionsTitle: Where in Dubai families ask for MYP science help
dubai/ib-myp-sciences-tutor.regionsIntro: Lessons are online, so an address in Dubai changes nothing about who teaches your child. It does change what time a session can realistically start, because school-run and office traffic differ sharply by community. These are the practical notes families in each area give us when we set a weekly slot.

regions.name: Dubai Marina and JBR
regions.note: Apartment living with no spare study room, so sessions happen at a kitchen table with headphones. Families here usually want a 6pm or later start because secondary buses are slow out of the tower cluster.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Al Barsha South
regions.note: Closest to several IB continuum campuses, so students arrive home early and 4.30pm slots work. Also where we see the most MYP 4 students needing two science specialists at once after the subject split.

regions.name: Mirdif and Al Qusais
regions.note: Long bus runs for students attending IB schools on the other side of the creek. A 5pm start is usually optimistic; 6.30pm sticks better across a whole term, which matters more than the rate.

regions.name: Dubai Hills Estate and Meydan
regions.note: Villa communities with purpose-built study space and reliable fibre, so screen-shared graph work and simulations run smoothly. Families here most often ask about MYP to DP science preparation a year ahead.

regions.name: Jumeirah, Umm Suqeim and Al Safa
regions.note: Mixed British and IB enrolment within a few streets, so siblings are often on different curricula. Sessions here frequently cover one MYP 4 physics student and one IGCSE 0625 student in the same household.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches, The Springs and The Lakes
regions.note: The communities where in-home tutoring is quoted highest in Dubai, because the drive out and back eats an evening. Online removes that premium entirely and widens the choice of subject specialist.

regions.name: Business Bay and Downtown Dubai
regions.note: Working parents who want a session they can sit in on for the last ten minutes. We keep a written summary after each lesson for exactly this group, since nobody is home to ask how it went.

schoolClusters.city: Western Dubai — Marina, Al Barsha, Umm Suqeim and The Meadows
schoolClusters.note: The densest concentration of IB continuum provision in the emirate, which means MYP 4 subject splits happen early and the demand for separate biology, chemistry and physics support is highest here. Students from these campuses arrive with criterion task sheets written in the school's own format.

schoolClusters.city: Eastern and central Dubai — Al Jaddaf, Festival City and Mirdif
schoolClusters.note: A smaller cluster where one or two schools carry most of the MYP enrolment for a wide catchment, so a student who falls behind has fewer in-school options and a longer commute to anything else. Online sessions matter more to this group than to any other in Dubai.

schoolClusters.city: Southern Dubai — Dubailand, The Sustainable City, Dubai Investments Park and Al Barsha South
schoolClusters.note: Newer campuses in fast-growing communities, several running the continuum from PYP upward. Criterion D work here often uses the community itself as the authentic context, which is a genuine advantage when sustainability is the subject of the task.

sections.heading: What an IB MYP sciences tutor in Dubai costs, with every figure sourced
paragraphs: Start with the published numbers rather than a brochure. Across the Dubai providers whose rates are actually visible, online one-to-one sits roughly between AED 45 and AED 300 an hour depending on the tutor's qualification, in-home one-to-one sits between AED 180 and AED 500 because the travel is inside the fee, and premium named tutors sit above AED 500. Those bands come from the providers' own pages, read in October 2026. They are quoted here as the market, not as an IB Gram price list.

The table splits those bands by MYP phase, because the work is not the same at every year. MYP 1 to 3 integrated sciences is largely knowledge, vocabulary and simple data handling, and a careful generalist teaches it well. MYP 4 and 5, where most Dubai IB continuum schools separate biology, chemistry and physics, needs someone who has marked criterion work at that level and can tell a weak hypothesis from a weak method. The step between those two rows is the largest single jump on the table, and it is the one families budget for least.

Two cells are deliberately marked as not usually offered. Criterion task coaching and eAssessment preparation are rarely sold as group classes, because the work is specific to one student's own draft method or one student's own data set. Four students cannot share a criterion B rewrite. If a provider in Dubai does quote a group rate for that work, ask precisely what the group does for the hour, because the answer is usually a generic lesson on how investigations work rather than anything attached to your child's task.

sections.heading: Five things that move the number in this emirate specifically
paragraphs: The first is the MYP 4 subject split. A household paying for one integrated science tutor in MYP 3 often needs two or three specialists in MYP 4, so the monthly figure doubles without the hourly rate changing at all. Families who plan for this a term ahead usually choose one specialist plus a fortnightly review of the other two subjects, rather than three weekly sessions they cannot sustain.

The second is travel. Dubai's geography prices in-home tutoring in a way that has nothing to do with teaching. A tutor crossing from Al Qusais to Arabian Ranches at 5pm commits an evening for one paid hour, and that is why the in-home column in the table above sits consistently above the online column. Online removes the premium and, more usefully, removes the geographic limit on who can teach your child.

The third is the exam-year premium: rates across this market firm up in the weeks before MYP 5 on-screen assessments and end-of-year summatives, because supply is fixed and demand is not. The fourth is the mandatory UAE subject load. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies in all Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, with instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, so the hours available in a week for anything else are genuinely fewer here than in a comparable school abroad. The fifth is scarcity: the International Baccalaureate accounts for 7 per cent of Dubai private-school enrolment, so MYP-experienced science teachers are a small pool competing against a much larger IGCSE and CBSE market.

sections.heading: What the hour is actually buying: the four criteria and their marks
paragraphs: A parent looking at an MYP report sees a grade and a comment, not a strand breakdown, which makes it almost impossible to tell what to buy. The criteria are the answer. Sciences is assessed against four, each marked out of 8 for a total out of 32, and they reward entirely different things. Criterion A is knowledge and its application. Criterion B is the design of an investigation. Criterion C is what the student does with data afterwards. Criterion D is the reflection on science in the real world, including the documentation of sources.

Knowing which one is weak changes the price of fixing it. Criterion A responds quickly to teaching, because most of the loss is command terms: a student who writes a description when the question says explain is losing marks on structure, not understanding, and that is a handful of sessions. Criterion B is the highest-value work in the programme, because the corrections transfer to every investigation the student will write for the next three years. Criterion C is mechanical and therefore cheap to fix once diagnosed, and criterion D is often lost purely on referencing.

Use the table to turn a report line into a shopping list. Ask your child's science teacher which criterion the last two summatives scored lowest on, then buy against that rather than against the subject. A tutor who asks for the criterion breakdown in the first message is reading the programme correctly. One who offers general science support by the month is selling hours rather than marks, and in a market where an hour runs from AED 45 to AED 650, that distinction is the whole decision.

sections.heading: Tutoring cost in context: what it looks like beside Dubai school fees
paragraphs: Tutoring is usually judged against other tutoring, which is the wrong comparison. Judge it against the rest of the education budget. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there will be no increase in school fees for private schools in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under the second of Dubai's economic incentives packages valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. For most families that is the first year in some time where the school line in the household budget is flat, which makes it the sensible year to spend deliberately on a specific weakness rather than reactively in April.

Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions give the shape of the commitment: roughly AED 240 to AED 600 a month at the budget tier, AED 600 to AED 1,200 at the mid tier, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 and above for specialist support in an examination year. Packages advertised in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions, which is a useful indication of what the travel component costs when it is itemised.

Two context points are worth holding. Dubai's private sector is still expanding, with seven new private schools opening for 2026-27, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places after six openings in 2025-26 and a 6 per cent rise in enrolment. More IB places means more MYP students and the same thin pool of MYP-experienced science teachers, so booking a regular slot early in the academic year is worth more than negotiating the rate. And if the budget is genuinely tight, a fortnightly session that runs all year beats a weekly one abandoned in November.

sections.heading: How many hours a term an MYP science student actually needs
paragraphs: The honest answer depends on the year group, and buying more than the year needs is the most common way Dubai families waste money on tutoring. In MYP 1 to 3 the usual pattern is one session a week for a single term, aimed at a specific habit rather than at the subject: graph conventions, unit discipline, reading a question properly. Twelve sessions of that work, done once and done properly in MYP 2, saves money every year afterwards, because criterion C habits are durable.

In MYP 4, the split year, the shape changes. One weekly session in the weakest of the three sciences plus a fortnightly review in the second weakest covers most students, which is about eighteen hours across a term rather than thirty-six. Three weekly sessions in three sciences looks thorough on paper and in practice produces a student with no evening left for homework, which is why it tends to be abandoned by half term and paid for in full.

In MYP 5 the calendar drives it. Schools running on-screen eAssessment set internal deadlines well before the external window, and the productive block is six to eight weeks of twice-weekly timed practice, roughly twelve to sixteen hours, front-loaded so the last fortnight is revision of marked work rather than new teaching. For a student who is already secure, a monthly check-in that reviews one marked script is enough and costs a fraction of a retained weekly slot. Ask for the smallest intervention that addresses the named criterion, and raise it only if the next marked piece says you need to.
bullets: MYP 1-3: one weekly session for one term, aimed at a habit not a syllabus
MYP 4: one weekly plus one fortnightly, about eighteen hours a term

sections.heading: Is a cheaper tutor in Dubai legally permitted to teach your child?
paragraphs: Price and legality are connected in this market, and almost nobody writing about Dubai tutoring says so. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and the eligible categories are broad: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so no amount can honestly be quoted.

Because the permit costs nothing, a tutor who does not hold one has no financial excuse. The official route is MoHRE's own service, listed as Issuance of a New Work Permit for Private Tutor Licensing, with no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system. A parent can simply ask to see the permit. A tutor who has one will show it; a tutor who deflects the question has answered it.

There is a second limit worth knowing in this country. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. That rule has been press-reported rather than read here from the current ADEK document, so verify it against ADEK before relying on it. The practical point holds anyway: an arrangement where your child's own science teacher tutors them privately for a fee is one to avoid, however convenient it looks.

Cost: granted free of charge, valid for two years
Route: MoHRE private tutor licensing service, two working days, no fee listed
