sections.heading: Academic honesty in criterion-marked work
paragraphs: Criterion-marked coursework raises the honesty question more often than exam-based courses do, because almost everything is produced at home over weeks. The boundary is the same in every subject group and it is not ambiguous. A tutor may teach content, explain what a descriptor rewards, model a technique on a different example, and give feedback on work the student has already produced alone. A tutor may not author any part of a submitted piece, may not supply text, data, research or analysis for it, and may not edit a draft into a finished state on the student's behalf.

In the Dubai search results this is not a theoretical distinction. Operations in this market sell finished Internal Assessments at fixed prices, and the same logic is applied to Personal Projects and MYP coursework. A student who submits purchased work faces a malpractice process rather than a poor grade, and the school's own academic-honesty policy, not a tutoring contract, governs the outcome. An agency willing to discuss producing a submitted piece is describing a risk, not a service.

There is a second boundary around materials. The IB's subject guides, descriptors, past eAssessment material and teacher support documents are the school's to hold and the IB's to publish. We reference them and point families to ibo.org and to the school's coordinator, and we do not reproduce or distribute them. A tutor offering an unlimited private library of IB documents is usually offering something they are not entitled to distribute.

Saying this out loud narrows the offer and improves it. What a family is buying is teaching, diagnosis and feedback on the student's own work. In a programme where the assessment is the student's own extended output, that is the only kind of help whose benefit survives into the Diploma, where the rules get tighter and the consequences get larger.

process.title: Send returned unit work, not the report
process.description: The useful documents are the student's marked criterion sheets and the task-specific clarifications that came with them. Those show which criteria are costing marks and in what language the teacher is marking. A report gives a grade out of seven that cannot be reverse-engineered, which is why diagnosis from a report wastes the first paid session.

process.title: Ask the coordinator three questions in writing
process.description: Whether the school enters students for MYP eAssessment, what the Personal Project checkpoint dates are, and when the Year 4 option decision is taken. All three change the plan materially, and all three are internal dates that are not published anywhere a family can look them up.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: One free 45-minute lesson per family, no card details collected. It is spent on a live unit from the student's own work rather than on a general assessment, and written feedback follows. If the match is not right, say so and a different tutor is proposed before any payment is made.

process.title: Agree the format and the output
process.description: A weekly subject-group slot, a criterion literacy block, or Personal Project coaching scheduled against the school's own dates. Each carries a named weekly output: a plan written against the clarification, a redraft, a dated journal entry. The output is what makes progress auditable.

process.title: Review against criterion scores, not feelings
process.description: At the halfway point, compare criterion scores from the start of the block with current returned work, criterion by criterion. Bands that have moved come off the plan. Bands that have not either get more time or are set aside deliberately in favour of one that will move.

whyPoints.title: Descriptors before content
whyPoints.description: Most MYP marks are lost to the wording of the task rather than to the subject. Sessions start from the published criteria and the task-specific clarification, because that is the document the teacher marks against and the one students read last.

whyPoints.title: Subject-group literacy, not driving distance
whyPoints.description: MYP families are a minority in a mostly British-curriculum district, so a proximity-based search returns IGCSE tutors. Teaching over live video changes the selection criterion to whether the tutor can read a criterion B descriptor in the right subject group.

whyPoints.title: The calendar belongs to the school
whyPoints.description: Unit windows, project checkpoints and option-evening dates are internal and unpublished. Any plan here is built against dates obtained from the coordinator in writing rather than against an assumed term structure.

whyPoints.title: A project plan that starts early enough
whyPoints.description: The Personal Project criteria reward development over time, which a journal assembled at the deadline cannot show. Coaching is scheduled backwards from the school's submission date so that dated entries exist across months.

whyPoints.title: Limits stated before payment
whyPoints.description: No home visits anywhere in the UAE, no part of a submitted piece authored by a tutor, no IB documents redistributed, no grade promised, and no IB session date published that has not been confirmed with the school or ibo.org.

whyPoints.title: Every figure attributed
whyPoints.description: Market rates here are credited to the organisation that published them and dated October 2026. Regulatory statements are credited to KHDA, u.ae or MoHRE. Nothing is presented as an IB Gram statistic without the data behind it.

faqs.question: Why does my child's MYP grade move up and down between units?
faqs.answer: Because different units assess different criteria. Each MYP subject group has four criteria marked out of eight, and a unit usually samples only two or three of them. A student who is strong on knowing and understanding but weak on evaluating will score well in a unit weighted towards criterion A and poorly in one weighted towards criterion D, with no change in effort or ability. The fix is to read the criterion scores individually rather than the grade out of seven, which is a conversion of criterion totals and hides exactly the information a parent needs.

faqs.question: What is a task-specific clarification and why does it matter so much?
faqs.answer: It is the sheet a teacher issues with an MYP assessment that restates the general criterion descriptors in the language of that particular task. It is the closest thing the programme has to a mark scheme. Students who read it before planning their work score differently from students who read it after submitting, because the descriptors tell them what shape the response has to take. Asking for it, filing it, and planning against it line by line is one of the cheapest grade improvements available in the MYP, and it transfers to every subject group at once.

faqs.question: My child moved from a British school into MYP Year 3. What should the first term cover?
faqs.answer: Criterion literacy, not content. A student arriving from a British or Indian middle school usually has solid subject knowledge and no experience of being marked against descriptors, so the early losses are in criteria B, C and D: method stated without justification, communication marks dropped on terminology, evaluation offered as description. Three or four sessions reading descriptors band by band, then re-marking their own returned work against them, moves more marks in that first term than any amount of extra subject teaching. Content gaps can be audited afterwards, once the marking system is legible.

faqs.question: Does my child's Dubai school enter students for MYP eAssessment?
faqs.answer: Only the MYP coordinator can tell you, and it is worth asking in writing because it changes what the final year prepares for. Schools that enter students add on-screen examinations in several subject groups and externally moderated ePortfolios in others, including Arts, Design and Physical and Health Education. Schools that do not assess Year 5 internally, and the record is the school's own. An eAssessment cohort needs timed performance practised alongside criterion work; a non-eAssessment cohort does not, and rehearsing exam technique there would be misdirected effort.

faqs.question: How early should Personal Project work start in MYP Year 5?
faqs.answer: About six months before the school's submission date, which usually means the goal and the student's own success criteria are agreed in the first term. The criteria reward development over time, and a process journal assembled in the final fortnight cannot show it, so late starts cost marks structurally rather than through poor work. The sequence that works is goal and criteria at six months, research and skills audit at five, product in development at three with the journal recording decisions, report drafting at six weeks, and the reflection written in the final fortnight.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Personal Project without crossing a line?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a boundary that should be stated before any session. A tutor may coach planning and time management, explain what the criteria reward, and give feedback on journal entries and report drafts the student has produced alone. A tutor may not author any part of the report, the product or the journal, and may not supply text or research for them. The supervisor at school holds the formal role. This matters because operations in the UAE search results sell finished assessed work, and a student who submits purchased material faces a malpractice process rather than a low mark.

faqs.question: Which MYP subject group causes the most trouble in Dubai schools?
faqs.answer: Design, more often than families expect, followed by Individuals and Societies. Design is marked substantially on a documented inquiry and development trail, so a strong finished product with no design folder behind it scores poorly, and students who treat it as a practical subject are surprised by the written weighting. Individuals and Societies loses marks on source evaluation: describing a source's content without assessing its origin, purpose, value and limitation caps a student well below the top band regardless of how the essay reads. Both are process problems and both respond quickly to explicit teaching.

faqs.question: Is MYP Mathematics Extended necessary for Higher Level maths later?
faqs.answer: It is the more natural preparation, particularly for Analysis and Approaches, but the decisive question is algebraic fluency under time pressure rather than the course label. A student on Extended who computes well but omits reasoning lines will still find Higher Level hard, and a Standard student with secure algebra can be bridged in a term. The honest audit is to look at criterion C and criterion D scores across a year of returned work, then test the student on timed, unaided algebra. That is better evidence than a grade out of seven or a course title.

faqs.question: What actually changes between MYP Year 5 and Diploma Year 1?
faqs.answer: Timed external performance, and the feedback cycle. The MYP assesses process generously and timed recall barely at all, so a student used to redrafting against a rubric has rarely produced a complete structured answer once, under time, without help. The Diploma also restricts how much feedback a teacher may give on internally assessed work, and its Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge rules are tighter. The content gap is usually smaller than the habit gap, and the habits are best started in Year 5 rather than discovered in the first Diploma term.

faqs.question: How many MYP subject groups can we realistically tutor at once?
faqs.answer: One with real weekly depth, or two if the student's independent-study time can absorb the work set between sessions. Beyond that the sessions become attendance rather than progress, because criterion work requires drafting and redrafting outside the hour. The more efficient alternative for a student struggling across several subjects is a criterion literacy block: three or four subject-light sessions on reading and using the descriptors, which transfers to all eight subject groups at once and usually moves more marks than a second subject-specific slot would.

faqs.question: Does the Arabic and Islamic Education timetable affect MYP study time?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is a real load the programme guide does not describe. Every Dubai private school delivers Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies alongside its licensed curriculum, with instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit and at least 25 minutes advised per lesson. KHDA also requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes strictly prohibited. The practical effect for a family is fewer free periods and a fuller week than an MYP timetable alone suggests.

faqs.question: Can tutoring in Arabic or Islamic Education follow a different syllabus?
faqs.answer: No, and it should not try to. KHDA states that for the mandatory subjects the use of different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited, and that schools must ensure teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval for those subjects. Support outside school is therefore best framed as language work and study skills around the school's own material, with the school remaining the authority on content. Families should also know that Arabic and Islamic education are excluded from the five subjects counted for British-track Ministry of Education equivalency, which is a separate rule.

faqs.question: What does MYP tutoring cost in Jumeirah 1 and the surrounding districts?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai market bands put qualified subject tutors online at roughly AED 150-300 an hour, in-home visits at AED 180-500 with travel included, and IB or IGCSE specialists at AED 200-450 or more. Bestimate's Dubai table gives in-home at AED 180-350; TutorChase publishes AED 270; monthly packages around AED 799 for eight online sessions appear in the market. Those are other organisations' published figures as at October 2026, not an IB Gram price list. For context, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that Dubai private school fees would not rise for 2026-27.

faqs.question: Is there any point tutoring an MYP student in Years 1 to 3?
faqs.answer: Often yes, but for a different reason than in Year 5. Early MYP years are where criterion habits form, and a student who learns in Year 2 to plan against a task-specific clarification carries that through to the Personal Project and into Diploma internal assessment. A short block at that stage is cheap and compounds. What rarely works in the early years is content acceleration: the programme is not content-limited, so pushing ahead of the class produces boredom rather than better criterion scores. One sixty-minute session a week is the sensible ceiling.

faqs.question: What happens if no tutor covers a niche MYP subject group that week?
faqs.answer: We say so and give a date rather than substituting someone who does not know the criteria. Design, Arts and Physical and Health Education have thinner coverage than Mathematics and Sciences, and a specific phase of Language Acquisition can be thinner still. Where the wait is longer than the deadline allows, the honest options are a criterion literacy block with an available tutor, which transfers across subject groups, or starting on the subject that is covered now. Both are explained before any payment, with the limitation named rather than concealed.

faqs.question: Do tutors working with UAE families need a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Private tutoring in the UAE runs on the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, which is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted. MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service states a two-working-day completion time.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-jumeirah-1.closingHeading: Ask the coordinator for the dates, then read the criterion sheets
dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-jumeirah-1.closingBody: Two things make an MYP year plannable. The first is the school's internal calendar: unit windows, Personal Project checkpoints, whether eAssessment applies, and when the Year 4 option decision is taken. The second is the student's returned work with its criterion scores and task-specific clarifications, which show in the school's own language where the marks are going. Send the second and ask the coordinator for the first, and the opening conversation can be about which criterion will move rather than about the programme in general. The trial is one free 45-minute lesson per family, no card details collected, taught on a live unit. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time.

intro.heading: A market with no dates in it
paragraphs: The research behind this page grepped sixty-odd competitor pages for exam-session awareness. The word November returned zero hits on every fetchable page. No competitor names a session, an entry deadline, or a results date. For a market selling exam preparation, that is a remarkable omission, and it is the single clearest gap available to a page like this one.

The omission matters because almost every planning error a Dubai family makes is a calendar error. A parent starts looking for help four weeks before the papers, when the useful window was twelve. A private candidate discovers an entry deadline has passed. A family budgets for an exam-term intensive in March, by which point every specialist in the emirate is booked. None of those is an academic failure; all of them are a consequence of nobody publishing the shape of the year.

So this page counts backwards. It sets out the board deadlines that are published and sourced, explains which dates belong to the board and which to your school, gives a ten-week plan with a measurable output in each week, and states plainly what ten weeks can and cannot change. It also covers the part of the cycle nobody writes about, which is what happens after results: enquiries upon results, remarks and retake entries all have their own deadlines, and they arrive while a family is still absorbing the grades.

One honesty note that shapes the whole page. IB exam dates in this project are not verified. The IB's own site returns an error to automated requests, so no IB session, upload or results date here has been confirmed from the IB itself, and none is published. What this page does publish are Cambridge and Pearson dates, which are sourced from those boards' own pages, and which illustrate the principle well enough to plan by. For your child's IB dates, ask the school's Diploma coordinator or the IB directly, and take the answer in writing. A page that invents a date a family builds a revision plan around has done more damage than a page with no dates on it at all, which is the position almost every competitor in this market occupies by accident rather than by principle.

Teaching is delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to addresses anywhere in the UAE; in-home visiting is a service offered only in India. In exam term that model has a specific practical value, because the specialists who are still free in March are rarely the ones who live within driving distance of your community. It also means a 9pm session during Ramadan, or a 7am slot on a weekend in the final fortnight, is an ordinary request rather than an imposition, and both of those turn out to matter when a candidate is sitting six subjects in a compressed window.

dubai/ib-online-tuition.programmesIntro: The calendar pressure differs by programme, and so does what a short run of sessions can achieve. Each note below names the window that matters at that stage.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: No external examination series for most pupils, which makes the calendar internal and therefore invisible. The window that matters is the school's own assessment cycle, because criterion marks accumulate into reports that inform Diploma option decisions. Pupils who are quietly behind in Year 9 meet the consequence at the Higher Level option blocks two years later.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools that switch to IGCSE at Year 10 hand their pupils an external calendar abruptly, with entry deadlines and board timetables that the family has never had to think about. The first encounter with a Cambridge or Pearson entry deadline usually comes as a surprise in Year 10.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The tightest calendar in school education. Coursework deadlines fall in the autumn and winter of the second year, mocks follow, and the examined components come last, with upload deadlines set by the IB in between. The ten weeks before the papers are the window this page plans, and they are worth more if the preceding twelve months were planned at all.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai private schools following the northern academic year sit the May session. Session windows, upload deadlines and results dates are set by the IB and revised, so confirm each with your school's Diploma coordinator or the IB directly. No date on this page should be treated as the authority for an IB deadline.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The DP courses inside the programme sit on the same examination calendar as any other Diploma course, while the reflective project and career-related study follow internal deadlines. Candidates often misjudge this and treat the whole programme as internally assessed, which produces a late discovery about the examined components.
programmes.countryNote: Because few Dubai schools license the programme, a candidate may be the only one in their year sitting a particular combination, which makes the school's exam administration unfamiliar with it. Confirming the entry position early is worth more here than in a large Diploma cohort.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: No external series, but Cambridge offers Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, which some Dubai schools use as a benchmark. Where a school does, those windows are worth knowing because they are the first external measurement a family ever receives and they are easy to over-interpret.
programmes.countryNote: Checkpoint results in Dubai schools are often the trigger for a family's first tutoring enquiry. The measured, useful response is to read which strands were weak rather than the overall benchmark, because a strand gap at age 11 is a few weeks of work and a headline score is not actionable.

dubai/ib-online-tuition.subjectsIntro: In the final ten weeks, each subject has one component that repays attention more than the others. The entries below name it, because a generic revision plan spends the same time everywhere and gains least.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The calculator-free paper, every time. A candidate who has been leaning on a graphical calculator for routine manipulation will lose marks there that no amount of content revision recovers. Ten weeks is enough to rebuild manual fluency if the drilling starts immediately.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Interpretation in context, drilled as a habit: every numerical answer followed by a sentence referring it back to the situation. This is a two-week change applied across every past paper attempted, and it is the highest-yield correction available in the course.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Paper 1 stem annotation, practised until it is automatic, plus the conventions on extended response: balanced equations, state symbols, mechanism arrows from the right origin. Conventions are checklist work and show up in marked papers within three weeks.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The data-analysis section, which is rarely finished in class and responds faster to coaching than anything else in the subject. Gradient meaning, uncertainty handling and limitation statements are learnable procedures rather than insight.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Command-term discipline and answer length. A candidate writing discuss-length answers to outline questions loses marks twice, on the question and on the time. Correcting it is a fortnight of supervised practice and it releases time across the whole paper.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram discipline: axes and curves labelled, shift drawn, and then explicitly referenced in the prose. Candidates who draw correct diagrams and never mention them forfeit marks already earned, which is the cheapest correction in the subject.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The pre-released case study, which should have been worked for months and usually has not. In a ten-week window the realistic goal is applying three or four tools properly to the stimulus rather than attempting the whole syllabus against it.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: The study bank. Four facts per named study, a method, a finding, a limitation and a link to the topic, held for enough studies to cover the examined options. This is systematic memorisation work with a clear finish line, which suits a ten-week window well.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 timing and Paper 2 comparative structure. Both are structural rather than knowledge-based, which means both can change inside ten weeks. Unseen analysis under timed conditions, repeated weekly, is the single most effective preparation here.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Case specificity: place, date, figure, consequence, for every example a candidate intends to use. Ten weeks is enough to convert a vague store of knowledge into a defined set of deployable examples, which is what the upper bands reward.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Pseudocode conventions, drilled against the published style, and the annually released case study. Python-fluent candidates lose marks for writing Python where pseudocode is required, and that is a correction measured in days rather than weeks.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: By the final ten weeks this component is normally submitted, which is exactly why it belongs on a calendar page. A candidate still writing a Theory of Knowledge essay in the revision window has a scheduling failure that started a year earlier, and the fix is next year's planning rather than this term's.

dubai/ib-online-tuition.regionsIntro: Availability, travel and school exam arrangements vary across the emirate in ways that matter specifically in exam term. These notes concern that window rather than the year as a whole.

regions.name: Dubai Marina and JLT
regions.note: Heavy competition for the 5pm to 7pm window in exam term, when every family in the cluster wants the same hours. Families who fixed a slot in the autumn keep it; families looking in March are choosing from what is left.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches and Dubai Hills Estate
regions.note: Long drives make visiting tutors scarcest precisely when demand peaks, so exam-term availability here is the tightest in the emirate for in-home arrangements. Online slots are unaffected by the February to April traffic.

regions.name: Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim
regions.note: Well supplied with experienced tutors year-round, which means exam-term scarcity bites later here than elsewhere. The constraint becomes subject-specific rather than general: Higher Level sciences go first.

regions.name: Mirdif and Al Qusais
regions.note: Large general tutoring supply and thin Diploma Higher Level supply, a gap that widens in exam term. Candidates here most often need a specialist who is not local, which is a straightforward arrangement over video.

regions.name: Downtown Dubai and Business Bay
regions.note: Pupils travelling back from schools across the emirate return late, so exam-term sessions here commonly run at 8pm or later. That is practical over video and close to impossible for a visiting tutor.

regions.name: Dubai South and Jumeirah Golf Estates
regions.note: Effectively outside the practical range of most tutors in exam term, when nobody is willing to add a long drive to a full week. Online delivery is not a preference in these communities during February to April.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Tecom
regions.note: Central and dense with IB schools, so demand is high and supply is reasonable. This is the cluster where booking three weeks ahead still sometimes works, which is not true elsewhere in exam term.

regions.name: Dubai Silicon Oasis and Academic City
regions.note: Exam-term requests here often combine revision with admissions deadlines, because candidates are managing conditional offers alongside papers. Scheduling around both is the practical challenge rather than finding a tutor.

schoolClusters.city: Schools with established exam administration
schoolClusters.note: Experienced exams officers, clear internal deadlines and reliable timetable communication. Candidates from these cohorts rarely have administrative problems and need technique work in the final stretch.
schools: Jumeirah English Speaking School Arabian Ranches

schoolClusters.city: Newer cohorts and unusual combinations
schoolClusters.note: Schools running the Diploma for only a few cycles, or candidates with combinations the school handles rarely. Confirming the entry position early matters more for these families than for large established cohorts.

dubai/ib-online-tuition.modesIntro: In the final stretch the booking shape should follow the calendar rather than a preference. These three are what the ten weeks before a session actually call for.

modes.title: Post-mock diagnostic pair
modes.description: Two sessions immediately after mocks, before the script goes cold. The first maps every lost mark against a fault type and produces a ranked list. The second starts on the cheapest fault. Nothing else in the final ten weeks produces as much per hour as these two.

modes.title: Ten-week weekly run
modes.description: One slot a week through the run-up, with a measurable output in each week: a timed section, a corrected past paper, a drilled convention checklist. Booked in the autumn, because the specialists who take these are unavailable by March.
bullets: A specific measurable output every week
Timed conditions from week three onward

modes.title: Results-window support
modes.description: A short arrangement after results, when enquiries upon results, remarks and retake entries all have deadlines that arrive during the least clear-headed fortnight of the year. The work is partly academic and mostly administrative triage.
bullets: Reads the marks breakdown before any decision is taken
Identifies which components a remark could plausibly move
Maps the retake entry deadline against the next series

sections.heading: What IB online tuition in Dubai is bought to do in the final stretch
paragraphs: In the ten weeks before a session, tuition can do four things and cannot do a fifth. Being clear about the four is how a family spends a limited budget in the right place, and being clear about the fifth prevents a great deal of disappointment.

It can clear convention faults, which are the cheapest marks available anywhere in the Diploma: missing state symbols, unlabelled axes, numbers without units, mechanism arrows from the wrong origin. It can fix timing, which is a triage skill rather than a knowledge one. It can drill command-term discipline so that an outline question receives an outline answer. And it can convert a vague store of knowledge into a defined set of deployable examples, which is what the upper bands reward in the essay subjects.

What it cannot do in ten weeks is rebuild two years of missing foundations. A candidate who has not understood moles since the first term of the first year is not going to acquire that in eight sessions alongside five other subjects, and any provider suggesting otherwise is selling hope. The honest version of that conversation produces a different plan: triage the subjects where marks are cheapest, accept the position in the subject that needed a year, and protect the grades that are reachable.

The calendar is what makes this allocation possible. A family that knows the mock window, the coursework completion date, the board entry deadlines and the session dates can place each intervention where it belongs. A family working from the single fact that exams are in May makes every decision late. That is the entire argument for publishing dates, and it is why the next section exists.
bullets: Convention faults: the cheapest marks in the Diploma
Timing and triage: a skill, not knowledge
Command-term discipline: a fortnight of supervised practice
Deployable examples: converting knowledge into usable material
What ten weeks cannot do is rebuild two years of foundations

sections.heading: The board calendars that are published and sourced
paragraphs: Three boards matter to Dubai families: Cambridge International and Pearson Edexcel for IGCSE and International GCSE, and the IB for the Diploma. Two of the three publish calendars that can be quoted. The third could not be verified for this project, and the difference is stated rather than smoothed over.

Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Its March 2027 series provides the clearest worked example of how far ahead the administration runs: the examination period is 3 February to 4 March 2027, final entries were due on 27 November 2026, forecast grades are due on 27 February 2027, results are released on Cambridge International Direct on 13 May and certificates follow in late June.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May or June and in November each year. The November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. For results timing, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, including International GCSE November 2027, which is why any session table should link the live official timetable rather than restate dates that can be revised.

For the IB, no date is published here. The IB's assessment pages return an error to automated requests, so nothing in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself. Secondary sources circulate windows for 2027, and they are not good enough to publish on a page a family might plan around. Ask your school's Diploma coordinator or the IB directly, and get the answer in writing.

sections.heading: Why entry deadlines sit months before the papers
paragraphs: The single most useful thing a family can understand about examination administration is that the paperwork runs on a different clock from the teaching. Cambridge's March 2027 series shows it starkly: final entries closed on 27 November 2026 for examinations beginning on 3 February 2027. More than two months separate the two, and a candidate who was not entered in November is not sitting the paper in February, whatever their preparation.

The reason is logistical rather than bureaucratic. Papers must be printed, allocated and dispatched to centres worldwide, zones have to be assigned, access arrangements have to be approved, and forecast grades have to be collected. All of that is upstream of the first paper, and none of it can be done retrospectively.

The practical consequence for a Dubai family is a distinction worth drawing explicitly. Board deadlines are immovable and are handled by your school's exams officer. School deadlines, including internal coursework dates and mock windows, are set by the school and occasionally negotiable. Confusing the two produces two characteristic errors: treating a board deadline as flexible, and treating a school deadline as absolute when a conversation would have helped.

The useful habit is to ask the exams officer, in writing, in the autumn, for three things: the entry deadline that applies to your child, the series they are entered for, and the zone or timetable version that applies. Those three facts prevent almost every administrative disaster that befalls candidates in this region, and they take one email to obtain.

sections.heading: The six Cambridge zones, and a real administrative risk
paragraphs: This is a small detail with a large consequence, and it affects families in this region more than most. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, and the examination timetable differs between them. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and adds that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one.

The way this goes wrong is entirely ordinary. A parent finds a timetable online, or in a parents group, or from a relative in another country, and plans the revision schedule around it. The dates are real dates from a real Cambridge document, for a different zone. A paper sat in the morning in one zone may be sat in the afternoon in another, or on a different day.

The protection is a single rule with no exceptions: the only timetable a family should use is the one issued by their own school's exams officer, confirmed in writing, for their own centre. Not a website, not a forum, not another family's copy, and not this page, which deliberately publishes no candidate timetable.

The same principle extends to IB candidates for a different reason. IB session windows and upload deadlines are set by the IB and revised, and secondary sources circulate dates that look authoritative. A candidate planning around a circulated date rather than a school-confirmed one is taking an avoidable risk during the worst possible fortnight to take one.

Timetables differ between zones, including by day and session
Cambridge cannot accept responsibility for a missed exam from a wrong timetable
Use only the timetable issued by your own school's exams officer

sections.heading: Private candidates in Dubai: what changes
paragraphs: A candidate sitting examinations outside a school as a private candidate takes on administrative work that a school would otherwise absorb, and the differences are worth knowing before the decision rather than after. This situation arises in Dubai more often than elsewhere, usually after a school move, a relocation or a decision to sit an additional subject.

The entry itself goes through a centre that accepts private candidates, and that centre sets its own fees, deadlines and subject availability, which are usually earlier and narrower than a school's. Entry fees are set by the board and the centre rather than by any tutor, and the only reliable way to budget for them is to ask the centre in writing. No figure for them appears on this page, because it would be a guess.

Two practical constraints catch private candidates in particular. Subjects with a required practical or performance component may not be available at every centre, and coursework components usually require a centre willing to supervise and authenticate them. Those two facts determine which subjects a private candidate can realistically sit, and they should be checked before any teaching is arranged.

The timetable rule applies with extra force here. A private candidate has no school exams officer quietly checking the zone version, which means the responsibility for confirming the correct timetable sits with the family and the centre. Ask the centre to confirm the zone and the version in writing, and keep it.
bullets: The centre sets its own fees, deadlines and subject availability
Entry fees come from the board and the centre, never from a tutor
Practical and coursework components are not available everywhere
There is no school exams officer checking the zone version for you
Confirm the centre, the series and the timetable version in writing

sections.heading: After results: the cycle nobody plans for
paragraphs: Results day is treated as an endpoint and it is a decision point, with several deadlines sitting immediately behind it. A family absorbing an unexpected grade has a short window in which to act, and acting well requires information rather than speed.

The first thing to obtain is the marks breakdown by component, which shows where the result came from. A grade that fell short because one paper underperformed relative to the others is a different situation from one where every component landed in the same place. The first may be worth an enquiry upon results; the second almost never is, and understanding the difference saves both money and hope.

Enquiries upon results, including remarks, have their own deadlines set by the board and are requested through the centre. They carry fees, they can move a mark down as well as up, and they are worth considering mainly where a grade boundary is close and a single component is out of line with the others. Retake entries have separate deadlines that may fall before the enquiry outcome is known, which is the genuinely difficult part of the timing.

For Dubai families there is an additional layer, which is equivalency. Recognition of a qualification for UAE university entry runs through the Ministry of Education and the emirate attestation authority, and it is a process a family follows rather than something a tutoring provider performs or can accelerate. Build the timeline for it from the authority's own guidance rather than from any third party.

sections.heading: A ten-week plan with something measurable in each week
paragraphs: Revision plans fail because they are lists of topics rather than lists of outputs. A plan built on outputs can be checked weekly by a parent with no subject knowledge, which is the only kind of plan that survives ten weeks of a teenager's resistance.

The plan below assumes one subject with one weekly session, after mocks, with a candidate who has a mapped fault list. If there are two subjects, run it twice with the heavy weeks staggered; if there are three, the honest advice is to pick two. Each week has one output that either exists at the end of the week or does not, and no output is an opinion.

The front half is about clearing cheap faults, because they are cheap and because early visible gains buy a candidate's cooperation for the harder work later. The back half moves to full-length timed papers under real conditions, which is the only way to test whether the corrections hold under pressure. A candidate who has corrected conventions in isolated practice and never sat a full paper will lose them again in the hall.

The final fortnight deliberately contains less new work than families expect. Week nine is a full timed paper and a comparison against week three. Week ten is consolidation of the two faults that still recur, plus the administrative check: timetable confirmed with the exams officer, equipment, and the sleeping pattern. Nothing new is introduced, because nothing new becomes reliable in ten days.

sections.heading: What ten weeks changes, and what it does not
paragraphs: Honesty here is worth more than encouragement, because a family that knows what is achievable allocates correctly and a family that does not spends the same money for less. The pattern is consistent enough to describe.

Highly responsive in ten weeks: conventions, timing, command-term discipline, diagram labelling, the data-analysis sections of science papers, and the conversion of vague knowledge into specific deployable examples. All of these are procedural, all are drillable, and all appear in marked work within three or four weeks of starting. For a candidate sitting two marks below a boundary, this is usually where the two marks are.

Partially responsive: a single topic never properly understood, which can be rebuilt in ten weeks if it is one topic and the candidate does the work between sessions. Weak extended-response structure, which improves but needs longer to become automatic under pressure.

Not responsive: two years of absent foundations, a coursework mark already submitted, and a grade needed for an offer that is three grades above current performance. Those are not tutoring problems and should not be sold as such. The right response is triage, which means protecting the grades that are reachable and being straight with the candidate about the one that is not. A family told this in February makes better decisions than a family told it in May. The decision triage produces is usually narrower than families expect: two subjects chosen to defend, one subject consciously left where it is, and the hours redistributed accordingly rather than spread evenly across six.

sections.heading: Evidence in the final stretch, and why it matters more now
paragraphs: In a ten-week window there is no time to discover in week eight that the arrangement is not working, so the evidence requirements tighten rather than relax. Three artefacts carry the weight, and all three come out of the sessions themselves rather than from a progress report.

The first is the ranked fault list from week one, which is the baseline everything else is measured against. The second is the sequence of timed attempts, one in week three, one in week seven and one in week nine, which are directly comparable because they were sat under the same conditions. The third is the weekly output, which either exists or does not.

Because teaching is delivered over live video on a shared board, all of this persists as files rather than as paper in a bag. In the last fortnight that archive becomes the revision material: a candidate reviewing their own annotated attempts, with each correction beside the error that produced it, is revising their own faults rather than a generic checklist. It costs nothing extra, having been produced as a by-product of the teaching.

The review question in exam term is also sharper than usual. If the week-nine paper shows the same faults as week one, the ten weeks did not work and the remaining fortnight should be spent on the two cheapest marks rather than on continuing a plan that has been tested and failed. That is an uncomfortable conversation and a far better one than the alternative, which is finding out on results day.
bullets: The week-one fault list is the baseline for everything after it
Timed attempts in weeks three, seven and nine are directly comparable

process.title: Email the exams officer in the autumn
process.description: Ask in writing for three facts: the entry deadline that applies to your child, the series they are entered for, and the zone or timetable version for your centre. Those three prevent almost every administrative problem that befalls candidates in this region, and they cost one email.

process.title: Book exam-term availability early
process.description: Specialist slots between February and April are taken by the autumn. Reserving the slot is the purchase; when the sessions happen is a separate matter. Families who do this pay autumn rates and get the person they wanted rather than whoever remains.

process.title: Send the mock script, not the mock grade
process.description: The script with the annotations is the instrument. The grade is a number produced against boundaries the school chose, often deliberately severe. One session maps every lost mark against a fault type and produces the ranked list the rest of the plan runs on.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: A full session with the proposed specialist at no cost and with no card required, spent on the mock script. You leave with the ranked fault list and an honest statement of which faults ten weeks can realistically clear and which it cannot.

process.title: Check the weekly output, not the mood
process.description: Each week of the plan has one output that exists or does not, checkable by a parent with no subject knowledge. If three consecutive weeks produce nothing, the arrangement has a problem that will not fix itself in the time remaining.

whyPoints.title: Dates published, with their sources
whyPoints.description: Cambridge and Pearson deadlines quoted from the boards' own pages, including the March 2027 series as a worked example of how far ahead entries close. The word November returned no hits across the competitor pages researched for this project.

whyPoints.title: No IB date invented
whyPoints.description: The IB's assessment pages could not be verified for this project, so no IB session, upload or results date appears here. A page that fabricates a date a family plans around is worse than a page with no dates, and this market has plenty of the latter.

whyPoints.title: The zone risk named
whyPoints.description: Cambridge allocates centres to six administrative zones with different timetables and states that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong version. The rule that follows is to use only the exams officer's copy.

whyPoints.title: A plan made of outputs
whyPoints.description: Ten weeks with one measurable output each, checkable by a parent with no subject knowledge. Topic lists are not plans, because nobody can tell from the outside whether a topic was revised or merely read.

whyPoints.title: Triage stated honestly
whyPoints.description: Ten weeks clears conventions, timing and command-term faults reliably. It does not rebuild two years of foundations, and saying so in February lets a family protect the grades that are reachable instead of spreading effort evenly across subjects.

whyPoints.title: Exam-term availability disclosed
whyPoints.description: Specialist supply genuinely runs out between February and April, and we say which subjects go first rather than taking a booking we cannot staff. A dated waiting position is more useful to a family in March than an optimistic yes.

faqs.question: When do Cambridge IGCSE exams actually take place?
faqs.answer: Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. There is also a March series in some regions: for March 2027 the examination period runs from 3 February to 4 March 2027. Which series your child sits is a decision made by the school, and the timetable that applies depends on the administrative zone your centre is allocated to, so the version to use is the one the exams officer issues.

faqs.question: How far before the papers does an exam entry close?
faqs.answer: Months. Cambridge's March 2027 series is the clearest illustration: final entries were due on 27 November 2026 for examinations beginning on 3 February 2027, more than two months later. Forecast grades for that series are due on 27 February 2027. The reason is logistical rather than bureaucratic, since papers have to be printed, allocated and dispatched and access arrangements approved. A candidate not entered by the deadline does not sit the paper, however well prepared they are.

faqs.question: On what dates did Pearson release its recent International GCSE results?
faqs.answer: Pearson publishes results on a set schedule per series. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. International GCSE examinations are available in May or June and in November each year, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so the live official timetable is the version to work from rather than any restatement of it.

faqs.question: Why does this page not give IB exam dates?
faqs.answer: Because none could be verified. The IB's own assessment pages return an error to automated requests, so no IB session window, upload deadline or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself. Secondary sources circulate dates for upcoming sessions and they are not a good enough basis for a family's planning. The reliable route is your school's Diploma coordinator or the IB directly, with the answer taken in writing. A fabricated date on a page a family plans around is worse than no date at all.

faqs.question: What are the Cambridge exam zones and why do they matter?
faqs.answer: Cambridge allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones, and the timetable differs between them, including by day and by session. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. The failure mode is ordinary: a parent finds a real Cambridge timetable online that belongs to a different zone. Use only the version issued by your own centre's exams officer, confirmed in writing.

faqs.question: Which deadlines belong to the school and which to the exam board?
faqs.answer: Board deadlines are the entry deadline, access arrangement approval, forecast grade submission, the examination period itself and the results release. Those are immovable and are handled by the school's exams officer. School deadlines are internal coursework dates and mock windows, set by the school and occasionally negotiable. Two characteristic errors come from confusing them: treating a board deadline as flexible, which is fatal, and treating a school deadline as absolute when a conversation with the coordinator would have produced a sensible accommodation.

faqs.question: What changes if my child sits exams as a private candidate in Dubai?
faqs.answer: The administrative work that a school would absorb becomes yours. Entries go through a centre that accepts private candidates, and that centre sets its own fees, deadlines and subject availability, usually earlier and narrower than a school's. Entry fees come from the board and the centre, not from any tutor, so get them in writing from the centre. Two constraints catch private candidates: subjects with required practical components may not be offered everywhere, and coursework needs a centre willing to supervise and authenticate it.

faqs.question: Is it worth requesting a remark after disappointing results?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the decision should follow the component breakdown rather than the grade. A result where one paper underperformed relative to the others, with a grade boundary close by, is the situation where an enquiry upon results is most worth considering. A result where every component landed consistently is almost never worth it. Enquiries are requested through the centre, carry fees, run to deadlines set by the board, and can move a mark down as well as up. Read the breakdown before anyone pays for anything.

faqs.question: Can we plan a retake before the remark result comes back?
faqs.answer: Frequently you have to, and it is the genuinely difficult part of the timing. Retake entry deadlines for the next series can fall before an enquiry upon results is resolved, which means a family may be deciding on a retake without knowing whether the original grade will change. The practical approach is to establish both dates immediately: the enquiry deadline and the retake entry deadline for the next available series, both through the centre, and then decide with the calendar rather than the hope in front of you.

faqs.question: How late is too late to start exam preparation for the May session?
faqs.answer: Ten to twelve weeks is a genuine window and four weeks is not nothing, provided the expectations match. In ten weeks conventions, timing, command-term discipline, diagram marks and the data-analysis sections of science papers can all change measurably, because they are procedural and drillable. In four weeks the realistic work is timed paper practice plus the two cheapest convention faults. What neither window can do is rebuild two years of missing foundations, and a provider who suggests otherwise is selling hope rather than teaching.

faqs.question: Why does specialist availability run out in February?
faqs.answer: Because demand across Dubai concentrates in the same ten weeks and the supply of people who have taught a specific Higher Level subject is finite. The same tutor with open slots in October has none in March. Higher Level sciences and Mathematics Analysis and Approaches go first, then Economics at Higher Level. The practical consequence is that reserving the slot is the purchase and should be done in the autumn, separately from when the sessions actually happen. Families who book in March choose from what remains.

faqs.question: What should a ten-week revision plan actually contain?
faqs.answer: One measurable output per week rather than a list of topics, because nobody outside the room can tell whether a topic was revised or merely read. Week one produces a ranked fault list from the mock script. Weeks two to six clear cheap faults and introduce timed sections. Weeks seven and nine are full-length timed papers that can be compared against each other. Week ten contains no new learning at all, only consolidation of the two faults that still recur plus confirming the timetable with the exams officer in writing.

faqs.question: Should we use the mock grade or the mock script to plan with?
faqs.answer: The script, always. Mock grades are produced against boundaries the school selects, sometimes deliberately severe to create urgency, while real boundaries are set per session by the board afterwards and are not published in advance. A mock 4 and a mock 5 can be two marks apart on the same paper. The script, by contrast, shows exactly where the marks went, and mapping every lost mark against a fault type takes one session and produces the list the whole plan then runs on.

faqs.question: Do exam-term sessions have to fit around Ramadan and school timings?
faqs.answer: They have to, and they can. School timings shorten during Ramadan and the working day changes, which moves when a candidate can genuinely concentrate; post-Iftar sessions often work better that month than a tired shortened afternoon. Eid holidays fall on a lunar calendar and move each year relative to the exam season, so the number of usable weeks before the papers differs year to year. Count usable weeks rather than calendar weeks when building a plan, and schedule over video so that a 9pm session involves nobody driving.

faqs.question: Are exam-term lessons for Dubai candidates delivered online?
faqs.answer: Yes, one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to addresses anywhere in the UAE; in-home visiting is a service offered only in India. In exam term that model matters more than usual for a practical reason: the specialists still free in March are rarely the ones living within driving distance of your community, and a visiting tutor adding a long drive to an already full week in February is the first arrangement to be cancelled.

dubai/ib-online-tuition.closingHeading: Start with the mock script and the exams officer
dubai/ib-online-tuition.closingBody: Two actions make the ten weeks before a session work, and the first costs nothing but an email. Ask your school's exams officer, in writing, for the entry deadline that applies to your child, the series they are entered for and the timetable version for your centre. Then send us the mock script rather than the mock grade. The trial session is a full hour over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with no card required, spent mapping every lost mark against a fault type. You leave with a ranked list and an honest statement of which faults ten weeks will clear and which it will not.

intro.heading: Sixty minutes, described rather than advertised
paragraphs: Almost every page selling online tutoring to Dubai families describes the experience and not the content. Lessons are interactive. Tutors are passionate. The platform is easy to use. None of that tells a parent what will happen between 5pm and 6pm on a Tuesday, which is the only question that matters when the alternative is a person sitting at the kitchen table.

So here is the structure. A Diploma session opens on the pupil's own marked work, displayed on a shared board. The first block identifies and names the fault, out loud, with the script in front of both of them. The middle blocks work the fault: worked examples the tutor builds live, then the pupil working alone on the same board while the tutor watches the pen rather than the face. The final block sets what the pupil will produce before the next session and writes the note that records what was addressed.

What makes that work is not enthusiasm, it is the board. A shared annotation surface where both parties write is closer to sitting side by side at a desk than video conferencing suggests, because the attention of both people is on the same page rather than on each other. Diploma work is written work, and written work is what a shared board is for. A pupil solving a problem while the tutor watches each line appear is being taught in the only way that actually reveals where the method breaks.

The second thing that makes it work is that nothing evaporates. A tutor who visits a Dubai home leaves behind whatever happened to be written on paper, which goes into a school bag. A session on a shared board leaves every worked example, every annotated script and every correction as a file the pupil can reopen in April. In the final weeks before the May session, that archive is the revision material, and it is specific to one pupil's faults rather than generic.

IB Gram does not send tutors to addresses anywhere in the UAE. In-home visiting is a service offered only in India, and teaching for Dubai families is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. The rest of this page is the honest version of what that means: the tools, the failure modes, how a science practical is handled, what the Dubai week does to scheduling, and what a camera genuinely costs compared with presence. None of it is an argument that screens are better than people. It is an argument that for written, specification-bound Diploma work the scarce resource in this emirate is a teacher who has marked that paper, and that such a person is reachable by video and usually not by car.

dubai/ib-online-tutor.programmesIntro: Session structure changes with age more than with subject, because attention span and independence change. The notes below describe what an online session actually looks like at each stage.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Shorter sessions, usually thirty to forty minutes, built around a small number of activities with visible progress inside each. A parent within earshot at the start helps, and the board is used for games and quick-fire work rather than for extended problems. This is the stage where presence genuinely helps most, and families should weigh that honestly.
programmes.countryNote: For Dubai primary pupils the practical scheduling constraint is the school transport window, which can return a child home as late as 4.30pm, and the mandatory UAE subjects that KHDA requires add to an already long day. A shorter, earlier session is almost always better than a longer one after 6pm.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Sixty minutes, with the criterion being worked on named at the start and revisited at the end. Middle Years pupils benefit from seeing a descriptor on screen beside their own work, which is difficult to arrange on paper and trivial on a shared board. Independent work inside the session matters more here than at primary level.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai Middle Years pupils in schools that switch to IGCSE at Year 10 often have a mixed assessment diet in Year 9, and an online session can hold both the criterion descriptor and an IGCSE specification extract on screen at once, which is the clearest way to show a pupil why the same answer scores differently.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The stage the online model suits best. Diploma work is written, specification-bound and evidence-based, and a sixteen-year-old can work independently on a shared board while a tutor watches the method rather than the room. Marked scripts, mark schemes, criterion descriptors and the pupil's own attempt can all be on screen simultaneously, which no kitchen table manages.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai Diploma candidates sit the May session, and the final ten weeks are when the retained session archive earns its keep: a pupil revising from their own annotated scripts works on their own faults rather than on a generic revision guide. Confirm all session dates with your school's Diploma coordinator or the IB directly.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Sessions mix Diploma course teaching with process coaching on the reflective project, and the mix shifts across the year. Because so few Dubai schools license the programme, the tutor is frequently not in the emirate at all, which makes live video the only practical arrangement rather than a preference.
programmes.countryNote: A Career-related Programme candidate in Dubai may be the only one in their school. Screen sharing a published criterion document and working through it line by line substitutes, imperfectly but usefully, for the peer group and departmental experience that a Diploma candidate has around them.

dubai/ib-online-tutor.subjectsIntro: What the screen is used for differs by subject. Each entry below names the specific thing an online session can do in that subject that a paper-and-table session cannot.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The pupil works a problem line by line on the shared board while the tutor watches the method appear. That is the single most diagnostic activity in maths teaching, and it is easier online than in person because the written work is large, saved and reviewable rather than squeezed into a margin.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistical output, a graphing tool and the question can be on screen together, which is how the interpretation step is actually taught. A pupil who writes a conclusion with the data visible beside it learns to refer back to context, which is where this course's marks sit.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Mechanisms drawn arrow by arrow with the tutor stopping the pen at the moment it starts from the wrong place. Paper 1 stems can be annotated on screen, which turns stem-reading from advice into a visible procedure the pupil repeats twenty times.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Graph work, gradient interpretation and uncertainty handling all benefit from a shared surface and a saved record. Data from the pupil's own practical can be loaded and worked on directly, which is more useful than any demonstration.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Mark schemes and the pupil's answer side by side, which is the fastest way to teach command-term discipline. Diagram labelling and data-based questions work well on screen, and the annotated versions are retained for revision.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams drawn live, labelled live, and then referenced in a written paragraph in the same session. The commentary portfolio can be worked with the article open beside the syllabus section list, which makes the coverage rule concrete rather than abstract.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The pre-released case study can be annotated collaboratively across several sessions, building a single marked-up document the pupil keeps. That document is the preparation, and it is the main reason to start on the case study months before the paper.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Study banks built as a shared document, four facts per study, growing session by session. The write-up of the experimental study is reviewed against its criteria on screen, with the descriptor visible beside the pupil's own paragraph.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Unseen texts annotated together in real time, which is exactly how Paper 1 is actually done under exam conditions. For Paper 2, two sets of notes can be displayed side by side so the comparative spine of each paragraph is visible rather than described.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Code and IB pseudocode can be shown together, which is the quickest cure for the commonest mark loss in the subject. Screen sharing a development environment while the pupil types means the tutor sees the error being made rather than the finished bug.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: A claim, a counterclaim and an example mapped on a shared board as the conversation happens, so the structure of the argument becomes visible to the pupil. The map is saved, and the candidate writes their own essay from their own map.

subjects.name: Arabic B
subjects.description: Oral components rehearsed on video, which is closer to the assessment format than a conversation across a table. Recordings of the pupil's own practice can be reviewed for range used accurately rather than range attempted, which is what the marking rewards.

sections.heading: What an IB online tutor in Dubai does for sixty minutes
paragraphs: A Diploma session has four blocks and they are not negotiable in order, because each one depends on the previous. What follows is the actual structure, with what exists at the end of each block.

The first ten minutes are the pupil's most recent marked work on the shared board. Not a conversation about how school is going, which is pleasant and uses the most valuable minutes of the hour. The tutor and the pupil read the lost marks together and the tutor names the fault out loud, in the pupil's hearing, in specific terms: this answer scored two out of five because the explanation stops before the cause. A pupil who can name their own fault is already most of the way to fixing it.

The next thirty minutes work that fault, and the sequence matters. The tutor builds two or three worked examples live on the board, narrating the decision at each step rather than presenting a finished solution. Then the pupil takes the pen. The tutor's job during that stretch is to watch the method appear line by line and intervene at the step where it breaks, not after the wrong answer arrives. This is the part of teaching that a shared board does better than a sheet of paper, because both people see the same large, saved surface.

The final twenty minutes split in two. Fifteen are the pupil working independently on a question they have not seen, under something resembling exam conditions, while the tutor stays silent and watches. Five are for setting what the pupil will produce before the next session and writing the note that records the component, the criterion and what changed. The note takes two minutes and it is the artefact a parent will actually use.

sections.heading: The tools, and the job each one does
paragraphs: Online tutoring is often sold on its platform, which is the wrong emphasis. The tools matter only in so far as each replaces something a tutor in a room would do, and four of them do almost all the work.

The shared annotation board replaces the sheet of paper between two people at a desk, and improves on it in two respects: it is large enough for both to write without crowding, and it is saved. The screen share replaces looking over a shoulder, which is how a tutor watches a pupil use a graphing calculator, a spreadsheet or a development environment. Document upload replaces the folder of marked work in a school bag, with the difference that the tutor can read it before the session rather than during it.

The video window itself does the least work and gets the most attention. Its job is to carry tone and to let the tutor see whether a pupil is lost, which it does imperfectly. Most of a session's real attention is on the board, exactly as it would be at a desk, and a tutor who spends the hour looking at the pupil's face rather than at their working is doing the wrong thing in either format.

What should be ignored is the long tail of features that sound impressive. Recorded lessons are occasionally useful and mostly unwatched. Gamified progress dashboards measure attendance. Artificial intelligence assistants that generate practice questions produce material not written to the specification, which is worse than no material. The useful technology list is short, which is why nobody markets it.

sections.heading: Connection, bandwidth and the things that genuinely go wrong
paragraphs: Dubai's domestic connectivity is good, and the failures that affect sessions are rarely about raw bandwidth. They are about the household, the device and the room, and all three are fixable in advance by a family that knows to look.

The commonest failure is the device. A pupil joining on a phone cannot write on a shared board usefully and cannot see a mark scheme and their own answer at once, so the session degrades into a conversation. A tablet with a stylus is good. A laptop with a mouse is workable. A laptop with a cheap graphics tablet is better than either for mathematics and chemistry. A phone is not a solution for Diploma work, and a provider who says it is fine is managing you rather than teaching.

The second is the room. A pupil sitting in a living room with a television on will not sustain fifteen minutes of independent timed work, and the tutor will see the attention go without being able to do much about it. A door that closes matters more than a fast connection. The third is scheduling collisions with the household: a session at 7pm in a flat where dinner happens at 7pm fails for reasons nobody will mention.

Genuine technical failure happens occasionally and should have a stated answer rather than an apology. The practical arrangement is that a session dropping in the first ten minutes is rescheduled at no cost, a session lost mid-way is continued or credited, and the tutor keeps a phone number to confirm what is happening rather than leaving a parent watching a frozen screen. Ask any provider what their answer is before you need it.

sections.heading: How a science practical works when the tutor is not in the laboratory
paragraphs: This is the fair question about online science teaching, and it deserves a straight answer rather than a reassurance. A tutor over video cannot supervise a titration or stand beside a pupil adjusting an oscilloscope, and nobody should pretend otherwise.

What matters is that the practical work in a Diploma science is done in the pupil's school laboratory under their teacher's supervision, because it has to be. The assessed individual investigation is carried out there, with the school's equipment and the school's risk assessment. Private tutoring is not where practical work happens in any delivery format, including in-home: a tutor at a kitchen table in Dubai Marina is not running a laboratory either.

Where tutoring genuinely contributes is before and after the bench. Before: interrogating the research question until it has a controllable independent variable, planning a method that will produce enough data points, and anticipating which variables will need controlling. After: processing the data, propagating uncertainties, drawing a conclusion the data actually supports, and evaluating the method honestly. Those are the parts the criteria reward most heavily, and they are entirely screen-based work.

The same logic applies to examined practical skills. Paper 2 data-based questions and the data analysis section of the Higher Level paper test processing and interpretation of unfamiliar data, not manual dexterity. Those sections respond extremely well to a shared board loaded with real datasets, and they are the parts of the subject that classroom time most often runs out before reaching.

sections.heading: Scheduling against the Dubai week
paragraphs: Sessions run on Gulf Standard Time, which sounds trivial and is not. A family being offered slots by a UK agency is being offered a tutor's afternoon, which is a Dubai pupil's late evening, and the arrangement either produces a tired pupil or quietly collapses after a month.

The real constraints in a Dubai week are school transport, co-curricular commitments and the household. Bus routes can return a pupil as late as 4.30pm, which makes a 4pm slot impossible regardless of intention. CAS commitments, sports fixtures and music lessons occupy fixed evenings. Dinner is a real appointment. A slot chosen without mapping those three things is a slot that will be cancelled, and repeated cancellation is how arrangements end.

The UAE calendar adds two things no competitor page in this market mentions. School timings shorten during Ramadan and the working day changes, which redistributes when a pupil can concentrate: post-Iftar sessions often work better that month than a tired shortened afternoon. Eid holidays fall on a lunar calendar and move each year relative to the exam season, so the number of usable weeks before a deadline changes from year to year.

The practical benefit of video delivery here is flexibility that in-home arrangements cannot match. A post-Iftar session at 9pm is straightforward when nobody is driving across the emirate to reach it. So is a 7am weekend slot in the final weeks before the May session, which some candidates genuinely prefer and which no visiting tutor would offer.
