sections.heading: The scientific investigation, criterion by criterion
paragraphs: The investigation is a single piece of work: one student-designed experiment, written up in no more than 3,000 words, marked out of 24 against four criteria of six marks each, worth a fifth of the final grade. It is marked by the school and moderated by the IB. Four criteria, six marks each, is the whole of it, and knowing that changes how a student allocates their time, because evaluation is worth exactly as much as data analysis and is usually given a fraction of the attention.

Two of the four criteria are where almost all of the loss happens. Research design fails when the question is too broad to answer with the apparatus actually available in a school laboratory in Dubai, which is the commonest version of the problem: an ambitious question, a borrowed data set, and no controlled variable. Evaluation fails when limitations are described generically, as human error, more trials and better equipment, rather than as the specific thing that limited this measurement on this apparatus.

A tutor's job on this piece is bounded and should be stated plainly. Questioning a research question, pointing at an uncertainty that has not been propagated, and asking why a conclusion goes beyond the data are all teaching. Supplying text, restructuring a report into its final form, or handing over a method is not, and under IB academic-honesty rules it puts the student's whole diploma at risk. The student does the work; the tutor asks what a moderator will ask.

sections.heading: Where Physics marks actually go missing, theme by theme
paragraphs: Diagnosis beats coverage. A student who has sat one mock has already told you where the marks are going, and a tutor who reads that script before the first lesson can usually name the three recurring errors inside twenty minutes. In this corridor the same handful of failures turn up again and again, and they are rarely about the hardest content in the course.

Theme A loses marks on momentum and on circular motion, almost always because the free-body diagram was skipped and the resolved components were guessed. Theme B loses them on the distinction between heat and temperature in words, and on the gas laws when a volume is left in cubic centimetres. Theme C loses them on standing waves, where students describe what a node is without saying what it means for the wavelength. Theme D loses them wholesale, because potential and field strength are treated as interchangeable and the signs are lost.

Theme E loses marks on decay calculations, where logarithms are the real obstacle, and on the photoelectric effect, where a student who can recite the equation cannot say which quantity the gradient of the graph gives. None of this needs a longer course. It needs a tutor who marks the student's own work against the published expectations and then refuses to move on until the same question is answered cleanly a second time, a week later. The pattern repeats often enough across themes that it is worth stating as a rule: the second clean answer a week later is the evidence, and the first one is only a hope.

sections.heading: The JBR afternoon: when a Physics session can realistically start
paragraphs: The most common reason a tutoring arrangement in the towers fails is not the tutor. It is a session booked at a time that only existed on paper. A slot agreed in September for 16:30 collapses in October when an activity starts, and after three rescheduled lessons the family concludes that tutoring does not work for their child. Picking the slot from the afternoon pattern, rather than from the parent's calendar, fixes that before it happens.

The patterns are predictable. On a plain weekday with no activity, a student bussing back from Al Sufouh is inside the tower before four and can start at a quarter to five with their head still working. Add one after-school activity and arrival slides past five, which makes an 18:00 start the honest option and makes new teaching a poor use of it. A double-period science day is the one to avoid entirely: three hours of physics before lunch means a fourth hour in the evening buys almost nothing.

Two patterns are worth planning for in advance. Mock fortnight frees up mornings, which is the only time in the year when timed papers can be sat and marked in the same session. And a shortened Friday, where the school runs one, gives the single unhurried block that suits the investigation, the one task that cannot be done well in forty-five minutes between a bus and a meal. That constraint is also why the pool of physics specialists willing to make the trip is small, and why the specialist who teaches Theme D best may not be in it.

sections.heading: What a Physics tutor may and may not touch, and who is permitted to teach
paragraphs: Two boundaries are worth knowing before you hire anyone. The first is academic honesty. Under IB rules the scientific investigation must be the student's own work, and a tutor who supplies a method, rewrites a conclusion or hands over text has exposed the student to a malpractice finding that can cost the whole diploma. Feedback, questioning and teaching are permitted and valuable. Production of assessed material is not, and any provider offering a finished investigation should be treated as a warning sign rather than a convenience.

The second is permits. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated: the private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years, and the eligible categories include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so no amount is quoted here.

The permit also carries a code of conduct that bars a teacher from tutoring students affiliated with their own school, which is why the offer of your child's own class teacher for private lessons is a question to ask rather than a perk to accept. Separately, a tutoring operation running premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which is a different thing from an individual's permit. IB Gram is an online matching platform and holds no regulator or examination-board endorsement of any kind.

process.title: Send the marked paper, not the report card
process.description: A report says a grade. A marked Paper 2 says where the marks went, which is what a physics tutor needs. Send a photograph of the last marked script, the current theme, the level and the school's investigation deadline, and the first session can start with a diagnosis instead of an introduction.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson before paying anything
process.description: The first lesson is a free trial, booked before any payment is made, and it is a teaching session rather than a sales call. Listen to how the tutor handles one question your child got wrong. If the explanation is clearer than the one that failed at school, that is the signal to look for.

process.title: Fix the session to one weekday and the bus timetable
process.description: Pick the slot from the afternoon pattern in the table above, not from the family calendar. A slot that survives an added activity in October is worth more than a slightly earlier one that collapses, because three reschedules in a term is how a sound arrangement gets abandoned.

process.title: Agree one measurable target for the first month
process.description: Not better physics. Something checkable: uncertainty propagation handled correctly in Paper 1B, or command-term discipline on three consecutive Paper 2 questions. A target you can verify on a marked script is what tells you in four weeks whether the hours are working.

process.title: Review at four sessions and change the tutor if the fit is wrong
process.description: Physics teaching is personal, and a tutor who is excellent for one student can be wrong for another. Reviewing at four sessions makes a change a normal step rather than a complaint, and a replacement who inherits the diagnosis rather than starting again loses nothing.

whyPoints.title: Taught on the guide your child is actually sitting
whyPoints.description: Five themes, two written papers, one scientific investigation, higher level content inside the themes rather than in options. Any tutor still planning around Paper 3 is teaching a course that was retired, and in a subject this cumulative that error costs a term.

whyPoints.title: Scheduled around the bus, not around a drive
whyPoints.description: An online slot does not move because Al Sufouh Road is slow, which means the session a JBR family books in September is the session they still have in February. The time saved is not a convenience; it is the difference between four sessions a month and two.

whyPoints.title: Specialism instead of proximity
whyPoints.description: The pool of physics teachers who can reach Dubai Marina by five on a weekday is small. The pool who can teach Theme D fields and defend an uncertainty calculation is larger and lives elsewhere. Choosing online means choosing from the second pool.

whyPoints.title: Rates published with their sources
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page is attributed to the provider that published it, with the month it was read. That is deliberate: in this market three of the six strongest ranking pages publish no price at all, and a parent cannot judge a quote without a benchmark.

whyPoints.title: Stated limits on assessed work
whyPoints.description: A tutor here questions a research question, challenges an evaluation and marks a script. They do not supply text for an investigation or an Extended Essay. That boundary protects the student's diploma, and saying so out loud is a differentiator in a market that includes providers selling finished coursework.

faqs.question: Does IB Physics still have a Paper 3?
faqs.answer: No. The guide in force for first examinations in 2025 removed Paper 3 and the old options. Assessment is now Paper 1, sat as a multiple-choice section and a data-analysis section and carrying 36% of the grade, Paper 2 of extended response carrying 44%, and one scientific investigation carrying the remaining 20%. If a tutor, a revision site or an agency page still advertises Paper 3 preparation or option-topic teaching, it has not been updated since the change, which tells you something useful about how current the rest of its advice is.

faqs.question: How much of the IB Physics grade is the scientific investigation worth?
faqs.answer: A fifth. The investigation is one student-designed experiment, reported in up to 3,000 words, marked out of 24 by the school and moderated by the IB. The marks split evenly across four criteria worth six each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. That even split is the part students miss. Evaluation carries exactly as many marks as data analysis, and it is routinely written in the last hour before the deadline, which is why it is the single cheapest place to recover marks.

faqs.question: My son is at school in Al Barsha and gets back to the tower at half past four. When can a Physics session start?
faqs.answer: Half past five or six o'clock, on a day without an after-school activity. A student who walks in at 16:30 needs a break before abstract work, and a session that starts the moment the bus arrives usually produces forty minutes of useful thinking out of sixty. If an activity runs, move the session to 18:00 and use it for problem sets rather than new teaching. On a double-period science day, skip physics entirely and use a different evening.

faqs.question: Is Higher Level Physics more content than Standard Level, or just harder questions?
faqs.answer: Both, and the extra content is positioned differently from how parents expect. Higher Level does not add separate chapters at the end; it adds material inside each of the five themes, so rotational dynamics and relativity sit within Theme A and induction and capacitance within Theme D. That means the shared content has to be secure first, because the higher level material is built directly on top of it. Paper 2 also runs two and a half hours at Higher Level against one and a half at Standard, which is a stamina demand in its own right.

faqs.question: Which Physics themes cause the most trouble in DP1?
faqs.answer: Theme D by a wide margin. Fields are taught as one unified idea covering gravitational, electric and magnetic cases, which is elegant and brutal: a student who does not separate field strength from potential will get the algebra right and the signs wrong, repeatedly. Theme B is second, usually through units left unconverted in gas-law work. Theme A looks harmless and quietly costs marks whenever a free-body diagram is skipped and the resolved components are guessed rather than drawn.

faqs.question: Will a Physics tutor drive out to a JBR tower for the lesson?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. Lessons for families in the UAE are one-to-one over live video, and IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai; household visits are a service it runs only in India. For physics specifically that is a better fit than it sounds. The limiting factor on a tutor who travels is the drive, which means a small pool, whereas an online slot gives access to teachers who specialise in the exact theme or component that is costing marks.

faqs.question: My daughter takes Mathematics Applications and Interpretation with Physics Higher Level. Is that a problem?
faqs.answer: It is a known friction point rather than a mistake. Applications and Interpretation spends less time on algebraic manipulation than Analysis and Approaches, so a student arrives at a Physics Paper 2 rearrangement with fewer repetitions behind them. The fix is usually narrow: logarithms for decay work in Theme E, rearrangement of multi-variable expressions, and resolved components in trigonometry. Three or four targeted sessions on those specific skills tend to do more for a physics grade than a general change of course.

faqs.question: What does an IB Physics tutor cost around JBR and Dubai Marina?
faqs.answer: Published market figures for this part of Dubai run from roughly AED 45-65 an hour at the budget online end, advertised by EdFlik, through AED 150-300 for a qualified online subject tutor, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. In-home visiting rates sit higher because travel is inside the fee: Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table gives AED 180-350 and independent home tutors quote up to AED 500. Named and examiner-tier specialists go further again, with BartyED publishing AED 650. All figures as read in October 2026.

faqs.question: How far can a JBR tutor help with the Physics IA without crossing the line?
faqs.answer: Yes, within clear limits. A tutor can ask whether the research question can be answered with the apparatus the school actually has, point out an uncertainty that has not been propagated, challenge a conclusion that goes beyond the data, and push an evaluation past human error towards specific limitations. What a tutor must not do is supply a method, provide text or restructure the report into its final form. The student authors every line. Any provider offering a finished investigation is offering a malpractice risk, not a service.

faqs.question: We have five weeks until the mock. Is it too late for Physics tutoring to help?
faqs.answer: Five weeks is enough for mark conversion, not for rebuilding a theme. Used well, that window is spent on timed Paper 1B and Paper 2 sections, marked live against the published expectations, with the three recurring errors identified in week one and retested in weeks three and five. Students commonly gain more from this than from new teaching, because the typical loss in a mock is not missing content but missing method: no diagram, no stated assumption, a command term misread, a unit abandoned halfway through.

faqs.question: How do online Physics lessons handle diagrams, derivations and graph work?
faqs.answer: On a shared whiteboard, with the student holding the pen more often than the tutor. The practical test of an online physics session is whether your child is drawing the free-body diagram or watching one being drawn. A good tutor screen-shares the student's own marked script, asks them to redo the question live, and types nothing themselves beyond a prompt. Graph work is done on the student's own plotted data, which also means the investigation and Paper 1B practice can share the same hour.

faqs.question: Does my child need to repeat laboratory work at home for the investigation?
faqs.answer: No, and they should not try to. The investigation is designed around apparatus available at school, and the research question should be chosen to match what the laboratory can actually supply. Where an online tutor adds value is before the data exists: testing whether the question is answerable, whether the controlled variables are genuinely controlled, and whether the measurement range will produce a gradient worth analysing. Afterwards, the work is in the processing, the uncertainty treatment and the evaluation, none of which needs a bench.

faqs.question: Is one Physics session a week enough in the final year?
faqs.answer: For most students, yes, provided the cadence changes at the right moments. One weekly hour through the term handles the current theme and keeps exam habits alive. Around the investigation deadline a fortnightly clinic on that specific piece is better value than general teaching. In the four to six weeks before mocks and before the May session, a short block of timed-paper work earns more than the same hours spread thin. Two sessions a week every week for two years is usually spending without a plan.

faqs.question: Can a Physics session move to a post-Iftar slot during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for most families it should. School days are compressed during Ramadan and finish earlier, which brings students back into the towers in the early afternoon when they are least able to concentrate. A slot around 20:30, after Iftar, usually produces better work than an afternoon one. Use that period for revision of material already taught rather than for new content, and plan the heavier sequencing for the weeks either side of it.

faqs.question: Does a Physics tutor need a UAE permit, and how would we check?
faqs.answer: Anyone giving private lessons in the UAE needs the private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible categories include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged 15 to 18. Ask the tutor directly which category applies to them. The application route is MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service, which lists a two-working-day completion time.

intro.heading: Physics in Jumeirah 3, counted from the exam date backwards
paragraphs: Most searches for an IB physics tutor in Jumeirah 3 happen in one of three weeks of the year: the fortnight after the first set of DP1 unit tests, the week mock results come home in January, and the panicked days after a scientific investigation draft gets a comment the student did not expect. The subject does not get harder in those weeks. The calendar does. Physics is the one DP subject where a term lost to vague revision cannot be recovered by working harder in May, because the paper rewards practised technique rather than remembered content.

So this page is organised around time rather than around topics. It sets out what the assessment model actually asks for, what the next eight weeks have to achieve depending on where your child sits in the two-year programme, and what a weekly session should produce by way of evidence that it worked. If your child is in DP1 and the first internal assessment deadline is six weeks away, the work is different from a DP2 student eleven weeks out from the May session, and a tutor who treats both the same is being paid to teach a syllabus instead of a student.

Jumeirah 3 is a villa district between Al Wasl Road and Jumeirah Beach Road, and the families here sit across a wide spread of schools: IB continuum schools in Umm Suqeim and Al Barsha, British schools in Al Safa and Al Sufouh running IGCSE then A Level, and a handful of students doing DP at schools a full thirty minutes inland. That spread matters for one practical reason. The school a child attends sets the internal deadline calendar, and no two of those calendars agree. A tutor working to the IB's published assessment structure but ignoring the school's own submission dates will have your child revising Theme D while a draft is overdue.

Online delivery is the part of this that reads like a compromise and is not. IB Gram runs every UAE lesson as one-to-one online tuition over live video; home visits are a service we offer only in India. The gain is specificity. A Jumeirah 3 family gets a Physics HL specialist who has marked uncertainty propagation badly enough times to spot the exact error your child keeps making, rather than whichever science graduate can reach Jumeirah 3 by 4.30pm. The second gain is the clock. A session that does not need a car can start at 4pm, pause for a 20-minute break, and finish before homework starts.

What follows is specific: the weightings of each paper, a week-by-week plan for a block of eight weeks, the four criteria the scientific investigation is marked against, what Dubai providers published as their 2026 rates, and the line a tutor must not cross on assessed work. Read the exam-session table even if your child is in DP1. Entry deadlines, internal submission dates and mock windows all sit months before the paper, and almost every family that arrives late arrives late because nobody counted backwards.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-jumeirah-3.programmesIntro: Jumeirah 3 students reach DP Physics along two routes: through an IB continuum school that ran the Middle Years Programme, or from an IGCSE science course at a British school in Al Safa or Al Sufouh. The gap to close in the first eight weeks of DP1 is different for each, so the programme notes below are written for this neighbourhood's actual intake.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Two years, six subjects, three at Higher Level. Physics sits in Group 4 and is assessed by two written papers plus a scientific investigation worth 20% of the grade. The subject guide in force for current candidates organises content into themes A to E, with HL extension material inside each theme rather than bolted on at the end, and a set of experimental and mathematical tools examined through the papers.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the DP cohort is a minority of the private-school population, which has a practical consequence for Jumeirah 3 families: a school may run only one Physics HL class, and if that class loses a teacher mid-year there is no second set to move into. Several families here use weekly online tuition specifically as continuity insurance against that, rather than as remediation.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Five years assessed against four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight. In Sciences those criteria reward knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. A student who scored well on criterion A and poorly on criterion C arrives in DP1 able to recall definitions but unable to handle a gradient, an intercept or an uncertainty.
programmes.countryNote: MYP students from Umm Suqeim and Al Barsha continuum schools usually transfer into DP Physics with strong investigation design and weak algebraic fluency, because MYP Sciences rarely demands the rearrangement speed Paper 2 assumes. The first four weeks of tuition for this group is normally pure mathematics applied to physics contexts, not new physics content.

programmes.name: IGCSE Physics into DP Physics
programmes.description: The commonest Jumeirah 3 route. Cambridge 0625 or Pearson 4PH1 ends with recall-heavy theory papers and a practical or alternative-to-practical component. DP Physics then asks for the same content expressed as relationships: proportionality, log plots, error bars and the reasoning behind a straight-line graph. Students who earned an A* by memorising definitions often meet their first real difficulty here.
programmes.countryNote: Year 11 students in Al Safa and Al Sufouh who already know they want Physics HL benefit most from a short bridging block in June and July, before DP1 starts. Six to eight sessions on vectors, logarithms, graph linearisation and uncertainty notation removes most of the autumn-term panic that drives the January search for help.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-jumeirah-3.subjectsIntro: Physics is rarely tutored alone. The combinations below are the ones Jumeirah 3 families actually request alongside it, and the notes say what each one assesses and where the marks tend to go.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Themes A to E, with Paper 1 split between multiple choice and data analysis, Paper 2 extended response, and a scientific investigation. Marks are lost disproportionately on uncertainty treatment, graph interpretation and the difference between the command terms explain, describe and state.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The usual pairing with Physics HL. The overlap that matters is calculus applied to motion and fields, plus logarithms for exponential decay. A student weak in AA algebra will read every Physics question twice and still mishandle the rearrangement.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Chosen by Physics SL students more often than schools expect. Its statistics and regression content actually helps the data-analysis half of Paper 1, but it gives less practice in symbolic manipulation, so algebra needs separate attention in sessions.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Taken with Physics by most engineering and medicine applicants here. The shared skill is quantitative reasoning under time pressure; the shared failure is the scientific investigation, where both subjects demand the same methodological rigour and students write two weak reports instead of one good method twice.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: A Group 4 alternative that some Jumeirah 3 students pair with Physics. Useful overlap in modelling and logic; no overlap at all in laboratory technique, which means the investigation has to be learned once rather than practised across two subjects.

subjects.name: Design Technology
subjects.description: Offered by a few Dubai IB schools and often misread as the easier Group 4 option. It rewards iterative design documentation rather than numerical problem solving, so it is a poor substitute for Physics on an engineering application and a reasonable companion to it.

subjects.name: Sports, Exercise and Health Science
subjects.description: Chosen by students who want applied science without heavy mathematics. Its mechanics content leans on the same force and moment concepts as Physics Theme A, so a tutor can treat the two together when a student takes both.

subjects.name: Extended Essay in Physics
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent research piece supervised by a school teacher. Tutoring here is process coaching: narrowing a research question, judging whether the measurement is feasible with school apparatus, and reading a draft critically. The argument, the words and the data must be the student's own.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The essay and exhibition both reward precise examples, and Physics gives good ones: measurement uncertainty as a knowledge limit, models that are known to be wrong but useful. Sessions tend to focus on turning a physics example into a knowledge claim rather than a summary.

subjects.name: IB Physics IA support
subjects.description: The scientific investigation is marked on research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. IB Physics IA support in a session means pressure-testing the research question, checking that the independent variable is genuinely controllable, and teaching uncertainty propagation before data collection rather than after.

sections.heading: What a Jumeirah 3 family is really asking when they search for a Physics tutor
paragraphs: The literal answer first: an IB physics tutor in Jumeirah 3, through IB Gram, is a DP Physics specialist who teaches your child one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, usually weekly, starting with a free diagnostic lesson. Nobody drives to your villa. The subject specialist is chosen for the level and the theme your child is struggling with, not for proximity to the beach road.

Underneath the search sits a different question, which is usually some version of how much time is left. A parent searching in October has a DP1 student whose first unit test on Theme A came back lower than their IGCSE results suggested it would. A parent searching in January has mock grades and eleven or twelve weeks. A parent searching in March has a draft investigation and a school deadline. Those are three different jobs, and the honest thing a tutor can do in a first lesson is say which one applies and what it realistically achieves.

The mistake that costs Jumeirah 3 families the most money is booking general science help in week six and discovering in week twelve that the sessions have been revisiting content the student already knew. Physics marks are lost in technique: reading a graph axis, propagating an uncertainty, choosing the right form of an equation, answering a six-mark question with six scoring points instead of three good sentences. A tutor who does not diagnose that in the first hour will fill a term pleasantly and change nothing.

So the first session has one job. The student works through a short mixed set under time, talking aloud, and the tutor records where the error happens rather than whether the answer is right. Three or four error families usually emerge, and the term plan is written against them. That diagnostic is free, it produces a written summary, and families are welcome to take the summary and work from it themselves.

sections.heading: The DP Physics assessment model, paper by paper
paragraphs: DP Physics is assessed by two written papers and one piece of internally assessed coursework. Paper 1 carries 36% of the final grade and comes in two parts: a multiple-choice section and a data-analysis section built on an unseen experiment. Paper 2 carries 44% and is extended response, mixing short answers with longer structured questions. The scientific investigation accounts for the remaining 20%, and it is marked by the school against IB criteria and then externally moderated.

That split is the single most useful fact on this page, because it tells you where tuition hours should go. Four marks in five come from written papers, and the data-analysis half of Paper 1 is the part students practise least. It is also the part that transfers: the skill of reading an unfamiliar experiment, identifying the controlled variables and interpreting a gradient is the same skill the investigation is marked on. Time spent there is counted twice.

Higher Level is not Standard Level with harder questions. It is more content inside the same five themes, longer papers, and a markedly higher expectation of algebraic fluency. A student can hold an acceptable SL grade while rearranging equations slowly, and the same habit at HL will cost them Paper 2 marks on time alone. The table below sets out the structure; the weightings are those published in the subject guide for current candidates, and your child's DP coordinator can confirm the version their cohort sits.

One caution about dates, since it comes up in the first lesson most weeks. IB examination and results dates are published by the IB and by your school, and this page does not restate them, because a date restated second-hand and then revised is worse than no date. Ask the DP coordinator for the cohort's own timetable and the internal submission calendar, and bring both to the first session.

sections.heading: The next eight weeks, counted backwards
paragraphs: An eight-week block is the unit most Jumeirah 3 families can realistically commit to, and it is long enough to change a grade if it is spent on the right things. The structure below assumes two sessions a week for a DP2 student working toward the May session, with the first session diagnostic and the last two spent entirely on recurring errors. A DP1 student runs the same shape over sixteen weeks at one session a week.

The reason this is written as a countdown rather than a syllabus plan is that revision has a natural order and most students get it backwards. They begin with the topic they like, leave the weakest theme until last, and run out of time before it is covered. Counting backwards forces the opposite: the weakest theme is rebuilt first, when there is still time to practise it, and the strong topics are maintained with short timed sets rather than re-taught.

Evidence matters as much as the plan. Each week should produce something checkable, because a session that feels productive and leaves no trace is indistinguishable from a conversation. A marked timed section, a graph drawn correctly to scale, an uncertainty calculated to the right number of figures, an error log with three entries closed out: these are the artefacts that tell a parent paying by the hour whether anything moved.

Ramadan falls inside the Dubai revision calendar in most years, and it changes the shape of a week rather than cancelling it. Families usually move sessions later, after Iftar, and shorten them to 45 or 60 minutes. Shorter and more frequent works better than long weekend blocks during fasting, and the last fortnight before a paper is a poor time to change tutor or format.

sections.heading: Where Physics marks actually disappear
paragraphs: Five error families account for most of the difference between a 4 and a 6 in DP Physics, and none of them is a knowledge gap. The first is uncertainty: students quote a reading uncertainty and forget that it propagates through a calculation, or add percentages where they should add absolutes. The second is graph work: plotting raw data when the relationship needs linearising, drawing a line of best fit through the origin because the equation suggests it should pass through, or reading a gradient off two data points instead of the line.

The third is command terms, and it is the cheapest to fix. State, describe, explain, outline, deduce and justify ask for structurally different answers, and the mark scheme pays for the structure. A student who writes a paragraph of correct physics in answer to a two-mark state question loses time they needed elsewhere, and a student who gives one sentence to a six-mark explain question loses four marks they already knew. One session on command terms, with past-paper mark schemes read side by side, usually moves Paper 2 more than a month of content revision.

The fourth is algebra under time. Physics Paper 2 assumes rearrangement is automatic, and for a student who learned to solve equations by substitution rather than manipulation it never is. This is the one gap that genuinely needs mathematics teaching rather than physics teaching, and it is why a Physics HL student weak in Mathematics AA often needs both subjects addressed in the same session for a few weeks.

The fifth is the written investigation, where marks are lost before any data is collected. A research question that cannot be answered with the apparatus available, an independent variable that cannot be controlled cleanly, too few levels of that variable to show a relationship: these are design faults, and no amount of careful writing afterwards recovers the marks. That is why the investigation clinic starts with the question and the method rather than the report.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation: four criteria, twenty-four marks, and the line a tutor holds
paragraphs: The internally assessed investigation in DP Physics is worth 20% of the final grade and is marked against four criteria, each carrying six marks, for twenty-four in total: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Those letters and totals are the single most useful piece of information a parent can have, because they convert a vague instruction to write a good report into four separate things that can be practised. Competitor pages in this market almost never name a criterion, let alone a mark allocation.

Research design is where the grade is usually decided. The criterion rewards a research question with a clearly identified independent and dependent variable, a method that controls the rest, and a justification for the range and number of measurements. Data analysis rewards correct processing, including uncertainties carried through to the final result and graphs that show the relationship rather than decorate the page. Conclusion asks for an answer to the research question supported by the data and compared with accepted physics. Evaluation asks for weaknesses weighed by their impact, not simply listed.

The boundary on a tutor's role is firm and worth stating plainly, because this SERP contains businesses that sell finished coursework. A tutor teaches technique, asks questions about a draft, points at a criterion and explains what the examiner expects to see. A tutor does not supply text, does not edit a report into shape, and does not provide a method for the student to adopt as their own. The report, the data and the reasoning must come from the student; anything else is academic malpractice under IB rules and the risk sits with your child, not with the tutor.

In practice that means feedback is delivered as questions. Which variable did you decide not to control, and why? What does the gradient of your graph physically represent? If your uncertainty is this large, can you still claim the relationship you have claimed? A student who answers those questions and then revises their own report has both learned the criterion and kept their work their own.

The number that does not appear on any rate card is the travel cost, and in this part of Dubai it is the biggest hidden item. Families who start weekly work early pay a lower rate for a better match; families who start late pay a premium for whoever is free. sections.heading: Permits, regulators and how a Jumeirah 3 parent checks a tutor is allowed to teach
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted and regulated. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. The MoHRE private tutor permit is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, with applications made through its app, website and e-services system. Anyone offering private tutoring without that permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you.

Schools are regulated separately and by emirate. Dubai private schools answer to the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which oversees the quality of private education in the emirate and inspects schools on a six-band scale running from Outstanding down to Very Weak. KHDA inspection bands are published per school on the authority's own site, and that is where to read them: a band is a judgement about a whole school across many measures, not a prediction about one Physics class. A school rated Very Good can still have a weak year in one Group 4 subject, which is precisely the situation that brings families to this page.

Two further rules are worth knowing before you hire anyone locally. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct with a similar restriction. Treat any offer of your child's own class teacher, privately, as a problem rather than a shortcut. And a tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit, which is a specific licence issued to training institutes; an individual online tutor is a different legal category entirely.

IB Gram holds no regulator or examination-board accreditation and claims none. We are an independent matching platform: we introduce a subject specialist, the lessons run online, and you can ask any tutor for their permit status before the first paid session. We also do not publish inspection ratings on these pages, because a rating read second-hand and then revised is a liability. Check the school's current report on the KHDA site and the permit position on mohre.gov.ae.

sections.heading: Getting started from Jumeirah 3, including what happens if nobody is free
paragraphs: The sequence is short. You send the level, the themes causing trouble, the school and the next deadline. We come back with one or two Physics specialists and a proposed slot in Gulf Standard Time. The trial lesson runs as a diagnostic, after which you receive a written summary naming the error families and a suggested plan length. If you continue, the slot is held weekly for the term; if you do not, the summary is yours to use.

DP Physics tutoring in Jumeirah is one of the narrower requests we handle, and honesty about availability matters more than a confident promise. A Physics HL specialist with current experience of the subject guide is a smaller pool than a general maths tutor, and in the eight weeks before a session that pool is largely committed. If no UAE-based specialist is free at the time your family needs, we say so and offer the two alternatives: a specialist in another time zone whose evening is your afternoon, or a wait for a slot that opens. We do not substitute a general science tutor and describe them as a Physics specialist.

A word on what good looks like after a month. The student can name their own error families without prompting. Timed Paper 1 sections are being completed inside the time rather than abandoned at question 25. The investigation has a research question that survived being challenged. And homework from school is being used as practice rather than treated as a separate burden. If none of that has happened in four sessions, the match is wrong and should be changed rather than persevered with.

Families in Jumeirah 3, Umm Suqeim, Jumeirah 2 and Al Safa share the same teaching slots, so the popular 4pm and 5pm weekday windows fill first each term. Booking the slot before the term starts is worth more than booking extra hours later, and a single weekly session held reliably for twelve weeks beats six sessions crammed into April on every measure we can see.

faqs.question: How many weeks of Physics tutoring does a Jumeirah 3 student need before the May session?
faqs.answer: It depends on what is wrong rather than on how far away the papers are. A technique gap in uncertainties, graphs and command terms is usually addressable in an eight-week block of two sessions a week, and most of the improvement shows up in timed Paper 1 work by week five. A content gap spanning two or three themes needs a term. Arriving with four weeks left means choosing: either the weakest theme or paper technique, not both. The diagnostic in the free trial lesson is designed to tell you which case applies before you commit to a length.

faqs.question: Does an IB physics tutor in Jumeirah 3 come to the villa?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram delivers every UAE lesson as one-to-one online tuition over live video; home visits are a service we offer only in India. For Physics that trade is strongly in your favour, because the pool of tutors who have taught the current subject guide at Higher Level is small and spread across time zones, while the pool who can reach Jumeirah 3 by 4.30pm on a Tuesday is tiny. Online also means a 4pm start is realistic, shared whiteboard files carry over between sessions, and nothing is cancelled because Sheikh Zayed Road has stopped moving.

faqs.question: What exactly is in Paper 1 for DP Physics, and why does everyone say it is the one to practise?
faqs.answer: Paper 1 carries 36% of the grade and has two parts: a multiple-choice section across all five themes, and a data-analysis section built on an experiment the student has never seen. The second part is the one students practise least and the one that transfers most, because identifying variables, linearising a graph and judging whether a conclusion is supported by the data is exactly what the internally assessed investigation is marked on. Time spent on Paper 1B therefore counts twice. Most eight-week plans we write put a timed data-analysis section in every single week.

faqs.question: My child got an A* in IGCSE Physics and is now getting 4s in DP1. What changed?
faqs.answer: The question style did. IGCSE Physics rewards accurate recall of definitions and standard calculations; DP Physics asks the same content to be used as relationships, with uncertainties carried through and graphs chosen to reveal proportionality. A student who learned to recognise question types rather than manipulate equations meets that wall in the first term of DP1. It is a technique problem, not an ability problem, and twelve to sixteen weeks of weekly work on algebraic fluency, graph linearisation and command terms usually closes it. Starting in October is far cheaper than starting in February.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Physics scientific investigation without breaking IB rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within clear limits. A tutor may challenge the research question for feasibility, teach uncertainty propagation using the student's own measurements, explain what each of the four criteria rewards, and read a draft and respond with questions. A tutor may not supply the research question, hand over a method, process the data, or rewrite the report. The investigation is worth 20% of the grade and is externally moderated, and work that is not the student's own puts their IB registration at risk. Feedback delivered as questions keeps the learning and keeps the authorship where it belongs.

faqs.question: How are the four Physics investigation criteria weighted?
faqs.answer: Research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation each carry six marks, giving twenty-four in total, which the school converts and the IB externally moderates. Research design is where most marks are won or lost, because a question that cannot be answered with the available apparatus caps everything that follows. Data analysis rewards uncertainties carried through to the final result. Conclusion must answer the question and compare with accepted physics. Evaluation must weigh weaknesses by their impact rather than list them. Knowing the letters and the mark split turns a vague task into four practisable ones.

faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued by MoHRE free of charge for two years, with applications made through the MoHRE app, website or e-services system. Registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18 can all apply. faqs.question: How do sessions work during Ramadan and school exam weeks?
faqs.answer: Timing shifts rather than stopping. Most Jumeirah 3 families move Physics sessions to after Iftar and shorten them to 45 or 60 minutes, which works better during fasting than long weekend blocks. School examination weeks are usually paused entirely, because a student sitting internal exams needs sleep more than an extra hour of fields revision. What we avoid is changing tutor or format in the final fortnight before a paper, when continuity is worth more than any marginal improvement in teaching style.

faqs.question: Is Physics HL necessary for engineering at a UAE university?
faqs.answer: Entry requirements are set by each university and change, so the only safe answer is to read the course page for the exact programme and intake year. In general, engineering and physical-science degrees in the UAE and abroad look for Physics and Mathematics at Higher Level, and some will accept Physics SL with strong Mathematics. Tutoring cannot change an admissions rule and nobody should suggest it can. What a tutor can do is make Higher Level survivable for a student whose algebra is the limiting factor rather than their physics.

faqs.question: What does the first Physics session actually look like?
faqs.answer: The student works through a short mixed set under light time pressure while talking aloud, and the tutor records where each error occurs rather than whether the answer was right. That usually surfaces three or four error families: uncertainty handling, graph interpretation, command-term structure, algebraic speed. The tutor then shows one fix live, sets two questions for the week, and writes a summary naming the families and a realistic plan length. You receive that summary whether or not you continue, and it is specific enough to work from alone.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover Physics HL and Mathematics AA together?
faqs.answer: Often, and for Physics HL students with weak algebra it is the efficient choice for the first month. The overlap is real: calculus applied to motion and fields, logarithms for decay, and the rearrangement speed Paper 2 assumes. Once the algebra is no longer the limiting factor, most families split the subjects again, because deep Mathematics AA work and deep Physics work compete for the same hour. We say which case applies after the diagnostic rather than selling two slots by default.

intro.heading: What a Palm Jumeirah family is actually buying when they pay for Physics help
paragraphs: Palm Jumeirah has no secondary school on it. Children living on the fronds, along the Shoreline, in the Golden Mile or at the tip travel off the island every morning through a single trunk-road junction, most of them to Al Sufouh, Al Barsha, Umm Suqeim or the Jumeirah beach strip. That geography matters to a Physics fee in a way nobody writes about: a tutor who drives to a frond villa is paid for the drive as well as the teaching, and the drive is not negotiable because there is one road on and off.

The market does not help a parent work this out. Of the pages ranking for Dubai IB tutoring searches, three publish no price at all, and the two that do quote US dollars - a currency no Dubai family pays school fees in. One ranking agency's own list of frequently asked questions poses the price question and then declines to answer it. So the first thing this page does is publish the bands, in AED, with the name of whoever published each figure and the month it was read. Those are market rates, not IB Gram's rates. What IB Gram offers before any money is discussed is a trial lesson.

The second thing worth doing is matching money to the mark scheme. Diploma Physics under the current guide is assessed through two written papers and one scientific investigation, and the investigation carries a fifth of the final grade on its own. A family that buys twenty hours of topic revision and none of it on the investigation has spent well and aimed badly. A family that buys four hours in the design week of the investigation, before the data exists, has usually bought the single most valuable block of the two years.

Where money goes wrong is predictable. It goes wrong on hours bought in the eight weeks before the May session, when the content gap is too wide to close and the only available gain is exam technique. It goes wrong on a cheap tutor who can do the physics but cannot read an IB mark scheme, so the student keeps writing descriptions where the command term asked for an explanation. It goes wrong on examiner-badged premium rates for topics a competent specialist fixes at half the price. And it goes wrong on in-home visits where a third of the fee is travel on the Palm's one access road.

This page is written to be used before the first payment. It gives the AED bands and their sources, the component weightings so the hours can be aimed, a comparison of online, in-home and group delivery with the island's travel reality priced in, and an honest account of what a tutor may and may not touch on an investigation that has to be the student's own work. IB Gram delivers all of it as one-to-one online tuition. Home visits are an India-only service and are not sold anywhere in the UAE.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-palm-jumeirah.programmesIntro: Palm Jumeirah children sit in three different IB programmes depending on their age, and the Physics question looks different in each. The notes below are specific to families commuting off this island rather than to IB programmes in general.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The two-year Diploma, taken with three subjects at Higher Level and three at Standard. Physics sits in Group 4 and can be taken at either level. Under the current guide the course is organised into themes covering motion, the particulate nature of matter, wave behaviour, fields, and nuclear and quantum physics, and is assessed by two written papers plus one scientific investigation. The investigation is internally marked against published criteria and externally moderated.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's Diploma cohort is small relative to the British-curriculum majority, which is why a Physics specialist is scarce near any one neighbourhood. A Palm Jumeirah student is usually one of a handful taking Physics at Higher Level in their year group, and the school's physics teaching load is spread across IGCSE and Diploma classes. Paid hours here are most often bought because the school cannot timetable extra one-to-one support, not because the teaching is poor.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Five years of broad study across eight subject groups, with Sciences assessed on four criteria rather than by percentage. MYP Sciences marks knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. A student can be strong on content and still score poorly because the design and evaluation criteria were never taught explicitly.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools Palm Jumeirah families use run MYP to year 5 and then Diploma, while others switch to IGCSE at 14. That fork decides what Physics looks like at 16. An MYP student who has never written a hypothesis with a controlled variable arrives in Diploma Physics with a gap that shows up in the investigation rather than in the papers, and it is cheaper to close at 14 than at 17.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led primary education organised around transdisciplinary themes, finishing with an exhibition in the final year. Science appears as inquiry rather than as a named subject, so a child can leave PYP confident at asking questions and unpractised at the arithmetic that later Physics depends on.
programmes.countryNote: Palm Jumeirah's own provision is early years and nursery; primary-age children already commute. For PYP families the useful Physics-adjacent investment is not Physics at all but number fluency and measurement, because the Diploma Physics students who struggle most are usually struggling with rearranging an equation rather than with the physics in it.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-palm-jumeirah.subjectsIntro: Physics is rarely the only subject a Diploma student needs help with, and the combinations are predictable. These are the subjects most often requested alongside it by families on the Palm and the Jumeirah strip.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Two written papers and one scientific investigation. Marks are lost most often on uncertainty treatment in the data-analysis section, on derivations that skip a line of algebra, and on explanation questions answered as descriptions. Higher Level questions assume complete Standard Level fluency rather than extra memory.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The route most Physics students take, and the one engineering admissions usually expect. Calculus and algebraic manipulation here are the same skills Physics Paper 2 needs, which is why weak maths shows up as a physics mark. The exploration is assessed separately and often collides with the Physics investigation deadline.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics-heavy and modelling-led, with a graphical-calculator expectation throughout. Taking Physics HL with Applications SL is workable but leaves gaps in algebraic fluency that have to be filled deliberately, and some engineering courses state a preference for Analysis and Approaches.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The other Group 4 subject Palm Jumeirah families most often pair with Physics. Shares the investigation structure and the data-handling demands, so one tutor can sometimes cover both internal assessments even where the content teaching needs two specialists.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Taken alongside Physics by students aiming at medicine or biomedical engineering. The assessment shape matches Physics, but the mark scheme rewards precise terminology far more, which catches out students who write fluently and imprecisely.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Frequently chosen with Physics HL. The solution development work is a separate internal assessment with its own deadline, and it tends to land in the same term as the Physics investigation. Planning the two together is a scheduling job, not a teaching one.

subjects.name: Design Technology
subjects.description: Offered by fewer Dubai schools and much less tutored, so availability near any single neighbourhood is thin. Shares a design-cycle logic with MYP Design, and students coming from MYP Design usually find the transition manageable.

subjects.name: Sports, Exercise and Health Science
subjects.description: A Group 4 alternative that satisfies the science requirement without Physics-level mathematics. Chosen by students who want a science but not a quantitative one, and it still carries an internal investigation with the same evidence standards.

subjects.name: Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.description: Can count as either a Group 3 or a Group 4 subject, which makes it useful for timetable problems. Assessment rewards systems thinking and data interpretation, and students strong at Physics data analysis often score well here with little extra teaching.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Compulsory, with an exhibition and an essay. Physics students often have the sharpest material available for it and the least patience with it. Support here is structural - argument shape, counterclaim, and evidence selection - rather than content teaching.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-palm-jumeirah.regionsIntro: Students on this page come from the island itself and from the coastal communities either side of it. Session timing differs by a surprising amount between them, because the constraint is the trunk road rather than the distance.

regions.name: Palm Jumeirah fronds
regions.note: Gated single-lane spines off the trunk road, with villa gates at the far end. A visitor arriving at 4:30pm faces the junction queue and then the frond itself. Online sessions remove both and let a 4:00pm start actually begin at 4:00pm.

regions.name: Shoreline and Golden Mile
regions.note: Apartment blocks along the eastern trunk, with visitor parking and building access to negotiate. Families here often have two children on different school runs, so a fixed evening slot is worth more than a flexible afternoon one.

regions.name: Al Sufouh
regions.note: The nearest off-island school cluster and the first stop for most Palm commuters. Secondary days here typically end mid-afternoon, which sets the earliest realistic session time for a student who still has to cross back onto the island.

regions.name: Umm Suqeim
regions.note: A dense school belt along the beach road with heavy drop-off and pick-up traffic. Students travelling back to the Palm from here arrive later than the distance suggests, so sessions scheduled before 5:00pm regularly start late.

regions.name: Jumeirah 1, 2 and 3
regions.note: Low-rise villa districts running along Beach Road with several schools inside them. A number of Palm families keep younger children in Jumeirah schools and move them off-island for secondary, so the two commutes run in opposite directions.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Al Barsha South
regions.note: Where much of the IB and American provision sits. The furthest regular Palm commute, and the one most likely to make a 4:00pm in-home visit impossible for a tutor based near the school.

regions.name: Pearl Jumeira and La Mer
regions.note: Newer coastal developments with a similar commuting pattern to the Palm and the same shortage of nearby secondary schools. Families here ask the same Physics questions and face the same thin local tutor pool.

regions.name: Al Safa and Al Wasl
regions.note: Inland of Beach Road, with a cluster of long-established British-curriculum schools. Several Palm students sit IGCSE here before moving to a Diploma school, which is where the Physics route decision gets made.

schoolClusters.city: Al Sufouh and Al Barsha - the main off-island destinations
schoolClusters.note: This is where most Palm Jumeirah secondary students actually study. Between them these campuses carry the bulk of the IB and American provision within a reasonable commute of the island, which is why Diploma Physics questions from the Palm usually trace back to one of them.

modes.description: A fixed slot each week, delivered live over video, with the term's hours allocated in advance to named components rather than to whatever happened in class that week. Over a Diploma year this is the shape that produces the most mark movement per dirham, because the sequencing is planned instead of reactive.

It works when the content is broadly there and the execution is not.

sections.heading: What an hour of Diploma Physics support actually buys from the Palm
paragraphs: An hour of one-to-one Diploma Physics teaching in Dubai is sold anywhere between roughly AED 45 and AED 650, and the spread is not mostly about quality. It is about tier, format and travel. At the bottom sit online tutors working from published worked examples. In the middle sit qualified subject teachers. At the top sit tutors marketing scarcity. Travel is the hidden variable: an in-home rate in Dubai includes the drive, and from a frond villa on Palm Jumeirah the drive crosses a single access junction twice.

The honest way to think about the fee is to ask what the hour is aimed at. Diploma Physics is assessed by two written papers and one scientific investigation, and those three things fail for different reasons. Paper 1B fails on uncertainty and graph reading. Paper 2 fails on command terms and on derivations with a missing line. The investigation fails at the design stage, weeks before anyone writes anything, usually because the research question cannot generate enough data to analyse. An hour spent on the wrong one of those is not a cheap hour. It is a wasted one.

This is where a Palm Jumeirah family has an advantage they rarely use. Because the island has no secondary school, the local tutor pool was never the relevant pool - every option already involves a commute. Once the commute is accepted as unavoidable, removing it entirely by teaching over live video costs nothing in convenience and widens the choice from whoever happens to live within a drive to every Diploma Physics specialist available. The question stops being who is nearby and becomes who teaches this syllabus.

IB Gram delivers one-to-one Physics tuition to Palm Jumeirah over live video. IB Gram does not sell home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. That is stated here rather than buried, because a family comparing an in-home quote against an online one needs to know which they are buying before they compare the numbers.

sections.heading: The AED bands the Dubai market publishes, and who publishes them
paragraphs: Below are the hourly bands currently published by providers serving Dubai, read in October 2026, with the source of each band named in the table. These are market figures and not IB Gram's prices. They are reproduced because a parent cannot judge a quote without knowing the distribution it sits in, and almost nobody in this market publishes one.

Two patterns are worth reading out of the table. The first is that the in-home band starts higher than the online band and ends higher, and the gap is travel. The second is that the specialist band and the premium band overlap heavily, which means a large part of what separates an AED 270 hour from an AED 650 hour is positioning rather than teaching. Where the premium band genuinely buys something is in narrow subject availability, and Physics at Higher Level is narrower than most.

Monthly packaging changes the arithmetic again. Online monthly packages have been published at AED 799 for eight sessions, and in-home monthly packages at AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour visits. Read per hour, the in-home package is not dramatically dearer; read per contact hour of actual teaching with travel stripped out, it is. Bestimate's Dubai 2026 estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support.

Whatever band a family lands in, the figure to ask for is the one that includes everything. Ask whether the rate is per hour or per lesson, whether a 90-minute session bills as 1.5 hours, what a late cancellation costs, whether written feedback between sessions is included, and whether the price changes closer to an exam series. Those five answers move the real cost more than the headline rate does.

sections.heading: Aiming the money: Physics components and what each one is worth
paragraphs: A Diploma Physics grade is built from two written papers and one scientific investigation. Paper 1 is split into a multiple-choice section and a data-analysis section and carries 36% of the grade between them. Paper 2 carries 44%. The scientific investigation carries 20% and is marked inside the school against published criteria before external moderation. Those proportions should decide where paid hours go, and in most families they do not.

The cheapest marks on the page are in Paper 1B, the data-analysis section. Uncertainty propagation, gradient work, linearising a relationship and reading a graph nobody has seen before are all teachable in a small number of hours, and most students have never been taught them explicitly because class time goes on content. A student who can handle uncertainty confidently picks up marks across both papers and in the investigation at the same time, which makes it the highest-return block of hours available.

The dearest marks are in late content recovery. If a student reaches February of the final year without secure work on fields or on nuclear and quantum physics, buying that content back costs many hours and competes with revision for five other subjects. This is the single most common way Physics money is wasted in Dubai: hours bought at the point of panic, at the highest rates of the year, on the problem that was least amenable to a quick fix.

Weightings and component structures change between guides, so the table below should be checked against the subject guide your child's school is actually teaching. Ask the Diploma coordinator which guide and first-examination year applies. A tutor who cannot tell you which guide they are teaching to is not the tutor to buy twenty hours from.

sections.heading: Four spending patterns that waste Physics money on this island
paragraphs: The first is buying hours too late. A block started eight weeks before a written series can sharpen technique and cannot rebuild a year of content. Families who start in the first Diploma year pay less in total and buy more, because the same money goes on learning rather than on triage. If a student is already inside the final two months, the honest advice is to narrow the aim hard - two topics and exam technique - rather than to buy more hours.

The second is paying for travel without noticing. On Palm Jumeirah the in-home premium is not a rounding error. A tutor coming to a frond villa crosses the trunk-road junction, drives the frond spine, clears a gate, and does it all again afterwards. That time is inside the quoted rate, so a family paying AED 350 for a 60-minute in-home session is buying roughly the teaching an online session delivers for substantially less. Some families want a person in the room and are happy to pay for it; the point is to know the trade being made.

The third is buying the wrong specialism. Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics look adjacent on a school report and are not interchangeable to teach. A general science tutor can keep a Standard Level student afloat and will struggle with Higher Level fields or with a derivation that needs calculus. Conversely, a brilliant Physics tutor cannot fix a mathematics problem that is really about rearranging equations. Diagnosing which subject is failing before buying a term of the wrong one is the cheapest decision available.

The fourth is buying support on work that must be the student's own. Internal assessment help has a hard boundary: a tutor may teach the method, discuss the research question, ask whether the data supports the conclusion, and give feedback on a draft the student wrote. A tutor may not supply text, data or analysis that then gets submitted. Anyone selling a finished investigation is selling the student a malpractice finding, and the hours are worse than wasted.

sections.heading: Online, in-home and group delivery, priced against the Palm's one road
paragraphs: Palm Jumeirah is connected to the mainland by a single trunk road, and every frond is a gated cul-de-sac hanging off it. The monorail runs along the trunk and serves the hotel strip rather than the residential fronds, so it does not help a school run or a tutor visit. For a parent weighing delivery options, that layout is the whole argument: the island is pleasant to live on and expensive to drive to on a weekday afternoon.

The table below prices the three realistic options against that geography. The figures in the AED column are market bands from the sources named earlier in this page, not IB Gram's rates. The travel column is the part no competitor page quantifies, and on this island it is the part that decides what an hour is worth.

Read across the rows and a pattern appears. Online delivery converts the whole fee into teaching and draws on every available Diploma Physics specialist rather than on the small number who live within a comfortable drive of the island. In-home delivery buys physical presence and pays for the junction. Group delivery buys a lower per-student rate and gives up the thing one-to-one is for, which is stopping on the exact place where this student's reasoning breaks.

None of this makes in-home tutoring wrong. For a nine-year-old who needs an adult in the room, presence matters more than specialism. For a Higher Level Physics student eight months from a written series, the opposite is true, and the Palm's geography makes the trade unusually clear. IB Gram's answer is online one-to-one for every UAE address, which is why the island's single access road never appears on an invoice.

sections.heading: Budgeting two Diploma years instead of one panic term
paragraphs: Most Physics money in Dubai is spent in the last six months of a two-year course, at the highest rates of the year, on the hardest problem to fix. Spreading the same budget across both years changes what it buys. In the first Diploma year the money goes on building uncertainty and graph fluency, on getting command terms right while there is time for habits to form, and on the investigation design before the data exists. In the second year it goes on consolidation and timed practice.

A workable shape looks like this. Term one of the first year: a short diagnostic block and then fortnightly sessions. Term two: a concentrated run on the data-analysis skills that feed every component. Term three, when the investigation is set: a few hours before the design is fixed, then feedback on the student's own draft. Second year: weekly sessions through the content-heavy terms, then timed-paper work with technique review. That sequence rarely costs more in total than a panicked final-term intensive and consistently buys more.

There is also a school-fee context worth knowing. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private-school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package. For a family already paying Dubai school fees, that freeze is the one piece of budget stability in the year, and it is the natural moment to decide what tutoring is worth over two years rather than reactively each term.

Finally, decide what you will not buy. Do not buy a package before a diagnostic session. Do not buy an exam-season intensive for a subject the student has not been attending properly, because attendance is the problem and hours will not fix it. Do not buy hours for a sibling simply because one child benefited. And do not buy anything on the promise of a particular grade - no tutor can promise a score, and anyone who does has told you something important about the rest of their claims.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation: what a Physics tutor may and may not touch
paragraphs: A fifth of the Diploma Physics grade comes from one investigation the student designs, carries out and reports. It is also where paid support is most often sold dishonestly, because a parent under deadline pressure is an easy customer. The boundary is not vague. Everything submitted must be the student's own, and the school signs a declaration to that effect.

Inside the boundary, a tutor can do a great deal. They can teach the physics the investigation depends on. They can press on whether a research question is answerable with the equipment available, which is the single most common design failure. They can explain what the published criteria reward, show worked examples of uncertainty treatment, and ask the questions an examiner would ask of a conclusion. They can read a draft the student has written and say where the reasoning does not hold. All of that is teaching, and all of it is allowed.

Outside the boundary is anything that puts the tutor's words, numbers or analysis into the submitted file. A tutor supplying data, rewriting sections, or handing over a template that becomes the report has crossed from teaching into malpractice, and the consequence falls on the student. One operator in this market openly sells finished internal assessments. That is an academic-integrity breach and an expulsion risk, not a shortcut, and no amount of urgency makes it worth considering.

The practical advice for a Palm Jumeirah family is to buy hours early and ask for process coaching, not rescue. Two or three sessions in the week the research question is being chosen are worth more than ten in the week before submission, cost less, and leave no ambiguity about whose work was submitted. Ask any prospective tutor directly what they will and will not do with internal assessment work. The answer is a reliable test of everything else.

sections.heading: Starting from Palm Jumeirah, and what the first session costs
paragraphs: The first step is a conversation about what is actually wrong, which is free. Useful things to have to hand: the current school report with the Physics grade and any predicted grade, which subject guide the school is teaching to, whether the student is at Higher or Standard Level, the date of the next school assessment, and a recent marked paper if one exists. A marked paper is worth more than a report, because it shows where marks were lost rather than how many.

The second step is a trial lesson at no cost. It exists to answer one question: can this tutor teach this student this syllabus. Watch for whether the tutor asks the student to explain their reasoning rather than explaining it to them, whether they name the component being worked on, and whether they can say which guide they are teaching to. Those three signals predict the next twenty hours better than any rate card does.

The third step is honest about availability. Diploma Physics at Higher Level is a narrow specialism and UAE-based availability for a specific weekday slot is not guaranteed. Where no UAE-based specialist is free at the time a family needs, the alternative offered is a specialist from the wider network teaching on Gulf Standard Time, and that is stated before anything is booked rather than discovered afterwards. Nobody else in this market discloses a coverage limit; this page does.

The fourth step is the schedule itself. Sessions are timed around the school day and the trunk-road reality, which usually means a start after 5:00pm for a secondary student travelling back from Al Barsha or Umm Suqeim, and a different pattern during Ramadan, when a post-Iftar slot often works better than an afternoon one. Lessons are delivered live online, one to one. IB Gram does not operate home visits anywhere in the UAE, and no UAE office or centre exists - the service is the teaching, delivered over video.
