Those are market figures from EdFlik, Tutopiya, Unitors, TutorChase, Bestimate and BartyED, not IB Gram's prices. What IB Gram offers before any fee conversation is a trial lesson at no cost, so the teaching can be judged first.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to put two children in the same Physics session?
faqs.answer: Per hour, yes. Small-group rates in Dubai are published at roughly AED 60 to 120 per student, against AED 150 or more for one-to-one. Whether it is cheaper per mark depends on the two students. Siblings taking the same level, at the same point in the course, with similar gaps, can share a session usefully. Siblings a year apart, or one at Higher and one at Standard Level, cannot: the session drifts to the middle and neither gets the diagnosis that one-to-one is for. A diagnostic session each is the cheaper experiment before committing.

faqs.question: How many Physics hours does an HL student usually need in the final year?
faqs.answer: There is no reliable average, and anyone quoting one is guessing. What is predictable is the shape. A Higher Level student with secure content usually needs weekly sessions through the content-heavy terms, a concentrated block on data analysis and uncertainty, two or three hours around the investigation design, and timed-paper technique work in the final term. A student with real content gaps needs more hours and should start sooner, because the same money buys learning in the first year and triage in the last. Start with a diagnostic session and plan the term from what it finds.

faqs.question: Does a higher hourly rate mean a better Physics tutor?
faqs.answer: Not reliably. The specialist band and the premium band overlap heavily in published Dubai rates, so a substantial part of the gap between an AED 270 hour and an AED 650 hour is positioning rather than teaching. What a higher rate does buy, sometimes, is scarcity: Higher Level Physics is a narrow specialism and genuine availability is limited. The useful tests are not price. Can the tutor name which subject guide they teach to, which component they are working on, and what they will not do with internal assessment work? A trial lesson answers all three.

faqs.question: Which part of IB Physics is worth paying for first?
faqs.answer: The data-analysis section of Paper 1. Uncertainty propagation, gradient work, linearising a relationship and interpreting an unfamiliar graph are all teachable in a handful of hours, and most students have never had them taught explicitly because class time goes on content. The skills then pay off twice more, in Paper 2 and in the scientific investigation, which carries 20% of the grade. After that, command-term work on Paper 2 explanations. Late content recovery is the most expensive block available and should be the last thing bought, not the first.

faqs.question: Do Physics tutoring rates rise as the May session gets closer?
faqs.answer: Effective cost does, even where the headline rate does not move. Availability tightens in the months before a written series, the slots left are the inconvenient ones, and the work left to do is the kind that responds least to hours. Some providers also package exam-season intensives at a premium. The practical consequence for a Palm Jumeirah family is that the same budget buys more in the first Diploma year than in the last term. Ask any provider directly whether their rate changes by season, and get the answer before booking a block.

faqs.question: What does the scientific investigation cost in tutoring hours?
faqs.answer: Far less than families expect, if the hours are bought early. Two or three sessions in the week the research question is being chosen typically do more than ten in the week before submission, because the common failure is a design that cannot generate analysable data. Later support is limited to what is legitimate: explaining the published criteria, teaching the physics involved, and giving feedback on a draft the student has written themselves. Nothing in the submitted file may come from the tutor. Buying early is both cheaper and the only version that leaves no ambiguity.

faqs.question: Is group Physics revision worth the saving over one-to-one?
faqs.answer: For broad revision across a syllabus, a group at AED 60 to 120 per student is reasonable value. For diagnosis, it is not, because a group cannot stop on the specific place where one student's reasoning about fields or uncertainty breaks down. Most families get the best result from a mixture: group or self-directed work for coverage, one-to-one hours aimed at the two or three error patterns a marked paper reveals. If only one can be afforded, buy the diagnosis, because revising the wrong thing thoroughly is the most expensive outcome available.

faqs.question: Can we pay for a single diagnostic Physics session rather than a block?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for a student stuck in the middle bands it is usually the right first purchase. One session spent on recent marked work, read against the published criteria, normally identifies one or two habits doing most of the damage - a missing line in derivations, uncertainty ignored, explanation questions answered as descriptions. Knowing that is worth more than a term bought on a guess. It also means the honest answer is available: sometimes the problem is mathematics rather than physics, or attendance rather than either, and no amount of Physics tutoring fixes those.

faqs.question: What happens to the fee if a Palm Jumeirah session is cancelled late?
faqs.answer: Ask this before booking anything, with any provider. Cancellation terms move the real cost of tutoring more than the headline rate does, and they vary widely: some providers bill in full inside 24 hours, some rebook once, some charge nothing. For a family on the island, the related question is what happens when a school event or a traffic problem makes a start time impossible. Online sessions are easier to shift than in-home visits for the obvious reason that nobody has already driven across the trunk-road junction to get there.

faqs.question: Does an hourly tutoring rate in Dubai include VAT?
faqs.answer: That depends on the provider, and it should be asked directly rather than assumed. The UAE VAT treatment of education services is a matter for the Federal Tax Authority, and a tutoring page is not the place to state it as settled fact. What a parent can reasonably insist on is clarity about the specific quote in front of them: whether the figure shown is the final amount payable, whether any tax is added at invoice, and whether the provider holds a tax registration number. Any provider unwilling to answer that in writing has answered a different question.

faqs.question: Why does a Physics specialist cost more than a general science tutor?
faqs.answer: Because the supply is much smaller and the work is different. A general science tutor can keep a Standard Level student moving and will usually struggle with Higher Level fields, with nuclear and quantum content, or with a derivation requiring calculus fluency. A specialist also knows the assessment: which command terms demand what, how the investigation criteria are applied, where the data-analysis section allocates marks. In published Dubai bands that difference shows as roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified general tutor against AED 200 to 450 and above for a subject specialist.

faqs.question: Is Physics tutoring in the first Diploma year money well spent?
faqs.answer: It is the best-value window in the course. In the first year the money goes on building habits while there is time for them to form: uncertainty fluency, command-term discipline, and a sound investigation design before any data exists. In the final term the same money buys triage on the problem least able to be fixed quickly. Families who start early generally spend less in total and get more for it. The counter-argument is that a student may not need help in the first year, which is exactly what a single diagnostic session will tell you.

faqs.question: Does my child need laboratory equipment at home for online Physics?
faqs.answer: No. The practical work for the scientific investigation is done at school, with the school's equipment, under the school's supervision, and that is where it belongs. What an online Physics session needs is modest: a stable connection, a device with a decent camera, a headset, a graphical calculator where the school specifies one, and some way to show working - a tablet with a stylus, or a phone positioned over paper. The single biggest improvement most families can make is the headset, because physics explanation depends on hearing the reasoning clearly.

faqs.question: How do we check a Dubai Physics tutor may legally charge for lessons?
faqs.answer: Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers categories including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published. Ask a prospective tutor whether they hold the permit, and check the official MoHRE service page for how it is issued.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest honest way to raise a Physics 4 to a 6?
faqs.answer: Spend first on finding out why the 4 is a 4. In most cases a marked paper shows two or three repeating habits rather than broad ignorance: explanation questions answered as descriptions, uncertainty omitted, derivations with a skipped step, or arithmetic collapsing under time pressure. Those are cheap to fix and worth whole grade boundaries. Then buy hours on the data-analysis section and on investigation process, since both pay off across components. No tutor can promise a particular grade, and a provider who offers one has told you how seriously to read their other claims.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-palm-jumeirah.closingHeading: Decide what the hour is for before you pay for it
dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-palm-jumeirah.closingBody: Palm Jumeirah families already accept a commute for school, so there is no reason to accept one inside a tutoring fee as well. The published Dubai bands on this page show what the market charges and who charges it; the component table shows where those hours actually move a Diploma Physics grade. Start with a conversation and a free trial lesson, bring a marked paper rather than a report card, and plan the term's hours against Paper 1B, Paper 2 technique and the investigation design. Lessons run live online, one to one, on Gulf Standard Time, with the coverage limits stated before anything is booked.

Each one has taken a cohort through Paper 1B data questions and the scientific investigation, and each works to a Gulf Standard Time timetable built around when a Greens bus route actually drops.

intro.heading: The real constraint in The Greens is the clock, not the subject
paragraphs: Parents in The Greens rarely start by asking whether their child needs help with Physics. They already know. What they ask is when a lesson could possibly happen. The Greens sits inside Al Thanyah Third, a low-rise grid of apartment blocks wrapped around Emirates Golf Club, with one artery in from Sheikh Zayed Road and another from Al Khail. Secondary school buses reach the community in a band that runs from about 15:30 to 16:30, depending on which school and which loop. By the time a fifteen-year-old has eaten, the afternoon is half gone.

That single fact decides more about tutoring outcomes here than any claim a provider can make about teaching quality. A session scheduled at 16:00 because it suited the tutor will be missed, moved or sat through in a daze roughly every third week. A session scheduled at 16:45, after the Dubai British School loop has cleared Al Thanyah, holds. The difference between those two bookings is the difference between twenty-eight lessons in a school year and eighteen.

Physics punishes gaps more than most Diploma subjects, which is why the timing matters this much. The 2023 course is cumulative: the kinematics and energy work in Theme A underpins the circular motion and gravitation in Theme D, and the wave treatment in Theme C reappears inside the quantum material in Theme E. A student who misses three consecutive weeks in February does not simply lose three weeks of content. They lose the scaffolding for the HL extension topics that arrive in the second year, and they discover it in a mock paper.

The other half of the problem is supply. The Greens has a dense population of international families and a thin population of people who have actually taught Diploma Physics. Chemistry and Maths tutors are findable within a short drive. A Physics specialist who can explain why a gradient of a velocity-time graph carries an uncertainty, and who knows that Paper 3 was retired with the 2023 guide, is a much rarer animal in any one neighbourhood. Searching by distance narrows the pool to whoever is nearby; searching by syllabus does not.

So IB Gram does the opposite of a proximity search. Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, and the tutor is chosen for the course your child is sitting rather than for the postcode they live in. Nobody drives anywhere. The afternoon window that exists after the bus is the window the lesson uses, and the specialist is the right specialist whether they are in Dubai, Mumbai or Manchester.

What follows is specific to this community: the schools The Greens feeds, the finish times those schools run, the realistic session windows that survive them, the assessment structure your child is being measured against, and the places Physics marks quietly leak away.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-the-greens.programmesIntro: Physics sits at the end of a long run-up. A Greens student arriving in DP1 has usually come through MYP Sciences at Emirates International School Meadows or Dubai International Academy, or through IGCSE Physics at Dubai British School or Dubai College. Each route leaves a different gap.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Physics
programmes.description: The two-year course assessed on the 2023 guide. Five themes — Space, time and motion; The particulate nature of matter; Wave behaviour; Fields; Nuclear and quantum physics — plus a compulsory scientific investigation worth a fifth of the grade. HL students take the same themes with additional depth and sit longer papers. Paper 1 splits into a multiple-choice section and a data-and-experimental section; Paper 2 is short answer and extended response.
programmes.countryNote: Among the schools a Greens family realistically chooses between, Dubai International Academy Emirates Hills, Emirates International School Meadows and GEMS Wellington International School all run Diploma Physics. Cohort sizes at HL are small, often a single teaching group, which means a student who falls behind in Theme D has nobody sitting next to them in the same position to compare notes with.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme Sciences
programmes.description: The feeder course for most IB Physics students. MYP Sciences is marked against four criteria — knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science — each scored out of eight. It builds experimental design and data handling early, but it carries very little of the algebraic manipulation that Diploma Physics assumes from week one.
programmes.countryNote: Emirates International School Meadows and Dubai International Academy both run the MYP through to Year 11, so a large share of Greens students enter DP1 from criterion-based marking rather than from an examination. The jump that catches them is not the content. It is being asked to rearrange an equation under time pressure without a criterion rubric explaining what good looks like.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: A smaller IB route that pairs Diploma courses with a career-related study and a reflective project. A CP student may take Physics SL as one of their Diploma courses, which means the same papers and the same scientific investigation but a different surrounding workload and a different set of deadlines competing for the same afternoon.
programmes.countryNote: The Career-related Programme is offered by only a handful of Dubai schools, so a Greens family on this route is usually travelling further for school than their neighbours. That longer journey compresses the available afternoon further, and it is the main reason CP Physics students here tend to book the Friday short-day slot.

programmes.name: The IGCSE Physics run-up
programmes.description: Not an IB programme, but the course most British-curriculum Greens students arrive from. Cambridge 0625 and Pearson 4PH1 both build strong recall and formula handling. Neither asks a student to propagate an uncertainty through a calculation, and neither requires the extended written reasoning that Paper 2 rewards at Diploma level.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai British School Emirates Hills, Dubai College and Kings' School Al Barsha all feed Greens households, and all run IGCSE before splitting towards A Level or the Diploma. A student moving from a grade 8 or A* in 0625 into Physics HL often meets their first real difficulty around uncertainties, which no IGCSE paper examined.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-the-greens.subjectsIntro: A Physics tutor is useful in proportion to how precisely they can name what is going wrong. The units below are the teachable blocks of the 2023 course as a tutor plans them, rather than a chapter list, and each carries its own characteristic failure.

subjects.name: Theme A — Space, time and motion
subjects.levels: SL and HL, with HL extension
subjects.description: Kinematics, forces, work, energy and momentum, then circular motion and, at HL, rotational dynamics and special relativity. The theme that everything later depends on. Students who cannot resolve a force on an incline reliably in DP1 will struggle with fields in DP2, because the geometry is the same problem in a different costume.

subjects.name: Theme B — The particulate nature of matter
subjects.levels: SL and HL, with HL extension
subjects.description: Thermal physics, the gas laws, the kinetic model, and at HL the thermodynamic treatment with entropy. Marks here are usually lost to units and to confusing temperature with internal energy. The arithmetic is gentle, which makes students careless with it.

subjects.name: Theme C — Wave behaviour
subjects.levels: SL and HL, with HL extension
subjects.description: Simple harmonic motion, wave characteristics, superposition, standing waves and the Doppler effect, with diffraction and resolution added at HL. The theme most often taught well and examined badly: students can define a node and still not interpret an unfamiliar interference sketch in Paper 1B.

subjects.name: Theme D — Fields
subjects.levels: SL and HL, with HL extension
subjects.description: Gravitational, electric and magnetic fields treated as one idea, plus electric circuits and electromagnetic induction. This is where most Diploma Physics students in Dubai first ask for help. Field lines, potential and potential energy get blurred together, and the sign conventions are unforgiving.

subjects.name: Theme E — Nuclear and quantum physics
subjects.levels: SL and HL, with HL extension
subjects.description: Radioactive decay, nuclear binding energy, fission and fusion, the photoelectric effect and, at HL, the quantum and nuclear structure extension. Arrives late in DP2 when revision has already begun, so it is routinely the least secure theme in a mock paper.

subjects.name: Paper 1A technique
subjects.description: Multiple choice across all five themes with no partial credit. Scoring here is a trainable skill distinct from physics knowledge: elimination, order-of-magnitude checks and recognising distractors built from a common algebraic slip. Many students lose more in Paper 1A than in any single theme.

subjects.name: Paper 1B data and experimental skills
subjects.description: Unseen apparatus, unseen data, graphs to draw and gradients to interpret with uncertainties attached. Nothing in the MYP or in IGCSE prepares a student for this. It is the single highest-return thing to drill with a tutor, because the skills transfer directly into the scientific investigation.

subjects.name: Paper 2 extended response
subjects.description: Short answers building into multi-part questions that cross themes. Command terms decide the mark: explain, deduce, outline and determine each demand a different shape of answer. Students who write everything they know for every verb run out of time in the final third of the paper.

subjects.name: The scientific investigation
subjects.description: One student-designed investigation, around ten hours of class time, a 3,000-word ceiling, marked on four criteria for a total of 24. Twenty per cent of the final grade, decided months before the examinations and almost entirely recoverable with structured feedback on the student's own drafts.

subjects.name: Mathematics for Physics
subjects.description: Logarithms for decay, small-angle approximations, vector resolution, unit algebra and rearranging before substituting. Physics HL students taking Maths AI rather than AA meet this gap most sharply. A Physics tutor who ignores the maths will keep re-teaching the same topic.

sections.heading: What time can an IB Physics session actually start in The Greens?
paragraphs: For most Greens households the honest answer is 16:30 at the earliest, and 16:45 if the school sits in Al Sufouh or Al Barsha. Dubai secondary timetables generally finish between 14:45 and 15:15, buses load for ten to fifteen minutes, and the run back into Al Thanyah Third takes between fifteen and forty minutes depending on the loop and the day. Add a meal and the first workable hour begins in the middle of the afternoon.

The variation inside that band is larger than parents expect. Regent International School sits inside The Greens itself, so its students are home before many buses have left their yards. Emirates International School Meadows runs a short loop and is usually the earliest bus back. Dubai College and GEMS Wellington International School are further west along Al Sufouh Road, and their loops arrive last. A single booking time cannot serve all of them, which is why a provider that offers fixed class times rather than fixed slots loses Greens students at the same rate every term.

The table below gives indicative windows for the schools this community feeds. Treat them as a starting point for a conversation rather than as published timetables: finish times differ by year group, co-curricular commitments move the bell, and bus routes are redrawn at the start of each academic year. The only number that matters is the one on your own route, and the reliable way to find it is to watch the drop time for two weeks before fixing a slot.

One more piece of arithmetic is worth doing before booking. A ninety-minute session starting at 16:45 ends at 18:15, which leaves a Diploma student their own evening for homework and sleep. A ninety-minute session starting at 18:00 ends at 19:30, by which point a DP2 student who was up at six has very little left. Later is not safer. The window immediately after the bus, before the day closes down, is the one that produces work.

sections.heading: The IB Physics course your child is actually sitting
paragraphs: Physics was rewritten for first teaching in 2023, and the version many tutors still describe no longer exists. The old options — astrophysics, imaging, relativity as an option block — are gone. Paper 3 is gone. In their place sit five themes taught to both levels, with the Higher Level course adding depth rather than separate option material, and a single internal assessment called the scientific investigation.

The assessment weighting is worth memorising because it changes where effort should go. Paper 1 carries 36% of the grade and is split into a multiple-choice section and a data-and-experimental section sat inside the same time allowance. Paper 2 carries 44% and is where the long reasoning lives. The scientific investigation carries the remaining 20% and is finished long before the examination session. A student who treats the investigation as a side task has handed away a fifth of the grade before the first paper is opened.

The practical difference between SL and HL is not a different syllabus. It is 240 taught hours against 150, additional depth inside each theme, and considerably longer papers. Paper 2 runs for an hour and a half at SL and two and a half hours at HL. That extra hour is not generosity; it is more extended-response marks, and stamina in the final forty minutes is a genuine differentiator in HL results.

This matters when you are choosing a tutor. Ask them which theme contains gravitational potential, or whether Paper 1B is sat separately. A tutor working from the pre-2023 course will answer the first question with an option number and the second with a yes. Neither answer is compatible with the course your child is actually taking, and the gap will not show up until a mock paper.

sections.heading: Where Physics marks leak away, theme by theme
paragraphs: Physics marks are rarely lost to not knowing the physics. They are lost to a small set of repeated technical failures, and each one is diagnosable from a single marked script. A tutor who cannot name which of them your child is doing is guessing, and a term of guessing costs more than the lessons did.

In Theme A the recurring loss is vector resolution under pressure. A student who can resolve a force on an incline when asked to resolve a force on an incline will often fail to recognise the same geometry inside a question about a banked curve or a pendulum. The fix is not more kinematics. It is twenty questions in which the geometry is hidden, until the recognition becomes automatic.

Theme D produces the largest single bleed in most Dubai cohorts. Gravitational potential, gravitational potential energy and field strength are three different quantities with three different units, and students who learn them as three similar formulae will mix them in any question that does not label which is wanted. Electric circuits add a second failure: internal resistance is taught once, appears in Paper 2 regularly, and is forgotten by almost everyone who has not been made to derive it.

Across every theme the quietest loss is command terms in Paper 2. State, outline, explain, deduce, determine and discuss ask for different amounts of writing and different kinds of reasoning. A student who writes a paragraph for every state and a sentence for every explain will be marked down twice: once for the missing reasoning and once for the time they no longer have. Marking a student's own script against the command terms, line by line, moves more marks in a fortnight than a month of new content.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation: a fifth of the grade, settled before the exams
paragraphs: The scientific investigation is the part of IB Physics most open to improvement and most often left until it is too late. It is one investigation of the student's own design, around ten hours of class time, with a 3,000-word ceiling and four marking criteria worth six marks each. Twenty-four marks in total, scaled to a fifth of the final grade, and unlike the examinations it can be revised, reconsidered and rebuilt before submission.

Dubai cohorts lose marks here in a predictable pattern, and most of it is visible in the research question. A question like 'how does temperature affect resistance' cannot be answered within ten hours because it does not specify a material, a range or a method of measurement. Criterion A asks for a design another student could repeat, and a broad question makes that impossible. Narrowing the question is usually the single highest-value hour a tutor spends on an investigation.

Criterion B is where physics students with good laboratory habits still lose marks. Uncertainties get recorded neatly in the raw data table and then vanish. They do not appear as error bars, they are not propagated into the gradient, and the final value arrives without a range attached. A moderator reading that sees a student who has collected data rather than analysed it. Criterion D compounds the problem: an evaluation that says 'human error' names nothing and therefore earns little.

The boundary a tutor works inside here is firm and worth stating plainly. The investigation must be the student's own work. A tutor may teach uncertainty propagation, may explain what each criterion rewards, may read a draft and say which criterion is unmet, and may ask the questions that make a student see their own gap. A tutor may not supply text, may not author a section, and may not hand over a method. IB academic-honesty rules make that distinction an expulsion risk for the student, not a stylistic preference.

sections.heading: Friday short days, Ramadan and the Dubai revision calendar
paragraphs: The UAE working and school week runs Monday to Friday with a short Friday, and that single structural fact is underused by every family who schedules tutoring as though it were a five-full-day week. Friday afternoon is the only genuine daytime block during term. A two-hour Friday session can hold a full timed Paper 2 and its marking, which no weekday hour between the bus and bedtime can.

Ramadan reorganises the day again. School hours shorten, energy drops through the afternoon, and the productive hours move either very early or to after Iftar. Families in The Greens who try to hold a 16:45 slot through Ramadan generally lose half of it. Moving the session to a post-Iftar evening window for those weeks, and agreeing that in advance rather than cancelling week by week, keeps the thread intact. A tutor who cannot shift timezone-wise for a month is the wrong tutor for a UAE family.

Counting backwards from the examination session is the part almost nobody does. Dubai schools sitting the May session run internal deadlines for the investigation and for the extended essay through the autumn and winter of DP2, with mocks in between. By the time the May papers arrive, the internal 20% has been locked for months. The work that moves a Physics grade therefore has to happen a long way before the revision period that parents instinctively plan for.

A note on dates. IB session and results dates are published by the IB itself and by your school's IB coordinator, and they change. This page deliberately publishes none of them. Cambridge and Pearson publish their own International GCSE timetables, which matter if a younger sibling is in Year 11, and those should be read from the board's live timetable page rather than from any tutoring site, including this one.

sections.heading: Practical skills when the lesson is on a screen
paragraphs: The reasonable objection to online Physics teaching is practical work, and it deserves a straight answer rather than reassurance. Your child's practical scheme of work belongs to their school. The laboratory is at school, the apparatus is at school, and the ten hours of investigation time are timetabled at school. No tutor, online or otherwise, replaces that, and any provider implying they can is describing something that is not theirs to offer.

What a tutor can do is the part schools have least time for: the analysis. Paper 1B does not test whether a student can clamp a boss head. It tests whether they can read unfamiliar apparatus from a diagram, identify what was controlled, decide which quantity to plot against which to get a straight line, draw error bars that mean something, and extract a gradient with an uncertainty attached. Every one of those is a screen activity. Shared datasets, a spreadsheet both people can see, and a graph built live are better teaching tools for this than a bench would be.

Screen sharing also makes a specific kind of feedback possible that is awkward in person. A tutor can open the student's own graph, zoom into the line of best fit, and show exactly where the chosen scale has thrown away two significant figures. They can replay a recorded explanation of uncertainty propagation three times before the next session. Both of those are routine online and clumsy across a kitchen table.

The honest limit is this: a student who has not been attending their school practicals will have a gap that tutoring narrows rather than closes. The first conversation with a tutor should establish how much laboratory time has actually happened, because the plan for a student with a full practical folder and a student with three loose sheets is not the same plan.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not touch on assessed work
paragraphs: This section exists because the search results your child's friends are using include sites selling finished internal assessments. Those sites are not an edgy shortcut. Under IB academic-honesty rules, submitting work that is not your own is malpractice, and the consequence falls on the student rather than on the website. A Diploma can be withheld. It is worth saying out loud to a sixteen-year-old under deadline pressure, because they will meet the offer.

The permitted boundary is wide and genuinely useful. A tutor may teach the underlying physics, explain what each marking criterion rewards, model the analysis on a different dataset, read a student's draft and name the criterion that is unmet, question a conclusion until the student sees the hole in it, and teach the mathematics of uncertainty until it is automatic. All of that improves marks and all of it is legitimate, because the thinking stays with the student.

The forbidden side is narrow and absolute. A tutor does not supply sentences for submission, does not author a method, does not hand over a dataset, and does not edit a draft into something the student could not have produced. The same line applies to the extended essay and to theory of knowledge. If a provider's offer is that something arrives finished, the offer is malpractice regardless of how it is described.

There is a practical test a parent can apply. Ask the tutor what they would do if your child sent a half-written investigation at ten at night with a deadline the next morning. The right answer is a list of questions sent back and an honest statement that the remaining work is the student's to do. Any answer that involves the tutor producing content is the wrong answer, and hearing it early saves a great deal of trouble later.
bullets: Permitted: teaching, criterion explanation, draft feedback, questioning, modelling on other data
Not permitted: supplying text, authoring sections, handing over methods or datasets
The consequence of malpractice falls on the student, not the website
Ask any prospective tutor the night-before-deadline question

sections.heading: KHDA reports, and what they tell you about a physics department
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which inspects them annually and publishes the outcome on a six-band scale running from Outstanding down to Very Weak. Dubai's private sector held 227 schools serving 387,441 students in 2024-25 across seventeen curricula, with International Baccalaureate programmes accounting for seven per cent of enrolment against thirty-seven per cent on the UK curriculum. That mix is why a Greens apartment block contains students on three different science courses.

An inspection report is more useful to a parent than its headline band. The reports break attainment and progress down by subject and by phase, which means a school rated Very Good overall can carry a science department whose secondary progress is only Good. If you are trying to work out whether your child's difficulty with Theme D is personal or structural, that breakdown answers the question better than a parents' group chat does.

KHDA also sets requirements that shape the timetable your tutoring has to fit inside. Arabic, Islamic Education and social and moral studies are mandatory in Dubai private schools whatever international curriculum the school is licensed to teach, with instructional time calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit. For an IB student those lessons occupy periods that are not available for Physics, which is part of why the Diploma feels compressed in Dubai schools specifically.

A word on what a regulator relationship is and is not. KHDA inspects and licenses schools, and it issues educational services permits to training institutes that operate premises in Dubai. IB Gram holds no such permit, claims no regulatory approval, and operates no centre in the UAE. Any tutoring provider describing itself as approved by KHDA, by ADEK, by the Ministry of Education or by the IB should be asked to show the permit number, because the claim is specific and checkable.

faqs.question: What time can an IB Physics lesson start if my child takes a school bus home to The Greens?
faqs.answer: For most routes, 16:30 is the earliest workable start and 16:45 is safer. Dubai secondary timetables finish between roughly 14:45 and 15:15, buses load for ten to fifteen minutes, and the run into Al Thanyah Third takes fifteen to forty minutes. Students at Regent International School, which sits inside The Greens, can start earlier because they need no bus. Students at Dubai College or GEMS Wellington International School in Al Sufouh usually need 17:00. The reliable method is to watch your own drop time for two weeks and then fix a slot ten minutes after the latest arrival you saw.

faqs.question: Has IB Physics Paper 3 really been removed from the course?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Physics guide for first teaching in 2023 restructured the course into five themes taught at both levels and removed the separate option paper entirely. Assessment is now Paper 1, split into a multiple-choice section and a data-and-experimental section, carrying 36% of the grade; Paper 2 carrying 44%; and the scientific investigation carrying 20%. A tutor who talks about option topics or about preparing for Paper 3 is working from the previous course. Ask any prospective Physics tutor this question directly, because the answer tells you within a sentence whether they have taught the current syllabus.

faqs.question: My son is at Dubai International Academy and finds Theme D fields impossible. Is that usual?
faqs.answer: It is the most common sticking point in Diploma Physics, and it is usually a naming problem rather than a conceptual one. Field strength, potential and potential energy are three distinct quantities with three sets of units, and students who learn them as three similar equations cannot tell which a question wants. Electric circuits add internal resistance, which is taught once and then assumed. The fix is narrow and quick: separate the three quantities explicitly, derive rather than memorise, and work through unlabelled questions until recognition is automatic. Most students need three or four focused sessions, not a term.

faqs.question: How many hours of IB Physics tutoring does a Greens student typically need before mocks?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on the diagnosis, which is why an honest answer starts with a diagnostic rather than a package. A DP1 student drifting in one theme often needs six to eight sessions. A DP2 student whose mock revealed losses across Themes C, D and E, plus weak Paper 1A technique, is looking at two sessions a week through a six to eight week block. A student whose real problem is the mathematics underneath Physics may need a longer run. Any provider quoting a fixed hour count before seeing a marked script is guessing at your expense.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Physics scientific investigation without crossing an academic-honesty line?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the permitted work is substantial. A tutor can teach uncertainty propagation, explain what each of the four criteria rewards, model an analysis on an unrelated dataset, read a draft and name which criterion is unmet, and question a conclusion until the student sees the gap themselves. What a tutor must never do is supply sentences for submission, author a section, or hand over a method or dataset. The thinking and the words stay with the student. That line is what keeps the diploma safe, and it is worth asking any tutor to state it before you book.

faqs.question: Does my child need laboratory equipment at home for online IB Physics lessons?
faqs.answer: No. The practical scheme of work and the ten hours of investigation time belong to your child's school, where the apparatus is. Tutoring covers the part schools have least time for, which is analysis: reading unfamiliar apparatus from a diagram, deciding what to plot to get a straight line, drawing meaningful error bars, and extracting a gradient with an uncertainty attached. All of that is better done on a shared screen with a live spreadsheet than at a bench. The first session should establish how much laboratory time has actually happened, because that changes the plan.

faqs.question: How are uncertainties and error bars examined in IB Physics?
faqs.answer: They appear in two places and they carry real weight in both. Paper 1B presents unseen data and asks a student to process it, which routinely means propagating an uncertainty into a gradient and stating a final value with a range. Criterion B of the scientific investigation marks the same skill on the student's own data, and this is where most marks are lost: uncertainties get tabulated once and then disappear, with no error bars on the graph and no range on the result. Neither Cambridge nor Pearson IGCSE examines this, so it is genuinely new in DP1.

faqs.question: Is Physics HL worth taking if my child wants to study engineering at a UAE university?
faqs.answer: Physics HL is the conventional route and most engineering faculties treat it as the expected preparation, usually alongside Mathematics Analysis and Approaches. What matters more than the general answer is the specific entry page of the specific programme, because requirements vary between institutions and between engineering disciplines, and they are revised. Read the university's own admissions page and, if the student needs certificate equivalency, the Ministry of Education's own guidance. No tutoring provider should tell you what a university requires, and tutoring is not a requirement for any admissions process.

faqs.question: Do The Greens and The Views share the same tutoring slots?
faqs.answer: In practice yes, and that is worth knowing before you book. The two communities sit either side of Emirates Golf Club on the same Al Thanyah Third approach, frequently on the same school bus loops, and they feed the same set of schools. Demand for the 16:30 and 17:30 Physics windows therefore peaks across both at once, and those are the first slots to disappear each September. Families who fix a slot in the first fortnight of term get the window they want; families who wait until after the first assessment generally take what is left.

faqs.question: What happens to our Physics sessions during Ramadan in The Greens?
faqs.answer: School hours shorten, afternoon energy drops, and a 16:45 slot that worked in January stops working. The approach that holds is to agree the Ramadan arrangement before the month begins rather than cancelling week by week: either an early slot before school pressure builds or a post-Iftar evening session. Both are normal for UAE families and both are workable online, since no travel is involved. A tutor who cannot move within the day for a month is the wrong tutor for a household in Dubai, and this is a fair question to ask at the trial.

faqs.question: Should my child take Physics HL alongside Mathematics Applications and Interpretation rather than Analysis and Approaches?
faqs.answer: It is possible and some students do it successfully, but it creates a workload a tutor has to plan around. Physics HL leans on algebraic manipulation, logarithms for decay, small-angle approximations and vector resolution, and Analysis and Approaches builds those explicitly while Applications and Interpretation takes a different route. A student pairing Physics HL with Applications usually needs part of their Physics time spent on the mathematics itself. That is manageable when it is planned for and expensive when it is discovered in DP2. Discuss the combination with the school's IB coordinator before the choice is locked.

faqs.question: What do Physics tutors charge per hour around The Greens and Dubai Marina?
faqs.answer: Published market rates in Dubai, taken from providers' own pages and from independent cost surveys, run roughly AED 45 to AED 150 an hour for budget or university-student online tutoring, AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 180 to AED 500 for an in-home visit including travel, and AED 200 to AED 450 or more for an IB or A Level specialist. Those are market figures attributed to their sources, not an IB Gram price list. Our own rates are discussed in the consultation against the number of sessions actually needed.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a Physics tutor to our apartment in The Greens?
faqs.answer: No. All UAE tutoring is delivered one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. Home visits are a service IB Gram offers only in India, and there are no home visits in Dubai. That is a deliberate choice rather than a limitation: it means the Physics specialist matched to your child is chosen from the whole pool rather than from whoever can reach Al Thanyah Third before six. For a subject with as few genuine Diploma specialists as Physics, the trade of travel for expertise is the one that moves grades.

faqs.question: My daughter is resitting Physics in a later session. Can a tutor pick that up mid-course?
faqs.answer: Yes, and a resit is one of the clearer tutoring briefs because the evidence already exists. The starting point is the component breakdown from the previous session: a student who lost marks mainly in Paper 1A needs technique work, one who lost them in Paper 2 needs command-term and extended-response work, and one whose internal mark was weak has a different problem again. The internal assessment mark usually carries forward, so confirm with your school's IB coordinator what has to be resubmitted before planning any sessions around it.

faqs.question: What does a KHDA inspection report actually tell me about a school's science teaching?
faqs.answer: More than the headline band does. KHDA inspects Dubai private schools annually and publishes outcomes on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak, but the reports break attainment and progress down by subject and by phase. A school rated Very Good overall can hold a secondary science department whose progress is only Good, and that detail is published. If you are trying to judge whether a difficulty with Theme D is your child's or the department's, the subject-level breakdown in the report answers it better than any parent group chat.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-the-greens.closingHeading: Fix the slot first, then the physics
dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-the-greens.closingBody: The useful next step for a Greens family is small. Note the actual bus drop time for your route, note whether your child is SL or HL, and find the most recent marked Physics script in the bag. With those three things a tutor can tell you within one conversation whether the problem is content, mathematics, uncertainty handling or examination technique, and which of the five themes is costing the most. The trial lesson then runs at the real time on the real day, so you can see whether a tired Diploma student engages after a bus ride. Everything is online, one-to-one, in Gulf Standard Time, and nobody drives anywhere.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-the-springs.tutorsIntro: The profiles below are Physics-first: people who teach the current Diploma Physics guide, mark against its four internal-assessment criteria, and can say which theme a dropped mark came from. intro.heading: The cost of IB Physics help in The Springs, before anyone quotes you a number
paragraphs: Ask five providers what an IB Physics tutor in The Springs costs and you will get five answers spread across a factor of ten. Budget online platforms advertise from the low double figures in AED per hour. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table puts in-home one-to-one work at AED 180 to 350 and subject specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above. One UK agency publishes AED 270 for its UAE work. A named-examiner service in Dubai publishes AED 650. None of those figures is a lie, and none of them tells you what your child's Physics problem will cost to fix.

The reason is that Physics does not fail in one place. A Springs student can be fluent in kinematics and unable to read a gradient off a log plot. Another can handle every calculation in Theme A and lose eleven marks across Paper 2 because nobody ever showed them what the command term 'deduce' requires that 'state' does not. A third has a scientific investigation due in eleven weeks with no measurable variable chosen yet. Those are three different jobs, needing three different numbers of hours, and a rate card cannot separate them.

So this page is built the other way around. It starts from the assessment, because the assessment decides where hours are worth buying. It then puts real AED bands next to the three jobs a Physics tutor is usually hired for, names the three ways families around Emirates Living spend money without moving a grade, and finishes with what happens when a household decides to start. Every figure carries the source it came from and the date it was published.

The delivery model is worth stating before the prices, because it changes the arithmetic. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a Springs townhouse or to any other UAE address; in-home visiting is a service we run only in India. Physics support for families here is one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time around the school run. That removes the travel component that in-home Dubai rates carry, and it widens the pool from whoever is free in Emirates Living to whoever actually teaches Diploma Physics well.

The Springs sits inside the densest private-school market in the country. KHDA counted 387,441 students across 227 private schools in Dubai in 2024-25, with 17 different curricula licensed and the International Baccalaureate holding seven per cent of that enrolment. Seven per cent of a market that size is a lot of Diploma students and a small, over-subscribed group of people who teach Physics at Higher Level. That scarcity, not the cost of an hour, is what makes Physics the subject families struggle to resource locally.

Physics content appears inside integrated science units rather than as a separate subject, so a student can arrive in DP1 having never written a full physics derivation.
programmes.countryNote: Emirates International School Meadows runs the IB continuum on the doorstep of The Springs, which means a sizeable group of local children meet criterion-based science marking years before they meet a Physics paper. programmes.name: Diploma Programme Physics
programmes.description: The current Physics guide organises content into five themes: space, time and motion; the particulate nature of matter; wave behaviour; fields; and nuclear and quantum physics. programmes.name: IGCSE and International GCSE Physics
programmes.description: Most British-curriculum schools around Emirates Living run Cambridge Physics 0625 or the Pearson Edexcel equivalent, tiered into Core and Extended at Cambridge with a practical or alternative-to-practical component. It is the qualification that decides whether Physics HL is a realistic Diploma choice two years later.

A grade 6 at Extended level is the usual signal that Physics SL will be comfortable and Physics HL will need deliberate mathematical support from the first week of DP1 rather than from the first mock.

programmes.description: Several campuses in the second ring around The Springs offer A Level rather than the Diploma. A Level Physics goes deeper into fewer topics and carries no equivalent of the Diploma's internal assessment weighting, which changes both the revision shape and the amount of supervision a student needs outside lessons.
programmes.countryNote: Worth naming on a cost page because the two routes need different numbers of hours. A Level Physics support tends to cluster into pre-exam blocks; Diploma Physics support spreads across two years because the investigation, the themes and the mathematics all mature at different speeds.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-the-springs.subjectsIntro: Physics is the page, but almost no Springs household buys one subject. These are the courses most often added to a Physics booking, with the specific thing each one tends to need.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Five themes, two written papers and a 3,000-word scientific investigation. Marks are lost most reliably in uncertainty propagation, in field-line reasoning, and in extended-response questions where the answer is right and the reasoning is not shown.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The usual companion booking for a Physics HL student. Calculus fluency, not algebraic neatness, is what decides whether a Physics derivation is readable. Students who take Applications and Interpretations alongside Physics HL need the gap closed early.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Shares the same assessment shape as Physics, including the 20% investigation, so one tutor can often coach both internal assessments through the same criteria. Energetics and equilibrium are where the overlap with Physics thinking is strongest.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Chosen by students who want the statistics and modelling route. It is a legitimate pairing with Physics SL. Paired with Physics HL it leaves a measurable calculus gap that shows up in Theme D.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The third science in most Springs timetables. Its investigation is judged on the same four criteria as Physics, which means a student juggling two science investigations has one skill to learn, not two.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Frequently added by Physics students aiming at engineering. The internal assessment is a developed product with documentation, so the supervision load lands in a different term from the Physics investigation.

subjects.name: Design Technology
subjects.description: Overlaps with Physics in mechanics and materials. Its coursework is substantial and runs long, so families pairing it with Physics HL should plan the calendar before booking hours.

subjects.name: Extended Essay in Physics
subjects.description: A popular choice for strong Physics students and a difficult one, because a measurable, repeatable experiment is harder to design than a reading-based question. Supervision is feedback on the student's own drafts, never drafting.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The core element Physics students most often underestimate. It asks for argument rather than calculation, and a 1,600-word limit punishes the habit of writing everything known about a topic.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Required in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum. It sits outside the IB grade but inside the weekly timetable, and it competes for exactly the hours a Physics student wants for revision.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-the-springs.regionsIntro: The Springs sits in the Emirates Living district, and its neighbours share its schools, its road geometry and its tutoring price points. These are the areas we work with on the same terms.

regions.note: Villas rather than townhouses, immediately north of The Springs across the same internal road network. Shares Emirates International School Meadows and the Emirates Hills campuses, so the Physics cohort is effectively one pool.

regions.name: The Views

regions.name: The Greens
regions.note: Apartment blocks with a younger demographic, mostly MYP and IGCSE rather than Diploma. Physics bookings here are usually 0625 rather than DP, and shorter.

regions.name: Emirates Hills
regions.note: Large plots, two IB-continuum campuses on its edge, and the highest concentration of Higher Level science students in this part of Dubai. Also the area where in-home rates quoted locally run hardest against the market bands.

regions.name: Jumeirah Park and Jumeirah Islands
regions.note: Across Sheikh Zayed Road, sharing Regent International School and the Dubai British School routes. Session timing is set by bus return rather than by distance.

regions.name: Al Barsha South and Dubai Hills Estate
regions.note: The eastward spill from Emirates Living, with newer campuses and a growing Diploma cohort. Families here often start Physics support in DP1 rather than waiting for DP2 mocks.

sections.heading: What an IB Physics tutor costs around The Springs, in AED and with sources
paragraphs: Dubai market rates for Physics tuition run from roughly AED 45 an hour at the budget end to AED 650 for a named-examiner service. The useful part of that range for a Diploma Physics student is narrower. Published 2026 rate tables for Dubai put qualified subject tutors working online at AED 150 to 300, in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 once travel is priced in, and IB or A Level specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above. One UK-based agency publishes AED 270 for its UAE tutoring. A Dubai premium service publishes AED 650 for examiner-led work.

Those bands behave differently at the two ends. Below about AED 150 an hour you are usually buying a university student who knows the physics and has never seen an IB mark scheme. That is adequate for homework rescue and poor value for Paper 2 technique, because the thing being bought is content the student can already read in a textbook. Above about AED 450 the premium is being charged for examiner adjacency rather than for teaching hours, and examiner status cannot legitimately be sold as access to marking, boundaries or paper content.

The middle band is where Diploma Physics work actually sits, and the honest answer to 'how much will this cost' is a number of hours multiplied by a rate, not a rate alone. A student who needs Paper 2 technique for a May series typically needs twelve to twenty sessions. A student rebuilding Theme D from scratch needs more. A student who needs the investigation steered to a defensible research question needs four to six. Multiply before you compare providers.

IB Gram does not publish an hourly price list on these pages, because the rate depends on the tutor matched and the subject level. What we publish is the market context above, the free trial lesson that precedes any payment, and the consultation where the hours are estimated out loud. Any figure on this page is a market rate from a named published source, not a quotation from us.

sections.heading: The three places Physics money disappears in Emirates Living
paragraphs: The first leak is buying content when the problem is technique. A Springs parent sees a 4 in a Physics mock and books twenty hours of teaching through the themes. The student already knew most of it; the marks were lost because 'explain' answers were written as 'describe' answers, because uncertainties were quoted to four significant figures, and because the final two questions on Paper 2 were never reached. Twenty hours of re-teaching produces a student who knows the course slightly better and scores the same. The diagnostic that would have found this costs one session.

The second leak is group classes bought at a per-head rate that looks efficient. Small-group science in Dubai is advertised widely and it works for structured content delivery. It does not work for a student whose problem is specific, because a group moves at the median and Physics failures are rarely median. A household paying a reduced group rate for sixteen weeks often pays more in total than one that bought eight properly targeted individual sessions, and the grade movement is smaller.

The third leak is starting late and paying the panic premium. Rates in this market do firm up as a series approaches, and availability for Higher Level Physics thins first. A family that books in October has a choice of specialists at the standard band. A family that books in late February is choosing from whoever is left, often at the top of the range, and buying hours that have to carry both content repair and paper technique at once. The calendar section below counts this backwards so the decision can be made early.

There is a fourth pattern worth naming because it is not a leak at all. Families who buy fewer hours than they expected to, after a diagnostic, frequently get better results than families who buy a large block up front. The reason is dull: targeted work on three known weaknesses moves more marks than general improvement across a course a student mostly knows.

sections.heading: Where the Physics grade actually sits: papers, weightings and hours
paragraphs: Spending decisions get easier once the assessment is on the table. In the current Diploma Physics guide, Paper 1 carries 36% of the grade, Paper 2 carries 44%, and the internal assessment carries 20%, at both Standard and Higher Level. Paper 1 splits into a multiple-choice section and a data-based section. Paper 2 is short and extended response. Higher Level sits longer papers covering the additional higher-level content inside each of the five themes. Confirm the version and the timings for your child's cohort with their Diploma coordinator before planning around them.

Read that weighting as a budget. Paper 2 is the single largest block of marks on the course, and it is the component most responsive to tutoring, because extended response is a trainable skill with a vocabulary. The internal assessment is a fifth of the grade, is completed months before the examinations, and is the component where a student has the most control. Paper 1 rewards breadth and speed and is the hardest to move quickly with extra hours.

The practical consequence for a Springs household is a spending order rather than a spending total. Secure the investigation first, because it is worth 20% and it has a deadline that does not move. Then put the bulk of weekly hours into Paper 2 technique across the themes the student is weakest in. Treat Paper 1 as something maintained with timed practice rather than taught. A plan built in that order tends to need fewer total hours than one built by walking through the syllabus from Theme A.

The investigation deserves its own note, since it is where the 20% is won or lost quietly. It is a single report with a 3,000-word ceiling, judged against four criteria worth six marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Students lose marks in research design more than anywhere else, usually by choosing a question with no genuinely controllable independent variable. That is a one-session conversation in September and an unfixable problem in March.

sections.heading: Tutoring cost in context: school fees, the fee freeze and a two-year Physics plan
paragraphs: Tutoring is a line in a household education budget that already has a much larger line in it. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai will not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. For a Springs family, that freeze is the reason a tutoring decision this year is a decision about new money rather than about absorbing a fee increase.

Put a Physics plan against that. A weekly 90-minute session at the mid band of the market runs into a monthly figure in the hundreds of dirhams; published monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions in Dubai sit at AED 240 to 600 for budget provision, AED 600 to 1,200 for mid-range and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support. Monthly packages advertised in this market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

The two-year shape matters more than the monthly number. DP1 Physics support is cheap and preventive: fortnightly sessions, an early investigation conversation, and a mathematics check. DP2 support is expensive and corrective: weekly sessions, a paper-technique block, and whatever the investigation did not get done. Families who spend modestly in DP1 generally spend less in total, because the expensive work is the work that has to be done against a deadline.

Dubai's school sector is also still growing, which affects availability rather than price. Seven new private schools open for the 2026-27 intake, four British-curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, adding 16,846 places; six opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose six per cent. More Diploma cohorts mean more demand for the same small group of Higher Level Physics teachers, and that pressure is felt as waiting time, not as a higher advertised rate.

sections.heading: Online or in-home for Physics in The Springs, judged on value rather than preference
paragraphs: The in-home question is the one most Springs parents actually arrive with, so it deserves a straight answer rather than a sales line. In-home one-to-one tuition in Dubai is real, it is widely available, and published rate tables put it at AED 180 to 350 an hour with home tutors advertised up to AED 500. The premium over online work is not a quality premium. It is the cost of the tutor's travel, the vehicle, and the dead time on either side of the lesson, which in practice is charged back inside the hourly rate.

The second cost is invisible and larger. Choosing in-home restricts you to Physics teachers who can reach Emirates Living inside an acceptable drive. In a subject with as thin a specialist pool as Higher Level Physics, that filter removes most of the candidates before quality enters the conversation. A Springs family optimising for a tutor who can park outside is optimising for geography, and geography does not teach fields and quantum physics.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; that service exists only in our India operation. Physics work for Springs households is one-to-one over live video, with a shared screen for diagrams, graph work and marked scripts. For a subject built on annotated diagrams and worked algebra, a shared screen is closer to how a Physics teacher actually works at a whiteboard than a notebook on a kitchen table is.

There is one genuine advantage to a physical presence, and it is worth naming: a younger student who will not sit still is easier to manage in the same room. For a fourteen-year-old on 0625 that can matter. For a seventeen-year-old on Physics HL preparing for a May series, the deciding variable is whether the person on the other side of the session has taught the course and marked to its criteria.

sections.heading: Counting backwards from the series your child is entered for
paragraphs: Physics spending is time-sensitive in a way most subjects are not, because the investigation has an internal deadline months before the papers. Working backwards from the examination series is the single most useful planning exercise a Springs family can do, and it is the thing no competitor page in this market does at all.

We do not publish IB examination or results dates on these pages. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so every date we could print would be second-hand, and a second-hand date on an examinations page is a liability rather than a service. UAE schools sit the May series as the main session, with November available; the exact windows, the internal upload deadlines and the results dates come from your child's Diploma coordinator, who works to the current official calendar.

Cambridge and Pearson publish their dates openly, and they illustrate how far ahead the real deadlines sit. For the Cambridge March 2027 series, the examination period runs 3 February to 4 March 2027, final entries are due 27 November 2026, forecast grades are due 27 February 2027, results reach centres on 13 May and certificates follow in late June. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November series; the November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026.

The operational point for a Physics family is that the entry deadline sits roughly three months before the first paper, and the tutoring decision that matters sits before that again. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that the correct zone timetable must be used, stating that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong version. Ask your school which zone it sits in before you plan a revision calendar around a published timetable.

sections.heading: What a Physics tutor may and may not do with an investigation
paragraphs: Spending money on internal assessment support raises a question parents are right to ask, because the answer separates teaching from malpractice. A Physics tutor may explain what each of the four criteria rewards, ask why a variable was chosen, point out that an uncertainty has been quoted without justification, question whether a conclusion is supported by the data, and read a draft the student wrote and say where the reasoning stops. That is supervision, and it is what the 20% component is meant to receive.

A tutor may not choose the research question, design the method, process the data, write any part of the report, or edit a draft into a different piece of work. IB Gram does not provide any of those things and will not take a booking that asks for them. The work has to be the student's own, and a report that is not is an academic-honesty matter for the student with consequences far larger than a Physics grade.

This has a practical cost consequence for a Springs household. Supervision is cheaper than it looks, because it is a small number of well-timed conversations rather than a long block of hours. Four to six sessions spread across the drafting window usually covers the research question, the method review, a first look at the analysis and a final read of the student's own draft. Families who ask for more hours than that are usually asking, without meaning to, for someone else to do the work.

The same boundary applies to a Physics Extended Essay, to Theory of Knowledge and to any school coursework. Official past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and subject guides are not ours to distribute; they belong to the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and the correct route to them is through the school or the board's own site. We reference them and point to them; we do not hand them over.

sections.heading: Permits, ethics and the questions that protect your money
paragraphs: A cost page is incomplete without the legal position, because the cheapest tutor in Emirates Living may be the one who should not be teaching your child. Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and it covers teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time through its app, website and e-services.

Because the permit costs nothing, a tutor without one has no financial excuse. Individuals offering private tutoring without a MoHRE permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published, so no figure should be quoted at you by anyone. Asking whether a tutor holds a current permit is a reasonable question and a cheap piece of due diligence.

There is a second rule that catches a common Springs arrangement. Abu Dhabi's ADEK professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff bar teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Verify the current wording against the authority's own policy before relying on it, but the direction is clear: your child's own classroom teacher is the wrong person to hire privately, however convenient the arrangement looks.

One further distinction matters in Dubai specifically. An individual tutor needs the MoHRE permit. A tutoring operation with premises and staff needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a six-month maximum to complete the permit and licence steps, and renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. IB Gram operates no premises in the UAE, holds no regulator permit of that kind, and does not describe itself as having one.
